He who constantly performed worship of the gods, under whose reign the subjects were happy,
and by whom many sacrifices were offered on the banks of the Tāmraparṇī.
And by means of that celestial chariot, the king departed for another world;
thus, having ascended the vimāna, he went to the abode known as Śveta.
Then, through yoga, he went to that abode resting upon the ocean of milk—
the sleeping Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who reclines upon Ananta.
Just as he was about to prostrate himself like a staff, Nārāyaṇa rose up;
he then honored the Lord of Śrī with jewels, pearls, and other precious gifts.
With beautiful leaves of gold, flowers such as diamonds and the like,
incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, garments, and likewise ornaments.
He worshipped the Supreme Lord with divine jewels and ten thousand gems;
having thus worshipped and bowed down, he sat down in the presence of Hari.
At that very time, a Brahmin named Viṣṇudāyaka came from that same kingdom, bringing tulasī, water, and flowers for the purpose of worship. ||22||
He too performed the worship of Śrī Hari with offerings such as leaves;
indeed, diamonds and other precious gems were covered by him with leaves, flowers, and the like. ||23||
Then, observing his own worship thus covered, the king said to the brahmin: "How is it that [this] is so beautifully adorned with gold, rubies, and other gems?"
"O Brahmin, worship was performed by me, yet it has been obscured by you with [your] leaves;
you have no sense of respect, nor do you understand true worship. (25)
O twice-born one, you do not even calculate its price, yet you treat it as unsurpassed; whereas leaves and such inferior things, you treat as superior. (26)
Thus addressed, that noble-minded twice-born man spoke there concerning the tonsure ceremony:
"O King, the worship of Viṣṇu, when accompanied by meditative devotion, is always dear to him. (27)
O sinless one, she who stands rooted in pride and egoism does not become beloved;
yet by you, worship is performed with flowers made of jewels, gold, and the like.
I too shall perform that very same worship with water and tulasī leaves; yet my worship, through its underlying intention, is superior to yours. (29)
"Speak, O King: what vow have you performed for the sake of royal splendor?
I have indeed performed nothing at all; tell me if anything great has been done by you."
Then Caula, full of pride, said to the brahmin: "That which was to be done has been done;
I have given gifts of gold, as well as gifts of jewels and diamonds. (3.1)
Indeed, infinite gifts of cows have been made and many sacrifices performed;
I offer diamonds daily for the worship of Śrī Hari.
"Though you are destitute, my devotion is superior because of your devotion [to me]. You have not performed a sacrifice, nor have you built a temple. (33)
"O Brahmin, see, everything has been done by me; furthermore, I shall perform another sacrifice and go to have a direct vision of Hari. (34)
Only those Brahmins who possess supreme devotion will understand this, and not otherwise;
first, I shall perform a sacrifice to Viṣṇu for the purpose of direct realization.
Having spoken thus and bowed to Śrī Hari, he went to the region of Caula.
Caula, having appointed Mudgala as his officiating priest (ācārya), commenced the sacrifice.
From Satyaloka upwards, there are the Vairājas, celibate students, sages, seers, the elders, the ancestors, and likewise the gods. (37)
Sacrifices, gods, gandharvas, and humans as well as those who honor the earth (brahmins);
rivers and streams, sacred fords, trees, and likewise creepers—[all these were present]. (38)
Cities, sacred fields, and shrines located in the netherworld and on earth, as well as the most excellent stars and the Vaiṣṇava deities. (39)
All the goddesses, who dwell in every abode and have their leaders liberated,
were summoned by the king for his own Vaiṣṇava sacrifice.
Gold, wealth, diamonds, and all such things were offered there;
garments, food, drinks, and objects of enjoyment were offered in their entirety. (41)
Indeed, the resonant chanting of the Vedas by the sages occurred there at that great sacrifice;
the embodied forms of the Brahmins were truly satisfied there at the rite. 42.
The fires attained satisfaction, the gods were liberated and fully gratified;
and the truthful goddesses dwelling within the cosmic egg became filled with joy. ||43||
A great sacrifice was performed, and it became renowned throughout all the worlds;
however, it was done out of pride and not with a state of desirelessness. (44)
Whatever is performed out of rivalry, or even out of malice or envy,
all that shall not bear fruit, unlike the fruit born of freedom from desire.
Viṣṇudāsa performed service in the temple of Hari;
with both his body and his inner being, he likewise performed the ceremonial bathing of Hari.
Awakening, worship, adornment, offering incense and lamps, the offering of tulasī leaves, sprinkling with water, and formal adoration; ||47||

The offering of flowers, leaves, fruits, and water for honor (arghya), the offering of sandalwood paste, the giving of unbroken rice grains (akṣata) and saffron, and likewise the offering of bilva fruit (śrīphala) and other such items. ||48||
The waving of lights, circumambulation, praise, prostration and so forth, as well as the request for forgiveness, chanting, and likewise listening [to the sacred texts]. ||49||
Sweeping, smearing [the ground], chanting of qualities, and offering;
likewise, the offering of betel, water, and fragrant substances. || 1.425.50 ||
The gift of a fan is the offering of wind; likewise, the holding of a chowrie and the bearing of an umbrella, as well as the practice of seasonal regimens and so forth. ||51||
Having likewise prepared a flower garden and beautiful flower garlands and the like, and having established a grove of Tulasī, one should perform the watering for the sake of Hari. (52)
In this manner, with affection and devotion, Viṣṇudāsaka practiced supreme devotion to Lord Hari day and night, remaining steadfast in his conjugal fidelity.
He observed the vows of the Ekādaśī and other days, joined with recitation,
along with self-restraint, great devotion, and constant remembrance of Kṛṣṇa.
Through worship consisting of the sixteen articles, through dance and song, and through intense service with devotion, he indeed passes the time in every way.
Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, tasting, and even speaking;
grasping, walking, lying down, praising, meditating, and making determinations—(he remains thus). 56.
Thinking, honoring, experiencing, and likewise cultivating;
remembering, recognizing, doubting, and erring. (57)
Reflecting, perceiving, and desiring, he indeed exists as Viṣṇu alone;
knowing that Viṣṇu is the abode created by himself everywhere, he meditated upon Viṣṇu. (58)
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; Oṃ, obeisance again and again.
Thus, by chanting these sixteen syllables, he indeed became one with Viṣṇu. ||59||
The Blessed One himself always accepts service from the brahmin;
the Blessed One himself accepts the king’s sacrifice and the substances offered therein.
The Lord became visible to the brahmin but invisible to the king;
for such were the causes of presence and absence, as well as of pride and lack of pride, in that very situation.
Once, Viṣṇudāsa prepared sweet food in the kitchen as was his daily custom, while you remained there for some time, unobserved.
Thinking that there would be an obstacle to the worship at midday and that cooking would have to be done again, he did not cook again, nor did he eat himself. (63)
He indeed offered fruit and water as an oblation to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
on the second day as well, he likewise took away the cooked food that had been prepared.
On the third day as well, Mādhava took away the cooked food in that same manner;
thus, for seven days, he took the cooked food without it being offered.
Anxious with worry, the twice-born man stood near the cooking fire for the sake of protection;
having prepared the food, he remained in a corner of the house, holding wood and stones in his hands.
Having fasted for seven days, he beheld a certain outcaste who carried off cooked food— one who was filthy, hungry, and possessed of a withered body.
Seeing him, the twice-born man was filled with compassion; remembering Hari, he said, "Stay! Do not eat anything harsh; rather, eat clarified butter and take it [with you]."
Seeing that brahmin who had spoken thus, he fled out of fear;
having fallen there in a swoon, Viṣṇudāsaka went toward him.
He gave him water and fanned him with the edge of his garment;
then Viṣṇu rose up and assumed his four-armed form.
He beheld the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the four-armed Hari, resplendent with the conch, discus, mace, lotus, Kaustubha gem, and other ornaments. ||71||
Having beheld Śrī Hari directly before his eyes, Viṣṇudāsa became exceedingly choked with emotion;
filled with love, he was unable to offer praise or speak.
Then the gods, who were present at the sacrifice, abandoned the ritual and departed;
they were asked by King Caula, "O lords of the gods, where are you going? (73)
They said to Viṣṇudāsa: "The Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa indeed granted a direct vision and appearance there in his very presence. (74)
"Let us go for the sake of seeing him, and we shall return quickly";
having said this, they went to where the four-armed Hari was.
The gods offered praise to him; the Gandharvas and Apsarases sang;
the divine Gandharvas danced, and the sages bestowed blessings. ||76||
At that time, that place became rich with the delight of song and instrumental music;
it was there that the sacrifices, all the gods, and the people of the fourteen worlds were present.
All the holy places and even the fires arrived there;
at that moment, the sacrificial ground became empty for an instant, being devoid of the gods.
Near the temple, Viṣṇu spoke to Īśvara and the others with devotion, service, affectionate feeling, and overflowing love. ||79||
"I am pleased with my servant Viṣṇudāsa, who is free from pride;
O deities, a direct vision of me has quickly come to him."
"I do not approach one who is full of pride with various kinds of offerings;
it is my firm resolve that I shall grant my direct vision only to those who are humble. (81)
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Viṣṇu embraced Viṣṇudāsa, placed him upon his own celestial chariot, and led him to the eternal abode.
Caulārāja saw him going toward the temple of Śrī Viṣṇu; he then quickly summoned his preceptor, Mudgara himself. 83.
And there he spoke to the sage: "The purpose for which I have commenced this sacrifice, and out of rivalry with whom all these materials were offered by me in the sacrifice—" (84)
Having previously attained Hari, he indeed went to Vaikuṇṭha;
for the sacrifice consisting of ritual action cannot possibly be completed by you.
I have not previously earned, nor have I acquired here, the fruit of what ought to be done;
therefore, neither wealth, sacrifice, nor charity will satisfy Hari. (86)
But Hari, it is certain, becomes pleased through devotion of heart alone, as well as through worship, recitation, and remembrance. (87)
"O Guru, perform the sacrifice; accept the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). Having sent away those who have arrived and been given their fees, go home. (88)
I shall follow behind for the sake of propitiating him;
for the Lord of Devotees is pleased by devotion, not by sacrifices or extensive gifts. (89)
"This brahmin was born as an illustration for the propitiation of Hari";
having said this, he entrusted the burden of the kingdom to his nephew.
The lord of men went to the sacrifice to propitiate Hari;
standing before the fire-pit, he offered the sacrificial materials.
"O Viṣṇu, grant me devotion always through my mind, speech, body, and actions.
Having recited this three times aloud while remembering Hari— 92.
Then, while everyone was looking on, the king fell into the Vāhnikuṇḍa; a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose, and Viṣṇu manifested himself at that moment.
Having made the king four-armed and taking him up in a celestial chariot,
Hari led the monarch to Vaikuṇṭha and granted him the status of an attendant.
Hari himself was pleased by my devotion, which was supreme in its fidelity to my husband;
when I am pleased, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa himself is pleased with the king. (95)
Dharmadatta, it is I myself who am that attendant Viṣṇudāsa;
and the king named Puṇyaśīla is he who is called Suśīla. (96)
"We two have come here for the sake of Rāma to take Kalahā to Vaikuṇṭha;
by virtue of your merit, she shall be taken there when you are born as a king named Daśaratha, and at that time Kalahā shall become Kaikeyī. (97)
Your third wife shall be a sharer in the portion of Dharma. ||98||
Placing his hand in the center of the hub of the chariot wheel, he will depart;
and seeing her devoted to her husband, you will fall into a state of delusion.
And she was told that for the granting of boons, it would be appropriate for the future time;
thus she will cause this very gift to be given according to one's desire, as if it were a formal ritual deposit (nyāsa).
When Rāma’s consecration has been attained and the destruction of the Rākṣasas is at hand,
Viṣṇu will incite him to request the status of a forest-dweller.
The destruction of Rāvaṇa and the others will indeed occur under the pretext of Sītā’s shadow;
thereafter, you shall return once more to Vaikuṇṭha.
Thus I have told you everything regarding the unfolding of future events;
by reading or hearing this, one shall attain passage to Vaikuṇṭha.
Listen, Lakṣmī: although the king has been consecrated in the kingdom of Cūla, the coronation of the son as the crown prince by the principal queen has not yet taken place.
In the Kali age, the consecration into that kingdom occurs as if for a sister's son;
indeed, among the subjects and the ruler, the sister's son shall become preeminent.
Moreover, O auspicious lady, listen: when King Cūla, though devoted to the Brahmins, brought about his own death, he then [sought refuge] with Mudgala.
Then they laughed, mocked, and uttered cries of "shame";
they spoke of his incompetence and proclaimed him a murderer of kings.
Having heard this again and again, Mudgara too became enraged, his inner self ablaze;
yet, just as he was about to enter the cauldron, he fell right there.
He was firmly and properly restrained by the Brahmins according to justice,
and he was forcibly stopped with great effort by the queen, her female attendants, and others.
Then, out of anger, he tore out his own matted hair with both hands;
having plucked out the lock of matted hair, he invoked it into the circle of fire.
And because of that, even today there are Brahmins known as Viśikhās in that lineage.
Then they performed an act of atonement and all went to their own abodes.

Thus ends the four hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Account of the Birth of Dharmadatta as Daśaratha and Other Events, including the Attainment of the Form of Viṣṇu’s Attendants named Suśīla and Puṇyaśīla by Colarāja and Viṣṇudāsa through Devotion to Hari, and the Transformation of Saurāṣṭrī Kalahā into Kaikeyī," in the first section, *Kṛtayugasantāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Mahālakṣmī! In Gokula, the daughters of the cowherds performed a vow consisting of devotion to their husband in order to attain Kṛṣṇa.

The maidens are great divine goddesses whose forms are the very abodes [of divinity]; they appear on the surface of the earth as if possessing physical bodies, yet that is not their true reality. All of them are divine, equal to Rādhā, equal to Śrī, and are embodiments of Brahman.
For not even an atom's worth of difference exists among them from their similarity to Kṛṣṇa.
There was conception and birth, childhood and then youth;
thereafter, she became Rohiṇī and a maiden—that divine state of the Kṛṣṇas.
All those with eyes of skin look upon themselves as they do others, yet it is not so;
for their very activity consists solely in attaining Kṛṣṇa as their husband.
All of them were devoted wives of Kṛṣṇa, dear to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, and had dedicated their entire being for the sake of Kṛṣṇa; what more, indeed, can be said of them?
Requested by those women who remembered their past births, Kṛṣṇa indeed appeared to them every day in their dreams as Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in the morning.
Smiling and perceiving her inner intent, he granted her the sacrifice of wifely devotion;
and they, by the command of Kṛṣṇa, performed that rite of devoted wives.
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, during the month of Vṛṣa, let them perform this vow which is dear to me;
I shall arrive and fulfill their heart's desires.
Just as they do everything for their own sake, let them all do everything for my sake;
let them quickly perform everything that is pleasing [to me], for I shall become your husband.
Thus, for those maidens who had been so addressed, such knowledge regarding their absolute devotion to their husbands arose through the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (11)
All those cowherd women, by the thousands, undertook a vow;
for their minds were fixed upon me, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
I gave them the wisdom for plunging into the Mārgaśīrṣa [month];
having gathered together in groups at the time of dawn during the Brāhma-yoga, they [should proceed]. || 13 ||
Having performed their ablutions in the Yamunā, they sing the praises of Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, they offer water-libations and gifts of unbroken rice-grains into the water for my sake.
Even while remaining within the water, I accepted the gift of wealth;
and at dawn, they offered the gift of food in the water, having remembered Kṛṣṇa.
In some places becoming Kṛṣṇa and in others becoming a fish, I take up whatever leaf, flower, or fruit is offered into that water as being dedicated to my own self.
I accepted all that [offering] in the water with a feeling of devotion toward them;
and for my sake, they went from house to house and performed worship.
Food fit for oblation was eaten by them for my sake and offered to me;
everything was done for the sake of my grace, and thus their vow was perfectly performed. (18)
With a satisfied heart, I have granted them a boon: that they shall have a virtuous husband as their own self. Listen, Lakṣmī, I shall describe the rite for the devoted wife of Kṛṣṇa.
Having risen at dawn during the Brāhma-muhūrta, they bowed to their venerable gurus; I was remembered, meditated upon for a moment, and "Kṛṣṇa" was repeatedly chanted.
Then, having gone to the bank of the Yamunā and performed their purification and other rites,
they bathed in the waters of the Yamunā and completed the cleansing of their faces and other duties.
Having smeared themselves with Tulasī clay and sprinkled their bodies with water from Tulasī leaves, they bathed in the river while keeping me in their hearts.
Remembering Him and uttering the name "Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa," they also recite:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, obeisance to the Lord. (23)
Then, wearing wet garments, they offered me unbroken grains, flowers, leaves, saffron and other substances, a lamp, fruits, and so forth. (24)
"Oṃ, salutations; this is offered to the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Having thus made the offering, they departed from the shore and [removed] their garments. (25)
Having put on [the garment] and sipped water accordingly, he then offered libations to his ancestors;
having paid homage to the sages and the gods, he applied the crescent-shaped mark with saffron.

On their foreheads, at the base of their throats, and on their hearts, those women devoted to Kṛṣṇa applied marks with sandalwood paste and other substances, drawing dots and lines as was appropriate.
Keśava is meditated upon on the forehead, and likewise Nārāyaṇa on the abdomen;
Mādhava is meditated upon on the chest, and Govinda at the hollow of the throat.
Viṣṇu was meditated upon in the right side of the belly, while Vāmana was in the left side;
Madhuhā was in the right arm, and Śriyodhara was in the left arm.
Trivikrama is meditated upon at the root of the ears, Hṛṣīkeśa on the ears; Padmanābha is meditated upon on the back, and Dāmodara indeed in the lower region.
Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, their husband, was meditated upon by them in every limb;
they also fashioned a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus upon their arms.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; obeisance!"—thus they meditated in their minds upon the mudrās of the sixteen Kṛṣṇas. (32)
Some placed fine garlands of *tulasī* on their necks as well as in their hands;
others placed garlands made of *dhātrī* fruits around their necks and in their hands. (33)
Having thus performed the ritual and bowed to their elders, they went home;
then, having sipped water for purification, they all entered the pavilion.
Seated upon auspicious seats in the lotus posture and facing the east,
they performed the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma) in the center of the pavilion.
Having established the Sun, the Moon, and Fire within the pericarp by mere designation, they placed them upon the rice grains.
Then, with great devotion, they fashioned an eight-petaled lotus out of rice grains;
there they meditated upon me as a divine husband, each according to her own suitability for a boon.
Some saw Acyuta seated and smiling, resembling ten million moons,
with four arms and holding weapons, while others saw him with two arms.
[Visualize] me, whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals, endowed with great heroism and strength, with the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem upon my chest, and clothed in yellow garments. (39)
Resplendent with divine ornaments, adorned with divine decorations,
his limbs anointed with divine sandalwood paste, and wearing divine garlands of flowers.
Adorned with a forest garland (*vanamālā*) encircled by *tulasī* garlands, resembling ten million rising suns, he was lovely and most enchanting. (41)
But as they meditated on me—my body embraced by the youthful Śrī and my lips kissing her—they, being innocent, cried out to me, "Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! 42.
Then they placed a conch shell filled with scented water,
and likewise set down a vessel containing fragrant flowers and other offerings to the right.
On the left, they placed a water-pot purified by a cloth and scented with fragrance;
they set down a bell and lamps, and offered incense on all sides. ||44||
Then the maidens placed four vessels there, intended for the arghya, pādya, ācamanīya, and madhuparka offerings. 45.
There, the young maidens placed mustard seeds, unbroken rice grains, flowers, tips of *kuśa* grass, sesame, sandalwood, fruit, and barley into the vessel for the guest-offering (*arghya*). 46.
They placed dūrvā grass, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and a lotus in the vessel for water for the feet,
as well as kaṅkola, cloves, and jasmine fruit.
They placed those [substances] along with water from sacred fords (tīrtha) into the vessel for sipping water (ācamanīya-pātra), as well as cow-products:
milk, curd, honey, clarified butter, and sugar.
Then, in the presence of Hari, they placed those [offerings] in the vessel of the madhuparka,
and out of a desire for Kṛṣṇa, they performed the ritual placement of their hands upon their own limbs.
May the head of Kṛṣṇa rest upon my head in every way;
may the auspicious forehead of Śrī Kṛṣṇadeva rest upon my forehead.
May the eyes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa preside over my two eyes;
may Kṛṣṇa’s ears be in my ears, and Kṛṣṇa’s nose in my nose. (51)
May Kṛṣṇa’s cheek rest upon my cheek, his two dark cheeks upon my two cheeks;
may Kṛṣṇa’s side-long glances rest upon my side-long glances. (52)
May the beloved pair of Kṛṣṇa’s lips dwell upon my two lips;
may Kṛṣṇa’s chin be upon my chin, and may the throat of Hari be upon my throat. (53)
May the shoulders of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa rest upon my two shoulders;
may the two beautiful arms of Śrī Hari be upon my two arms, and his two hands upon my two hands. 54.
May Kṛṣṇa’s heart be in my heart; may Hari’s navel be in my navel; may Kṛṣṇa’s hips be in my hips, and may Hari’s waist be in my waist. (55)
The secret of Kṛṣṇa is hidden within my secret parts; my two thighs are the two thighs of Hari. My knees are the knees of Kṛṣṇa, and my shanks are the shanks of Hari. ||56||
May the feet of Kṛṣṇa be upon my feet; may Kṛṣṇa be in me in every way.
May the senses of Kṛṣṇa be in all my senses in every respect.
"May the inner senses of Hari indeed abide within my own inner senses.
In this way, they performed a heart-touching remembrance of me. 58.
Then those devoted wives remembered themselves as being equal to me, and [remembered] the auspicious Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, their beloved husband, saying: "Be pleased! (59)
They entered, saying, "You are the husband of the cowherd girls; grant us auspiciousness.
Then they worshipped Śaṅkha with flowers, sandalwood, and water.
They performed an anointing with well-perfumed oil,
and likewise they performed an anointing with musk and sandalwood.
Then, although I had already been bathed with waters scented with fragrant perfumes,
I took up the water from the conch again and again for the sake of bathing.
They respectfully offered the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and bathed him;
they also performed the consecration (abhiṣeka) with the waters of sacred fords (tīrtha), which were pleasant to the touch.
They respectfully rubbed sandalwood, the essence of fragrance, and other substances; they repeatedly wiped my body with a cloth. (64)
They offered an arghya with fruit, as well as water for washing the feet and water for sipping;
they then presented the madhuparka and divine garments.
They presented me with divine ornaments and jewels, perfumes and the like,
collyrium, hair oil, and sandalwood paste for the purpose of making sectarian marks.
Then those maidens offered saffron and other substances, as well as liquid essences; they also presented lac-dye, cosmetic ointments, and the like.
They offered him a lion-throne, as well as an umbrella, chowries, and a fan;
they also gave him a mirror, combs, and white powder.
Then they offered garlands of tulasī, flower wreaths, and crest-ornaments; they presented clusters of flowers, golden ornaments, and leaves.
They gave me a flute with a sweet sound, and I played it;
placing me upon a swing, they rocked me back and forth with great devotion.
They offered as an oblation (naivedya) milk-rice mixed with cakes,
as well as water, fruit, betel-leaf, vegetables, areca nuts, and other such items.
They served them with fans and likewise attended upon them;
they again offered incense and lamps, and gave flowers with devotion.
They fed me excessively with mouthfuls out of great affection;
being satisfied, I drank water and took betel leaf. (73)
Having bowed down to them, they performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) again and again;
they offered hymns of praise, prostrated themselves, and likewise circumambulated them once more.
They offered a handful of flowers as a request for forgiveness for their offense and entreated him for a boon, saying: "Be our husband forever. (75)
Having laid him upon the couch, they stood around him with reverence;
they massaged his feet and served him according to their desire.
O beloved, at that time their hearts were fulfilled by me through touch, through embrace, through my affection, and through indescribable passion.
Then they attained a happiness such as had never been experienced before;
immersed in bliss, they then offered the auspicious water of honor (arghya).
Then, having sent me away, they indeed performed their household duties;
they ate the prasāda that had been offered as part of my worship. (79)
Remembering again and again the great bliss given by me, they were exceedingly joyful;
they performed their domestic duties and felt no fatigue.
While they were engaged in the task of fetching water, they saw me in the water within the jar;
while they were engaged in threshing the grain with the pestle, they indeed saw me in the grains.
Indeed, they saw me on the grinding stone during the task of grinding flour;
and at the time of sweeping, they saw me upon the floor.
At the time of cooking, whether in the cooking vessel, the pot, or the food bowl—whether seen, heard, or touched—they beheld me alone. (83)
In the mirror, in their own faces, in their eyes, in oil, in clothing, in ornaments,
in their hearts, and in all their activities, they beheld none but me.
They became possessed of divine bodies, free from the obstruction of physical walls; having abandoned the perception of a material body, they assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa.
One became a woman and the second became a man, and they took their pleasure;
one was the wife and the second was the husband, and they rejoiced together. (86)
One became a female friend and the second a male friend, and so they kissed;
one became a bride and the second a groom, and so they shone forth. (87)
Thus, I have created this internal darkness within them; for those who are dyed by the colors of devotion to Kṛṣṇa’s conjugal fidelity, there can be no separation from me.
Having attained such a state, they went to bathe in the waters of the Yamunā near a kadamba tree; and there I too remained unobserved among them.
Having assumed the form of young maidens, she went indeed together with them for the sake of bathing;
and they descended into the sacred ford, having laid their garments upon its bank.
And in their hearts, those maidens remembered me to bathe and sport with them,
each one individually, in such a way that no other knew.
There, in that water, she sports as an external maiden while being an internal person;
she alone perceives each act of dalliance, and no other does so at that time.
Having thus satisfied their minds and being fully gratified, they then said:
"O Kṛṣṇa, though you have the form of a maiden in the water, you have come from the forest. (93)
Taking their garments, he climbed the Kadamba tree;
my mind has fulfilled that which was intended by them in that forest. (94)
"I acted in that manner so that Kṛṣṇa might see my body, since I disregarded Varuṇa while I was established in a vow. (95)
"Having gone outside, my dear ones, offer salutation with palms joined to the sun.
Thus I beheld them according to their inner disposition. (96)
Then, being satisfied, they felt that their purpose was accomplished;
he gave them garments and repeatedly granted them boons as well. (97)
"I shall delight you, I shall truly please you as you desire, for you are dear to me;
I shall offer you the entire fruit of my vow, ever renewed. (98)
I have always satisfied those truthful women with my state of being their beloved; indeed, they have always been one with me, day and night. (99)
Divine desire, divine delight, and a divine state were produced by me;
indeed, through my divine nature, that [state] became divine for them.
Action performed without desire is said to be that which is always offered unto Me; it destroys bondage, bestows peace, and brings about liberation through direct dedication to Me. (101)
"Just as they have done, no other woman shall ever do so";
thus I became pleased with them, their beloved and sole companion. (102)
Those beloved women attended upon me and attained me in the supreme state;
all of them were beloved of Kṛṣṇa, devoted to Kṛṣṇa, and dear to Hari.
The wives of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, women devoted to their husband Kṛṣṇa,
constantly worshipped me and delighted me in my presence.
And they constantly fed the Infallible One with sweet foods;
they always held in their hearts Me, the bestower of eternal bliss. (105)
Thus, she who shall serve her husband with devotion to her husband will, having obtained me as her husband, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, attain final liberation.

Thus ends the four hundred and twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of Lord Kṛṣṇa as Consort by the Maidens of Gokula, Who Were Devoted to Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa through Chastity and the Performance of Vows and Worship with One Hundred and Eight Offerings," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the account concerning their restoration, which took place when Kṛṣṇa returned and resided in Dvārakā. || 1 ||
Afflicted by grief, they all abandoned water and food;
yet Śrī Kṛṣṇa and I repeatedly approached them once more.
Having gone there in an invisible form, they were consoled and propitiated;
they were nourished and gladdened by means of playing and other activities as they desired. || 3 ||
I delight with each gopī individually in my invisible form;
those standing by my side do not perceive me at all, because they possess only physical eyes.
Those divine women, who know and speak on the banks of the Yamunā, meet with me in solitude; they praise me and laugh. || 5 ||
Unable to remain for even a moment without me,
they met on the shore and resolved to go to Dvārakā to be in the presence of their beloved.
All those women, possessing divine bodies, having assumed pairs of forms,
remained forever in that very Gokula in a single form each.
But by the second divine [vehicle], thousands of the wives of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa arrived together, having brought gifts according to their means.
Invisible in form due to their supernatural powers, they traveled by way of the sky;
within the span of a single ghaṭikā, they reached the auspicious and divine lotus-pond.
Having learned of them through my yogic power, I returned in great haste;
I welcomed them and assumed a thousand forms.
He quickly bestowed joy upon him, and thereafter gave him food and other provisions; he accepted the gifts and subsequently dispelled his long-standing distress.
Thus, for a long time, he protected them in Dvārakā on the island;
and all of them, gratified by his command, served him according to their desire.
Once, on Mount Raivata, I invited them to sport;
they arrived, wandered about, took their pleasure, and called out to me.
On the bank of the river Svarṇarekhā, fragrant with sweet-smelling flowers,
they attained the bliss of desire in that delightful forest of ten million trees.
Having seen that most delightful place, Raivatapattala,
they decided to feed me and remembered their provisions.
The forest goddesses dwelling there, the yoginīs of Yoginīgiri,
the wives of the Siddhas, and the female servants of Ambā brought all kinds of food from every direction.
They brought various vessels made of gold, silver, and leaves, as well as bowls made from the leaves of the *brahmadruma* tree.
They too, considering their birth to have borne fruit and being greatly delighted,
fed him exceedingly and performed the rites of hospitality with great respect.
The daughters of Raivata and the maidens of Gaukulya likewise fed the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who was present in ten million forms. || 19 ||
Whatever foods were fit for consumption during the Kārtika month and worthy of being offered in the mountain of grain (annakūṭa),
those they brought forth for the sake of Hari in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
They fed them all near the Nārāyaṇa lake;
listen, O Lakṣmī, to the names of those whom I ate at that time.
I shall describe to you, without omission, the foods, drinks, condiments, and so forth, as well as thousands of vessels made of gold and silver. (22)
There were many extensive and beautiful vessels made of palāśa wood, as well as thousands of kacolas, shallow bowls, and kuḍavas. ||23||
Then, auspicious jars of water, together with their accompanying vessels, were placed upon the vast surface of the earth in my presence.
Then, milk-rice (pāyasa) offered by maidens from the wish-fulfilling cows was served;
it was an excellent preparation of milk cooked with sugar and fragrant rice.
Then, green gram endowed with fragrance was placed in serving vessels, along with various side dishes mixed with lime juice and other ingredients. (26)
And fruits, roots, and cooked dishes, exquisitely scented with camphor and other aromatics,
along with hundreds of varieties of side-dishes, were indeed placed in serving vessels.
And grapes mixed with mangoes and karamardakas, combined with black pepper, long pepper, ginger, camphor, ela, and fresh ginger; ||28||
There were various decoctions and medicinal extracts, savory and bitter,
as well as jambu-fruit juices mixed with the juices of leafy creepers, and likewise roasting-fires.
And various kinds of linctuses, filled with the fragrance of flowers,
were placed by them in vessels— excellent things that retained their warm quality.
And auspicious round *maṇḍakas* mixed with sugar and milk, along with blooming flower-shaped sweets, were served in the vessels. (31)
The finest butter, produced from the milk of buffaloes in the dairy enclosures, was offered—excellent, containing both the flower-stalks and sugar-candy. (32)
Powders made from fresh leaves, fruits, and other ingredients were placed in small packets,
while *pūrikās*— a type of fried cake— prepared with those same ingredients and accompanied by *saubāhlikas* were served on platters.
There were hundreds of hollow cakes (polikās), as well as apūpas and pūpakas;
there were very sweet polikās, beloved pūrikās, and yugapolikās.
There were also large polikās and likewise full-sized prapolikās;
there were roṭakas filled with ghee, and śāṭakas filled with ghee. ||35||
Chickpeas of various kinds, fresh mung beans and lentils prepared with spices, fried dough-strips (sūtrapheṇya), thin pancakes (parpaṭa), and cakes made from pumpkin and mung beans; ||36||
Then, nine types of sweetmeat balls were joyfully offered,
including those made of milk-rice enriched with nutmeg, black pepper, cardamom, and saffron.
Such prepared food, cooked in milk and served in vessels,
was of variegated colors and manifold flavors, excellent and consecrated with black mustard seeds.
They prepared many kinds of foods made from tamarind, curd, and mango, as well as those composed of grape juice, sugarcane juice, plantain, bilva fruit, and other essences. (39)
Roots cooked in ghee or cooked in oil, as well as cooked leaves and powdered mineral exudates; ||1.427.40||
It is mixed with flour, ālībīja seeds, the kernels of coconut,
khasa seeds, and cloves, combined with ghee and sugar.
In a cauldron, small quantities of sesame seeds and rice were cooked with milk;
these glossy and beautiful *pheṇikā* cakes were joyfully offered to them again and again. (42)
Three types of *pūrikās* were offered, cooked in ghee and mixed with camphor;
they were infused with the seed-syllable of Cāraḷī and smeared with the seed-syllable of Khasa. ||43||
There were many kinds of sweetmeats (modakas) infused with raisins and spices,
containing jaggery, sugar, and candied sugar, all kneaded with milk.
There were those cooked in water and those cooked in ghee, roasted in fire-pits,
and even flour-meals fried in ghee or lightly drizzled with a small amount of ghee.
Auspicious sweetmeats (modaka) should be prepared with the kernels of coconuts, cardamom, cloves, and camphor, mixed with bamboo flowers, jasmine flowers, and other such ingredients. 46.
Sweetmeats made from tree resin, mixed with ripe *guṇḍrā* and other ingredients;
almond sweetmeats, sesame sweetmeats, pearl-like sweets, and so forth. (47)
There were other round sweets (golaka) made from the flour of mung beans and chickpeas;
there were rice-based sweets (tāṇḍula-laḍḍuka), and also sweets made from the flour of black gram and other grains. ||48||
And those round, fragrant, and beautiful four-piece cakes were placed by them in dishes and offered to Mahāśubha. (49)
There were also pieces of cakes from Mohana-sthala, as well as parpika-flour pastries,
binduka-balls, laḍḍukas, and various kinds of black-gram sweets.
The *granthakas*, the *kalikās*, the *sevikās*, and the *caturvaṭas*; the *bāṣpāṭas*, the *śāṭakas*, as well as the *śaṣkulyas* and the *piṇḍakas*. ||51||
The Gaṇagranthas, Śarkapāras, Kaṃsāras, and Birañjakas; milk, water, sandalwood, Pītasāras, and buttermilk. ||52||
There were *saṃyāvas* and other sweetmeats, *jāmbavas*, and *prasūtrakas*;
likewise, there were sweets, non-sweets, bitter things, and savory condiments. (53)
Likewise, prepared *kulatthikā* beans, *rājamāṣa* beans, and so forth, were filled into vessels and leaves according to the available materials. (54)
There was fermented gruel made from ginger, cloves, and mangoes;
and fermented gruel made from *āmalaka*, lime, and pomegranate.
The fermented gruel (āranālaka) of *marīcaka* bulbs and *śuṇṭhī* roots; the fermented gruel of *kairaṭa*, *karmada*, and *śigru* plants. ||56||
Likewise, he gave juices of radishes, leaves, and dates,
as well as wild bamboo shoots and fermented rice-gruel.
A side dish of kṣīrikā, amṛtā, and galakī;
and a side dish of ghṛtāśā, dugdhī, and paravalā. ||58||
There were side dishes of *kunārā* roots, *mṛdālū* roots, and *raktālū* roots;
and sauces made from *bṛhatī*, *suvāsā*, and *methikā*. (59)
Sugarcane juice, the water of *puṣpikā*, grapes, and the fruit of the *kṣīrikā*; mangoes of nine colors and plantains that are like nectar. (1.427.60)
Āmalaka fruits, bilva fruits, and various juices were repeatedly joyfully placed by those auspicious women into the vessels. (61)
One *prastha* of milk with sugar, half a *karṣa* of ghee, a small amount of honey, a little ginger, a little black pepper, and a small amount of camphor. (62)
They gave me strained decoctions to drink after [the meal],
as well as excellent betel leaves accompanied by the finest ingredients.
There, water was offered to me by them according to the prescribed rite;
I was given [gifts] and fed by all of them individually.
Satiated repeatedly by mouthfuls that touched their throats and were truly worthy of being drunk,
they all took them in their hands and gave those morsels to me.
I take [the food] into my mouth with devotion and consume it quickly;
for the deities, the Ṛṣis, the sages, and likewise the ancestors have arrived. (66)
"I ate for the sake of sight, yet they accepted my gift;
thus was my meal prepared by them, providing great satisfaction. (67)
Having eaten them all myself, I fed each one of them in turn, giving morsels of food, kisses, and touches. (68)
To all of them, I have given the offerings of all things that bestow grace and satisfaction;
they have been fed, and water and betel-leaf have been presented. (69)
Then the deities became fish in the Nārāyaṇa lake,
and even the ancestors became birds, thereby obtaining grace.
There, in the groves, he was served by young maidens with great satisfaction,
and he was likewise highly adorned with garlands and wreaths of flowers.
On the Raivata mountain, which always bestows happiness, he was saluted, honored, and repeatedly entreated for the sake of obtaining a dwelling on that mountain. (72)
I gave them this command: "Go indeed toward Gokula.
But they said, "O Kṛṣṇa, always protect us here on this mountain. (73)
O Mādhava, always come here for the sake of bestowing happiness;
we have all been offered to you in body, action, and mind. (74)
Now that you have arrived, where else could we go, apart from the feet of our beloved?
We are always your servants; grant us happiness indeed through union with our lover. (75)
The Lord, assuming manifold forms, gratified Rati with various desires.
Then, O Lakṣmī, Brahmā arrived there for a certain purpose.
Others do not know what is to be kept secret; I alone, Nārāyaṇa, know it. (76)
Then Brahmā said to me: "This secret must not be spoken for as long as the Kṛta, Tretā, and Dvāpara ages endure. (77)
Since Kali performs his sovereignty upon the earth while remaining utterly hopeless,
having failed to find a place anywhere else, he went to the Lokācala mountain in a fit of rage.
He performs penance right there for the sake of attaining that very place;
indeed, you must go there yourself to bestow the fruit of his penance.
O Ocean of Compassion, you who protect the world, a boon must be granted;
the age of Dvāpara has passed, and the Kali age will now prevail upon the earth.
O Lord, sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā, as well as Dharma and the deities and others,
shall not remain upon the earth for five thousand years.
For that duration, Kali will dwell upon the earth powerless; however, in due course, when the strength of the Tiṣya age has arisen on the surface of the world, [it will prevail]. ||82||
Manifesting in all human forms, he will dwell [among them],
and from that point on, he will sow the seeds of unrighteousness everywhere.
He will strive by every means to make the world uniform;
for his own nourishment, he will render the entire world devoid of dharma. (84)

At that time, there were distinctions of caste and distinctions of religious duty, as well as the avoidance of the untouchable, the approaching of women who should not be approached, and the eating of what is forbidden to eat and so forth. (85)
At that time, Manu, Yama, and others will effect the purification of both gods and outcastes;
thereafter, all shall become afflicted with disease for the protection of Dharma.
O Kṛṣṇa, then once again in the Raivata region of Saurāṣṭra, you must manifest yourself on the banks of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake. ||87||
O Lord, as one who is the presiding authority over all sciences and all dharmas, you must certainly be known by the name Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (88)
Through your instruction, Vṛṣa, being exceedingly devoted and nourished, shall live for a long time everywhere among all people on this earth. (89)
Having recognized the Blessed One as marked with the signs of the fish, the banner, the bow, the trident, the svastika, and the thunderbolt, those people then took refuge in him.
They will come and they shall cross over [the ocean of existence] through the sight and service of you;
then, O Kṛṣṇa, by your divine splendor, devotion shall prevail upon the earth. (91)
Prosperity shall come everywhere and people will attain liberation. Om, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; salutations! ||92||
Having received this mantra from their guru with devotion, they shall go to that abode.
Then, when the power of the Kali age (Tiṣya-bala) has arisen, the subjects will become like outcasts (cāṇḍāla).
Then, both the sense of "mine" and "otherness" will perish along with their roots;
the bond of kinship and the bond of wealth will become a mere matter of self-interest. (94)
Then again, O Kṛṣṇa, you must appear repeatedly—again and again—for the destruction of the Kali age and for the sake of truth and true dharma. (95)
You must repeatedly manifest yourself for the purpose of bestowing the training, as long as there are deities upon the earth, images [of the Buddha], and sacred waters within the water. (96)
"May purity and strength prevail among men, and may Kali [be subdued]!
Hari replied, "So be it," while Brahmā stood before him, bowing down.
When Hari had served all the delicious food to Brahmā,
Kṛṣṇa then spoke this reply to the young maidens in jest.
Furthermore, I, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, shall indeed appear on earth in Surāṣṭra for the purpose of overcoming the Kali age. (99)
"Therefore, all of you beloved ones, perform austerities on Mount Raivata;
when I become manifest there, a perfect union shall take place for you right then."
Having heard this, they became deeply distressed with tears in their eyes;
for during that time of separation, they were indeed unable to endure the torment.
And then the Blessed One, having consoled them again slowly,
spoke to those who were unable to endure separation for five thousand years.
Indeed, only a moment’s time remains before you depart for Satyaloka;
this very day, O maidens, go forth together with Brahmā.
"May my beloveds, filled with longing, behold the world of Brahmā for even a single moment; then, impelled by Brahmā, may they return here once more. (104)
"By means of these divine bodies, may they indeed become devoted to me;
and I myself shall be present here in Saurāṣṭra as the Blessed One."
Indeed, Kṛṣṇa alone is to be recognized by his signs when he is in the midst of the virtuous;
for all of you possess divine bodies in every house throughout Saurāṣṭra and other regions.
Having taken birth then, you shall indeed become possessed of devotion to me;
through your virtuous association, millions of men and women as well [shall attain it].
In every house there will be those who practice devotion to me;
I, the Teacher, shall wander in secret form like an ascetic.
Having obtained happiness from Me alone, people shall go to My abode.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; obeisance to the Lord. 1.09.
Those who shall thus perform the recitation will indeed go to my abode;
they shall perform service to me, worship of me, and the chanting of my names.
Those people who indeed listen to my stories shall go to the supreme, eternal abode inhabited by Śrī.
Having been addressed thus, they became joyful and, together with Brahmā, went to the true world of Brahmā (Brahmaloka); Śrī Kṛṣṇa went to Dvārakā.
Thus have I related this account of mine to you, which destroys sin and suffering;
for having recollected what previously occurred, I have now narrated it here. (113)
All of them are my wives and have surrendered themselves to me;
having renounced everything for my sake, they are all devoted to their husband.
By the mere sight and touch of them, people shall indeed attain liberation;
how much more so for me through my yoga and by direct contact with this divine seat?
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have told you this auspicious account of my former existence;
for in age after age, I shall indeed become Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Many times, in every age, I come into being and I manifest forth:
as the splendor of the Kṣatriya, the splendor of the virtuous, the splendor of asceticism, and as the Lord of Sages.

He is the splendor of the scriptures, the splendor of knowledge, and the splendor of Dharma; he is the teacher of teachers, the nourisher of Dharma, the nourisher of devotion, the protector of devotees, and the ruler. || 1.18 ||
The protector of Satī, the beloved husband, the bestower of delight, the Lord of Ramā;
the giver of sovereignty, the protector of sacrifice, the destroyer of the Daityas, and the mendicant. || 119 ||
The remover of suffering, the bestower of happiness, the refuge, the four-armed one,
the powerful, the one who has reached the further shore, and the one whose body is marked by the Kaṇa-sthala [sign].
"O beloved, those who are steadfast in devotion to Kṛṣṇa as their husband shall always cross over [all obstacles];
thus I have told you my heart's secret: Kṛṣṇa alone is the husband, and no other. (121)
Day after day, I shall protect, I am protecting,
and I have protected those Mañjuhaṃsas who are endowed with devotion and devoted to their wifely fidelity.

Thus ends the four hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Gopīs of Gokula Offering One Hundred and Twelve Kinds of Food and Enjoyments to Śrī Kṛṣṇa on Mount Raivata after Their Arrival at Dvārakā, the Statement of His Manifestation Everywhere from Saurāṣṭra onwards, and the Reappearance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa through the Devotion of His Consorts," in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the delightful story of Vīrabāhu and his virtuous wife.
In the city of Kāmpilya, there was a highly intelligent man named Vīrabāhu. (1)
The king was a speaker of truth and my supreme devotee among brāhmaṇas;
he was devoted to the bhāgavatas and took delight in my stories.
He was a donor who provided refuge to the helpless, faithful to his wife, and blessed with sons;
his beloved wife was radiant, a great saint, and devoted to her husband.
Except for me alone, Vīrabāhu knows no other deity;
once, the great sage Bhāradvāja went to his house.
The king offered hospitality, a welcome, the respectful water-offering (arghya), and a seat;
he bowed to him with devotion and spoke, being greatly delighted.
Today my birth has become fruitful; today my day has become fruitful;
today my kingdom has become fruitful; today my home has become fruitful.
My hermitage is fruitful, and my wealth and kinsmen are fruitful as well,
since I, a knower of Brahman, have seen him and his feet have entered my home.
The virtuous go to the home of one with whom Hari is pleased;
for him in whose house there is a devotee of Hari, there is the destruction of ten million sins.
Your abode has become a sacred ford (tīrtha), for by the dust of your feet the heavens are sanctified;
O Sage, sovereignty, prosperity, elephants, horses, and all else exist solely for your sake.
By the grace of beholding you, I have been made one who is liberated while living;
you are a great devotee of the Lord, and there is nothing that I cannot give to you.
Even a very small offering dedicated to a Vaiṣṇava yields fruit equal to Mount Meru, provided that the feet of the virtuous Kṛṣṇa, the yogi, are not present in one's home. (11)
That house and that day shall become as fruitless as a dwelling for the dead;
for that house and that day are likewise devoid of the arrival of the virtuous.

O Knower of all dharmas, tell me that which is the supreme means for those living the life of a householder—a means that is liberating, excellent, a destroyer of bondage, and a bestower of the abode of Hari. (13)
Being pleased and remembering Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Bhāradvāja said: "O King, may it be well with you; you who are dear to your devotees. (14)
Prosperity, O King, is easily attained, but the state of the heart is indeed difficult to find;
for that devotion which you possess has been earned through many births.
For one toward whom the compassionate Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, [is gracious], his devotion toward the virtuous is indeed most divine and bestows liberation. 16.
Śrī Hari is indeed always to be served, and the saintly persons are always to be served; likewise, by women, those virtuous wives who are devoted to Kṛṣṇa as their husband should be served. (17)
Wealth, grain, sons, fame, sovereignty, good fortune, honor, health, splendor, and lordship are obtained by the virtuous through their blessings. (18)
By him by whom the virtuous are satisfied, Kṛṣṇa is fully gratified;
when Kṛṣṇa is pleased, the entire world—including its gods, sages, and humans—is pleased. 1.9
If Hari is not pleased, everything—even if it is pleasing—is useless.
You are blessed, O great king; you truly shine as a great devotee of Viṣṇu.
Blessed are you, for you shine with excellence because you have a devoted wife;
she has accomplished both aspects of that devotion to her husband.
Since her lord Śrī Hari Kṛṣṇa has been thus wedded to her beloved,
she has attained happiness in this world and shall likewise attain the divine abode.
There is no such means in this world for the liberation of the householder stage as a devoted wife at home and eternal devotion to Kṛṣṇa. (23)
In a kingdom where the subjects are devotees of the Bhagavān, Vaiṣṇavas, righteous, and virtuous, one should always reside; but not in a kingdom ruled by one who is not a Vaiṣṇava.
It is better to dwell in a sacred forest hermitage than in a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava,
where a king devoted to the Lord governs the earth.
That indeed should be considered Vaikuṇṭha, for its fruit is Vaikuṇṭha itself;
such a king is a true devotee and a worthy recipient of the blessings of the virtuous. (26)
That kingdom prospers constantly due to the conjugal fidelity of the husband and wife;
O King, I behold you, a devotee of Viṣṇu, as the very eye that makes my vision fruitful.
And my two ears are likewise fruitful, since I hear of the devoted wife;
for the devoted wife was created by Brahmā as the very embodiment of Lakṣmī herself. (28)
The Vaiṣṇava who is devoted to his wife was indeed appointed as a deliverer by Brahmā;
for the sight of Vaiṣṇavas is truly bestowing of peace and likewise bestowing of liberation.
And you have obtained a vision here of me, who abide in the sacred tradition of your glory.
May it be well with you; I shall depart; be happy, O lord of men.
May there always be auspiciousness and freedom from widowhood for your wife Kāntimatī;
may you both possess unwavering devotion to your husband and to Keśava.
May you always possess the realization of oneness with your husband Kṛṣṇa, who is full of splendor;
for previously, you have observed the vow of devotion to your husband with great effort. (32)
In a previous birth, this Patiṣṭhava was a violent man, an atheist of wicked conduct, a Śūdra devoted to the pleasures of others. (33)
Ungrateful, ill-behaved, and devoid of virtuous conduct, you have indeed always treated him like a god through your actions, thoughts, and speech. (34)
Served with the thought that he was Kṛṣṇa and through the bull-like virtue of your devotion to your husband,
you have not conceived of any other man, even while in the state of a Śūdra woman.
Devoted to my husband, a great virtuous woman, avoiding the touch of others,
and free from evil intentions and the like, I served my husband, Hari.
At one time, when this husband of yours had lost his wealth and come to the forest,
you, though yourself wasting away, did not abandon your husband Hari.
Once, while the two forest-dwelling spouses were subsisting on rabbits and other such fare,
they beheld in the forest a sage who had lost his way.
A Brāhmaṇa who was a devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and a true Vaiṣṇava, who at midday was thirsty, had fallen down, and was likewise unconscious. || 39 ||
And you two attended upon that Brāhmaṇa named Devaśarman, who was remembering Kṛṣṇa in his heart, with water and with fanning.
Even by massaging his feet and by eating fruits and other food,
one should regard the Vaiṣṇava Brahmin as Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, and Hari— the savior.
In that delightful hermitage pervaded by shade, they respectfully spent their time;
he was properly served, bathed, and fed by you two. (42)
Bowing down with all eight limbs out of heartfelt devotion, he is indeed a Vaiṣṇava;
you have come as our guest for the sake of delivering us both. (43)
"O brahmin-sage, by the mere sight of you, the destruction of our sins has occurred.
Speak, O brahmin, if some assistance is required in the forest."
Then the Brahmin said: "Indeed, through the conjunction of merit in this forest, a meeting with you has occurred for me; I have truly been restored to life within the depths of the woods. (45)
"What shall I do for you two? Tell me whatever you desire.
The Śūdra replied, "Act so that there may be no sight of the world of Sūrya. (46)
I am going with my wife to the eternal abode of Kṛṣṇa;
you should show me favor by granting me instruction. (47)
Then Devaśarman said: "Listen to your former history;
in a previous birth, you were indeed a righteous Brahmin in Avanti. (48)
And then this wife of yours was devoted to her husband, ever dedicated to dharma, and a hospitable hostess to guests. (49)
By your command, this well-cooked food for you has indeed been offered on the eleventh day to Brāhmaṇas and guests for their meal. (1.428.50)
"Merit arises from giving you food, while demerit arises from eating it;
by the power of that merit and demerit, one indeed follows the path commanded by Yama. (51)
"You two took birth in a Śūdra family mixed with merit;
as much merit as there was, so much wealth, grain, and other possessions did you possess. (52)
Your merit has been exhausted, and therefore this forest dwelling has come upon you;
however, in the city of Vidarbha, your grandson remains. (53)
By that means, he performed the Ekādaśī vow of Hari;
he bestowed that merit upon you both, and by its power, it has come to you.
Your auspicious conduct has always remained fixed upon righteousness;
likewise, at that time, Kāntimatī’s mind was ever devoted to her husband's service. (55)
By the power of that merit, there shall always be union for you two; no separation shall ever occur, neither has it occurred in the past, nor will it happen in the future. (56)
In a very short time, you two shall go to heaven; there, by the power of the virtue of your devotion to your husbands, you will enjoy happiness for a very long time. (57)
Having experienced [this] in the world of mortals, you two shall indeed obtain birth as Śūdras;
and both of you, having been born, will be solely devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu.
"Furthermore, by the power of my service, you shall attain a future auspicious birth;
and by the power of your devotion to your husband, you two shall obtain a long-lasting kingdom. (59)
Having spoken thus, that Brahmin departed for the sake of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites;
meanwhile, both you—the King and the Queen, both devotees of Viṣṇu—met with the law of time (passed away).
"Furthermore, you two have been born here;
you have a virtuous wife, and you yourself are devoted to your spouse, always serving those like me. (61)
Out of devotion as a faithful wife, you serve Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the Consort of Kamalā, the Lord of Lakṣmī, and the Protector of the virtuous.
"This virtuous wife of yours always serves you, O Kṛṣṇa;
as a result of that, you shall have a long-lasting kingdom, and your son will be a true Vaiṣṇava. (63)
Your subjects are always devoted to Nārāyaṇa and likewise faithful to their husbands;
they are devotees of Viṣṇu, and for that reason, you shall attain victory in this matter of liberation.
Always practice devotion to Hari and serve your gurus and ascetics;
O virtuous woman, always observe the vow of a devoted wife and protect your marital fidelity.
"Indeed, by conducting yourselves in this way, you shall attain eternal heaven; and at the end, you will certainly go to the supreme, divine abode, Goloka. (66)
Through the merit of observing the Ekādaśī fast, by serving as a guest to a brāhmaṇa,
and through the devotion of your wife, you have obtained this kingdom and other blessings.
Always worship Viṣṇu, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; O virtuous woman, worship your husband, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, as your master.
Having spoken thus, the great sage Bhāradvāja departed for Badarī;
both of them practiced devotion and both went indeed to my abode.
Listen, Lakṣmī! To him who chants my name with devotion to Kṛṣṇa as his sole husband, I grant Vaikuṇṭha, Goloka, and the imperishable state.
My name must be uttered especially at every single moment;
one should say "Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa" and "Prabhā-Kṛṣṇa," which bestows joy.
"One should utter 'Hari-Kṛṣṇa,' which removes suffering and bestows supreme liberation;
this is my solemn promise, O Lakṣmī, regarding one who has come for refuge in every way. (72)
One attains all desires, as well as Vaikuṇṭha and even Kamalā;
indeed, I grant to my devotee everything that truly belongs to me.
If one utters "Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa," remembers Him,
or worships Him in any manner whatsoever, I shall indeed deliver him.
O beloved, those who utter the name of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa in the presence of death—Death, Yama, and his messengers indeed depart, leaving him behind. (75)
At the time of death, he into whose ear the words "Rāma, Rāma" have entered is led to Vaikuṇṭha by the attendants of Rāma; of this there is no doubt. (76)
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; salutations!"—as he thus recites this mantra, I lead him to my own imperishable state. (77)
Wherever there is a wife devoted to her husband who offers even a single leaf of *tulasī*, and wherever there is a virtuous and great devotee of the Lord, there I am present. (78)
I am Kṛṣṇa, the husband; Kṛṣṇa is the master; Kṛṣṇa is indeed the beloved.
He is the lord of Ramā, Prabhā, Māṇikī, and Pārvatī—the husband of women. (79)
O virtuous lady, since all women are born from but a hundred-thousandth part of Pativrata, he alone is the beloved of women who is the beloved of Lalitā.
Thus has the practice of service been described to you through the state of oneness;
by reading or hearing this, one obtains the fruit of devotion to one's husband.

Thus ends the four hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how Liberation was Granted by Bhāradvāja to the Couple Vīrabāhu and Kāntimatī—after Three Births as a Brahmin, a Śūdra, and a King—on Account of Their Conjugal Fidelity," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga Cycle, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the story of my wife, the daughter of the Sun,
who was the best of female companions in the midst of Goloka and possessed of a most radiant smile.
Whenever her friends gather for a grand play in the garden, she laughs there again and again.
Once, accompanied by Rādhikā and millions of gopī women,
they went to bathe in a divine lake created for my sake.
Then, having slipped upon the moss with her feet, Rādhikā fell;
Yamunā ran toward Rādhikā to catch her and laughed.
Rādhā said: "O Yamunā, why do you laugh at this jest?
Laughter filled with mirth is not at all becoming when it is misplaced."
I have fallen, covered in mud, my back struck by a stone;
water has entered my nostrils, mouth, and eyes—do not joke!
Thus awakened, she too took hold of Rādhā and, grasping her,
gave her other garments and such items for her to wear.
Her face, hair, and back were washed and well-adorned;
then, seeing Rādhā once again, she laughed repeatedly.
But Rādhā, being angry, spoke mostly to her servant Yamunā:
"May you have hair like Śiva’s matted locks and be covered in mud."
Then Yamunā, being enraged, spoke again and again to Rādhā:
"O beloved, sport with me even in mud and in moss."
"Never indeed shall I sport while abandoning you.
Knowing both [her thoughts], Kṛṣṇa said: "Do not say such things, do not say such things, my dear!"
"O beautiful ones, how shall I remain deprived of you both?
I shall go to that place where the Yamunā flows most abundantly."
Having become the river Yamunā, the daughter of the Sun, on the surface of the earth,
that virtuous lady first created the Himālaya mountain and then went to Vṛndāvana.
Rādhā also, having become a cowherd girl, the daughter of Rāpaṇa,
constantly wandered on the bank of the Yamunā amidst its moss and mud.
Born from the expansion of Kṛṣṇa’s secret assignation, Yamunā, in the form of a maiden, serves her husband Hari. 15.
Once, while the wives of Kṛṣṇa were sporting with Kṛṣṇa in that forest,
Yamunā saw those young girls playing there.
Upon merely beholding Kṛṣṇa, that woman, longing for her beloved, desired him;
Kṛṣṇa then said to her, "O Yamunā, henceforth become a maiden."
"I shall perform your marriage with the daughter of King Kalinda;
become my wife quickly, of this there is no doubt. (18)
She was born as a maiden from the second body of Kalindarāja, and she too was married by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Once, the wives of Kṛṣṇa, distressed by separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
seeing the joyful Kālindī, questioned her, having cast aside their resentment.
O daughter of the Sun, just as we are the wives of Kṛṣṇa, so too are you;
we are consumed by the fire of separation, yet how can you exist without it? (21)
Having heard that, Kālindī, the daughter of the Sun and a servant of Kṛṣṇa, said:
"I indeed always attain the divine Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (22)
The Blessed One never goes far away, leaving me behind;
Rādhikā is the Great Queen, whose soul is Kṛṣṇa and whose form is Kṛṣṇa. (23)
I am indeed a portion of Rādhikā; I am not separate from the form of Kṛṣṇa.
Without Rādhā there is no Kṛṣṇa, and I do not exist without Rādhikā. 24.
And Kṛṣṇa does not know oneness with me at all when I am absent;
even so, the service of Rādhā is indeed preeminent.
Then, gladdened by that bliss, I truly experience no separation;
for a virtuous woman devoted to her husband carries him within her womb, her heart, and her vow. (26)
She undoubtedly protects both the side [of the body] and the self-consciousness;
whether in dream, in the waking state, or in sleep, she delights together with her Lord.
There is no difference between the two bodies; their state is merged with that of the husband.
Whenever he so desires, the husband, whose essence is Nārāyaṇa, becomes real for the Satīs. (28)
Having arrived, he is the giver of bliss; there is never any separation.
Whatever happiness a virtuous and devoted wife desires, [he grants it]. (29)
Assuming the form of a husband for the sake of bestowing various kinds of happiness, Hari fulfills the desires of the minds of devoted wives in every way.
Therefore, for noble women devoted to their husbands, there is indeed no separation from their lord;
he himself is this very Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, our husband and master.
"I am the fulfiller of all desires; I have no separation from anyone anywhere.
Having heard this, those women said, "O Kālindī, if indeed by you... (32)
"Kṛṣṇa always dwells with you; show him to us now!"—when she was thus addressed, she laughed and indeed [pulled] her own garment with her hand.
He separated her by the distance of one cubit from his right side;
meanwhile, standing there at his side, he embraced Yamī and laughed.
Beheld by them as he repeatedly delighted Kālindī, Kṛṣṇa then caused all those charming women to become momentarily stunned upon seeing Hari, their husband.
Then they praised the wifely devotion of the daughter of the Sun, for that alone is true wifely devotion wherein the husband is Nārāyaṇa himself. (36)
The inner self exists in every way as the very nature of Nārāyaṇa;
it is never liberated [from Him], just as the Self is never separated from itself.
Thus, there may indeed be some woman who is devoted, wise, and faithful to her husband through her actions, but she is not so by her mind alone. (38)
There is indeed some woman who is virtuous by virtue of her mind, but not by her actions;
there is some woman who is virtuous by virtue of her intellect, but neither by her mind nor by her actions.

If whatever exists by means of the three [factors] does not exist as a self-subsistent reality, then everything arises precisely for the sake of separation from them and is devoid of a self. (1.429.40)
That which is known as *pātivratya* (devotion to one's husband) by its very nature—that supreme *pātivratya* has certainly been attained by me at all times through the grace of Rādhā. ||41||
Servitude, lordship, and devotion to a husband—therefore Kṛṣṇa resides within me. We are the heroines of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, appearing as portions of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. (42)
And by virtue of our connection with Him, even eternal enjoyment exists for us;
He alone is She, and She alone is He—that very Rādhā, the treasure-house of love. 43.
The love of those two took on a beautiful form as the flute;
I have observed that the presence of Rukmiṇī and the others resides within Rādhā. (44)
All of you are united with Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
you are joined to the great ocean of eternal bliss and are never separated from it. 45.
But you do not know this; therefore, you have fallen into agitation.
If there were indeed fidelity within yourselves, such agitation would not occur. (46)
Even regarding their devotion to their husbands, the gopīs, like you ladies, were subject to delusion; that delusion, appearing as a semblance of separation, was destroyed by Uddhava. (47)
If there should be a perfect union between Uddhava and you all, the illusion of separation will vanish, and you shall attain the bliss of being with your beloved. 48.
Desiring eternal purity through the dust from the feet of the gopīs upon the ground of Govardhana Hill, Uddhava took the form of a *vallikā* creeper. 49.
But he who is ever blissful and devoted to his wife remains there;
if you wish to meet him in person, then assemble at that place.
A great festival with his wives, accompanied by recitations, songs, and music, should be commenced there; his vision will certainly be attained. ||51||
"Thus, the fulfillment of one's own desires is inevitable.
Having been told this, those wives of Kṛṣṇa went quickly to the grove of creepers. (52)
Not far from Govardhana, they began a festival of kīrtana;
with their minds focused on nothing else, they became absorbed in the aesthetic flavor of songs to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (53)
Then Uddhava, burdened with such love, wearing garlands, divine, and clad in yellow garments, arrived from among the clusters of grass, shrubs, and creepers.
Singing the praises of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, dancing, bowing, and laughing, he assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa; seeing him thus, the women were greatly amazed. (55)
They honored Uddhava, who was the very embodiment of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
seeing him in the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the women were bewildered and wept. (56)
Then Uddhava, perceiving the fire of separation within the hearts of the women,
drew Kṛṣṇa forth from his own heart and presented him to them for a moment.
There, by means of his yogic power (yogamāyā), Kṛṣṇa manifested himself in a thousand forms;
he became the beloved who fulfills every desire in every grove for each of his dear consorts.
He gave his beloved embraces, kisses, and love-filled dalliance; he bestowed upon her the highest bliss. (59)
He indeed extinguished their fierce fire of separation;
Kṛṣṇa likewise bestowed peace upon them, just as he had done for Uddhava.
He bestowed upon them the virtue of devotion to their husbands, as Kālindī does eternally;
and he, the bestower of eternal self-bliss, remained dissolved by their side.
Just as one who desires pleasure proceeds according to his wish, seeking the fulfillment of his vow regarding the three states [of body, speech, and mind],
so too did they take Kṛṣṇa by the hem of his garment and go home.
Uddhava, having led Hari away among the creepers, departed;
this indeed, O Daughter of Padma, is declared to be the nature of her devotion to her husband (pātivratya) performed by herself.
By hearing and reciting this, one obtains that same vow;
one shall find Kṛṣṇa constantly by one's side, on one's garment, and in one's heart—of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the four hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of how Kālindī’s Pātivratya [devotion to her husband] and Uddhava’s Pātivratya caused the other wives of Kṛṣṇa to attain firmness in their own devotion to their husband," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: When I, Viṣṇu, am the speaker and you, Lakṣmī, are intent upon listening,
then the hearing of this Saṃhitā shall grant liberation within two months.
When Lakṣmī is the speaker, Viṣṇu is the listener, and I am also present,
then the hearing of this Saṃhitā, lasting for six months, bestows liberation.
Through the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Saṃhitā*, the eternal [state] is attained; you have obtained the dharma of devotion to your husband from my own mouth. (3)
Indeed, by Rādhā hearing the Saṃhitā from the mouth of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
and likewise by the other gopīs from the face of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In Kāśī, at Kuṅkumavāpī, in Badarī, and in other divine abodes,
she certainly exists by her portion according to her fitness throughout the entire creation.
Men and women who have attained supreme devotion to Narayana as their husband have gone to eternal liberation and my eternal abode.
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to this delightful narrative which destroys the bonds of worldly existence.
In the land of Pañcāla, there was a king who was a devotee of Viṣṇu, righteous and pure.
King Nirbhayavarmā, who was solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa,
constantly worshipped Śrī Nārāyaṇa with a garland of tulasī.
With joy, he constantly performed meditation, worship, and ritual acts, dedicating everything to Nārāyaṇa and Hari, preceded by the offering of his entire being.
One son of his was named Dānaka; he was righteous, possessed of ninefold devotion toward Kṛṣṇa, and solely devoted to the Lord of the Gopīs.
Fearless, he performed most severe penance endowed with devotion;
meanwhile, a daughter was born in his house, possessed of a portion of the splendor of Rādhā-Lakṣmī.
Jīvantī and Lāvaṇyavatī, both devoted to celibacy,
serve their husband Nārāyaṇa out of fidelity to their marriage vows.
Through direct devotion, Hari-Kṛṣṇa accepts the service performed by them;
for both of them are solely devoted to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In whose house the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa shines eternally— that woman who is established in her vows, endowed with austerity, and devoted to the service of the gods.
And where the mad Savitrī, the maidservant of Kṛṣṇa, shines;
and where Kumāra dwells in the western Vyāghrāraṇya forest, which is the abode of the Rākṣasa Tala. || 15 ||
He entered the forest to visit the sacred ford for the purpose of beholding Śyāma;
there he found the forest and the yogins dwelling on Mount Raivata.
And in some places they roamed about in the forms of tigers, lions, and other beasts;
on the road, Kumāra saw more than a hundred lions and tigers.
Terrified by fear, he quickly climbed a tree;
however, the lions remained seated near the tree, as if they were without fear.
Seeing those lions motionless, the enraged Dāni set his mind on killing them;
with fury and splendor, he released terrible arrows. (1.9)
One was pierced by an arrow and met his death;
then those others, who were men in the form of sages and ascetics, quickly became [human beings]. (1.430.20)
The sages said to the king: "We are residents of Raivata;
we are yogis who have arrived for the sake of the pilgrimage of Śyāmaśārṅgin. (21)
"O best of kings, do not slaughter these animals of cruel form, having recognized their true nature.
Having heard this and seeing the sages, Kumāra was overcome with grief. ||22||
"Alas! An ignorant yogi, a brahmin, has been slain by me in the forest;
a sin consisting of the killing of a human being has been committed by me at this holy place of pilgrimage. (23)
"How indeed might there be atonement for this killing of mine?"—
having reflected thus, Droṇa descended and then fell at his feet.
"O great sages, strike me repeatedly with arrows for the sake of destroying my sin;
may the sin consisting of this killing of a Brahmin perish from me. (25)
But the compassionate sages, filled with mercy, spoke these words to that devotee of Viṣṇu who was devoted to the duty of providing shelter, as he had indeed come for refuge: ||26||
But we are virtuous yogis of Raivata, capable of enduring the pairs of opposites; we are perfected beings, divine, possessing celestial bodies, and moving according to our own will. (27)
"We are capable of reviving everyone who has died; do not grieve.
Having said this, they poured the hot water of the Talaśyāma tīrtha upon the corpse.
They all joined [the arrow] with their stream [of water] and cried out, "May you live!
Thereupon the sage arose and bowed repeatedly to those gurus.
Now, being exceedingly pleased, he worshipped them repeatedly from his heart;
meanwhile, the sages attained a state of invisibility within the forest.
However, because the sin arising from the killing clung to the donor,
he became extremely agitated there in the forest, tormented by that act of slaughter.
Addicted to the sin of killing and having adopted the way of life of a hunter, he wandered about;
pursued intensely by the guilt of his slaughter, he found no place of rest anywhere.
Wandering about, he indeed went to the forest of lions where the Sarasvatī flows;
there, in ancient times, during the Kṛta age, she cast the submarine fire into the ocean.
Then that youth reached the excellent sacred field of Somanātha and proceeded to the Prācī Sarasvatī, where the great sage resided.
One named Trita, possessing a divine body, was resplendent within a leaf-hut;
by him [the other] was honored, and he fell upon the ground at his feet. (35)
She performed the washing of his feet, the massaging of his feet and so forth, as well as fetching water, service, and likewise providing him with fruit for food. ||36||
The sweeping of the hut and hermitage with a broom must be performed without hesitation,
as well as the arrangement of leaf-patterns using the leaves of the *brahmavṛkṣa* and other trees.
