Then, having bathed them at the Vetāloddhāraka Tīrtha, they gave them water, food, the remnants of Kṛṣṇa’s offerings, and tulasī.
Having abandoned their terrible state as *vetālas* and attained divine forms, they acquired the four-armed form through the merit of his grace. || 11.3 ||
Having ascended the celestial chariots by the thousands, those Vaiṣṇavas,
having become the attendants of Viṣṇu, departed for Vaikuṇṭha.

Having thus brought about the liberation of the various classes of *vetālas*, the king and the others departed for Kāśī and Yamunā, while they [the *vetālas*] returned again to their respective places.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has been told this supreme and great sovereignty of devotion to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa belonging to the daughter of Gālava.
By hearing, remembering, or even reciting this, one obtains the fruit of devotion to one's husband;
having obtained the fruit of devotion to one's husband, a man shall attain liberation.

Thus ends the four hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Vidyādhara Sudarśana’s Attainment of Human Birth and Subsequent State as a Vetāla due to His Disrespect toward the Daughter of Gālava, and the Liberation of the Daughter of Gālava through the Power of Kṛṣṇa’s Devotion by Means of the King of Kāśī," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga Cycle, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Lakṣmī, all that is auspicious among the auspicious resides in you.
Just as you are devoted to me with the vow of a wife, there is no other such as you.
O my beloved, you who dwell eternally upon the surface of my chest—
without you, my body is devoid of splendor, like a piece of withered wood.
It truly exists; of this there is no doubt—that beautiful [city] shines forth for you within my supreme, imperishable abode, where I, the Supreme Person, reside.
You exist as my beloved, known as Jayā and Lalitā;
in Goloka, you are Rādhā, Durgā, and Sarasvatī to me, who am named Kṛṣṇa.
You exist as Gaṅgā, Padmā, and Pañcarūpā, and thereafter as Koṭisvarūpiṇī;
you abide as my wife, devoted to the vow of fidelity.
"You dwell in Vaikuṇṭha as the beloved of Nārāyaṇa;
you are my virtuous wife in the form of Lakṣmī, assuming millions of forms."
In the station called Amṛta, you are the beloved of me, Nārāyaṇa, the All-pervading;
and in the fourfold Vaikuṇṭha, you are the sovereign Mahālakṣmī.
You are Sītā, Prabhā, Māṇikī, Pārvatī, Maṅgalā, and Satī;
you abide as a great chaste lady, devoted solely to your husband.
Svāhā, the wife of Agni, resides within me, whose nature is that of fire;
without you, I never accept food or any offering made into the sacrificial fire.
Even for the gods, the oblation is obtained from your hand every day;
you, being the virtuous Svadhā, exist as the sustenance for my ancestors and my own forms.
In offerings to the gods, offerings to the ancestors, and in acts of libation, nothing offered is ever attained without you;
you are the eternal sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) for my sacrifice, embodying the dharma of devotion to one's husband.
"Without a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), however, I truly do not become complete as a rite;
indeed, in a sacrifice without a dakṣiṇā, no fruit and no son is produced. (1.2)
Everything performed without fruit is mere labor, consisting only of expenditure;
[this is so] for me, who am Kārtika, she who is named Devasenā. (13)
You alone are Mahālakṣmī; indeed, there is no victory without you.
You are that goddess Ṣaṣṭhī, compassionate and the very embodiment of the Mother.
You are the nurse of children, the protector of infants known as Ṣaṣṭhikā;
you are the giver of offspring and the one who provides for the protection of progeny. 15.
Bestower of the nourishment of offspring and devoted to the warding off of obstacles—
you are indeed that divine Mānasī, appearing in the form of Jaratkārvī.
The mother of the Nāgas and the mother of Astīka, she is the eternal protector from poison;
she is my devoted wife, who took the form of Jaratkāru.
By your mind you are a female serpent, the supreme mistress of the serpent species; for you, O Blessed One, are the mind-born daughter of Kaśyapa.
Having performed austerities for three yugas for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul,
and having beheld the body of Jaratkāru at Śrī Puṣkara, Hari [appeared].
I am named Jaratkāru, the Lord of the Gopīs;
you are Jaradgaurī, a devotee of Viṣṇu, devoted solely to your husband.
Jaratkāru, Jaradgaurī, Siddhayoginī in thought, Vaiṣṇavī, Nāgabhaginī, Śaivī, and likewise Nāgeśvarī. ||2 1 ||
O Goddess, you are the beloved of Jaratkaru, the mother of Astika, and the remover of poison;
endowed with great knowledge, you are worshipped by all.
For one who recites your names, no fear of serpents exists;
in ancient times, Kaśyapa gave you to Jaratkāru, the lord of sages.
Unasked, the best of sages accepted [the bride] at the command of the Brahmin;
having performed the wedding, the great yogi rested for a long time through his asceticism and slept upon the lap of the goddess at the foot of a banyan tree in Puṣkara.
The sun went to its setting, and the time of twilight was passing away. ||25||
"Without performing the twilight devotions (sandhyā), my husband would incur the taint of killing a Brahmin;
therefore, being most virtuous, she enlightened her husband. (26)
But having realized this, he became enraged and spoke with deep anger:
"O virtuous woman, tell me, how was my sleep interrupted by you? (27)
Futile are the vows and other observances of that woman who harms her husband;
likewise, her asceticism, fasting, charity, and religious duties are all in vain. (28)
By her, the husband was honored, and Śrī Kṛṣṇa was likewise honored;
for the sake of the vow of devotion to one's husband, Hari himself appeared in the form of a husband. (29)
All gifts, sacrifices, and as many sacred fords and priestly fees as there are;
ascetic penances, fasts, religious vows, and the worship of the gods—(all these are surpassed by this).
A wife devoted to the service of her husband does not even equal a fraction of the merit of service rendered to one's master;
such a wife dwells in Vaikuṇṭha together with her husband.
Devoted solely to the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, she rejoices;
she does what is displeasing to her husband and speaks what is unpleasant, even when it is pleasant.
"She shall go to the Kumbhīpāka hell and thereafter be born as a Cāṇḍālī.
Having heard this, Satī fell at her husband's feet and said: (33)
Out of fear of violating the twilight prayers, you have even abandoned sleep;
O observer of noble vows, grant forgiveness for my wicked command as your beloved.
She who causes the interruption of love-making, eating, or sleep—even a mere servant—shall go to the hell known as Kālasūtra. (39)
Having spoken thus, she immediately fell at her husband's feet,
for Sūrya had indeed seen Jaratkāru about to pronounce a curse upon him.
The blessed Lord Bhāskara arrived together with Sandhyā.
Seeing Sūrya, Jaratkāru reproached him, saying, "O Ravi, how [is this]? (37)
O Lord, you wish to set without my twilight prayer;
you perceive that my sleep has been interrupted without my twilight prayer. (38)
The Sun said: "Listen, O Brahmin; I did not set at that time.
Without your twilight prayers, how could I go to my setting? (39)
"Forgive me, O Blessed One, O Brahmin; it is not fitting for you, O Sage, to curse me.
Upon the anger of a Brahmin, the world perishes; when a Brahmin is pleased, the world remains stable."
"That brāhmaṇa, a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, shall bring about the welfare of the world.
Having heard this, the twice-born man became peaceful and bestowed his blessing. (41)
Then Sūrya went to his own place, and Jaratkāru likewise;
for the young wife, considering herself a bond to the old man, regarded him as a poison.
Having reflected with her mind, she abandoned her wife who was afflicted by grief;
she then remembered her preceptor Śambhu, as well as her chosen deity Hari and Brahmā.
They quickly approached Kaśyapa, their progenitor;
indeed, they came together through the power of their devotion to the dharma of wifely fidelity. ||44||
Then Jaratkaru, filled with wonder, bowed down to them and asked this question: "How is it that you have come here? (45)
Brahmā said: "O great serpent, this beloved wife is not ordinary;
by virtue of her devotion to her husband, she is capable of protecting creation."
And here is this portion of Mahālakṣmī, devoted to dharma;
she would not speak in vain, so you must act accordingly and not otherwise. (47)
Your lawful wife, who is most virtuous and devoted to her husband, must not be abandoned;
by abandoning her, you will suffer a perpetual loss of dharma.
Because of that, you will go to hell; consider the world beyond!
For the sake of protecting the Dharma, bring forth a son by her. (49)
Whether he be an ascetic, a celibate student, a mendicant, or even a forest-dweller,
having first ensured the birth of virtuous sons through his wife, he may thereafter become a sage.
But he who, having failed to produce offspring, abandons his beloved wife out of dispassion—his ascetic merit shall flow away like water from a ladle. (51)
Even a tree does not cast away a creeper clinging to its trunk;
indeed, the Self never casts away its own intellect, which is like its own wife. ||52||
The sound does not leave the day or the night, nor does it exhaust its power;
the sun does not abandon the sky—how then could Jaratkāru [abandon] his beloved? 53.
Thus addressed, Jaratkāru accepted the word of Brahmā;
he did not thereafter abandon his beloved, and those gods departed for heaven.
Then Jaratkārvī said to her husband, who was endowed with wisdom:
"For a husband and wife alike, the renunciation of sense-objects is in every way preferable. (55)
The mutual abandonment of husband and wife is certainly not praiseworthy;
if one does not desire sense-objects, they should dwell together and live happily. (56)
The contempt shown by a husband toward his wife leads to her death;
she who is abandoned by her husband is indeed stripped of honor on this earth. (57)
Becoming a vessel for universal contempt and deprived of all good fortune, she would no longer even be fit for a braid of hair adorned with collyrium and dots of sandalwood paste. ||58||
The life of a woman who has been treated with contempt is indeed in vain;
therefore, O Lord Jaratkāru, if you desire supreme asceticism— ||59||
Then, by your mere will, grant me a mental son;
at your command, I shall always perform penance in your presence.
"I shall perform service for my beloved, having abandoned the objects of the senses;
or else, wherever residence is deemed appropriate by the command of my beloved. (6.1)
There I dwell, by the command of my beloved, either in the forest or nearby;
wherever I abide, O Lord, it is solely through your very presence.
O giver of life, deprived of my beloved husband, I do not wish to remain alive;
I am yours and belong to no other—where else could I dwell without you? (63)
Keeping you at a distance within my heart, I shall dwell on the mountain in the forest;
yet, keeping you close in my heart and upon my breast, I shall remain—please show me mercy. (64)
Thus addressed, Jaratkāru, having considered his pure wife,
brought about that contact with her navel through yoga for the sake of obtaining a son.
By the mere touch of the sage's hand, she immediately became pregnant.
Her husband said, "An excellent son shall be born to you from [the seed of] Manasa."
The foremost among those who have conquered their senses, most righteous, the leader of the Vaiṣṇavas,
he was radiant, ascetic, illustrious, and endowed with all virtues.
He was the best among those who know the Vedas, the foremost among yogis and the wise;
he was a devotee of Viṣṇu, righteous, and the supreme savior of his lineage. (68)
You are devoted to your husband, virtuous, very dear, and sweet-spoken;
you are most righteous, a mother to your son, well-born, and the protector of your family.
Be such a mother of a son who is honored by the world; for what other woman exists who is as true a mother as one who brings about the realization of the connection with Kṛṣṇa? 1.436.70.
O beloved, who is a son other than he who assists in attaining Hari?
O auspicious one, who is a kinsman other than he who bestows devotion to Hari? (71)
He who releases one from bondage shall be a father who shows the path to Hari;
she truly is a mother who delivers one from dwelling in the womb. (72)
He who bestows the abode of Kṛṣṇa is the Guru, the giver of devotion to Viṣṇu;
he is the Lord, the protector of liberation—whether he be Kṛṣṇa himself or a Vaiṣṇava. (73)
O virtuous one, that very teacher is indeed Kṛṣṇa himself, the giver of knowledge;
he is the giver of knowledge, the giver of liberation, the bestower of Kṛṣṇa’s mantra, the Lord, and the Guru. (74)
Knowledge has been given by me to you, and the bull [of dharma] has been given by you to me;
knowledge and dharma do not excel service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (75)
The Lord is the giver of knowledge and the giver of truth; through knowledge, bondage is shattered.
For the destruction of bondage, the Guru is the giver of devotion and the giver of knowledge to Kṛṣṇa.
He is the husband, he is the cosmic order, the master, the lord, the beloved Nārāyaṇa;
he is the enemy and the slayer of disciples who does not liberate one from bondage. //77//
How can he who does not liberate one from the suffering of being born from his mother’s womb, nor from the torment of Yama, be considered a guru, a husband, or a kinsman? (78)
"O virtuous lady, observing your vows, worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa at my command—the Supreme Brahman, the infallible Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who bestows excellent liberation. (79)
"I abandoned you through a ruse; O beloved, forgive this fault of mine.
You are even superior to me in dharma, in virtuous conduct, in devotion, and in the chanting of mantras."
O devoted wife, you abide in knowledge, devotion, and dispassion;
through you, my birth has attained its fruit, and liberation is now within my grasp. (81)
"Since you have granted me this victory over the three worlds through truth, I shall perform a most rigorous penance at Puṣkara. (82)
Having fixed the intellect, senses, and so forth upon the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, those who follow the path of worldly activity find no interest in wealth, women, or homes. (83)

O Goddess, tell me: for those who seek the goal of renunciation and are free from worldly desire, their minds may sometimes waver regarding their steadfastness in the service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet while living together with Him. (84)
Therefore, for a husband and wife on the same ground, constant cohabitation will lead to agitation and bondage; separation, however, will result in excellence. (85)
Therefore, separation is indeed appropriate; practice that which is truly best.
Whether you dwell with me or far away, I am always pleased with you. (86)
"Noble lady, act so as to bring about the severing of our bonds and our liberation.
Having heard the words of Jaratkāru, Mānasī Kamalākalā [acted accordingly]. (87)
He considered separation to be appropriate, not union—even with his wife, who was always by his side and in her fertile season. (88)
The husband should unite with his wife in desire, or the wife should do so according to her impulse at times;
therefore, in this matter, it concerns a husband and wife who possess knowledge and desire liberation.
Having understood that separation is appropriate where no fear exists—whether far or near—the duty of devotion to one's husband is his command. (1.436.90)
A husband who desires his own welfare should always regard the vow of his wife as being for his own sake;
for desire, when it becomes a fault, does not bestow well-being but leads to hell.
Therefore, it is better that this couple, who desire liberation, be separated;
I must go today into the presence of Satī Pārvatī.
"Indeed, on Kailāsa, liberation alone is to be attained through the words of my beloved. Having reflected thus, Satī, the mind-born daughter of the Nāga king, [proceeded]. (93)

With eyes full of tears of grief, she spoke out of modesty to her beloved, as dear to her as life: "O Lord, for the sake of my ultimate welfare, this separation from you is indeed considered by me to be a blessing. (94)
Just as the Blessed One is pleased, so shall I act and not otherwise;
I, however, shall go to Kailāsa to remain constantly at the feet of Pārvatī. (95)
"I shall indeed perform worship there of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
O friend, whenever I remember you, then you shall come to me. (96)
The breaking of kinship arises from affliction, and after that, the estrangement of sons;
more grievous than that is the separation from the lord of life, which brings about the severance of one's vital breaths. ||97||
To women devoted to their husbands, the husband is dearer than even a hundred sons;
because he is dearer to women than anything else, he is called "Pati" by the gods.
As [affection is felt] by those with an only son toward their son, as by Vaiṣṇavas toward Hari, as by those with one eye toward that eye, and as by the thirsty toward water; 99.
Just as thieves [are intent] on the property of others, as lustful men [are intent] on a woman, as the learned [are intent] on the scriptures, and as merchants [are intent] on trade; || 1.436.10 ||
Likewise, O Lord, the mind of virtuous women is ever fixed upon their beloved;
what can I do so that my beloved may be as pleased with me as Vṛṣa himself? || 101 ||
Having spoken thus, that daughter of Jaratkaru fell at her husband's feet and said to me,
"O ocean of mercy, lead me to Kailasa."
And report this supreme austerity to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī,
so that I may become free from doubt and honored there with respect.
Having been addressed thus, Jaratkāru said to her, "So be it," and for a moment he held her in his lap and gazed upon her face with love.
The ocean, a treasure-house of compassion, touched his beloved with his hand for the sake of their separation;
he bathed that virtuous woman with the water of his eyes and with his mind.
Trembling with fear of separation, she covered the sage’s chest with her tearful eyes;
then, through his wisdom, both of them became free from sorrow.
The two of them went to Kailāsa and paid homage to Pārvatī and Śiva;
Jaratkāru then related his own story to Śambhu.
Śambhu became pleased, and Pārvatī even more so;
for yogis there is no such thing as the pain of separation—such is their state. (108)
Having entrusted Śambhu with Pārvatī and his own wife Jaratkāru,
the brahmin went to Puṣkara on Mount Arbuda for the sake of penance.
But having mentally obtained the Guru Śambhu and the venerable Pārvatī,
she rejoiced constantly through her penance and grew up in the Guru’s residence.
Then, when the time had passed, the virtuous woman gave birth to an auspicious boy, a portion of Nārāyaṇa and the teacher of great sages and yogis. || 111 ||
Thereafter, Śaṅkara performed his purificatory rites and taught him the Vedas and other scriptures, as well as the knowledge concerning the supreme Brahman.
She possessed devotion toward her own husband, and toward Lord Hari, the beloved deity, and her guru;
and because of that, her son was made a believer by Śrī Hari.
Then Jaratkāru was remembered for the sake of seeing his son;
having arrived and seen his son, he bestowed blessings upon him.
Having bowed to Śambhu and given his beloved [in marriage], he went to Mānasa-puṣkara;
then Āstika also went with his father to Śrī-puṣkara.
Having performed penance for three hundred thousand divine years to [propitiate] the Lord Śiva,
he then went to Kailāsa to pay homage to his own mother.
Followed by his mother, Āstīka went to Kaśyapa;
seeing his daughter with her son, Kaśyapa attained great joy.
That virtuous woman, devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa and intent upon the path of liberation, remained for a very long time in her father’s house together with her son.
Accompanied by her sons, that daughter of Mānasa was present at the snake sacrifice by virtue of her devotion to her husband,
her righteousness, and the power of Āstīka.
Through devotion to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, she protected all the serpents;
O Lakṣmī, you are that very Mānasī, for you became a female serpent through your mind.
You alone are Maṅgalacaṇḍikā in the destruction of the wicked Tripuras;
you are the bestower of auspiciousness upon the gods and the fierce destroyer of the Daityas.
Indeed, you became Surabhi, the giver of milk to embodied beings;
and on earth, you became Kambharā, the Mother of the World, Nārāyaṇī. 1.22.
Padminī, Tulasī, Vṛndā, Prabhā, Pārvatī, Bhārgavī,
and Mādhavī— you have become many, yet you are the sole upholder of my devoted wifehood.
You are Haṃsā, Mañjulā, Campā, Dayā, Muktā, and Devikā; you are Śānti, Śāntā, Savitrī, Rukmiṇī, Śrī, Jayā, and Anilā.
Hemnī, Mauktikā, Svarṇā, Sītā, Padmāvatī, Prathā,
Rādhā, Gaurī, Kasturikā, Nalinī, Vijayā, and Mudā.
As Hariṇī, Lalitā, Candrā, Kumudā, and Sarojinī,
you exist in many forms and serve [the Lord] in age after age.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have told you this vow of devotion to Kṛṣṇa, which destroys sin and suffering; by hearing or reciting it, liberation and happiness shall be attained.

Thus ends the four hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of Lakṣmī’s Many Incarnations within the Jaratkāru Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the First Section of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā," concerning the departure of her husband Jaratkāru for penance, her residence on Kailāsa, and the birth of her son named Āstīka.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
O Lakṣmī, in ancient times there was a king named Manojava in the Lunar dynasty;
he worshipped the gods with sacrifices and the Brahmins with heaps of food.
He gratified the ancestors with *kavya* offerings and served Hari;
yet, pride arose within him, which brought about the destruction of his wealth, sons, and other possessions.
Egoism, arrogance, greed, violence, lust, anger, and passion—all these, together with their companions, are the causes of the destruction of prosperity. (3)
That king developed a greed for acquiring the wealth and property of Brahmins;
indeed, out of greed, he seized their money and grain.
Out of greed, the king seized the wealth of even the gods;
indeed, out of passion, he confiscated their fields and their means of livelihood.
Then, due to the destruction of his merit and as a result of the ripening of his cruel deeds,
his enemy Golabha besieged his city with a great army.
For six months those two fought; Golabha was victorious, and Manojava, accompanied by his son and wife, departed for another forest.
In a place where no food was to be found and fruits were available only here and there,
a hungry child went to his mother and begged for food.
"O mother, give me food; hunger afflicts me greatly.
O father, give me some food; otherwise, my death is certain. (9)
Having heard the name Sumitrā, the father then spoke softly to his wife:
"O Sumitrā, what shall I do now? Where shall I go for the sake of acquiring food?"
"He will die before long, and that shall indeed be our fate as well.
How is it that Brahmā created me, unfortunate and purposeless? (1.1)
Indeed, in my previous birth, I did not bestow gifts of food, nor was Śambhu—Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa—worshipped by me. (12)
O beautiful one, even the gods such as Sūrya, Agni, and Varuṇa were not worshipped, nor were means of livelihood provided by me in my previous birth. (13)
But when people had departed, I reflected that it had been stolen from another;
by that sin, indeed, I became arrogant in this very birth. (14)
Indeed, out of egoism, I seized the fields of gods and brahmins; I also seized wealth belonging to gods, brahmins, and even those who were righteous.
Thus, all my misdeeds have resulted in the loss of my kingdom, defeat, dwelling in the forest, and the lack of food and other necessities. (16)
My wife and children are hungry and thirsty, like those in the forest;
alas, what course shall I take, overcome as I am by hunger and thirst? (17)
Since previously water and food were never given in charity, nor was an oblation offered, nor was a pilgrimage performed, nor was a funeral rite (śrāddha) ever observed. (18)
Neither was the guest honored, nor was food provided for his kinsmen;
there was no food for the children, nor even grass and such for the cows. (19)
O beloved, you did not provide refuge for virtuous women, nor did you perform service for the righteous; nor indeed was even a grain of flour or other food ever given to living beings.
Otherwise, how indeed could such a hardship as this have befallen me—[the lack of] fruit, water, leaves, bulb, root, flower, and sandals? (21)
Betel, sandalwood, an umbrella, a fly-whisk, ointment, clothing, ornaments, a carriage, a mount, or even anything else whatsoever—[he gave all these]. 22.
"Ultimately, even that which was given in such a manner would not have been [properly] bestowed;
through that sin, this entire mass of suffering has come upon me. (23)
Neither the aśvattha nor the mango tree, nor the kapittha or the tamarind, nor indeed trees bearing fruits such as the amṛta, were planted or watered. (24)
No coconut or myrobalan trees have been planted, nor have resting places been established for travelers and pilgrims. (25)
O beloved, previously no dharma-śālās were ever built by me; nor was service such as sweeping and smearing performed in the temple. (26)
Neither were tanks and such constructed nor were they caused to be made; neither were wells dug, nor was a flower garden planted, nor was a grove of *tulasī* established. (27)
Because of that sin, this mountain of all my miseries has come upon me;
neither sacrifices were performed nor were sacrificial fees offered. (28)
Fasting was not observed among the vows, nor was it caused to be observed by another;
and in the most excellent month during the rainy season, worship of the gods was not performed. ||29||
I have not offered food oblations, water for drinking, or the waving of lights; nor have I performed temple festivals, congregational chanting, or the concluding rites of the vow.
Not even a single, most purifying garland of *tulasī* was worn upon his neck;
nor was any *japa* ever performed by him, nor ever caused to be performed.
"Because of that sin, this mountain of all my suffering has come upon me.
Lamenting thus, the king fell into a swoon of grief.
Then Sumitrā, whose very deity was her husband, embraced him and lamented:
"Alas, my lord! Have you not gone [to the forest] out of sorrow? Or have you perhaps met death in the woods? (33)
O Indra among kings, if you have died in this desolate forest, leaving me, who am without a protector, along with my son, then I shall follow you as one who has lost her husband.
And his son Candrakānta, having embraced his father, wept; meanwhile, the great sage Parāśara, the lord of yogis, [remained silent].
Having arrived there by chance, the devoted wife Sumitrā and her son both rose and paid their respects upon seeing him. (36)
Comforted by the sage, the two then spoke to him regarding how their kingdom had been seized by Golabha, their arrival in the forest, and their hunger and other hardships.
Having heard that account of the king’s familiarity with her and his fainting as it truly happened,
Parāśara, the son of Śakti, [spoke] to the devoted wife.
He said to Sumitrā: "Let there be no fear in you upon my arrival here;
indeed, whatever inauspiciousness existed has been destroyed by the sight of me, a virtuous man. (39)
"I awaken the king; behold the prowess of Kṛṣṇa!
Having said this, the king of sages took water in his hand and recited a mantra.
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; salutations to the Lord!
And he touched with his hand that king, who was like a corpse. (41)
King Manojava, having risen, bowed down to him and said:
"O Blessed One, protect me from this most terrible distress! (42)
Parāśara spoke the mantra again and again to his virtuous son;
he caused sin to burn away and established [him] among the devotees of the Bhāgavatas. 43.
That lord of sages gave the queen an excellent meal of wild fruits and superior water, and he bestowed upon her fruit that is inexhaustible. 44.
In the morning, having indeed bathed the form of the glorious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with water, worship should be performed; the fruit [of this] is attained together with the image itself. (45)
Therefore, because it is to be honored with flowers and other offerings, sixteen fruits will arise as nectars in the morning and sixteen in the evening.
"Those very things are to be eaten until the destruction of the calamity.
Having said this to Sumitrā, he spoke of the virtue of devotion to one's husband.
Listen, Sumitrā, you must always, even in the forest, at the very break of dawn, properly prepare your body in accordance with the requirements of place and time. (48)
Having worshipped the husband according to the rules and having worshipped the fruit with devotion,
one should kindle the fire and offer sacrificial fuel sticks, flowers, and fruits.
For the sake of your husband’s victory and for the destruction of his enemies,
pluck out one lock of hair from your head, and no other.
"O virtuous lady, offer oblations to the purifier (Agni) separately in the evening and in the morning;
say, 'Svāhā to Rudra-Agni for the destruction of enemies.'"
Perform the fire-oblation for forty days, endowed with the vow of Brahman;
O virtuous lady, observing celibacy, victory shall be yours.
O virtuous one, you should perform this practice at the Setubandha on Mount Gandhamādana,
by the shore of the ocean at the holy site named Maṅgala.
Having been addressed thus by the king, that virtuous and devoted wife went together with her son;
having paid homage to Parāśara, she subsisted on a diet of fruits.
Having fed her son, the protector, and having bathed at the sacred ford,
that virtuous woman then chanted the mantra of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa as prescribed.
Having offered oblations and other rites into the fire, she offered her hair into it according to the mantra;
at the forty-second evening, she offered that lock of hair.
From that smoke, there immediately arose a bow that struck fear into the world,
as well as two inexhaustible quivers and a sword with a golden hilt.
There was one shield, one mace, one spear, and a great club;
as well as a conch shell, a chariot equipped with horses, banners, and a charioteer.
The general, accompanied by his army, possessed an impenetrable armor,
as well as many missiles and weapons, vehicles, and mounts.
O Lotus-born One, all things such as food and drink are produced from the fruit;
likewise, divine garments and ornaments are the highest forms of royal prosperity.
"Medicines as well as mounts—everything has been provided for him from that source.
A voice from the sky said to her, "O auspicious and virtuous lady, may victory be yours! (61)
Thus reminded, the venerable great sage Parāśara,
that best of brahmins, arrived instantly with a smile and stood before him.
Then Parāśara [taught] to the king the Brahmā weapon, together with its mantras,
along with its ancillaries (aṅga), its secret lore (rahasya), its method of discharge (utsarga), and its method of withdrawal (upasaṃhṛti).
Then the king gave the instruction; having been urged by the sage, he bowed and, becoming the sovereign lord, ascended the chariot.
There he commanded the queen: "Remain steady in the middle of the chariot;
as long as the battle lasts and until victory is won, do not descend from the chariot. (65)
The army of the hair on your head is indeed a chowrie,
and your husband remains free from obstacles as long as you remain seated upon the chariot.
If you indeed remain seated upon the chariot, there shall be life for the dead;
by the power of her devotion to her husband, this king shall be free from all obstacles.
Then, O virtuous lady, always remain standing on the chariot with your son by your side until you reach the courtyard of your own royal palace. 68.
"You must remain in the courtyard of the palace for now, and thereafter in the chariot;
before you descend, you must first ensure that your son has a prosperous future. (69)
Descend even before that; become one who treads upon the earth, for by then the chariot and the army born of hair shall meet their destruction.
"Go, O virtuous one; depart, O King; Prince, obtain the kingdom.
Having spoken thus, and having made a mark like a drop of sandalwood paste upon his forehead, she vanished. (71)
Accompanied by his wife, his son, and his army, that king went to his own city for victory and blew his conch shell again and again. (72)
Gola-bha quickly went forth accompanied by his army for battle;
the fight lasted for three days, and the army of Gola-bha was destroyed.
On the fourth day, King Golabha was also destroyed;
thereafter, the lord of the earth, Manojava, along with his sons and wife, [perished] in his own [city].
They entered the palace and then descended from the chariot;
at that moment, the army, the chariot, the weapons, the fruits, and so forth, all vanished.
He ruled a kingdom from which all enemies were destroyed, yet he harbored no egoism;
he performed dharma, sacrifice, recitation, charity, and meritorious deeds without ceasing.
He constantly performed service for the gods, Brahmins, virtuous women, and the righteous;
he honored guests and practiced many acts of charity and dharma. ||77||

He practiced the duties of digging ponds, the duties of providing charitable food, and likewise the duties of performing sacrifices; he also performed the duties of watering trees and the duties of offering ancestral rites.
He practiced the duties for a livelihood, such as the protection of elephants and so forth, as well as the duties of cattle-herding and other such observances, and the duties of religious vows.

He himself performed and caused others to perform those duties that protect the subjects, such as the worship of the gods, as well as other virtuous acts such as storytelling and the dissemination of knowledge.
Having abandoned malice, slander, and the like, he became devoted to non-violence;
and the beautiful queen also observed the duties of a virtuous wife.
But especially in the east, that auspicious female ascetic was constantly devoted to meditation upon her own master, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
She was constantly devoted to serving her beloved, likewise dedicated to celibacy, intent on the worship of the gods, a performer of the Kṛṣṇa-vow, and stainless. 83.
Bathing at the three daily junctures, devoted to her husband as her supreme goal, eating but one meal a day, intent on the sacrifice of recitation, she was a server of the virtuous. (84)
And she always subsisted on the water from sacred bathing places and the food of sages and arhats;
thus did the maidservant serve her own master like a female attendant. (85)
The king, too, was constantly devoted to non-violence and became intent upon righteousness;
he caused all his subjects to be initiated into the Vaiṣṇava fold.
In particular, he would constantly summon virtuous men and have them form circles for the continuous chanting of the names of Hari.
Having invited the sages to his home, he listened to auspicious discourses on the Vedas and Shastras together with his family, and he served the Sātvatas.
Thus, he who was as swift as thought protected [the earth] for a thousand years;
then, having consecrated his son in the kingdom, he departed for asceticism.
Meditating upon Kṛṣṇa, the king departed for Goloka without delay;
Sumitrā also remained as a shadow beside her husband for the sake of ascetic penance,
embracing her husband’s body and generating fire from her own person.
Having ascended his funeral pyre, he attained the imperishable abode of Hari.
O Lakṣmī, this account devoted to the virtue of wifely fidelity has been told to you;
whoever hears it or reads it shall obtain the fruit of all religious duties.

Thus ends the four hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Destruction of King Manojava’s Kingdom and Sovereignty through His Atheism, and the Restoration of his Kingdom and Attainment of Liberation through the Devotion of his Wife Sumitrā to the Mantras and Offerings taught by Parāśara, and through Her Chastity which Summoned Divine Armies," in the first section on the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, Lakṣmī, to this wonder that occurred in a former life,
which was performed by you when sent by me for the purpose of testing my devotee.
In ancient times, there was a king named Puṇyanidhi, born of the Lunar dynasty, who,
being devoted to Hari, ruled over the kingdom of the Mathurā district.
Once, that king went to Setubandha for the sake of visiting holy places—
that supreme sacred site of Setu, which contains within it Mount Gandhamādana.
Having heard this from the scriptures and having gathered his retinue devoted to Hari,
he constantly bathed at Dhanuṣkoṭi and other holy sites, and [visited] Rāmeśvara.
Accompanied by his family, he attended the sacrifice and performed it there with joy;
at the conclusion of the Viṣṇu-sacrifice, he was eager for the auspicious concluding bath (avabhṛtha).
He bathed at the Dhanuṣkoṭi tīrtha together with his wife and his retinue;
there, Śrī Hari [appeared] in order to test the king's devotion, [just as] Lakṣmī was tested by him.
Sent from Vaikuṇṭha, she who dwells in the lotus, appearing in the form of an eight-year-old girl, arrived at Dhanuṣkoṭi and remained there.
Having bathed and performed acts of charity, the king beheld that virtuous woman—
a maiden of exquisite beauty and lovely eyes.
The treasure-house of merit questioned her, who was composed of the splendor of all ornaments and adorned with a halo of moonstones: "Who are you? Whose daughter are you? (9)
"In this matter, O maiden, tell me everything exactly as it is according to the sacred tradition.
Having heard this, the maiden became distressed and spoke to that best of kings.
"O King, I have neither mother nor father; desiring to visit sacred fords, I wander as one without a protector, O Lord of Men, and thus I earn my food. (11)
Then the king said, "O maiden, come together with me.
The maiden replied, "If you protect me, O King, by becoming my father. (1-2)
Then, O King, having become your daughter, I shall dwell constantly with you in your house, always beholding you, my father. (1.3)
"O King, let no one take my hand without my own consent;
then, O King, I shall dwell in your palace as a servant of my father. (14)
The king said: "O maiden, since I have no daughter among my children, you must always be my daughter; for I have only this one son."
O auspicious one, to whomever you have affection, to him I give you;
having become the daughter of my wife, dwell in my inner apartments.
The maiden said: "O King, if anyone should forcibly seize me by the hand while knowing me to be helpless, then, O monarch, you must [punish him]. (17)
Only he should be one who is instructed—whether son, friend, or kinsman—for princes are prone to go astray due to royal arrogance. (18)
They attack when there is an imbalance of place and time; I am afraid of that.
May that fear of mine never arise while I am by your side.
Thus addressed, the king said, "So be it," and then the monarch placed his daughter into the hand of his own wife and spoke to her.
"O beloved, protect this virtuous woman from any other man by all means.
Having thus instructed her and taken her with him, the king returned to his own home.
Having protected and nourished the maiden, he lived with her in great happiness.
Then Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a man, arrived there for the purpose of testing her. 22.
While the young girl was gathering flowers with her friends in that flower garden, a resident of a sacred place arrived there, having assumed the form of a Brahmin. ||23||
The Brahmin gave water from a sacred ford and a *tulasī* leaf to the maidens;
then, slowly, he forcibly seized her hand. (24)
Then that maiden cried out, and the other maidens cried out as well;
the gardener, however, related that occurrence to the king.
The king, accompanied by his soldiers and mounts, arrived swiftly at the place where the brahmin—who had forcibly attempted to seize the hand of the maidens—was being pointed out by them. ||26||
But having been seized by the king, bound and fettered, he was sent to prison; meanwhile, those maidens went to their own abode. ||27||
Then, while sleeping at night, the king saw that brahmin in a dream,
adorned with a conch, a discus, a mace, a lotus, and a forest garland.
[He saw] Hari, whose chest bears the Kaustubha gem and the Śrīvatsa mark, who wears yellow garments, who is dark like a fresh rain-cloud, and who is honored by Garuḍa and others. (29)
With a beautiful smile and teeth like jasmine buds, adorned with golden earrings,
He is worshipped by His attendants, sages, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Prabhā, and others.
Beside him, upon a lotus, he beheld his own daughter in the form of Kamalā, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, possessing a divine form.
She held a lotus in her hand, her hair was dark and curled, her limbs were being consecrated by the elephants of the quarters, and she was adorned with divine ornaments.
He beheld Mahālakṣmī, his own daughter, the wife of Viṣṇu;
having seen her thus, the king suddenly rose and reflected.
He went to the maiden's chamber, observing silence and remaining still, in order to examine whether the maiden was present in the chamber or not. (34)
Or rather, as for the dream seen by me— whether it be true or indeed false—
it is true that that Kamalā remains ever new upon the bed of Viṣṇu.
Or does Viṣṇu shine in the middle of the night together with her? Or is the Brahmin himself Viṣṇu, and is he currently in fetters or not? (36)
Or else, [he thought], "Is this one who is the very form of Viṣṇu lying here with a maiden?
Thus did the king ascertain everything, unknown to the people. (37)
Gradually, during the middle of the night, he reached the maiden's chamber;
there he beheld the maiden exactly as he had seen her in his dream.
Then the king, having seen from afar that Hari had indeed become silent like Śrī, went quickly to his own wife and spoke to her, who possessed divine vision. (39)
At that very moment, having mounted his horse at the place of fetters, he went there to see him; however, the Brahmana was not seen.
Having attained even greater wonder, he went again to the queen’s palace; accompanied by his wife, he experienced great marvel and rejoiced exceedingly. 41.
Thinking, "May there be no obstacle to Hari’s sleep with Śrī during the night," the king indeed did not go to his daughter's house. ||42||
Then, when the sun had risen, he went to the maiden's chamber, purified;
there he saw his daughter engaged in the worship and service of Viṣṇu.
Having learned that the king had arrived, the daughter of Hari took her leave and immediately went outside Rumā. (44)
Having prostrated before her father, Lakṣmī led him into her own home;
at that moment, Viṣṇu assumed the form of a brahmin, appearing like a mendicant.
King Viṣṇu, overwhelmed with love, praised him who was in the form of a brahmin:
"Salutations to you, O Lord of my sons; be gracious, O Lord of Kamalā! (46)
O you in the form of a brahmin, salutations to you; forgive my transgression.
Salutations to you, O lotus-eyed one, wielder of the discus, Lord of Śrī. (47)
Salutations to the one marked with the Śrīvatsa; salutations to the wearer of the Kaustubha gem;
salutations again and again to you, the lord of Pārvatī and the master of Lakṣmī. ||48||
Salutations to Viṣṇu, the Lord of Māṇikī, the Master of Radiance;
salutations to you, Śrīnivāsa, Śrīkṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. ||49||
Salutation to Hari, the Lord of Padmā, the husband of Padmāvatī;
salutation to You, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Padminī, the Lord of Bhārgavī.
Salutations to Nārāyaṇa, to Rāma, the husband of Sītā;
salutations to you, the lord of Sarasvatī, the master of Gaṅgā. ||51||
Salutations to you, the lord of Virajā; salutations to the lord of Śrī Durgā; salutations to the lord of my daughter; salutations to the lord of Haṃsāmañjulā. ||52||
Salutations to you, whose self is the dark Brahmin; salutations to you, the innermost Self within the heart.
O embodiment of compassion, salutations to you; salutations to the Lord of Kambarā. 53.
Homage to you who hold a banner, a bow, a fish, and a trident in your hands;
homage to you whose hands bestow well-being and who possess a beautiful form. ||54||
O Supreme Lord, you have been bound by me with fetters and snares;
forgive these offenses of yours against me, your ignorant devotee. (55)
Having thus praised Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama,
he then fell at His feet and offered praise to Lakṣmī, the consort of Viṣṇu.
Salutations to her whose very nature is compassion; salutations again and again to her who has been attained by herself.
Salutations to her whose nature is that of a daughter; salutations again and again to the divine Goddess. (57)
Salutations to you, the wife of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who are both hidden and slender;
salutations again and again to Kamalā, who dwells upon the chest of Viṣṇu. ||58||
Salutations again and again to you, Rādhā, Sarasvatī, and Padminī;
salutations to you, Durgā, Mahālakṣmī, and Śāradā. ||59||
Salutations again and again to you who are Gaṅgā, Tulasī, and Vṛndā;
salutations to you who are Padmāvatī, Bhārgavī, and Kambharā.
Constant salutations to Siddhi, Puṣṭi, Svadhā, and Svāhā;
salutations to Dakṣiṇā, Maṅgalā, Pārvatī, and Śrī. ||61||
Salutations to you, Māṇikyā, Prabhā, and Lalitā;
salutations again and again to you, Jayā, the goddess Jānakī, and Draupadī. ||62||
Salutations again and again to Nārāyaṇī, to Sandhyā, and to Goddess Ṣaṣṭhī; salutations again and again to Mātṛkā, to Kṛṣṇā, and to Mañjulā. ||63||
Salutations to you who are known as Faith, Intelligence, Prosperity, the Sustainer, and the Swan;
salutations again and again to the Earth, to the Embodiment of All Knowledge, to Wisdom, and to the Protectress.
O Mother of the World, salutations again and again to you, the primordial nature, and to your daughter;
whether in my state as her daughter, I have been censured or commanded by you. (65)
O Lakṣmī, please forgive me in every way for my addressing you as "thou";
all the worlds are your children, and you two are the parents of the universe. (66)
"Your transgression must be forgiven by your parents; please be gracious.
Thus entreated, the two gods [spoke] to King Puṇyanidhi. 67.
He said, "O King, you must never feel fear;
for when you performed the sacrifice at Setubandha, I was indeed Hari."
Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person,
became well-pleased, and Kamalā was sent by me.
She was seen by you at the final ablution (avabhṛtha) for the sake of completing your sacrifice;
she remains here with you now by my command.
"Out of devotion I am subject to you, bound by the noose of devotion;
I always forgive the offense of a devotee, of this there is no doubt. (71)
To know your devotion at all times, that Lakṣmī, my beloved Ramā, who is constantly protected and nourished by you, remains in your house. (72)
Therefore, I am exceedingly pleased; for this virtuous woman is of my own nature.
He who possesses devotion to Lakṣmī in this world is declared to be my devotee. (73)
O King, he who is averse to her is my enemy, without a doubt;
you, however, have always worshipped Ramā with devotion. (74)
"Since I am non-different from Lakṣmī, my worship has already been performed;
therefore, no offense such as that arising from fetters has been committed by you. (75)
Because he protected Lakṣmī by fulfilling her word, and because he placed the one who committed an offense against Ramā in shackles. (76)
"I am exceedingly pleased by this as well, O King, for my wife has been protected by you; thus, while performing that protection, you have fulfilled the agreement made previously. (77)
That convention was observed; that service was rendered by you to me.
That is dear to me, O King of Kings, and that service is also dear to me. (78)
"This Lakṣmī is your daughter; you have always acted with truth," he said;
and thus addressed, that Puṇyanidhi became one whose eyes were filled with tears.
Then Lakṣmī said to him: "O Father, I am pleased by your service;
though I am independent, I am always protected by you."
For the sake of fully nourishing your devotion, we two, Viṣṇu and myself, have come here;
being satisfied by your devotion and service, may you be happy. (8.1)
O King, by the grace of us both, may prosperity be yours;
may you possess the sovereignty over great realms forever, certainly. (82)
May you possess firm devotion to our pair of feet;
and at the end of this body, may you attain our eternal abode. (83)
"May your devotion always be intent upon Kṛṣṇa’s wifely fidelity," having spoken thus to her beloved Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Mahālakṣmī [departed]. (84)
He suddenly vanished, and Garuḍa also became invisible;
the attendants appeared, intent upon pronouncing blessings. ||85||
Vindhyāvalī, the king’s wife, rejoiced, overwhelmed with love, upon seeing Śrī Kṛṣṇa and his attendants. 86.
When the divine Lakṣmī realized, "A son has been born to me," she was constantly served, cherished, and always protected by me. (87)
She was delighted, made to laugh, consoled, instructed, fed repeatedly, bathed, and enjoyed herself with me in the garden. (88)
She was given drink, massaged, adorned upon her head, and filled with great joy;
she was summoned by me and seated upon the jeweled lion-throne.
O daughter, O son, O maiden, O young girl!
O beautiful one, O dear one, O mother! She repeatedly offers consolation in times of sorrow.
Constantly touched and adorned by her friends, she was sent forth;
she was made joyful in the great garden and delighted amidst the objects of pleasure. 91.
Pleased by the granting of favorable requests, she was thus obtained through good fortune and was not separated from me even in a dream. (92)
And my daughter was never once kept far from my side;
oh, what excellent fortune and supreme success for my wife! 93.
The profit earned by me through the service of that woman, as well as my house, mansion, beds, coverlets, and household goods—[all these belong to her]. (94)
Bowl-bases, seats and so forth, vehicles and mounts, and divine palaces—these offerings indeed bestow liberation. (95)
My house has undoubtedly become the divine Vaikuṇṭha;
for everything that was touched by my daughter has been gazed upon by Lakṣmī. (96)
All that has attained divinity; what shall I describe as my good fortune?
Oh Lakṣmī, my mother! O daughter, O son, O virtuous one! 97.
If I possess eternal devotion for you, the Illustrious One, and if I possess devotion to my husband Kṛṣṇa, who is Nārāyaṇa, through my wifely fidelity; ||98||
"Then, O virtuous one, grant me your sight, O mistress of my life; O daughter, how have you become invisible, and why are you not seen by me? (99)
Having spoken thus, she joyfully shed tears from her eyes;
meanwhile, Lakṣmī appeared with a face bright as the moon and a smiling expression.
Having emerged from the chest of Śrī Hari, she went to the lap of her mother;
then, out of affection, the little daughter vanished for a moment into her mother's bosom.
The king’s beloved smelled the head of her daughter who was seated on her lap, and said:
"O daughter, O child, you have been in the abode of Śrī Kṛṣṇa."
"O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, at the end of my life, you must lead me to your side while I am united with my husband.
Having said "Om," she drank sweet water and gazed upon his face. (103)
O beloved, Lakṣmī quickly vanished, Nārāyaṇa disappeared,
and his attendants and Garuḍa also vanished in an instant.
Taking you with me upon Garuḍa, I reached Vaikuṇṭha;
the king, having attained detachment, placed the burden of sovereignty upon his son.
Furthermore, he went to the meritorious holy site known as Setumādhava;
there, accompanied by his wife and meditating upon Hari, he spent the remainder of his time.
Having meditated upon Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, he attained liberation at the end of his body;
and Vindhyāvalī, his wife, followed him in death.
Devoted to her husband as his very life-breath, and dedicated to Lakṣmī and Kṛṣṇa,
that virtuous woman produced fire from her big toe upon the funeral pyre.
Just as he began to burn them, Lakṣmī and Narāyaṇa arrived as a divine couple to lead them to the supreme Vaikuṇṭha.

Having caused those two devoted ones, who were observers of the vow of Hari and faithful to their husband, to ascend a celestial chariot, they, possessing divine bodies, led them to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, this auspicious account of your own life has been told to you;
by reading or hearing it, one attains the state of Vaikuṇṭha. (111)

Thus ends the four hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of King Puṇyanidhi’s Attainment of Lakṣmī in the Form of a Daughter through the Performance of Sacrifice at Setubandha-Rāmeśvara in the Kṛta-yuga Lineage," and the Account of the Supreme Bhāgavata King with His Wife Receiving the Grace of Nārāyaṇa, the Arrival of the Lord in the Form of a Brāhmaṇa, the Divine Vision, and the Leading of Them to Vaikuṇṭha, in the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta-yuga. ||438||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the instruction formerly given by my father Dharmadeva to the Apsaras Vardhinī at the place of penance.
In ancient times, Dharma himself performed a truly great and severe penance for a thousand years in Dharmāraṇya for the welfare of all creatures.
Upon the Dharma, bamboo trees and pillars grew from the base of an anthill;
Mahendra and the other gods, perceiving this, were seized by intense fear.
If Dharmadeva indeed performs such fierce austerity,
this world will be reduced to ashes by the fire arising from it.
Then, for the purpose of obstructing his asceticism, the gods and others joined together and dispatched an Apsaras endowed with beauty and virtue to Dharmāraṇya.
Having gone there, she paid homage to her aged father, who was covered in dust;
drawing him out from the bamboo thicket, she spoke auspiciously of the Dharma.
"What is the cause of your asceticism? Dharma said to those dwelling in the sky: "I perform this severe penance for the sake of protecting those who dwell upon the earth."
"How have you, a young woman, beautiful and virtuous, come to this forest?
She replied, "O father, by means of your ascetic power, Mahendra and the other gods [have been subdued]. (8)
Terrified, they sent me to ascertain the cause of their asceticism;
O worshipful one, the cause has indeed been known—it is auspicious, and therefore there is no fear.
I shall speak to the lords of the gods and others so that they will become free from affliction;
however, if any offense has been committed by them toward me, please grant me your grace.
"I am a virtuous woman sent under the control of another;
having obtained the sight of my aged father, I have become purified. (11)
It does not please me at all to create an obstacle for anyone’s meritorious deed;
however, being impelled there by the power of destiny, I shall indeed go.
"O Grandfather, if you would instruct me so that it may become auspicious, I shall indeed go back after having informed Mahendra of the reason for my penance. (13)
O father, the state of being an Apsaras does not please me, for it involves dancing and such;
servitude is painful and destructive to all one's merits. (14)
O Father, for women who have committed many sins, service arises even when there is no restraint from their masters regarding their state as female servants. (15)
"O Father, that my good deeds should result in falling into another's hands and becoming another's enjoyment—this too, I believe, is an obstacle to merit; it does not please me. (16)
Having heard her words, Dharma, who is praised for his righteousness, was pleased with that upholder of dharma;
and he said to her, "Inform Mahendra of the cause of your ascetic penance."
Come quickly, O virtuous daughter; I shall do what is auspicious for you.
O Vardhinī, cast away your fear and come without delay.
Having been addressed thus, she bowed to the Bull and, being delighted, departed in haste;
she informed Mahendra and the others of her penance for the sake of protecting her subjects.
Having quickly reached the Forest of Dharma that accords with righteousness, the auspicious lady bowed with supreme reverence to Dharma, who was situated within the anthill. || 1.439.20 ||
Subsisting on fruits and roots, she served [her husband] day and night;
and she gradually uprooted the bamboo stalks situated within the anthill.
She gradually removed the earth from his dharma-body,
until that body was reduced to mere bones by means of the water of the sacred ford.
The skillful one bathed him; his body attained the state of a sprout, and there he assumed a divine form with a radiance equal to a hundred suns.
By his mere will, Dharma appeared; he beheld the virtuous Satī as a maidservant. Having fallen at the feet of Dharma, she offered him water for washing. (24)
She offered a leaf, a flower, fruit, and so forth to the Bull (Śiva);
she inquired after his welfare and performed the washing of his feet.
The gracious Śrī Dharmadeva said to her: "The glorious Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa created the eternal virtues, as well as the insentient and sentient beings. (26)
For the sake of protecting dharma, the Lord himself, the soul of all, formerly created men and women, as well as the Brahmin devoted to his wife.
And he created his wife, devoted to her husband, and spoke those words to her:
"Listen, O virtuous lady; I shall describe to you those bulls that belong to the quality of goodness (sāttvika)."
If by protecting [these] women the highest welfare may be attained, O virtuous one,
then as long as she remains a maiden, one should observe the vow of the virgin-cow (kumārikā-vrata).
One should indeed serve one's mother and father and attend upon one's guru;
devoted to celibacy, one should worship Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (1.439.30)
Once married, that woman should observe the vow of devotion to her husband;
if she is not married, she should remain a celibate student.
Whether she has already experienced worldly enjoyment or not, whether she was previously married or even if she is a widow,
if she certainly desires the supreme good, she should be devoted to the practice of celibacy.
Devoted to her chastity toward Kṛṣṇa, she shall be born as a celibate woman;
always abiding in dharma, she remains a devoted wife to Kṛṣṇa as her beloved.
O daughter, just as a woman devoted to her husband remains steadfast toward her beloved lord, Kṛṣṇa, so too should you remain; I shall tell you those beneficial virtues.
She should be pure in speech, mind, and body, devoted to the worship of those worthy of worship, free from greed, possessed of faith, and full of devotion to Kṛṣṇa as her Lord. ||35||
Kṛṣṇa is her master and husband; she has undertaken a vow for Kṛṣṇa’s sake. She who is perfected in her vow for the sake of her husband is celebrated as a *pativratā*. 36.
That woman who is devoted to her husband, intent on serving him, and who observes vows toward her beloved husband as if he were Kṛṣṇa himself, [is truly a chaste wife]. ||37||
Having heard this, Vardhinī spoke to Dharmadeva, O Lotus-born One:
"Tell me, what are the characteristics of all those women who are devoted to their husbands? (38)
Then Dharmadeva spoke at length for the enlightenment of the people:
"The life of that man in whose house there is a devoted wife is fruitful. (39)
She whose service, performed with all its constituent parts, is equal to [the service of] Śiva himself; she who is ever devoted to serving him;
she whose very story, when told, constantly bestows merit and brings about spiritual purity.
She eats when the master has eaten; she remains still when he remains still; she performs her duties when he does;
she sleeps when he has fallen asleep; and she awakens first. ||41||
When her beloved has gone to another land for the sake of some business, she should remain devoid of ornaments until he returns from his journey. 42.
Desiring the increase of her husband's lifespan, she should not utter his name;
even when reviled, she should not revile him in return, and even when struck, she should remain serene. (43)
When there is an order of business, she says, "It is done, my lord," and she does so;
when summoned by her master, she goes quickly, abandoning all other tasks. (44)
"Speak, beloved! I am here, become your servant; today I shall do whatever you command. Thus she should speak all such sweet words and perform everything that he directs. (45)
One should not say "no," but rather say, "May my favor be granted.
One should act in such a way that the master becomes satisfied and pleased. 46.
Standing at the door of the house, she should not look long at other men;
nor indeed should she give to another what ought not to be given while her husband is absent.
One should personally prepare the unmentioned requisites for bathing and worship;
one should arrange all items, such as leaves and flowers, according to the appropriate time. 48.
She should never be anxious; rather, being joyful, she should serve her husband, awaiting his affection and fully pleasing him.
She should always eat the food-remnants (prasāda) enjoyed by her husband and avoid other things;
likewise, she should avoid social gatherings, festivals, processions, weddings, theatrical performances, and the like.
O Vardhinī, a devoted wife shall certainly not go out without her husband;
rather, being solely intent on the duty toward her lord, she may go only with the permission of her husband. 51.
Whether he is asleep, seated, standing, playing, or intent upon his duties,
a virtuous wife should attend to him for her own sake, removing any obstacles that may arise.
When the onset of menstruation has occurred, being impure for three nights,
she should observe her state of ritual impurity and must not go outside the house under any circumstances.
A virtuous wife should not show her face outside with its luster dimmed, nor should she allow others to hear sounds from within the house once she has gone out.
Having bathed on the fourth day, the passionate woman becomes pure;
once the fourth night has passed, she is fit for the worship of the gods and other such rites.
Having become pure and worthy of service, she should behold her own master;
or else, having remembered her own master, she should behold the sun. (56)
For if seed is obtained on odd nights, one will indeed give birth to a daughter;
but if conception occurs on even nights, one will indeed give birth to a son. (57)
The opening of the lotus of the womb remains constant until the sixteenth night; beyond that, it becomes closed, and the bodily constituents (dhātus) become useless. 58.
When [the teacher] was menstruating or ill, another beautiful woman touched him twelve times each, bathing again and again. (59)
She should have the garments she previously wore cast far away;
by sprinkling them with water at the end, the menstruating woman becomes pure.
At a wedding, a festival, a journey, a social gathering, while riding a vehicle on a road, during travel, on a pilgrimage, at a sacrifice, when giving a gift, or in a place of calamity; |||6||

In battle, in the narration of sacred stories, in knowledge, in the rite of initiation, in the forest, in the state of renunciation, in the state of yoga, in wonder, and in the steadfastness of austerity; ||62||
In a state of no refuge, dependent on others, in a solitary prison, without assistance, devoid of the status of a laborer, and remaining unconscious; ||63||

In cases of extremely urgent business, during the conjunction of a corpse (śavayoga), during impurity due to birth or death (sūtaka), while traveling abroad, in another's house, and so forth; and during celibacy, religious vows, or sacrificial rites. ||64||
In the acquisition of knowledge, in the observance of fasts such as the Cāndrāyaṇa, and in necessary duties toward one's brothers, sons, father, and others; (65)
Having bathed and observed a single fast, a woman in her menses is indeed purified;
for her beloved is the very embodiment of Dharma, and her husband is the very embodiment of Kṛṣṇa himself. (66)
The husband is her dharma, the husband is her duty, and the husband is her purity; it is not otherwise.
As long as she is united with her husband, the menstruating woman remains pure.

Just as during the four-month period of the rainy season, rivers are always in their menstrual flow, yet they become pure upon union with the ocean and remain in their flow when not united with it. ||68||
Therefore, purity resides under the husband's control, for it is the union with the husband that effects purification;
a virtuous woman should never speak ill of her husband.
Turmeric, saffron, a tilaka mark, vermilion, collyrium,
as well as a head-cloth, betel-leaf, and auspicious ornaments.
Desiring long life for her husband, a wife who is dear to him should avoid grooming her hair and wearing fine ornaments such as bracelets. (71)
She should not go outside alone, nor should she perform her bath naked; she should be skilled in the arts of love and free from pride and laziness. (72)
In whatever way the husband finds pleasure, in that very manner should the wife act as his companion.
[This includes] righteousness, religious observances, recitation of mantras, service, worship, and pleasing the husband. (73)
Thinking thus, one should act for the satisfaction of her husband; in doing so, everything becomes well-done.
Not by the water-scooper, nor by the grinding stone, nor by the hearth, nor by the pestle. (74)

One should not sit upon a ladle, nor on a large cooking pot, nor on a threshold, nor on a mechanical device, nor on a stone, nor on ground that has been pounded with a clod of earth, nor on the seat used for ritual practice and the like. (75)
One who is destitute, devoid of beauty, impotent, aged, diseased, lacking passion, lacking desire, lacking power, and in a state of misery; ||76||
Knowing her husband to be equal to Kṛṣṇa, she would not transgress his will even though she was capable of doing so,
remaining as happy as if there were no shortage of ghee, salt, oil, or other provisions.

If there should be an attainment [of food], it should be described as such; one should never cause distress. One should feed [the guest] from a vessel made of clay, and one should not feed him with the remnants of one's own meal.
A woman should always bathe, drink from, and dwell at the sacred ford of the water used for washing the feet [of her husband];
for her own husband is superior to Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the five gods.
A virtuous woman should never perform a vow or a fast by transgressing her husband's will;
nor should she ever give anything away when she is asked for something difficult.
A woman who reviles her husband, becomes angry, and causes him distress is born as a bitch in a village or as a jackal in a desolate forest. (8.1)
Having worshipped the feet of her husband, she should partake of the food offered as his grace;
she should never sit on a seat higher than her husband's, nor should she go outside [without him]. (82)
She should never have the thought of residing in another's house, nor should she ever utter words that are distressing or harsh. (83)
In the presence of elders, she should not speak loudly nor engage in jesting;
moreover, in a public place, a virtuous woman should not call out to her beloved with a loud voice.
That woman of evil mind for whom her own husband does not please on his bed is born as an owl, a female ruddy goose, or a tree-dwelling creature. 85.
A woman who strikes her husband becomes a tigress or a female cat;
she who casts amorous glances at another man will certainly become one-eyed.
She who eats sweets without her husband becomes a sow or a bat;
she who makes her husband perform menial tasks becomes mute or a beggar woman.
A woman who is envious of her co-wife will repeatedly suffer from diseases of the female organs;
one who shows her face to another man will become ugly and have a foul countenance. (88)
If she gladdens one with her emotions, shows her body to another, and touches yet another, that woman becomes a lizard, a widow, and then a prostitute. (89)
Seeing him returning after having performed his work with great effort,
she [attended to him] with water, seats, betel leaves, and by massaging his feet and other such services.
By fanning him, by offering fruits, and by pleasing speech, she who thus delights her husband enjoys eternal happiness. (9.1)
A father, mother, son, and brother are considered givers of little and limited things; but the beloved husband is always the giver of everything immeasurable to his wife. 92.

The beloved deity, the most excellent teacher, the sacred ford, the worthy recipient, and even Dharma, merit, vows, and penance—all these are considered to reside in the husband; she should worship him as such.
Without her husband, a corpse is useless; likewise, a wife without her beloved is so, for even though she is well-bathed, scented, and adorned with ornaments, she is indeed impure. (94)
A husband is the source of all auspiciousness; without him, there is no auspiciousness.
Even a most wicked mother becomes auspicious for her son only when she has a husband. 95.
She is a great devotee of the Lord, virtuous, and auspicious to all;
she is a widow, shaven-headed, renounced, and clad in fire-like garments, yet truly auspicious.
A Vaiṣṇava widow whose husband is Kṛṣṇa is indeed eternally auspicious;
yet whatever woman is made a beloved wife by her lover is also truly auspicious.
Wearing a garment of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, she is eternally auspicious;
she is a devoted wife to Kṛṣṇa, supported by Kṛṣṇa—she is some indescribable, ever-auspicious woman. (98)
She who has a garland of *tulasī* on her neck, a sectarian mark (*puṇḍraka*) on her forehead, and the *lakṣmī-bindu*, she is the auspicious beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (99)
She is the giver of the guru’s mantra and the giver of knowledge; she is Maṅgalā, the widow, the shaven-headed, the deformed, and the eunuch; she is Vaiṣṇavī and eternally auspicious.
Seated upon the lap of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, beloved of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and the consorts of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa—all of them are indeed divine and auspicious. (101)
At the giving away of the maiden, the Brahmins recite the verses for the chaste wives:
"May you become the companion of your husband, whether he be living or even deceased."
She who follows her husband’s corpse from his home to the cremation ground is virtuous; following the funeral pyre, she gains at every step the merit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice.
Having dragged her husband from the hand of Yama, that virtuous woman shall go to heaven;
for upon seeing a virtuous woman, the followers of Yama flee, abandoning their master.
The sun, the submarine fire, lightning, the stars, the planets, and so forth—
even millions of gods— tremble before the splendor of a wife’s devotion to her husband.
For as many millions of tens of thousands of years as there are hairs on the body of her husband, that virtuous woman shall possess a lifespan in heaven.
Through her husband, she enjoys divine happiness, and from that she shall attain liberation; blessed are her parents, blessed is her husband, and blessed is her family. 107.
Three generations on the father’s side, three on the mother’s side, and three on the husband’s side—
by the merit of the devoted wife, they all go to heaven along with her.
The foot of a devoted wife indeed sanctifies the earth as a sacred ford;
the sun, the moon, and the Gandharvas truly fear to touch her who is faithful.
Even the waters themselves long for union with the feet of a devoted wife;
yet there is no destruction of that sin in this world which cannot be destroyed by the Gāyatrī.
A devoted wife surely brings about its destruction through her fidelity;
for is this worldly existence not composed of women who pride themselves on their beauty and charm? 11.111.
Yet, a virtuous Vaiṣṇava woman devoted to her husband may sometimes be found;
with such a devoted wife, a home is called a true household.

In the duties of the household, in the fruits of dharma, in happiness, in offspring, in the world beyond and in this one, and in the honoring of ancestors, guests, and deities, the wife is the foundation. (1.13)
A home may become purified by a wife devoted to her husband who is like the Gaṅgā,
or a family may become purified by a woman endowed with devotion and fidelity to her husband.
By her whose husband is wedded, through that service to her husband,
heaven, liberation, and likewise the feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa are to be attained.
She whose husband has gone to heaven while she is pregnant, yet remains devoted to her duty,
shall become a *kṛṣṇapativratā* (a woman devoted to Kṛṣṇa as her husband), capable of enduring the bull of widowhood.
A woman should constantly worship Kṛṣṇa, feed Hari, and cherish Him; she should serve Kṛṣṇa in every way, having made Him her own husband.
A devoted wife, having remembered Kṛṣṇa upon her own bed, may obtain sleep;
she should rub fragrant substances on Kṛṣṇa and offer them to Kṛṣṇa.
Remembering Śrī Hari as her husband, she should offer water with kuśa grass and sesame seeds.
She should meditate upon and worship her husband, the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Whatever was dear to her husband, she should always offer that to Kṛṣṇa—
bathing, charity, pilgrimage, listening to sacred stories, and worship.
In the month of Vaiśākha, one should offer water-pots; in Kārtika, ghee-lamps;
and in Māgha, grains, sesame seeds, and so forth, to the Lord who is dark-complexioned (Kṛṣṇa).
In Vaiśākha, one should provide a water-stall (*prapā*), and in the month of Śiva (Mārgaśīrṣa), one should give a water-dripper (*galantikā*).
Uśīra root, a fan, an umbrella, fine garments, sandalwood paste,
betel leaf with camphor, the offering of flowers, excellent food,
a water vessel, the gift of flour, and noble fruits such as grapes and plantains.
One should indeed offer all kinds of food and vegetables, as well as pulses, to Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the month of Kārtika, saying, "May my husband be pleased."

One should offer clarified butter and the like, as well as woolen blankets and other items, for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa; one should also give a bell, a bed, a vessel of clarified butter, wealth, and a milch cow.
One should offer a gift of lamps for the satisfaction of Lord Kṛṣṇa,
whether it be a young maiden, one who is widowed, or one who is without a husband.
Likewise, the religious duties pertaining to Kṛṣṇa must be protected in every way;
Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is to be worshipped and served within the heart. 127.
Thus addressed by Dharmadeva, Vardhinī remained in Dharmāraṇya as a lifelong celibate, ever devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
Devoted to her husband Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
that virtuous woman constantly worshipped Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, in his embodied form.
The servant of the ancestors served Dharmadeva as he was performing penance;
then Hari Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, being pleased, arrived.
Having made her possess a divine body, he led her to his own abode,
after likewise granting Dharmadeva the boon he desired.
"I shall constantly protect the subjects even through austerity;
yet, austerity must be brought to an end"—thus addressed, he was indeed Vṛṣa himself.
He desisted from his ascetic penance and went to the true abode of the Unborn;
Nārāyaṇa, having taken Satī Vardhinī with him, went to his own dwelling.
Thus has been told, O Lakṣmī, this account of Vardhinī’s devotion to her husband;
by reading or hearing it, a person shall attain heaven and liberation.

Thus ends the four hundred and thirty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation of Apsarā Vardhinī, sent by Indra to obstruct Dharma’s asceticism in Dharmāraṇya, through the realization of her wifely devotion to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Now, O Lakṣmī, in Vṛṣāraṇya there are the protectors of the Brāhmaṇas and others—
chaste wives, great saintly beings, who were established as Mothers by Viṣṇu.
But those goddesses, devoted to Nārāyaṇa and ever protectors of the world, are intent on their devotion to their husbands; listen with respect as I describe them. (2)
I shall also fully relate that auspicious narrative concerning the origin of Dharma, which was formerly told there among the Brahmins along with its sub-stories; listen.
Long ago, in the abode of Goloka, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa brought forth from Himself a son, a brahmin devoted to his wife.
That brāhmaṇa, however, by the command of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
arrived here at Goloka accompanied by his own devoted wife.
In the Forest of Dharma, the thousand-eyed, thousand-faced, and thousand-footed one,
devoted to his wife, assumed thousands of his own forms.
All these Brāhmaṇas were of virtuous conduct and auspicious vows;
they were skilled in the entirety of the Dharma and proficient in all the Śāstras.
Renowned for their asceticism and knowledge, devoted to the sacrifice to Brahman,
all those sages dwelt there— powerful ones who knew the three periods of time.
In ancient times, eighteen thousand sons of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa established twenty-four gotras here.
Bhāradvāja, as well as Vatsa, Kauśika, and Kuśa; Śāṇḍilya, Kaśyapa, Gautama, and likewise Śāndhana. || 1.440.10 ||
Jātūkarṇya, Vātsya, Vasiṣṭha, Dhāraṇa,
Ātreya, Bhāṇḍila, and Kṛṣṇāyana Laukika.
Upamanyu, Gārgya, Mauṣaka, and likewise Mudgala;
Gāṅgāsana, Kauṇḍinya, Puṇyāsana, and Parāśara. || 1-2 ||
These twenty-four existed in ancient times during the Yuga:
Āṅgīrasa, Śaunaka, Kāśyapa, Jāmadagnyaka, Laugākṣi, and Māṇḍavya; from them they became members of various lineages (gotras).
But listen also to me regarding those who were born as the most excellent. || 14 ||
Those of the Bhāradvāja gotra are endowed with five pravaras:
Āṅgīrasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Sainya, and Sainyasa. || 15 ||
Gārgya and so forth—these are their five pravaras; these twice-born ones are indeed Vaiṣṇavas.
O Lakṣmī, the twice-born in the Vatsa gotra have five pravaras as follows: || 16 ||
Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni—those born in the Kauśika lineage are endowed with these three pravaras. || 17 ||
Viśvāmitra, Aghamarṣin, and Kauśika—
these three who were born in the Kuśika lineage are endowed with these three pravaras.
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Audala—
these three are those born in the Śāṇḍilya gotra, endowed with three pravaras.
Asita, Devala, and Śāṇḍilya— these three,
O Lakṣmī, are Kaśyapa Brāhmaṇas endowed with three pravaras.
Kāśyapa, Āpavatsāra, and Naidhruva—these three;
and those who belong to the Gautama lineage—these indeed are the five Pravaras. ||21||
Kautsa, Gārgya, Pravaha, Āsita, and Devala—these were the sages; however, for Śāṇḍilya, there was no independent *pravara* (ancestral lineage) existing [among them]. 22.
Likewise, for Jātūkarṇya, there is no independent pravara;
the Brahmins born in the Vātsya lineage are endowed with five pravaras.
Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni;
then those born of the Vasiṣṭha lineage, endowed with three pravaras. ||24||
Vasiṣṭha, Bhāradvāja, and Indrapramada—these are the three pravaras for those of the Dhārīṇa gotra. (25)
Agasti, Darvi, Śveta, Dadhi, and Avāhana—
these are the ones born in the Ātreya gotra, endowed with five pravaras.
Ātreya, Arcanānasa, Śyāvāśva Āṅgirasa, and Atrika—
however, at that time, Bhāṇḍīla had no independent lineage (pravara).
Likewise, for a Kṛṣṇāyana as well, there is certainly no independent pravara;
and similarly, for a Laukika too, there is certainly no independent pravara. || 28 ||
