Having deceived his hand for that long, he departed quickly with a laugh;
I was immediately awakened by the sound of bracelets on his arms. (42)
Having indeed plunged for a moment into the lake of nectar that is the stream of happiness, I have now fallen into the fierce fire of separation from it. ||43||
O friends, the great fire of separation from him burns me intensely;
yet for my life-breaths that are about to depart, hope is a mighty medicine. 44.
Oh, what power he possesses! Oh, what strength and what action!
Oh, what beauty he has, and how wonderful is his charm! (45)
Oh, his crest-jewel is a beautiful peacock feather;
his forehead is lovely, and his eyes are as long as lotus petals. (46)
Your face is sweet with a gentle smile and filled with sweet laughter;
your countenance is as radiant as ten million moons, encircled by a halo of splendor.
Her eyebrow removes the pride born of desire; her chest is like cool sandalwood paste;
her hands are very soft and well-nourished; and the sides of her arms are captivating. 48.
There, my belly and hips, as well as my heart, have indeed become numb;
yet my thighs, which bring delight to the eyes like two shining jewels, remain as they were. (49)
The feet are tender, and the touch is supremely alluring; oh, how long has that certain person’s capacity for bestowing happiness endured! 1.468.50.
There, my very body was offered by me for the sake of joy;
oh, what a yoga! What strength it has! Oh, what prowess and firmness of limb! (51)
"Through repeated practice, my power has been conquered and taken away;
Kālī and Kamalā say this to their affectionate and charming circle of friends. (52)
"Without him, this tenth stage would surely overwhelm me.
Hearing these words of hers, her attendants then fell into a swoon. (53)
Then Kṛṣṇa arrived for the sake of their good fortune;
in a dream, the Lord appeared in a beautiful youthful form and embraced them.
Having granted them that happiness there, she indeed vanished in an instant;
Śaśilekhā, Anaṅgalekhā, and Citralekhā then woke up.
Seeing the marks of Kṛṣṇa’s embrace upon their own bodies,
and looking at one another, they blushed with shame.
The female friends, intensely thrilled with joy, danced;
they rejoiced greatly, for even the hearing of Kṛṣṇa’s name became a direct vision of him.
In the morning, those four, upon seeing him, spoke to their father, Vasubhūti, who was equal to a father and a true Vaiṣṇava, regarding the sight of the Gandharva.
Just as Kṛṣṇa was seen in the dream, just as Kṛṣṇa was propitiated, and just as the boon was previously obtained from Mahādeva, so indeed it came to pass. ||59||
Having heard everything, the father said to those four maidens:
"O daughters, I have offered you with water for the sake of Kṛṣṇa alone."
If Kṛṣṇa should come here today, you must offer him my salutation and praise; O great goddesses, let there be the offering of words: "May the Blessed One be my husband. (6.1)
Where indeed can the son-in-law, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, be found?
By the granting of a boon from Śaṅkara, he has been obtained by you yourselves.
I am blessed, I have accomplished my purpose; my lineage is forever blessed, for the Blessed Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, is its son-in-law. (63)
Blessed are you, ever virtuous; blessed are you, devoted to your husbands.
Blessed are you, wives of Kṛṣṇa; blessed are you, women who have taken vows for Kṛṣṇa. (64)
Having spoken thus, she caused a pavilion to be constructed by the command of her daughter,
with the desire that the maiden might be given in marriage to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
On the second night, that Mādhava arrived;
he indeed enjoyed those maidens, and the Supreme Lord was addressed by them.
Overcome by compassion, Kṛṣṇa said, "So be it," for the sake of the marriage;
and at the very dawn, during the Mahābrāhma muhūrta, in the presence of the sacred fire— ||67||
In the midst of his cows, Vasubhūti gave his daughters to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul,
and he worshipped Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa with devotion.
Dark-complexioned, in the full bloom of youth, well-nourished, and clad in yellow silk garments;
beautiful, smiling, peaceful, the beloved of Rādhā, and captivating to the mind. 69.
With a face like the full moon of autumn, adorned with jewel ornaments,
and graced by a pair of jeweled earrings shining upon his cheeks.
Adorned with jeweled armlets, bracelets, and jeweled anklets,
he wears a brilliant necklace of gems that hangs down as far as his knees.
His neck and chest were resplendent with a garland of *mālatī* flowers, and his body was adorned with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron. (72)
He possessed excellent ears and beautiful cheeks, with lips like the ripe bimba fruit and a row of teeth resembling the seeds of a ripe pomegranate.
Adorned with peacock feathers, his topknot was bound; he was higher than the highest, and shone at the roots of his ears with a pair of *kadamba* flowers. (74)
Having worshipped him who was adorned with all ornaments, the father of the maidens bowed down;
then the Lord Kṛṣṇa accepted those divine maidens according to the prescribed rites.
Resplendent like the full moon of autumn, they were enchanting with their beautiful faces;
their eyes surpassed the beauty of autumnal midday lotuses.

All around, their eyes were radiant with variegated kohl applied to the lashes of their stars; their noses, possessing the beautiful splendor of the beaks of the king of birds, proclaimed their excellence.
Resplendent with large pearls worthy of adorning the space between their breasts,
they were adorned with braided hair and encircled by garlands of jasmine.
Their earrings were like the rays of the midday sun in summer,
and the beauty of their pair of lower lips surpassed that of ripe bimba fruits.
Resplendent with rows of teeth shining like strings of pearls,
their beautiful smiles possessed a pure luster like slightly blossomed kunda flowers.
Adorned with dots of musk and dots of vermilion, and joined with jasmine flowers, the skull-bowls are endowed with splendor. (81)
They were devoted to Kṛṣṇa as their beloved, graced with a beauty equal to Kṛṣṇa’s own;
their cheeks were exceedingly lovely and rounded, and they were endowed with horripilation.
Adorned with necklaces of the finest essence of precious gems upon their chests, they possess firm breasts that are as beautiful as a pair of lovely *śrīphala* fruits. (83)
Endowed with the beauty of rows of petals and radiant with the luster of excellent gems, their bellies are perfectly circular and most enchanting. (84)
Adorned with various triple folds and a deep, rounded navel,
they were decorated with a network of girdles fashioned from the essence of excellent jewels.
They bewilder the minds of the lords of yogis with the playful contraction of their eyebrows, which are like the essence of the arrows of Kama;
the soles of their lotus-feet are adorned with the splendor of the radiance of land-lotuses. ||86||
Adorned with jewel ornaments and beautified by liquid lac-dye,
their two hands— with their red lac— seemed eclipsed by the splendor of the finest gems.
They were delighted by the tinkling of anklets fashioned from the essence of the seven precious gems, and they were beautifully adorned with jeweled bracelets, armlets, and conchs. ||88||
Resplendent with garments as pure as fire and adorned with clusters of jewel-set rings,
their bodies were like handfuls of the radiance of beautiful campaka flowers.
Adorned with a playful lotus possessing a thousand petals and joined with jeweled mirrors, Hari himself is the bridegroom to the young bride.
Delighting him in many ways and having bestowed upon him highly valuable wedding gifts,
he was sent forth by means of celestial vehicles to the supreme state.
By that very same body, through their association with Kṛṣṇa, those beloved ones became worthy of Goloka and equal to Rādhā and Lakṣmī. 92.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have narrated to you this meritorious account devoted to wifely fidelity, which consists in the attainment of Kṛṣṇa and which grants liberation even through its mere hearing. 93.
From reciting this, one obtains that merit which bestows good fortune through Kṛṣṇa;
an unmarried man obtains a jewel of a maiden from an excellent family. (94)
Having heard this, even a maiden, endowed with devotion to Kṛṣṇa, will obtain a virtuous husband through faith and become a devoted wife. (95)

Thus ends the four hundred and sixty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of Kalāvatī, the Dancer, Attaining the State of a Gandharvī in a Future Birth through the Devotion of a Chaste Wife to Kṛṣṇa by Means of Śaṅkara, Along with Her Three Friends, and Subsequently Marrying Kṛṣṇa and Attaining Goloka," in the first section concerning the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the story of Kṛṣṇa accompanied by the wives of the twice-born;
by hearing which, through the power of devotion to one's husband, liberation of the mind shall occur.
Once in ancient times, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as children,
went from Vṛndāvana to the auspicious Madhuvana on the bank of the Yamunā.
With thousands of cows, the princes played with one another; then, exhausted, hungry, and thirsty, the children spoke these infallible words: || 3 ||
"Hunger oppresses us, O Kṛṣṇa; what food shall we eat here in the forest?
Śrī Kṛṣṇa then said to them, "O girls, go into my presence."
One should worship me at the sacrificial site by offering food to the Brahmins— those descendants of Aṅgiras and Viṣṇu who are seekers of liberation— while they are begging for alms.
And if the twice-born, established in sacrifice, do not give food to you because they do not know me, Viṣṇu, whose form is concealed by Māyā; (6)
"Therefore, O beloved, ask the compassionate children.
Having heard Śrī Kṛṣṇa's words, those bulls among boys went [to them]. (7)
Standing before the brahmins with their necks bowed for the sake of alms,
the boys said to them humbly, "O best of the twice-born, give us food."
The twice-born did not hear them; though hearing, they gave no heed.
Therefore, they departed from that spot and went to the kitchen. || 9 ||
Where the Brāhmaṇa women were cooking rice-gruel and other foods in the kitchen, [the king] went there and, bowing down, requested food from the wives of the Brahmins with great persistence.
"You are indeed all mothers, the wives of Brahmins devoted to their husbands;
O mothers, give food to us, the hungry cowherd boys. (11)
Having heard the gentle words of the children and indeed having seen them, those virtuous women asked with respect: "Who are you, and by whom were you shown here? (12)
"O cowherd boys, tell me what food has been obtained here;
we shall give you delicious, warm food accompanied by various side dishes. (13)
Hearing this, the delighted children, holding sticks in their hands, sang of them, saying:
"Sent by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, they have shown us your great kitchen. (14)
"The Mothers have given us food; let us go quickly to their presence.
It is not far from here, in Bhāṇḍīra, in this most beautiful Madhuvana forest. || 15 ||
"Having heard this most excellent and tender account concerning Kṛṣṇa, [they said: 'Food was given by us when requested by the two brothers staying beneath the banyan tree. (16)
With all their limbs covered in horripilation, joyful and with eyes filled with tears of bliss,
they remembered Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and [offered] cooked rice, milk-rice, and curd.
Having prepared sweet foods such as *svastika* cakes, *laḍḍuka* sweets, and excellent *supolikā* pancakes, along with various side dishes, soups, and the like, the women placed them in vessels. (18)
"Since we have silver vessels and the like,
we ourselves shall come along with our children," they said, and departed with joy.
Those chaste wives, blessed and eager for the sight of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, were delighted in their minds as they formed various desires. (1.469.20)
Having gone there, they saw Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Baladeva; seeing the boys seated in the shade of a banyan tree, they saw Hari once again.
Dark-complexioned, in the bloom of youth, clad in yellow silk garments, beautiful, smiling, peaceful, the beloved of Rādhā, and captivating to the mind. ||22||
His face is like the full moon of autumn; he is resplendent with ornaments of jewels, and his cheeks shine with a pair of jeweled earrings.
Adorned with jeweled armlets, bracelets, and jeweled anklets,
he wears a radiant garland of jewels that hangs down as far as his knees.
Her neck and chest were adorned with a garland of *mālatī* flowers, and her body was anointed with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron. ||25||
Hari has ears like those of a deer, beautiful cheeks, and lips like the ripe bimba fruit;
he is adorned with a row of teeth resembling the seeds of a ripe pomegranate.
The Lord, whose crest-jewel was beautifully bound and shone like a peacock’s feather,
was exquisitely adorned by clusters of kādamba flowers held at his ears.
The Supreme Lord, who cannot be attained through meditation even by yogis, who is intent on bestowing grace upon His devotees, and who is being praised by Brahmā, Śiva, Dharma, Śeṣa, and Indra. 28.
Upon seeing Kṛṣṇa thus resplendent, filled with the tenderness and love of the beauty of ten million Cupids, the wives of the twice-born bowed down with devotion. (29)
And according to their own knowledge, they praised the Supreme Lord:
"You, O Kṛṣṇa, are the supreme Brahman, the manifest Lord of Śrī, the infallible Acyuta. (1.469.30)
You are devoid of qualities and formless, yet you yourself appear with form and possess qualities;
you are the witness-nature, untainted, the Supreme Self, and beyond all outward manifestation.
He is more excellent than the Imperishable (akṣara), indeed transcending even the Imperishable;
He is served by the Liberated (mukta), served by Śrī, and worshipped by Rādhā, Ramā, and others. ||32||
He was chosen as their husband by Pārvatī, Māṇikī, Lakṣmī, Prabhā, and others,
as well as by Prakṛti, Puruṣa, Mahāviṣṇu, and Brahmā.

You are the supreme cause of Śiva and the other [deities], as well as of the mantras; whatever is insentient, consisting of the principles (tattvas), and whatever is sentient, all is permeated by you. (34)
All-pervading by you is that which is the locus of brilliance through the power of your splendor;
all sovereign powers, such as Śakti and the rest, have their origin in your formless self.
You are all-bliss, the Supreme Lord, the Master, dearer than life itself;
though possessing a body, You cannot be grasped by those who lack divine vision. 36.
Maheśa, Kārtikeya, Śeṣa, Dharma, Vidhi, Guru, and Sarasvatī—all are dull-witted; what then are we in the matter of praising him? (37)
Pārvatī, Kamalā, Rādhā, Sāvitrī, Śāradā, Prabhā, Māṇikī, Śrī, and Lakṣmavatī—we are none other than these who manifest here. (38)
"O God, friend of the distressed, be gracious to us; have mercy!
Thus did those wives of the brahmins pray at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. (39)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Hari granted them fearlessness and said, "Choose a blessing; it shall come to pass."
Then those virtuous women said: "O Lord, we accept this supreme boon;
grant us your own servitude and firm devotion at your lotus feet. (41)
We behold Your face at every moment and serve Your lotus feet;
grant us Your supreme grace, for we shall never go home again.
Having heard the words of the devoted wives, Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of compassion,
said "Om," and partook of the food offered by the brahmin's wife, which was like nectar.
Having fed the children, the Blessed One himself ate;
meanwhile, there [appeared] a supreme chariot made of gold.
They beheld that divine attendant who had come from Goloka, possessing the luster of a jeweled mirror and adorned with garments of the finest quality. 45.
It was equipped with golden jars, supported by pillars of jewels and the like, adorned on all sides with chowries, and garlanded with flowers from the Pārijāta tree. 46.
It was fashioned with a hundred wheels, adorned with forest garlands and other ornaments,
and well-pulled by excellent divine attendants who were equal to Kṛṣṇa.
Clad in yellow garments and adorned with jewel ornaments, they were endowed with fresh youth, dark-complexioned, and captivating. ||48||
With two arms, holding flutes in their hands, wearing the excellent attire of cowherds, and with their curly topknots bound by peacock feathers and guñjā garlands; ||49||
Kṛṣṇa was attended by his attendants, while the wives of the brāhmaṇas,
having been awakened for the purpose of going to Goloka, were joyful of countenance.
Having bowed to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and cast off their human bodies, the gopīs immediately became [divine beings] and went to their desired destination, Goloka. 5.1
Kṛṣṇa, having created shadows that were indeed duplicates of their forms,
sent those women who desired the Brahmins back to the houses of the Brahmins.
The Brahmins conducted a search, asking, "Where have they gone?
Then, seeing their wives returning on the road, they attained peace of mind.
With all their limbs marked by horripilation and their faces and eyes radiant with joy, they said: "Oh, how exceedingly blessed we are, and you too, O devoted wives! (54)
Those wives who were devotees of Kṛṣṇa, equal to Lakṣmī and Rādhā in their love for Hari, [practiced] austerity, chanting, vows, knowledge, Vedic study, and worship. (55)
Bathing at sacred fords and fasting become fruitful through service to Kṛṣṇa;
for those by whom Śrī Kṛṣṇa has been served, what need have they for mountains of merit? (56)
What need have they for ten million trees who have obtained the wish-fulfilling tree?
What need have they for ten million ritual acts whose hearts hold Śrī Kṛṣṇa? (57)
Thus, fully aware of the greatness of Kṛṣṇa as well as that of his wives in every respect, they went to the sacrifice; thereafter, they indeed returned to their homes.
Their love for Him was even greater than that; in all their sports and activities, their courtesy and service were such as could not have been conceived by the Brahmins. (59)
Since the Blessed One is attained through the supreme merits of previous births,
those women who were formerly the wives of the seven ṛṣis and were devoted to their husbands [attained him].
Those women were virtuous, peerless in beauty, and supreme;
all were in the bloom of fresh youth, with full hips and breasts.
Clad in divine garments and adorned with jewel ornaments,
they possess the luster of molten gold and faces like blooming lotuses with gentle smiles.
Standing at the site of the sacrifice together with their master, they performed the offering of substances and other items into the fire; Agni, beholding them, desired them.
Then the Fire-god repeatedly touched them with the rays of his own flames; and beholding their limbs again and again, he became infatuated.
Even while consuming sacrificial food, the exceedingly lustful one, having made physical contact, embraced them repeatedly with invisible hands and through unseen means. (65)
He performed a subtle act of love by embracing them with his flames;
yet those devoted wives did not perceive the movement of the fire at all.
The divine seer Aṅgiras, having perceived the secret conduct of Agni,
who was filled with lustful intent, cursed him for bringing about his own end.
"From this day forward, O Agni, let there be no fulfillment of your desires regarding your crest, your hands, your flames, nor your embers and so forth. (68)
May you always be a neuter being, consisting of flame and bestowing great merit;
may you possess a form and be endowed with desire, and Svāhā likewise be such as that.
Thus cursed, Vahni then emerged and became possessed of a flame,
by whose power sacrificial rites such as *yajña* and *yāga* become meritorious.
Then Aṅgiras, seeing that they were impure because they had intentionally touched the fire, cursed them for the sake of attaining purity: "Go, therefore, to a human womb! (71)
"Your hand shall be taken by Brahmins of noble birth.
Having been told this, they were overcome with grief for a moment and bowed down to him.
All those devoted wives requested what was beneficial and true:
"O best of sages, do not abandon us; for we are sinless and devoted to our husbands. (73)
"Unknowingly touched by another, you truly ought not to abandon me;
you ought not to inflict punishment upon devoted servants. (74)
When shall we behold your lotus-feet, [safe] from the stroke of a sword, from the fall of a thunderbolt, and likewise from every other weapon? (75)
The separation from one's beloved is always terrible and unbearable for virtuous women;
[so too was it] for those most devoted to Brahman, the virtuous ones, who had other beloveds in the form of great sages. (76)
"O Lord of Brahmins, how shall we leave our devoted wives and go to the surface of the earth? If we must go, tell us when we shall return here. (77)
But when women seek refuge with their husbands out of fear of others, to whom can they go for refuge when they themselves are agitated by the fear of their own husbands? (78)
"O most righteous one, grant safety to those who are indeed filled with fear;
for who is unable to inflict punishment upon a son, a disciple, or a wife? (79)
"Who indeed is capable of inflicting punishment or even restraining them?
Having heard these words of the passionate women, Aṅgiras wept out of love. (1.469.80)
Having regained consciousness and questioned her brothers, she then spoke to them words that were beneficial,
truthful, pleasant, appropriate, and supremely enlightening for others.
O beloved, a husband should never, under any circumstances, enjoy his own wife when she has been enjoyed by another; for until her purification, sin is transmitted to him.
She is fit neither for rites to the gods nor for those to the ancestors; being joined with sin, she is unworthy of cooked offerings.
By embracing her, a husband loses his prosperity and is destroyed by his own splendor. (83)
For such a person, the deities and ancestors do not truly become happy through the offering of oblations or the act of satiation; they consume only lukewarm food.
Therefore, the protection of one's wife must be practiced with effort every day;
at every step, the beloved should be guarded by those who are truly wise and vigilant. (85)
A woman should not be dependent on another, for she is indeed a casket of faults;
one ought always to guard both one's wife and one's cooking vessel. 86.
Because of mutual contact, those [objects] are impure; yet they are pure when held in one's own hand.
The purification of impure things occurs through time, through ritual observance, or through birth. (87)
Therefore, those wives who have not been seen by others through the efforts of their ancestors, and who do not look upon the sun, are pure and devoted to their husbands. 88.
But that woman who, though her husband is to be won over, remains steadfast out of fear for the family dharma, she certainly goes to Vaikuṇṭha together with her beloved. 89.
In the twinkling of an eye for the world of the sages, twenty years on earth will pass quickly; indeed, purity through birth is desired.
Go now to the earthly realm, to the womb you desire;
for by the offering of food to Kṛṣṇa, there shall be your release from the curse. 91.
By the power of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, you shall assume three forms;
in the form of divine maidens, you will certainly go to Goloka. (92)
In the form of celestial maidens, you shall go to the world of the sages;
in the form of shadow-maidens, you shall go to the houses of the brahmins.
"You shall certainly attain death as the wives of brahmins belonging to your own class;
this curse of mine upon you today is even more severe than a boon. (94)
"Enjoyment, liberation, and the attainment of a home—these three shall be obtained. Having been told this, they departed from the sacrificial ground and went to the earth on the bank of the Yamunā.
Having been born in suitable households as the wives of brahmins,
they offered food to Hari with devotion and went to Goloka itself.
Then those women departed for the world of their beloved in other forms; however, those women went to the houses of the brahmins in the form of shadows.
It became certain that for them, the curse was indeed superior to prosperity;
oh, how the immediate anger of the virtuous conduces to their benefit! 98.
Indeed, how could anyone possess greatness without adversity?
For it was through the abandonment by their beloveds that the wives of Brahmins were liberated from worldly existence. 99.
Thus has been told, O Lakṣmī, the vow of the devoted wife and the vow dedicated to Hari;
by reading or hearing this, one attains enjoyment, liberation, and likewise exaltation.

Thus ends the four hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, titled "The Liberation through the Chastity of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and the Feeding of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the Other Children Tending Cattle at the Yamunā Bank," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, concerning how the wives of the Seven Sages were transformed into the wives of Brahmins due to a curse resulting from their enjoyment of fire.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the auspicious account of a chaste woman born of the serpent race.
On the beautiful bank of the Yamunā, Kṛṣṇa went accompanied by Balarāma. || 1 ||
He sported near the water with cowherds, bulls, and cows;
likewise, the cows, bulls, and children, afflicted by thirst, drank the water. || 2 ||
That water was indeed poisoned due to the presence of the serpent Kālīya;
some there fell into a swoon, while others even lost their lives. || 3 ||
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having understood this, then restored them to life;
Kṛṣṇa, having ascended a Kadamba tree, assumed a most massive body.
Mādhava fell into the midst of the water upon the serpent;
at that time, the emergence of the water reached a height of many cubits.
Seeing the human being, that serpent fled with the force of its rage;
it pursued that human form in order to seize Hari.
Indeed, his dark body became like heated iron through that splendor;
with his throat and belly scorched by Kṛṣṇa’s radiance, the serpent was greatly distressed.
Having spoken thus, he indeed vomited again;
his teeth were broken and his mouth was stained with blood from chewing the black diamond-hard [substance].
O beloved, the Blessed One stood above the head of Raktavaktra;
the serpent, overwhelmed by the weight of the earth, fell down unconscious.
Regaining consciousness once more, he repeatedly struck Śrī Narāyaṇa with his hoods and Śrī Kṛṣṇa with his tail, employing various maneuvers.
The Blessed Śrī Hari, the moon of the arts, raised his hood and,
with a graceful maneuver, struck it again and danced.
The hood became limp, and the serpent grew soft and large;
seeing him then in a state of fainting, the female serpents wept bitterly.
The wives possessed the qualities of their lord and lived solely for the sake of their husband; among them, the most excellent was his auspicious and virtuous wife named Surasā. (1–3)
Together with the nāginīs, the virtuous woman wept out of love before Hari;
quickly bowing down to Śrī Hari with her palms joined in reverence, she stood there. 14.
Holding his lotus feet, she, overwhelmed with fear, said to Śrī Kṛṣṇa:
"O Beloved of the World, O Bestower of Honor, grant me my husband! (15)
To women, the husband is dearer than life; there is no kinsman superior to him.
I am a devoted wife to the Naga, yet I am one who acts according to my own will.
"O Lord, if it be with a serpent or a deer, I would be afflicted by the sorrow of widowhood;
therefore, O Master, let my death come first, and then that of my husband. (17)
"If he perishes, my own destruction will follow, and you will incur the sin of killing a woman.
Having heard the words of the Naga's wife, Śrī Kṛṣṇa spoke to her.
Arise, arise, O Mistress of the Nagas! Choose a boon and cast away your fear.
Accept your beloved, O Mistress of the Nagas; may you live long, free from old age and immortal.
Abandoning this Yamīhrada, go elsewhere with your family;
go to Khaṇḍaramaṇaka and there be happy.
O auspicious lady, Garuḍa, having offered praise with devotion by means of the mark of your lotus feet, shall bow down at my feet as your husband.
Having heard this, she, bowing with devotion, spoke sweetly to Mādhava:
"O Hari, grant me firm and unwavering devotion to your lotus feet."
O Lord, may my mind wander like a bee around Your lotus feet;
grant me always that good fortune which is Your own beloved. 23.
Having prayed thus, Surasā gazed upon the face of Śrī Hari;
she drank in his countenance with her eyes, which were devoid of blinking, like those of the virtuous.
With the hair on all her limbs standing on end and overflowing with tears of joy, she,
overwhelmed by an excess of devotion, spoke before Kṛṣṇa.
I will not go to Ramaṇaka; I have no need for it. Let the serpent do as he pleases in this world; make me your servant! 26.
Having heard the words of the Naga's wife, the Lord of Śrī said, "So be it. In the meantime, a divine chariot quickly arrived.
Accompanied by the foremost of his attendants and possessing divine articles of equipment,
the attendants of Śrī Kṛṣṇa descended from the chariot with its hundred wheels.
Having bowed to Kṛṣṇa and led her away, they went to the supreme Goloka;
Kṛṣṇa, having created a shadow-form, gave that female serpent to the snake.
The serpent perceived not the slightest agitation caused by the Kadamba tree;
having descended from the head of Hari, he placed his hand upon the serpent's body.
Having regained consciousness, the serpent saw Hari before him, as well as Surasā, his devoted wife, with eyes filled with tears. 3.1.
Having prostrated before Bālakṛṣṇa, he wept, overwhelmed with love;
Śrīkṛṣṇa then said to that supreme devotee, "Choose a boon."
"O serpent, since you are my devotee, remain at ease and abandon fear;
I bestow grace upon him who is my devotee and has offered himself completely to me. (33)
Having first subdued that [creature] somewhat, I shall bestow grace upon it;
for any man who anywhere kills serpents born of your lineage, [he shall suffer]. (34)
"Sin equal to the killing of a Brahmin will certainly befall him who strikes with a staff upon the marks of my lotus feet. (35)
"Indeed, it is certain that his sin will be double that of killing a Brahmin;
Lakṣmī, having uttered a most terrible curse, will depart from his house. (36)
The decline of his lineage, lifespan, and fame will be certain;
at the end of his body, his death shall come from the bite of a serpent. (37)
There will be fear for those born of his lineage from your own lineage;
yet those who, upon seeing my footprint marked with a beautiful lotus, [behold it] among those born of your lineage... [38]
They will bow down with devotion and be liberated from the fear of the serpent;
go quickly to Ramaṇaka and abandon your fear of the lord of birds.
Seeing the imprint of my foot upon your head, the bird will bow down;
you and those born of your lineage shall never have fear of Garuḍa.
"O serpent, choose now another boon as well that you desire.
Thus addressed, Kālīya said: "Grant me devotion and the remembrance of You. (41)
Grant me eternal servitude at Your lotus feet in birth after birth;
may that [life] be fruitful wherein there is constant remembrance of Your lotus feet. (42)
If there is no remembrance of your feet, then dwelling in heaven is fruitless;
however, for one engaged in meditation upon your feet, that very place is indeed supreme.
Whether for a moment or for ten million eons, whether it be the full span of a man’s life or even a single instant—if it passes in the service of you, it is fruitful; otherwise, it is fruitless.
But for those who serve your lotus feet, there is no depletion of their lifespan;
nor do they experience birth, death, disease, grief, pain, or fear. (45)
O Brahmin, for as long as this Manu has been established by Ananta,
for that long have I, through your grace and by means of meditation upon you alone, become one of your own color.
But Garuḍa himself, recognizing me as a devotee who was yet unripe, took me far from that place out of his firm devotion and humbled [the serpent]. ||47||
But by you, having bestowed firm devotion, I have been accepted as your own; and Garuḍa has been commanded: "Do not devour my devotee, O serpent! (48)
I have been favored and always protected by you;
O Lord, ocean of compassion, friend of the wretched, forgive me, the lowest of men! (49)
To the lord of serpents who was speaking thus, Hari then said, "Let it be so.
Having granted the boon to the lord of serpents, Hari spoke again, saying, "Go."
The serpent said, "O Viṣṇu, when shall I behold your lotus feet?
Having prostrated himself a hundred times, he departed for the region of Ramaṇaka.
The water became like nectar, and all living beings were delighted;
listen, Lakṣmī, to the reason for his departure from that former place. ||52||
By the command of Śeṣa, the hosts of nāgas, out of fear,
perform the worship of Garuḍa every year on the full moon day of Kārtika.
Having bathed well at that great holy site, Puṣkara, they performed his worship with flowers, incense, excellent lamps, as well as food offerings and sacrificial oblations.
At that time, however, Kālīya, though arrogant, did not do so;
instead, he prepared the materials for the serpent-worship and was intent on devouring them by force.
Just then, Garuḍa arrived there and fought with those serpents of the Kālīya species; the snakes fled before him.
They went there for refuge to Ananta; having gone there, the king of birds waged a tumultuous battle and the bird conquered Ananta.
But Kālīya fled and went to the pool of the Yamunā;
due to the curse of Saubhari, that lord of birds was not able to go there.
Once in the past, Garuḍa, desiring to eat fish,
approached the vicinity of Saubhari as he was performing austerities on the bank of the Yamunā.
He seized a fish with his beak, and by the turn of fate, that fish,
released from the beak, then fell near the son of Subhara.
"Provide protection for those who have come for refuge," said the King of Fishes to the sage Garuḍa, who was preparing to seize him once again.
Go far away, go far away from my presence, O lord of birds!
I shall quickly reduce you to ashes if you come near my lake.
"By my curse, you shall indeed be reduced to ashes instantly.
Having heard the words of Saubhari, the lord of birds trembled.
Remembering the feet of Kṛṣṇa again and again, he bowed down and departed;
for this reason, that Garuḍa did not come to the pool of the Yamunā.
Thereupon, having attained fearlessness, Kālīya remained there;
by the majesty of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he then became divine among the devotees.
He went to the region of Ramaṇaka together with the shadow of the Nāginī;
but Surasā, in her original form, attained liberation.
Even though she was an animal in the form of a serpent,
being devoted to her husband, she attained and protected her husband, having manifested in two forms for the sake of his deliverance.
Having entered into the service of Kṛṣṇa, even his shadow remained in the abode of her husband;
thus indeed was protection provided by Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
O Lakṣmī, what indeed is difficult to obtain here for one who meditates upon the Blessed One?
Even that which is difficult to obtain in the next world becomes easily attainable.
Therefore, Kṛṣṇa, who fulfills the desire for happiness, should always be meditated upon;
by reading or hearing of him, no fear of serpents arises.

Thus ends the four hundred and seventieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of the Lord by the serpent Kālīya dwelling in the Yamunā lake through the chaste Nāginī Surasā, the Perpetual Good Fortune of her Husband, and the Fearlessness of the Serpent in the Yamunā Lake due to the Curse of Saubhari upon Garuḍa the Eater of Snakes, as well as his Subsequent Residence in Ramaṇaka," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the story of Maṇḍūkī which brings about liberation;
in the Forest of Bliss (Ānandakānana), there stood the beautiful temple of Śambhu.
A single female frog always resided there in the presence of Śiva;
she performed circumambulations, subsisting on the remains of offerings and unbroken grains of rice.
Once, while she had gone outside for the sake of gathering grass and other materials for the monastery,
a certain crow spotted that female frog here and there among the vegetation.
Taking her up with his beak as she was wallowing, the crow went outside the field;
by that crow, the female frog was thrown out from the field.
Having died from the blow of a beak, she was reborn as a Gandharva maiden in the house of Puṣpabaṭu due to the merit of her circumambulations and other virtuous acts.
However, she had consumed moss and other such things from the *liṅga* of Śaṃkara;
by the power of that merit, she became pure and endowed with a sweet voice.
From her very childhood, she became highly proficient in songs;
that virtuous woman was named Mādhavī and remained devoted to Śambhu as her husband.
With beautiful limbs and a graceful form, marked by the most excellent characteristics,
she became a highly fortunate woman who remembered her past lives and was the best among devotees.
Knowing the secrets of perfect song and possessing an exceedingly sweet voice,
she sings at the proper time the *ṣaḍja* or *ṛṣabha* note.
That young woman sings the Gāndhāra, Madhyama, Pañcama, or even the Dhaivata note; at times she sings the Niṣāda with preeminent loftiness.
With the Ṣaḍja scales, the Madhyama scales, and the Gāndhāra scales—
therein, in the Ṣaḍja scale, she properly joins the melodic modulations (mūrchanās).
And when the night has passed its midpoint, during the third watch extending toward dawn, at sunrise with the pure Ṣaḍja note, in a state of longing, accompanied by the Aśvakrāntā meters; (12)
Likewise, in the middle villages, there is the Sauvīrī for the Hāriṇas, and the Aśvā for those who follow Kāla; these are pure middle-toned songs consisting of sound.
And then there is Pauravī; furthermore, among the Gāndhāra scales, there are Nandikā, Viśālā, Sumukhī, Citrā, Citravatī, and Sukhā.
And with her virtuous intellect, she properly joins the conversations exactly as they were spoken;
furthermore, she joins those forty-nine [syllables] in sequence through the process of elision.
The Agniṣṭoma, as well as the Atyaṣṭoma, the Vājapeyaka, the Ṣoḍaśī, the Puṇḍarīka, the Aśvamedha, and the Rājasūyaka. || 16 ||
Having displayed these and other such [movements], he performs the auspicious song,
consisting of one hundred and one rhythmic beats (*tāla*), as well as the *dhruva* and other [sections] characterized by their regularity.
It takes up and likewise sings the six passions beginning with *sannipāta*, as well as the five musical scales (*rāga*): *śrīvasanta*, *pañcama*, and *bhairava*. (18)
She diligently expels the cloud-like Jaṭularāyaṇa;
and for each [of the five], she—that virtuous woman—is the five passionate ones. 19.
He proclaims from his own throat thirty-six passionate women,
and likewise another sixty-five according to the distinctions of place and time.
As many as there may be palm trees, so many are the passions;
the virtuous woman, skilled in song, sings them all at all times. (21)
Mādhavī, whose speech is sweet, constantly gratifies Śaṅkara—the embodiment of the syllable Om—with passionate dances, worship, and hymns of praise. ||22||
Even after attaining priceless youth, he held it in low esteem;
his mind, though naturally fickle, attained steadfastness in Śambhu. (23)
Indeed, hunger, thirst, sleep, fatigue, and the like did not afflict her;
she remained ever unwearied in mind as a servant of Śaṅkara. (24)
She considered even a moment, which is the form of an obstacle, to be useless time;
whatever time had passed for her, separated by even a single blink, was spent in vain. (25)
Thinking, "He shall perform an expiation for not looking upon Śiva," she nevertheless did not abandon her service at all. (26)
Thirsting for water, she drinks even the nectar named Śambhu;
her two eyes do not desire to see anything else, even though it has entered her ears. (27)
Her ears were indeed incapable of perceiving any sound other than the word "Śiva," and her hands, exceedingly beautiful, were constantly engaged in forming garlands for Śiva’s sake. (28)
Nowhere else did her feet move except out of a desire for happiness;
she never took the name of anyone other than him. (29)
She cries out for Śiva, Śambhu, Hara, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Satī, the supreme Lord, her own Master, whose name is Praṇava.
The tongue does not know any other taste than its own;
it constantly cleanses the colored patterns and the palace on all sides.
That Mādhavī joyfully performs the worship of the image, the daily cleaning of the vessels, and the service of the temple. (32)
She constantly serves with great devotion and the mindset of a daughter those who are devoted to Hari and who honor them. (33)
On the fourteenth day of the month of Vaiśākha, Mādhavī,
having observed a fast during the day and performed a vigil at night, remained steadfast in her virtuous vow.
Then, after the devotees who had gathered out of devotion had departed in the morning,
he performed the sweeping and other rites, and worshipped Śambhu with heartfelt devotion.
Singing a sweet song and dancing with her own natural grace,
she meditated upon Śrī Hari Kṛṣṇa within the image of Oṃkāreśvara.
As the ascetics were looking on with extreme emotion, the high-minded one, by means of this very earthly body, [attained his goal]. (37)
Right there, that girl, whose essence is rasa, merged into the form of the syllable Oṃ;
and there, in that light, she became composed of light itself.
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, a devoted wife attained a divine state; there, Śambhu [manifested] for her liberation. 39.
He gave her the mantra of Kṛṣṇa and placed a garland of tulasī around her neck:
"Oṃ namo bhagavate śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine namaḥ. (1.471.40)
Hara bestowed the mantra, the forehead mark (tilaka), and the status of a Vaiṣṇavī;
then, having become four-armed, the Sovereign Lady went to Goloka. ||4 1 ||
On the banks of the Matsyodarī in that sacred field, devoted wives bathe at Goghaṭṭa and behold the divine temple of Kṛṣṇa. 42.
Those who [bathe] in Pañcanada and then, after first bathing there, go into the presence of Oṃkāra, indeed go to the imperishable worlds of the Dark-Cloud-like One (Kṛṣṇa). ||43||
Then, having bathed at Matsyodarī, and thereafter at Goghaṭṭa,
one should go to the temple of Śrīghanaśyāma, which is situated to the south of the Matsyodarī garden.
Having worshipped Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa and Viśveśvara of Kāśī, and having bowed to Gaṇeśa and Hanumān, one indeed becomes liberated. ||45||
From the very moment the Lord of the Universe arrived from Mount Mandara, I too became Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa in the Ānandavana grove at Kāśī. ||46||
On the shore of Matsyodarī, in a magnificent palace adorned with seven peaks, shaped like a lotus and exceedingly beautiful, he who is named Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa resides. (47)
I, who am established in the realm of Goloka as the son of Kambharā here on this earth, am that very same one dwelling there within the image together with you. 48.
O beloved, there the brāhmaṇas constantly chant my eternal names:
Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa and likewise Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (49)
Likewise, the wise worship Viśveśvara and Oṃkāra as long as there is no impairment of the senses and as long as there is no exhaustion of life.
As long as there is auspicious yoga and intense contemplation of the meritorious mind,
for that long should the Lord Hari, the bestower of liberation, be served with diligent effort.
The Goddess Śrī, the bestower of great bliss, shall never forsake those who have taken refuge in the Abode of Fortune within the Forest of Bliss belonging to Śambhu. 52.
Having heard this chapter, people whose minds are fixed on the illustrious Lord shall be liberated from all sins and attain the imperishable state. ||53||

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of Mādhavī’s Liberation after her Death as a Maṇḍūkī through the Grace of Śiva, and Her Attainment of the State of a Gandharvī by Singing in the Abode of Śiva through Devotion to Him," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. [471]
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to another story concerning a female pigeon,
regarding her husband while she was living in a temple.
Through the dharma of devotion to her husband, through service, and through pleasing him,
as well as by the grace of the God of gods, both worldly enjoyment and liberation were attained.
In the Kalpa named Rathantara, in the temple of Trilocana,
upon the Vīrajaka seat, in the field of Ratnasāti, which is most beautiful.
On the peak, which was resplendent with brilliantly shining golden jars, a pair of pigeons lived, having made their home there. || 4 ||
Performing circumambulations every morning, evening, and at midday, he saw [the bird] flying about, its wings fanning air in this direction and that. || 5 ||
One should always remove the dust clinging to the temple by constantly uttering the name "Trilocana" for Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (6)
The auspicious *rātrikā* offering recited by the devotees was accepted by them even from a mere morsel; it certainly increases their devotion. (7)
Every day during the daytime, as they wandered about the palace— which was crowded with devotees—
they performed circumambulations while eating rice and other food.
And they both drank the beautiful water that had come from the Nala;
as they were thus wandering in the vicinity of Mahādeva, [the following occurred].
A great deal of time passed for the two brahmins of virtuous conduct;
then, on one occasion, they were positioned within a window at the top of a temple.
Seeing them, a hawk descended with speed, desiring to seize them from the opposite shore;
but having flown up, the two went inside a temple out of a desire for protection.
The hawk watched for their departure from that place and thought, "How might these two be captured by me simultaneously? (12)
In the evening, the hawk went to another place because those two had not been found;
then the female dove, skillful and devoted to the service of her husband, [remained].
Observing the bird Kāla, she said to her husband, the pigeon:
"O dear, wise pigeon, that hawk is a powerful enemy. (14)
"O Lord, O Master, he will devour us both before we reach another place—bringing upon us widowhood, misfortune, or the destruction of both. (15)
If it were indeed committed by a hawk, it would surely be a great calamity;
for you, my lord, there is the vow of a wife, and likewise for me, there is the vow of a husband.
"The next world would be ruined; indeed, it would be obstructed by that.
Having heard these words from the virtuous woman, whose voice was sweet as a kalaviṅka bird, her husband said to her:
"O virtuous lady, there is no anxiety in the temple of Durgā, for she is the refuge of Śiva."
"But from this day forward, my dear, you must dwell with the utmost purity."
One who dwells in a fortress cannot be overcome by anyone anywhere, even if he is weak; since the house itself is of the nature of a fortress, what fear can there be therein?
"Indeed, she shall not find another good place to dwell that is as secure as this,"—
having heard these words of the pigeon, the female pigeon then [spoke].
Resorting to silence right there, with her eyes fixed upon the feet of her husband, she—
though having pointed out the path of what is beneficial— desired to do only what was pleasing to her beloved.
"The virtuous wife should remain silent and always carry out her husband's word.
Then, on another day, a hawk arrived and saw the couple.
Wandering around the palace with an undiscriminating vision,
he indeed departed, believing that those two unassailable beings were stationed between the peaks.
Then, when the hawk had departed into the sky, the beloved female dove spoke again to her husband: "O Lord, that wicked destroyer has been seen. (24)
"He will certainly cause us some obstacle at some point; therefore, O Lord, we must go to another place that will be conducive to our happiness. (25)
Having heard her words, Kalarava spoke again:
"O innocent one, what will he do? For Durga is like heaven to us both. (26)
O beloved, dwelling within the celestial palace where he has no entry and does not even know the one who would grant it, brings him security and well-being.
Even if, by some chance, there were a sudden visitor in the sky, nevertheless I know those movements which my enemy does not know. (28)
The eight modes of movement are declared to be: *praḍīna*, *uḍḍīna*, *saṇḍīna*, *kāṇḍa*, *vyāḍa*, *kapāṭikā*, *sraṃsanī*, and *maṇḍalavatī*. (29)
Whirling, emptying, flowing, upward movement, curvature,
falling, fainting, and being bound— these are the eight movements, as well as others.
I know all of that, my dear, and I possess complete skill therein;
just as there is no other bird in the sky equal to me.
"Stay in happiness; what anxiety is there while I, your beloved, am alive?
Having heard these words of her husband, that virtuous woman remained silent as if mute.
On the following day as well, the hawk, having arrived there upon the lotus-stone,
sat down for some time with a heart exceedingly joyful.
Having wandered about and searched the path for entry,
and seeing that those two were indeed situated within, he returned once more to the path of the sky.
Then Pārāvatī, being terrified, spoke again to her husband:
"O beloved, this place must be abandoned, for it is defiled by the gaze of the enemy. (35)
"That cruel one is indeed approaching excessively with the desire to seize me.
Hearing his beloved's words, he said: "What will he do, my dear? (36)
For this is generally the nature of women: a disposition toward timidity.
Then, on another day as well, that hawk arrived with the desire to seize her.
Standing there facing those two for a period of two watches, he looked at them again and then quickly departed; she then said to him: (38)
"O Lord, let us go to another place, since death is near to us here;
you have described many kinds of destinies—why this insistence? (39)
Wherever we may dwell, success will face us with effort;
for that man who does not abandon his own country, even if it is beset by calamities.
Though strong, he met his destruction like a cripple deprived of fate; afflicted by his impending condition, the bird did not heed what was spoken by his beloved. (41)
He said, "Do not fear, O virtuous lady; there is no place superior to this.
Then, on another day, at the very dawn, that hawk—
Having reached that place on the way, Bala remained there until evening;
when the sun had set and the bird had departed, Pārāvatī spoke to her husband: ||43||
"O Lord, this is the time for your departure; leave this house.
Even after abandoning me, go forth; later it will be appropriate. (44)
While you live, nothing on the surface of the earth is difficult to obtain:
a wife again, a friend again, wealth again, and a home again. (45)
If the self is protected by a man, even at the cost of wives and wealth—this beloved kinsman, the self, must be guarded as a great treasure. (46)
This self is the supreme acquirer of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa;
as long as there is security for the self, so long is there security in the three worlds. (47)
Therefore, O Lord, having heard my words which are conducive to welfare and endowed with sound policy, go elsewhere from here; otherwise, you will remember me [with regret].
Although addressed thus by his wife, whose intellect was intent on serving her husband,
he did not depart from that place, being restrained by destiny.
Then, at dawn, the hawk arrived and spoke forcefully to him:
"Come outside from this place; today you shall become my prey."
"Or rather, being hungry and intent on my own interest, I do not see the hardship;
O beloved, I shall either enter your house or kill you. (51)
Having spoken thus, he entered within; then the bird was seized by his talon like a hawk, and having seen this, that powerful woman seized the female bird.
They both indeed cried out in distress, for they were protected by no one;
meanwhile, the hawk repeatedly considered that place to be free from obstacles for devouring him.
Meanwhile, the wise Khagī caused a commotion in the sky and said:
"O Lord, please fulfill my final request. (54)
"Seize the foot of the enemy firmly with your beak for your own liberation," thus commanded,
the hawk did exactly so and experienced great pain.
Then, while the hawk was intensely preoccupied,
the female dove escaped from his mouth by force with a mere fraction of her body.
She too, being questioned, repeatedly struck the assailant with her beak and feet;
by that, the pigeon was indeed released by him, who became thoroughly agitated.
The hawk fainted from the exertion of both [wings] while falling from the sky;
indeed, fortune bestows its fruit upon one who exerts effort, even if that person is weak.
Therefore, those possessed by passion praise exertion in all circumstances;
thus, although the two of them had sustained wounds, it was indeed due to the power of destiny. (59)
Possessing life, they remained for a long time on the charming bank of the river Sarayū in the city of Sāketa, and then met their death.
There he became a bird, a Vidyādhara born from a garland of Mandāra flowers,
an abode of manifold sciences, known by the name Parimalālaya.
Having reached the age of youth, he became devoted to the worship of Śiva;
intent upon the life of celibacy, he undertook a strict vow of self-restraint.
I shall observe the excellent vow of a devoted wife, remaining faithful during my fertile seasons; for as long as I live, I shall not eat even the slightest morsel without first worshipping Mahādeva.
Thus she constantly observed that discipline;
then that bird-like Naga maiden, devoted to the virtue of chastity, became known by the name Ratnāvalī.
Always assuming any form at will, she dwelt in the forest of Sāketa;
she had two female companions, Prabhāvatī and Kalāvatī. (65)
When she had attained youth, being beautiful, auspicious, and capable of assuming any form at will,
the virtuous Ratnāvalī, though still a young woman, undertook a religious vow.
"Having seen Śambhu in the morning with his matted locks, I shall break my silence, and not otherwise.
Day after day, she [worshipped him] with many-colored, fragrant, and beautiful flowers.
Then, having worshipped Hara with garlands, sandalwood, lamps, and other offerings,
all three sang a song beautiful with the radiant Gāndhāra note.
Skilled in rhythm and tempo, they all three perform the *lāsya* dance through various formations of the *rāsa-maṇḍala*, accompanied by lutes, flutes, and drums.
Filled with joy, three Naga maidens played musical instruments,
while adorning [the place] with various fragrant garlands, sweeping, and anointing.
They constantly served Hara with dance, song, and excellent food;
however, once in the month of Vaiśākha, on the third lunar day, they observed a fast.
They kept a vigil during the night and performed worship in the morning;
then, at the hour of midday, they fed the virtuous.
They indeed offered delicious food and water to Śaṅkara;
they performed the ārātrika ceremony and presented handfuls of flowers when the time came.
Then Śrī Śaṅkara, being pleased, appeared before them in person,
his body white as pure camphor and adorned with a crown of matted locks.
With his left thigh resting upon truth, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, the god with a serene countenance is the enemy of Kama and the bestower of liberation. (75)
Upon beholding him, those maidens were overcome with horripilation;
they bowed down and offered praise with voices choked and exceedingly faltering.
Victory to you, O Śambhu! Victory to you, O lover of your devotees! Victory, O Lord! Victory to you, O Lord of the virtuous woman! O Lord of creatures, O Lord of the universe, victory to you! 77.
Victory to you, O Lord of liberation, O Lord of devotees, O purifier Śaṅkara!
May victory be yours; salutations be unto you; obeisance to you, repeated obeisance.
Having spoken thus, the young maidens prostrated themselves on the ground like a staff;
embracing them, the Blessed One, the treasury of compassion, spoke to them. (79)
The son of one named Mandāra, known by the name Parimalālaya,
shall become the husband of you all— he who is the foremost among the Vidyādharas.
Having enjoyed pleasures in every way for a long time in the world of the Vidyādharas,
you will thereafter attain detachment and achieve the perfection of liberation.
"All three of you are my devotees, and that Vidyadhara is mine as well;
all four of you shall attain liberation here at the end. (82)
In a previous birth, service was performed by you toward me;
because of that, servitude as well as the vow of celibacy (brahmavrata) was likewise established for you.
By that merit, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself shall become your guru and the bestower of liberation.
And may they become highly fortunate women, devoted to Kṛṣṇa as their husband;
I myself shall chant the name of my husband, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of All. 85.
"You ladies should also worship him; let them receive his supreme mantra, and let them take this water of grace served by Acyuta. (86)
Having done so, Hara gave them the mantra that grants easy liberation:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; obeisance. (87)
Having imparted [the mantra] three times, he gave him a leaf of Tulasī;
he also placed a garland of Tulasī upon his neck and in his hand.
Then Hara himself applied a drop of sandalwood paste upon his forehead;
having thus performed the rite according to the rules, he [placed] the image fashioned from jewels.
She said, "May there always be well-being for you, O Acyutā; may there be unbroken good fortune, perpetual devotion to Viṣṇu, service to Kṛṣṇa, and likewise the vow of a devoted wife."
May there always be such propitiation of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
may service to the husband and service to Kṛṣṇa be ever one and the same for you, without distinction. (91)
Having spoken thus and placed his hand upon their heads, he vanished from sight;
they, with hearts full of joy, went home and sang out in delight.
Having attained a divine state, they are unobstructed by barriers such as walls and move through the paths of the sky like lotuses.
Remembering their previous births, they were truthful and devoted to the practice of celibacy;
by the command of Śambhu, they became intent on devotion to Kṛṣṇa through the mouth of Sāttvata. (94)
O Lakṣmī, those who have become liberated while living (jīvanmukta) attain independent movement here; formerly, there was a twice-born man named Nārāyaṇa who was like a pigeon. ||95||
The son of Amuṣyāyaṇa was devoted to the vow of serving his father;
bitten by a serpent and having died, he then became this pigeon.
The two daughters of Cārāyaṇa were Bhavānī and Gautamī;
they became the wives of Nārāyaṇa, the son of Āmuṣyāyaṇa. 97.
Having fallen into the misery of widowhood and overcome by wretchedness, they came to dwell in the most wonderful hermitage of a certain sage, by the power of fate. (98)
While the sage was then eating plantain fruits he had gathered, those two maidens, having perished due to his curse, became female monkeys. (99)
Having fallen into the water at that most excellent sacred ford (tīrtha), they then gave up their lives;
subsequently, those two were born as daughters of the Nāgas, having taken refuge in a hermitage within a temple of the gods.
The two virtuous women Prabhāvatī and Kalāvatī, devoted to the dharma of Kṛṣṇa,
were the two friends of Parimalālayā, the wife of the Vidyādhara king.
Knowing that those two auspicious Vidyādharīs were full of love for him, his parents subsequently gave them both to him in marriage.
Thus, her three wives— Ratnāvalī, Prabhā, and Kalāvatī—
were devoted to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and dedicated to their wifely virtue.
Filled with happiness, they constantly worshiped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa by performing worship,
chanting, offering food, offering praise, waving lamps, and seeking forgiveness.
They constantly offer handfuls of flowers during regular and occasional festivals;
on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Kārttika, they perform the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
Intending for her Jayantī, they undertook the vow of Kṛṣṇa;
meanwhile, Kṛṣṇa himself, the lord of Rādhā, Ramā, and Prabhā, [arrived] from Goloka.
He arrived in his celestial chariot to lead them away together with their husbands;
having revealed his own divine form, he took them in that most excellent of vehicles.
He went indeed to Goloka and granted liberation in the form of service;
speak, O Lakṣmī, there is no difference in the devotion of devotees before Kṛṣṇa.
Wherever he may be born, a devotee shall attain the feet of Hari;
indeed, all the children of that Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa are truly his own.
Having worshipped Him, they indeed go to the supreme, eternal abode;
by hearing this story of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, one is liberated from sin.

Thus ends the four hundred and seventy-second chapter, titled "The Description of How the Pigeon Couple, by Taking Refuge in the Temple of Śiva, Attained Birth as Vidyādharas; How Parimalālaya the Vidyādhara Had Three Wives—Ratnāvalī, Prabhāvatī, and Kalāvatī; and How All Four of Them Attained Liberation through the Kārtika-Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī Vow and Devotion to Kṛṣṇa," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to how a miracle occurred at the sacred site of Dharmapīṭha in the forest of Ānandakānana; I shall relate that account of the asceticism of Dharma.
That Dharma-pīṭha is indeed said to be located in the sacred field of Ānandakānana;
by the mere sight of that pīṭha, a person is liberated from sins. || 2 ||
Formerly, Vivasvat’s son, the best among the upholders of dharma, performed austerities in that sacred field for the sake of showing favor to the world. || 3 ||
In the cold season he stays in the midst of water; during the rains he dwells under the open sky;
in the heat he stands amidst five fires, and at times he goes out into the intense wind.
He remained for a long time with the tips of his toes and big toes touching the ground;
then, after that, he likewise stood on one foot for a long time.
Then he subsisted on air; thereafter he drank a small amount of water, merely the size of a drop on the tip of a blade of kusha grass; and after that, he was without food.
Thus he spent a divine cycle of four yugas performing penance,
desiring to behold the illustrious Śaṅkara through meditative absorption multiplied fourfold.
Śaṅkara, satisfied by the penance of that man of steady mind,
went to grant him boons to that witness who was the very embodiment of Dharma.
