she became a supreme Vaiṣṇavī and went to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Even she who may be devoid of fortune, devoid of a home, and devoid of [auspicious] karma,
shall indeed obtain both worldly enjoyment and liberation through austerity and propitiation.
By reading and hearing this, one shall attain such a noble state;
having made the lines of fortune auspicious, one shall go to the service of Hari.

Thus ends the four hundred and ninetieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Austerities of Śarmavatī, the Poison-Maiden of Vṛka, the King of Saurāṣṭra, Following the Loss of Her Father’s Kingdom; Her Recollection of Previous Births and the Like; Her Worship of Gaurī and Śambhu; The Test; The Granting of Boons; The Vision of Śivā and Śiva; The Journey to Kailāsa; And Subsequent Liberation in Vaikuṇṭha through Devotion to Nārāyaṇa," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the wonder I shall tell you of at the excellent Muṇḍīra Tīrtha on the bank of the Nāga River in Camatkārapura. || 1 ||
In the auspicious city named Viṭaṅka, on the shore of the ocean,
there was a Brahmin named Śara who, in his youth, was afflicted with the disease of leprosy.
Śarabha’s wife was the virtuous Sudhāmnī, endowed with excellent character; she was constantly devoted to the service of her husband and was never unsteady in her senses.
He beholds even his leprous master exactly as he desires,
and serves him with joy, both in the manner of a slave-girl and in the manner of a wife.
He also gathered various medicinal herbs, even those of great value,
as well as ointments for that purpose and diverse kinds of wholesome foods.
Likewise, she constantly and respectfully summoned the best of physicians,
and she caused them to perform treatment so that his health might be restored.
In whatever manner he takes medicines,
in that very manner the disease spreads through his body due to the ripening of past karma.
Once, a brahmin guest traveling along the road arrived at his house;
seeing him there, exhausted and having reached his home, his virtuous wife [acted].
Unknown to him, Śara gratified him with devotion as a householder by offering food and other provisions; then, once he had eaten and was well-rested, the brahmin Śara questioned him.
"From where have you come, O Brahmin, and to what other place are you going?
The traveler replied, "I am coming now from the city of Camatkārapura."
"I am going to Kāntīpura, O twice-born one, where my residence is always;
there I became afflicted with leprosy due to the ripening of my past karma. (11)
Although various medicines were constantly employed, the leprosy was not destroyed; rather, it increased slightly day by day. (12)
Moreover, I have heard from a physician in the auspicious city of Camatkarapura that there exists a holy site,
Sūryātīrtha, which is auspicious and destroys the disease of leprosy.
At the site of Muṇḍīrasvāmin is the temple of Sūryadeva;
having undertaken a vow, one should go there, bathe, and worship the Sun.
Because of that, his leprosy vanished; it was a divine miracle.
Then, taking wealth with me, I went to the holy site of Ravisthala.
Rising daily at dawn and having bathed, I behold the Sun;
I worship him according to my ability, and I bow down to and remember him. (16)
Especially on Sundays,
I remain without food and keep a vigil at night with songs, musical instruments, and hymns of praise.
Thus performing worship and observing the vow for as long as a year, at the end of that year, the Sun-god spoke to him in a dream: ||| 18 ||
"I am pleased with your devotion; therefore, let your leprosy depart, for in a previous birth you stole gold from a deity."
"You have been born here as one afflicted with leprosy, and that sin of yours has been dissolved.
Om Hrām Hrīm Hraum Sah, salutation to Sūrya, the destroyer of disease.
Having spoken thus, Ravi bathed me there with water.
At that moment my sleep vanished and I saw my body free from disease;
indeed, I was filled with wonder upon seeing myself devoid of illness.
Therefore, O best of Brahmins, go to the auspicious Camatkārapura;
having resorted to Sūryatīrtha, worship the Sun for one year. Recite the prescribed mantra day and night by means of rotating the rosary. (22)
The destruction of all diseases shall come to you through service rendered to the Sun;
may it be well with you, for I shall go to my own home, satisfied by you here. (23)
Having spoken thus, that brahmin departed; then that twice-born man, afflicted with leprosy, gazed upon the face of his own wife like a wretched person.
The wife, a virtuous and faithful woman, agreed with what the traveler had said:
"O Lord, you must go to that holy place where the sun resides, the destroyer of leprosy. (25)
I shall always remain there with you, devoted to serving you; for what greater gain is there for me than the service of my lord? (26)
Thus addressed by his virtuous wife, the brahmin husband, endowed with wealth,
reached the temple of the Sun in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara.
Having seen the vast field of Sūryagraha, filled with ascetics,
he set his mind upon austerity and attained detachment through merit.
Then he said to Sudhāmnī: "O beloved, I am blessed, and so are you;
by great merit, we have seen sacred fords, holy fields, ascetics, and the sun."
"O beloved, liberation has indeed been attained by us through coming to this sacred field;
having emerged from the delusion of Māyā, we shall worship Hari forever."
We shall adopt the livelihood of a monk and live according to reality;
let illness come or let it not come, for the disease of birth will surely exist.
"O virtuous lady, seek peace in Hari; peace now dwells within me.
May you also always possess peace; do not fall into distress. (32)
"O beloved, I have fallen into despondency because of the arrival of this field of merit;
if you wish, O dear one, go home now. (33)
"Having abandoned my own body at this sacred ford, I shall attain liberation," he said, while repeatedly chanting, "O Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, protect me! (34)
The Brahmin performed his worship, and then his wife said to him:
"O beloved, I have never eaten while you had not yet eaten. (35)
O illustrious one, even when you are awake, she does not sleep in solitude;
for her mind finds no rest anywhere else except at the feet of her beloved.
"In my heart, there is no other happiness at all except the service of my beloved;
this beautiful woman, together with her lover, is truly always fortunate. (37)
How can I depart for the next world, abandoning this auspicious day made holy by my beloved? How can I go home, leaving you behind as my traveling companion?
A house made of stone is not truly a home; rather, my home is you, my conscious self, who have been obtained through the marriage ceremony for the sake of the next world.
A home indeed possesses a truly beautiful form when it always contains virtuous women who provide enjoyment, rest, pleasure, and likewise the alleviation of distress. ||1.491.40||

For the sake of attaining happiness for oneself, the mind, the body, and the senses, a house named after its owners was purchased by me through the surrender of the very substance of my life-force. (41)
I have indeed gone there forever; nothing remains for me to go to.
How can I, no longer a housewife, enter another home deprived of you?
Therefore, O Lord, I shall perform pilgrimages together with you;
I shall sustain my bodily existence through whatever is obtained while serving you. (43)
Bound by the fetters of dharma, I swear this by my own truth:
my wife, who shares in the practice of dharma, shall go along with me.
Having thus understood her firm resolve, that brahmin was exceedingly pleased, thinking, "I am blessed, for such a virtuous woman is my beloved."
Then, while the couple remained thus devoted to Hari,
there occurred a great festival on the bank of the Nāganaḍī river during the month of Śrāvaṇa.
In an assembly of more than a hundred thousand people, the two went to behold the sun and performed auspicious worship with special offerings.
At that time, the Brahmin encountered a great crush of people;
though he fell amidst the throng, being unable to rise, he did not get up again.
But that woman, exhausted by the crush of the crowd, was unable to carry [the child] upward;
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, obeisance to the Master. (49)
Having thus performed her recitation, that virtuous and devoted wife [chanted]:
"Oṃ, salutation to Savitṛ, the supreme self in the form of a witness."
Having thus performed the recitation of mantras, that detached brahmin devotee continued;
meanwhile, for the sake of protecting the two of them, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa became the sun.
Having arrived at the same time, he took hold of both of them with his divine hand, raised them into the sky, and wiped them both clean.
Having freed the twice-born man from leprosy and having restored the virtuous woman to a divine form, may there be auspiciousness for all those dwelling at the sacred ford who behold this. (53)
Having thus honored them with blessings, they bestowed the granting of boons;
and having remained for a long time upon the surface of the earth, they became forever happy.
"You two shall go together to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
Having spoken thus, he then accepted the auspicious worship offered by the couple.
Then, having taken them both, the two Nārāyaṇas departed by means of their divine vehicles to their own world, as did the Brāhmaṇa accompanied by his beloved wife.
At that time, he became as rich in the beauty of fresh youth as a god;
the inhabitants of the city were filled with extreme wonder. (57)
Hundreds of thousands of men there performed the worship of the couple and other rites;
having attained the fruit of the sacred ford, they became purified.
Through separation from Sūrya and Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
he obtained a divine vision in the auspicious city of Camatkārapura.
In the solar field, in the abode of the Sun, those devotees of Hari, having accomplished their purpose and being freed from sin, became established and constantly took refuge in Śrī Hari.
Thus, that virtuous wife devoted to her husband, having served her leper husband,
eventually went to the abode of Hari in Camatkārapura in ancient times.
From the recitation, hearing, or even the chanting of this, enjoyment, purification, and liberation certainly come to pass; there is no doubt about it. (62)

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation of the Leper Brahmin named Śaraka from Viṭaṅkapura in Saurāṣṭra—who was a thief of divine property—along with his chaste wife Sudhāmnī, through the construction of the Sūryagṛha Tīrtha on the Nāgamatī River at Camatkārapura and the vision of Sūrya and Nārāyaṇa," in the first section, the *Kṛtayugasantāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, how the two wings of Garuḍa fell in Camatkārapura due to the irreproachable devotion of a faithful wife; I shall tell that to you.
Furthermore, I shall tell you how, by her grace, they became united;
formerly, O descendant of Bhṛgu, there was a Brāhmaṇa who was a friend of Garuḍa.
He had a daughter named Mādhavī, adorned with all virtues;
then, for the sake of her marriage, the twice-born spoke to Garuḍa.
"Seek out a suitable, auspicious, and worthy bridegroom who is a Vaiṣṇava and a Sāttvata, so that I may give my daughter to him. (4)
Then Garuḍa said: "Having placed your daughter upon my back, I shall carry you around the entire circle of the earth."
"Therefore, having yourself seen a bridegroom who is suitable and endowed with virtues for that maiden, bestow him upon her; I shall be the means."
Thus addressed, that brahmin immediately mounted the back of Garuḍa with the maiden and went to see the auspicious bridegroom.
Whichever brahmin youth that maiden beheld with her heart,
at that moment he no longer remained in her mind in any way whatsoever.

One who is of noble lineage but deformed is not as highly esteemed as one rich in beauty but of low birth; yet another is seen who, though endowed with both beauty and noble lineage, is devoid of virtues. (9)
One endowed with virtues is not wealthy, and one who possesses wealth is not possessed of virtues and the like;
even though described as possessing everything, someone is seen to be crippled and senseless.
He was seen to be free from physical defects, possessed of the aforementioned qualities, and engaged in the path of sexual union;
thus a long time passed as they wandered daily upon the earth.
They had a desire in their minds to see the Lord Nārāyaṇa;
they went to the abode of Śvetadvīpa and they went to Badarīvana.
Afterward, they went to the Ocean of Milk and they joyfully went to Vaikuṇṭha.
They went to the house of Bali and also went to Kuṅkumavāpikā.
They went to Bhṛgukṣetra, Vṛndāvana, Śrīraṅga, and Parvata;
likewise, they went to Mahendra, Gandhamādana, Meru, and to heaven.
By means of those [merits], they went to Satyaloka, where they indeed beheld the sage Nārada;
and he was questioned by them in a conciliatory manner regarding Viṣṇu, the eternal Brahman.
"O sage, where does the lotus-eyed Lord reside at present? All the abodes of Viṣṇu have been searched by me everywhere. (16)
"Though we were filled with joy, Keśava was not seen there;
Nārada said that the Blessed One is always present everywhere. (17)
Because you were impure, Keśava was not seen by you there;
for he whose mind is free from latent impressions, devoid of qualities, and has attained divinity [is the one who sees him]. 18.
Viṣṇu is seen by those very people who possess desire; he is not seen by others.
Therefore, for the sake of purifying the mind, take up residence upon the earth.
In the divine city of Camatkārapura, at the sacred site of Hāṭakeśvara,
there Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa will unite with you.
Go without delay to the city of Camatkāra for the sake of attaining that;
there, at the Mahāsarovara lake during the Cāturmāsya, Janārdana resides.
Nārāyaṇa was reclining upon the waters in the Nāga River;
then the three [deities] arrived there at the Jalaśāyi lake.
And having caused the Brāhmaṇa to enter his field with his daughter at an auspicious time, Garuḍa said: "The Blessed One himself shall be obtained through ascetic penance."
May they attain purification through austerity, recitation, worship, and vows.
Om, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; salutations! 24.
"Thus, through constant recitation, purification occurs upon the destruction of latent impressions.
Having spoken thus, Garuḍa went there into the presence of Nārāyaṇa. (25)
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; salutations!
Thus chanting, they both remained in the midst of the water, abstaining from food. (26)
The father of the daughter fasted and performed supreme austerity;
at the end of many years, Garuḍa beheld her as a servant at his feet.
[He saw] you, Lakṣmī, intent on massaging his feet while gazing at his face,
and another aged woman likewise seated beside Lakṣmī.
And the king of birds saw Śāṇḍilī there, established in meditation, emaciated in limb, and observing celibacy; he also saw another woman of beautiful youth standing by her side.
She saw the virtuous Narmadā, who removes the sins of many lifetimes,
as well as another man— an aged, peaceful, and emaciated ascetic.
There Garuḍa beheld the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya;
they and he bowed down to him, and Garuḍa was honored by them in return. Slowly, he [approached]. ||3 1||
He beheld Viṣṇu, wide awake, with a smiling face, who is affectionate toward his devotees; as the Lord asked, "From where have you come? the king of birds replied concerning his welfare.
I have a beloved friend, a Brāhmaṇa born of the lineage of Bhṛgu;
he has a daughter named Mādhavī who is indeed a celibate student (brahmacāriṇī).
No husband equal to her has been found within the circle of the three worlds;
indeed, the lotus-eyed one, endowed with all virtues, is her husband.
One who resembles the lotus-eyed lady is established in my heart;
therefore, O Nārāyaṇa, accept her hand in marriage.
Having heard this, Nārāyaṇa said: "That maiden is a portion of Lakṣmī.
Listen, O sinless one, I shall tell you the ancient narrative concerning Vaikuṇṭha. (36)
Once, that Mahālakṣmī became filled with pride, thinking:
"There is no other woman equal to me, nor even Nārāyaṇa himself. (37)
"By me, through my creative power, the entire creation has been made beautiful;
without me it would be harsh. Therefore, I am in every way the most excellent. (38)
"Today I must not go into the presence of Nārāyaṇa;
Nārāyaṇa himself shall come here to my house for this essential purpose. (39)
Thinking, "He will come; I shall see him and observe what kind of affection he shows," Lakṣmī did not go to the abode of Nārāyaṇa.
And Nārāyaṇa, having perceived Jaya and Pārṣada, spoke thus:
"Today Lakṣmī exists full of pride, as if she were arrogant. (41)
If he should come to my door, entrance must not be granted at all;
yet, having recognized him as Nārāyaṇa through divine vision, [I turned] away. ||42||
When a long time had passed, Lakṣmī returned, casting aside her pride;
but the attendant Jaya said, "O Mother, there is indeed no command from Hari."
I am always the servant of Hari, yet I am the servant of you, O wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
however, standing here at his door, I must obey his command. (44)
"Since I am appointed at his gate, his command is considered paramount. Do as you wish, mother; the restriction was made by my master. (45)
Having spoken thus, he fell at her feet with affection;
she was then indeed restrained from the doorway by that doorkeeper.
Considering that to be an insult to her very self, the virtuous and proud Satī remembered the lotus feet of Hari and prepared to cast off her body. (47)
Then, having learned that Gṛhalakṣmī was indeed enraged in every place throughout the three worlds, Brahmā, Maheśa, Viṣṇu, Dharma, and Bhāskara [set out]. ||48||
Candra, Kāma, Kubera, Vahni, Vighneśvara, Anila, as well as the Ṛṣis, Munis, Manus, and Maheśvara; ||49||
Then, weeping, they approached Padmā;
and they praised Mahālakṣmī, the virtuous and distressed queen of Hari.
Forgive me, O Blessed Mother, you who are of a forgiving nature, supreme beyond the supreme,
whose essential form is pure being, and who are entirely free from anger and other such passions.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, you are the peerless ideal among all virtuous goddesses;
without you, the entire world is like one dead and devoid of fruit.
You are the embodiment of all prosperity and the universal form for all beings.
You are the presiding goddess of the Rāsa dance; all women are but portions of you.
On Kailāsa you are Pārvatī, while in the Ocean of Milk you are the Daughter of the Sea;
in heaven you are the Fortune of Heaven, and on earth you are the Fortune of Mortals.
In Vaikuṇṭha you are Mahālakṣmī, in every mouth you are Sarasvatī;
you are Gaṅgā, you are Tulasī, you are Prabhā, and you are Pārvatī.
You are Sāvitrī, you are Māṇikī, and you are Padmā; you are Padminī and Satī; you are Mañjulā and Bhārgavī, and you are Kambharā, the virtuous Manasā.
You are Vṛndā, Haṃsā, and Rādhā; you are the sovereign Mūlaprakṛti.
You are the beloved of Kṛṣṇa at Bhāṇḍīra, and Candrā in the sandalwood forest.
Virajā was in a grove of campaka trees on Mount Śataśṛṅga, Sundarī in a lotus grove, Padmāvatī in a grove of lotuses, and Mālatī in a grove of mālatī flowers. (58)
You are Kundadantī in the Kunda grove, Suśīlā in the Ketakī grove, and you are Durgā as Kadambamālā in the forest of Kadamba trees. (59)
Royal fortune dwells in the royal palace, and domestic fortune in every home;
be gracious, O Mother of the worlds, O Lotus-born One, do not go to death.
Having heard this hymn of praise to the gods and having ceased her weeping, Satī spoke to them with great composure;
they too listened with reverence.
I do not renounce my body now out of anger, nor out of detachment;
rather, it is because I have reflected upon what exists after death.
In that Great Lord, who is all-pervading, equal toward all, devoid of qualities,
the Self of all, and eternally blissful, there is equality between a blade of grass and a mountain.
How can there be any purpose in serving him, for whom there is equality between a female servant and Lakṣmī, who is capable of creating a hundred thousand Lakṣmīs by the mere play of a frown?
I am the chief among his wives, yet now I have been cast out by the doorkeeper;
I am no longer desired even by the full retinue of his servants' servants.
"O mistress, being thus unfortunate, I shall give up my life;
having made this resolve regarding the fire, may all go well. (66)
That woman who is ill-fated toward her husband is indeed ill-fated in every respect;
for her there is no happiness in bed or at the meal, and her life is in vain. (67)
The birth of one who has no affection for her beloved is meaningless;
is that [affection] found in a son, wealth, beauty, prosperity, or even youth? (68)
She who has no devotion for her beloved, the supreme one who is dearer than all else, is impure, devoid of dharma, and abandoned by all auspicious actions. 69.
He is the kinsman, the refuge, the sustainer, the deity, and indeed the preceptor;
he is the master superior to all, for there is no preceptor superior to the master.
O gods, for foolish women, even their father, mother, son, or brother are distressed when asked to give this wealth; indeed, it is only the husband who is the giver of all their possessions. (71)
But only a certain great virtuous woman knows her husband as her lord; for she is born of a most noble lineage, possessed of excellent character, and a protector of the family.
Vows, propitiation, charity, truth, merit, and long-standing austerity—all become reduced to ashes and rendered useless for a woman devoid of devotion to her husband. (73)
Therefore, I shall say nothing harsh to my husband, the lord;
yet, due to the offenses of his servants, I shall certainly give up my life. (74)
If a great chaste wife speaks unharshly to her husband regarding his faults,
yet is unable to endure them, she may lawfully give up her life.
Service to the husband is the vow of women; service to the husband is the supreme austerity; service to the husband is the highest duty; service to the husband is the worship of the gods. (76)
Service to the husband is the supreme truth; the chanting of the names of gifts and sacred fords is likewise.
The master embodies all the gods; the master is pure and embodies all the gods. (77)
Janārdana, who is the embodiment of all merit, appears in the form of a husband;
she who always eats the remnants of her husband's meal and drinks the water from his feet is a *satī*. (78)
The deities always desire the sight and the touch of her;
therefore, all sacred fords purify even sinners from their evil. (79)
Having spoken thus, that great virtuous woman wept indeed again and again;
and Brahmā, filled with fear, spoke with his neck bowed in devotion.
There will be no good fortune for Jaya, the gatekeeper;
even Vijaya shall become an accomplice in your act of transgression. (81)
Out of fear of offending your beloved, you did not curse those two fools;
yet they shall become Rākṣasas because of their reviling of Sanaka and the others.
If a most virtuous man does not curse one who has committed an offense out of forbearance, his total destruction will surely come to pass; do not delay, O noble lady! (83)
If one is unable to curse and not empowered to inflict punishment,
then indeed Dharma inflicts punishment upon the offending person.
"Forgive everything, O Mother; go, go to the beloved end-maker!
And appoint me, your devotee, to the task of creation. (85)
Having spoken thus and placing her at the forefront, he went quickly together with the gods and the lords of sages to the presence of Nārāyaṇa in order to offer praise. 86.
O Blessed One, bestower of happiness upon the gods of gods and others alike, you who grant the perfection of enjoyments, accept this virtuous Kamalā. (87)
By which we all have become prosperous, and without which we would be like mere stones—what more is there to be praised? Accept her for the sake of the world. (88)
Having heard the praise of Brahmā and seeing Lakṣmī standing before him, weeping with her face bowed down, he spoke to the lotus-born one:
"I know all; I am the omniscient one, the soul of all, and the protector of all.
I am the teacher of all and the giver of the fruits of all actions, O lotus-born one. My equanimity is equal toward devotees, wives, kinsmen, and everywhere else."
Especially devoted to me, he is indeed superior even to his wife. Your two sons, who are my devotees and gatekeepers, are formidable;
forgive my offense and that of those two who are full of devotion.
Filled with devotion to me, the powerful one does not fear the Daityas;
protected by my discus, he is intoxicated by the honey-wine of devotion.
However, because of your hymn of praise, I must come to you, O Creator.
Even for my two powerful sons, Pradīpa and Pradāsana, rebirth is inevitable for the sake of singing the praises of the virtues of Jaya and Vijaya;
therefore, I have indeed created this occasion. || 94–95 ||

Then, after some time, due to the anger of Sanaka and the others, it shall come to pass. Listen to another [account]: on this earth, in the region of Ānarta near the ocean, in the city of Camatkārapura, there was a Brahmin named Śāṇḍilya.

Desirous of me, he performed penance together with his wife for the sake of a daughter. At the end of a thousand years, I appeared before him with a gracious countenance and spoke to him in order to grant a boon.
His wife chose for him a daughter equal to Lakṣmī and endowed with virtues; "So be it," I said, and then I went to my dissolution.
Śāṇḍilya, joined by his beloved, awaits the arrival of that daughter.
"In this matter, I have created this very sign by means of Lakṣmī.
Let her, endowed with the form of Lakṣmī, go there in the guise of a shadow.
I never desire even the slightest fault in Lakṣmī regarding her devotion to her husband."
Indeed, let this body of Lakṣmī, which is subject to defects and is merely of the nature of a shadow, go into the wife of Śāṇḍilya for the sake of granting a boon as a daughter. 10.2.
When all the gods were addressed thus, they were filled with wonder at Lakṣmī;
indeed, no one truly knows the heart of Nārāyaṇa.
Then, having heard that, Śāntā and Lakṣmī became delighted;
by her husband’s command, Mādhavī quickly departed in the form of a shadow.
This daughter of Śāṇḍilya is known as Mādhavī;
there, Śrī Hari took hold of Lakṣmī with his divine form.
And Mādhavī, devoted to celibacy, desires me alone as her husband, who am like unto herself—the Lord of Lakṣmī; she does not desire any other husband.
O Garuḍa, you do not know this story at all because of your illusory power;
bring that Mādhavī, my devoted wife, here to my presence.
"She is a portion of Lakṣmī, the very embodiment of honor, the daughter of a sage, and my beloved;
having seen her myself later, I shall do what is appropriate. (108)
Thus addressed, Garuḍa brought her into his presence;
then the Brahmin, having bowed to that eternal Lord, spoke.
"O Blessed One, accept this maiden; she has always desired only you.
O Blessed One, please come," he said to her as they all listened attentively.
A maiden with a serene mind, like Lakṣmī, entered his side;
she took her place on a single bed at the right side of the Enemy of Mura.
Then Lakṣmī, her limbs overcome with anger and adopting the behavior of a queen, spoke to that girl, considering her to be a rival wife. || 112 ||
"O sinful woman, since you have cast shame far away and, full of joy, have mounted my beloved's bed right before me. (11.3)
"Therefore, you must surely be a deformed old woman.
Upon hearing this, the maiden and her father were both overcome with grief.
Viṣṇu Hari himself said: "Do not think thus; you shall become Lakṣmī.
To me, one who is mature in knowledge and whose countenance reflects that maturity is considered a true elder, for she increases one's wisdom."
Devoted to the knowledge of Brahman, she shall be the Madhu-vidyā as well as the Mādhavī;
presiding over the Śāṇḍilya-vidyā, she will become one whose wisdom has increased.
Having spoken thus, she became Śāṇḍilī; that Mādhavī, the beloved of Hari, now exists eternally in the Ocean of Milk as the fortunate Lakṣmī.
Devoted to the life of celibacy and dedicated to the service of Nārāyaṇa,
Śāṇḍilya, having given away his daughter, felt that he had fulfilled his purpose.
There, Garuḍa, filled with doubt, questioned Śrī Hari:
"Indeed, the celibacy of women is truly a subject of uncertainty."
Especially when she has reached the stage of youth, I do not believe it; for one who is certainly in the prime of youth and yet born of an animal womb— || 1.492.120 ||
"Youth must indeed be transformed; it is not for the sake of remaining untransformed.
Having heard these words of his, the female student Śāṇḍilī—
At that very moment, due to the censure of the virtuous woman by the lord of birds, the chaste Vaiṣṇavī, observing a vow of silence, said nothing at all.
Both his sides having met with destruction, he then became a mere torso;
likewise, he was unable to move even a single step anywhere.
Hari said: "O Garuḍa, your two wings have indeed perished because of censure;
for your celibacy was defiled by doubt regarding Śāṇḍilī."
"Therefore, having bowed to Śāṇḍilī, propitiate her and be happy.
Garuḍa praised her and bowed down to her again and again. (125)
Being pleased, Śāṇḍilī touched the twice-born man with her hand;
thereupon, his two wings were produced and joined together at that very moment.
Garuḍa prostrated before Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī Śāṇḍilī, as well as the local inhabitants and the Brāhmaṇa Śāṇḍilya.
Placing him upon his back, he went to the auspicious field of Camatkārapura;
having set that brahmin down there, Garuḍa departed for heaven.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have narrated to you this account of Lakṣmī’s former life, which is devoted to the virtue of devotion to her husband and which destroys both sin and suffering. (129)
Whoever should hear this, or cause it to be read, or likewise cause it to be heard,
shall obtain enjoyment and liberation in that abode, as well as the very rare devotion of service.

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-second chapter, titled "The Description of Mādhavī, the Daughter of a Brāhmaṇa from Camatkārapurī, Becoming the Wife of the Lord; Her Being Śāṇḍilī as an Incarnation of Lakṣmī; the Falling of Garuḍa’s Wings due to Doubt Concerning the Vow of Celibacy for Women; the Restoration of His Wings through the Grace of Śāṇḍilī; and the Humiliation of the Lord by Lakṣmī for the Purpose of Her Descent," in the first section on the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. ||492||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, Lakṣmī, both Śāṇḍilī and Kamalā were indeed in the Ocean of Milk;
they performed service for me, Nārāyaṇa, by massaging my feet.
Dakṣa was held by Lakṣmī at my right foot, while Vāmaka was supported by Śāṇḍilī at my left;
then Lakṣmī spoke to Śāṇḍilī regarding her own left foot.
"Give me your left foot; it is the supreme treasure for a servant.
It is beautiful, a lovely-limbed woman, radiant on its left side, and a source of dear enjoyment. (3)
"Take my right foot, for that which is my left side belongs to you;
for a woman's nature is to be on the left, while for a man it consists of half the body."
"In the same way, the good fortune of one who conducts herself thus increases incessantly.
Śāṇḍilī said: "I will not give [him], for Dakṣa was previously taken by you. (5)
"How can you, who are self-supported, abandon the assembly of Dakṣa?
I must perform service to Śiva; I will not give you away under any circumstances."
Lakṣmī became enraged and cursed her, saying, "Become horse-faced! Śāṇḍilya also cursed Lakṣmī, saying, "You shall indeed become elephant-faced! (7)
For both of them were born in such a manner in the Ocean of Milk in the presence of Viṣṇu;
the Blessed One fell into grief, saying, "O dear one, how has this been done?"
Thus, they both incurred curses against one another that were improper and extremely difficult to overcome;
then, being distressed, they spoke to Viṣṇu, who reclines upon Śeṣa.
"O Blessed One, act in such a way that there may be liberation from the curse for both of us.
Then Nārāyaṇa said, "He was indeed born by my will alone."
By my will, there shall also be the release from that curse;
I shall go to the surface of the earth for the sake of destroying the burden of the world.
In that regard, this Śāṇḍilī shall indeed become my sister;
you, Lakṣmī, shall become horse-faced, and she shall become elephant-faced.
There I shall become the Lord Hari, the son of Devakī;
and she who is the other beloved wife of Vasudeva, named Suprabhā— || 13 ||
From her was born Mādhavī, who was Śāṇḍilī with the form of a horse's face.
Seeing that daughter born with such a deformed appearance, Jaśasvinī (Suśobhanā) was filled with grief.
Accompanied by Vasudeva, she fell into the deepest despondency;
yet that daughter, endowed with youth and possessed of such a countenance, was born. (15)
Seeing her horse-faced form, no one chose her as a bride;
then the Blessed Kṛṣṇa [set out] toward Camatkārapura.
He sent her away to perform asceticism;
then, having performed that penance, Brahmā became pleased and spoke to her for the sake of granting a boon.
She chose the face of a woman—one that was auspicious, gentle, and beautiful;
Brahmā said, "So be it," and she indeed became one with a lovely countenance.
The daughter of Pāṇḍu, the son of Pṛthā who followed Kṛṣṇa, married her who was renowned by the name Subhadrā—a mother of heroes and beloved of her husband. 1.9.
To her was born a heroic son who is known as Abhimanyu;
at the end of time, that devoted wife indeed returned to the abode of Hari.
Then Lakṣmī, in the form of an elephant-faced goddess, went to the Ānarta country;
she performed penance at that excellent sacred field known as Hāṭakeśvara.
She indeed gratified Brahmā with her rigorous asceticism;
then, at the end of a year, Brahmā, having attained satisfaction, spoke to her.
"Choose a boon, O Goddess of gods, whatever resides in your mind.
Lakṣmī said: "O Lord, I choose that my face be turned toward the east. (23)
Brahmā said, "So be it; may you become Mahālakṣmī. Having thus received the boon, she of the auspicious countenance departed.
Mahālakṣmī, who is of beautiful form, [dwells] toward the one who reclines upon the Ocean of Milk;
thus is she Mādhavī, and Mahālakṣmī the Sovereign as well. 25.
Once the sacred field of Nagara has been established, Candrabhāryā will, with devotion and true faith, worship Mahālakṣmī and Mādhavī with great respect.
She shall become endowed with good fortune and possessed of sons;
for as long as one year, she shall subsist on eating only a single meal a day.
That woman who worships me while abstaining from pungent food and salt shall experience neither the suffering arising from her husband nor misfortune. (28)
However, all incomparable good fortune will be perfectly realized;
wealth, grain, gold, palatial mansions, and cattle shall be obtained. (29)
Having become pure, a man or a woman who recites this with devotion, causes it to be read, causes it to be heard, or listens to it, shall attain great good fortune. (1.493.30)

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-third chapter, titled "The Description of how Aśvamukhī Mādhavī and Gajamukhī Lakṣmī later became Subhadrā and Mahālakṣmī," in the first section, the Kṛtayuga-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Now, O Lakṣmī, listen to another divine narrative concerning the land of Hāṭakeśvara— a tale full of wonders and endowed with the vow of Brahman.
There was a king named Camatkāra, who founded the city of Camatkārapura on the bank of the river Nāgavatī, which was adorned by his very name.
For the protection of that city, deities were created by him;
established according to the prescribed rite, those auspicious ones protect its inhabitants.
Then that monarch had a daughter named Ambā, and another daughter named Vṛddhā; both of them were adorned with virtues.
The King of Kāśī married both of them in the presence of Brahmins and the sacred fire. Then, after some time, [the kingdom was attacked] by the Yavanas stationed in the north.
A great battle took place and the King of Kāśī met his death;
then Ambā, as well, being old, was reduced to the sorrow-inducing state of widowhood.
They went to their father’s house located in the land of Hāṭakeśvara,
where for a hundred years they performed supreme and rigorous penance.
They performed the daily worship of Durgā preceded by fire-offerings for the sake of destroying their husband's enemies; however, Durgā was not pleased.
Then, having attained detachment, they desired the destruction of their own bodies through Atharvan mantras originating from the Kṣurikā-sūkta, recited by brahmins.
Having repeatedly cut their own flesh, purified by mantras and offered with devotion,
they performed a fire sacrifice in a well-kindled flame.
Then, from that fire-pit, a woman with a beautiful face emerged, four cubits in height,
clad in white garments, and radiant like the rising sun.
Likewise, another [form] emerged from that pit— eight-eyed and eight-faced, resembling molten gold,
holding a sword, and terrifying.
There was yet another such power, most terrible;
they then spoke for the sake of a boon to the beloved of the King of Kāśī.
And they both said: "Our lord, the King of Kāśī, has indeed been slain in battle by the Yavanas; therefore, we choose their destruction. (14)
"So be it," they said, granting the boon; then, from the sacrificial pit, thousands of Mothers emerged, beyond counting and possessing manifold forms. (15)
There, one had the face of an elephant, another likewise the face of a horse;
another had the face of a dog, and yet another the face of the king of birds.
Others had the forms and bodies of animals, while others possessed human faces; some had three heads, some five heads, and others likewise had seven heads.

Some had faces on their shanks, some on their hips, some on their chests, and some were faceless; some had faces on their sides, some on their backs, some on their hindquarters, and some even on their tails.
Some had one hand, some two hands, some ten hands, and some were handless;
others had twenty hands, some had many feet, and some were footless.

Some have one foot, some have their feet turned upward; some have one eye, some have two eyes; some have many eyes; some are mounted on elephants, some are mounted on horses, and some are seated upon bulls.
They are seated upon men, monkeys, lions, goats, donkeys, and tigers;
they are seated upon snakes, lizards, mice, sea-monsters, tortoises, and cocks. ||21||
Mounted upon birds and other creatures, they dance, adorned with laughter; many have their hair standing erect, some have disheveled hair, and others have hair covering their limbs.
Some had long hair, some hair like that of a horse, and others had short teeth;
there were those with prominent teeth, those with long teeth, and those with elephant-like tusks—truly terrifying to behold.

Those with iron teeth, those with long ears, those with deformed ears, those with ears like winnowing baskets, those with spike-like ears, those with bad ears, those with many ears, and those with beautiful ears; ||24||
Some were clad in skins, some were naked, and others were clothed in hair;
they held swords in their hands, spears in their hands, and carried arrows, nooses, and bows. ||25||
Adorned with spears, mallets, bhūśuṇḍis, prāsas, and tomara-shafts,
they indeed set forth for the destruction of the Yavana clans.
The kingdom of those evil-minded ones, filled with children and the elderly,
along with their women, was devoured by those goddesses.
Having thus driven them out from that kingdom, they returned once again.
They call it Camatkārapura, the destroyer of the Yavanas. ||28||
Honored and established by those two widows, they then said:
"Give us food and also lodging. (29)
Then the Great Queen gave them clothing and food, saying:
"Those women in this mortal world who sleep while pregnant... (1.494.30)
At the time of twilight and at dawn, they become attached to sensual desires and do not perform their ablutions; may you receive that as food for your womb. 3.1.
Those who go forth weeping through the crossroads and the forests—let their embryos, which have been bestowed upon you, be enjoyed by you. (32)
Those [worms] which crawl about in a state of impurity, and which sport and sleep—indeed, the embryos of all of you are for your very food. (33)
That boy for whom the sixth-night vigil shall not be performed will become food for you; of this there is no doubt. (34)
Or, wherever he does not go to the fire in the lying-in chamber, he shall become food for you, assuming the form of a child. (35)
The child who resides in that lying-in chamber, which is entirely devoid of auspicious things—that one has been assigned to you. (36)
Those children who sleep during the twilight hours while situated in the open air—all of them have been offered to you for the sake of food. (37)
If on the arrival of one's birthday, no auspicious rite is performed at the end of the year, that body of yours has been assigned to him. (38)
The man who, having performed an oil massage, does not bathe—he has been given to you for the purpose of food; there is no doubt about this. (39)
Any man who stands defiled by food remnants, or one who stands in the middle of a crossroads,
should be devoured by all of you with an unwavering mind.
Any man who, deluded by lust, approaches a woman during her menses, or sleeps naked, or bathes [while naked], is, in your opinion, fit to be eaten. 41.
At midnight, he lies down facing south while consuming curd;
a man who reviles you should especially be eaten [by him]. (42)
Thus, the abodes and the food offerings for the cruel goddesses were provided in their house; consequently, they attained satisfaction. (43)
And they protect the city and the sacred field of Śrī Hāṭakeśvara. Then, by his father Camatkāra, the king of the subjects— ||44||
A beautiful and spacious temple was constructed on the bank of the river;
by a kick of her foot, Ambā turned the ground into a cave-like space.
When his own sandals had been placed there by the aged mother,
the princess herself established them in that cave with her own hand.
Then Ambā spoke to all the goddesses who were endowed with humility:
"These divine sandals of mine shall always remain within the cave. (47)
To be used by everyone and never to be taken outside anywhere—whosoever shall go out while wearing these sandals out of delusion, [she shall suffer]. (48)
Released from her divine state, she will become a female jackal;
people who are practitioners of yoga shall come here and perform worship of the two sandals. (49)
They will joyfully offer oblations to you in that manner;
and those who give these shall attain a perfection that is very difficult to obtain.
Then all those goddesses, stationed within the cave,
surrounded those two sandals that grant liberation within that temple.
O auspicious one, whether they be women or men, by worshipping them from afar and bowing down to those goddesses,
they shall attain their desired wishes.
In the past, they were meditated upon by Śambhu from his third eye, and thus they shall attain supreme perfection, free from birth and death. 53.
Indeed, a radiant maiden clad in white garments was revealed;
she was made to be constantly devoted to the worship of the sandals established by Ambā. (54)
But the Mother said to that girl: "The lineage of your disciples consists of maidens who, having been initiated, are of the very nature of goddesses and are not merely human. (55)
The worshipper of these two should be devoted to lifelong celibacy from childhood;
then he gave him a gem-encrusted staff, two fly-whisks, and a radiant parasol.
The virtuous woman gave him the mantra, the ritual for worship, a garment, and a neck-thread;
she who received the mantra was the maiden Paramparā.
Indeed, all those born of the maiden lineage shall become [accomplished] through the mantra:
Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, obeisance to Ambā Nārāyaṇī, Svāhā Om. (58)
With this mantra, the lineage of the maiden is indeed declared;
[the rite is performed] with the hand of the maiden born of that lineage. (59)
Indeed, the man or woman who performs the worship of the sandals,
as well as the one who performs the worship of the maiden, shall be endowed with supreme happiness.

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of King Camatkāra’s Worship of Ambā-Vṛddhā’s Sandals through the Austerities of His Daughters Ambā and Vṛddhā, and How the Kumārikā Lineage Itself Perpetuates This," in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, I shall narrate the sin-destroying story that originated at Agnitīrtha in Camatkārapura in ancient times.
In the Lunar dynasty there was a powerful king named Pratīpa.
He had two sons: the elder was Devāpi, and after him came Śantanu.
The king met his death, and Devāpi departed for ascetic penance;
Śaṃtanu was then swiftly installed in the kingdom by the subjects. || 3 ||
When such a transgression had occurred, Śakra did not rain at all;
consequently, the entire world fell into distress, being tormented by hunger.
In other worlds, women have been abandoned by their husbands, sons by their own fathers, and likewise mothers by their sons; what need is there to speak of others?
Thus, humans and other beings born after three years die;
yet, by the power of destiny, if it is sometimes seen that someone [survives] for some time, [it is due to past merit].
The grain, whether harvested or unharvested, is carried off by powerful enemies;
all the trees have become withered, as have the rivers and reservoirs.
At that time, all people were devoid of wealth, sacrifices were abandoned, and men and women became extreme atheists, lacking both vows and righteousness.
All the sages were afflicted by hunger, especially so;
in the meantime, in that forest, the great sage Viśvāmitra—
With his entire body reduced to skin and bone, afflicted by hunger,
he wandered here and there until he reached a certain village that was devoid of water.
It was filled on all sides with the remains of dead mortals, reduced to mere skeletons;
it was the abode of that flesh-eater amidst the corpses of the deceased.
The house of the Caṇḍāla was indeed enveloped in a foul stench;
there he saw a dog that was dead, withered, and long deceased.
Then, devoted to the duty for times of distress, he took it up,
struck it dry with a staff, and cut it into pieces.
Having led them to a place where water and wood were available,
he washed them in the water and cooked them in the fire.
As soon as he had taken [the offerings], offered libations to the ancestors, and was about to offer them into the fire, the Fire-god vanished from sight out of fear of impurity. || 15 ||
Having directed his anger everywhere upon the earth, in the fire-sanctuary, at the place of sacrifice, in his own mind, and especially toward Śakra. || 16 ||
Then, because the fire had vanished and the oblation was lost, the offering to the gods was suspended;
consequently, the gods, led by the celestial sages, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu, were obstructed. (17)
They wandered over the surface of the earth in search of fire.
Then, having seen an elephant in a forest on the Himalayas, they questioned him.
"If you have seen the Fire, the consumer of oblations, here, then tell us.
The Elephant replied, "He is moving about right here in this dense thicket of bamboo."
"Having entered while remaining hidden, I was burned by him;
having said this, they went to where the fire was located."
Then Agni cursed that elephant who had carried out his command:
"Since you have reported my secret, your tongue shall always [be cut off]. (21)
Having said, "Let it indeed be otherwise," she emerged from the pillar;
she was not seen by the gods within the pillar, for they remained clinging to its back, desiring to see her.
Then the parrot was seen by the gods wandering on the Himalayas;
they asked him, "O parrot, if you have seen the fire here, tell us."
The parrot said: "My nest is here on this sacrificial peg;
my young ones are there as well, and the fire has arrived at that spot. (24)
We were all burnt by him and have only with great difficulty emerged;
there the fire remains in a concealed form—let them recognize it.
Thus addressed, the Fire-god then became enraged and cursed Śuka:
"O bird, because I have been revealed by you to the gods... (26)
"Therefore, O Śuka, your speech shall not be clear.
Having thus cursed Śuka, the Fire-god was sought out by the gods. ||27||
Then, having rendered himself invisible, he went to another land;
reaching the holy site of Puṣkara, he remained at the bottom in the midst of the water. (28)
Having perceived this through their meditative concentration, the gods, filled with eagerness, questioned the fish: "O Fish, tell us, where has Vahni come to and where does he abide? 29.
The fish said: "He indeed dwells beneath this lotus;
we have been scorched by him and stand upon the shore, truly in great distress."
To the fish who had spoken thus, the enraged Anala uttered this curse:
"May these fish, which devour their own kin, become eaters of all things."
Having thus uttered the curse, he fled from that place with great speed;
reaching Aśvapaṭṭasara, Anala settled in Saurāṣṭra.
Having perceived this through the activity of meditation, the Suras went to Kuṅkumavāpikā and questioned the tortoise who had come out and was situated on the shore of the lake. ||33||
"If you say this, O tortoise, he replied, 'Fire has entered here into the depths of this water; having come, it has burned us who have emerged outside. (34)
While the gods were filled with longing to see him there, Anala then cursed the tortoise: "Your lineage shall never attain growth."
Having thus uttered the curse, he then departed from that place with the desire to see the God,
and went to the river of the Nāgas in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara.
Having entered a very deep reservoir of water and taken refuge there, the fish and frogs were burned by the entry of fire. (37)
Having emerged onto the shore, the gods went to Dardura and asked him whether Agni was indeed present there or not.
The frog said: "A fire has arrived here in this deep water;
by it, many leeches dwelling in the midst of the water have indeed been burned. (39)
"Having emerged with great difficulty, I live by taking refuge in the gods.
Hearing that, the gods eagerly searched for him in the water.
The Fire-god cursed that frog because he had been offered to the gods; therefore, become deficient and tongueless here upon the surface of the earth. 41.
Having spoken thus, as soon as fire emerged from that place, Brahmā said to him: "O Fire, remain steady!"
Why do you flee, concealing yourself from the gods upon every spot you see?
For you are the primordial one and stand as the very mouth of all the gods. 43.
An oblation properly offered into you reaches the sun;
from the sun rain is born, from rain comes food, and from that, living beings.
Therefore, you alone are considered the creator and the ordainer of the worlds;
when you are satisfied, the universe is sustained, and when you are angry, it perishes.
All sacrifices, all essences, and all cooked offerings abide in you;
O inner mover, it is by taking refuge in you that living beings live. 46.
"Tell me, why are you born in concealment? Be a bestower of happiness.
Having heard this, Agni said to Aja: "Listen to the reason for my concealment. (47)
Due to a drought caused by Mahendra, there occurred a depletion of medicinal herbs;
consequently, I was joined with flesh by Viśvāmitra. (48)
"Fearing the consumption of forbidden food, I remain hidden; it is not otherwise.
Having heard this, Brahmā said to the Lord of Gods: "For what reason do you not rain? (49)
Indra, setting aside his elder brother Devāpi, made the younger-born Śaṃtanu, the lord of the earth, the protector of subjects. ||1.495.50||
"I do not rain because of that sin, due to the transgression of the proper order";
Brahmā said, "For that sin has already been experienced by Śantanu."
All premature deaths and other deaths caused by famine occurred;
Śantanu remained hungry, for he had indeed consumed that which was sinful.
"O Mahendra, by my command, bring forth rain for the sake of the subjects.
Thus addressed, he commanded the Puṣkarāvarta clouds. (53)
The great clouds rained down and filled the watery expanse;
then Brahmā spoke to Agni: "O Purifier, become manifest! (54)
"In the Agnihotra sacrifices, in the rites of the Brahmins, and in the oblations—choose a boon as you desire; I grant it to you out of a wish for your welfare. (55)
Wherever your presence is concealed, each such place shall become a sacred ford (tīrtha) identical with yourself;
and the well-known Vahni-tīrtha shall likewise become a purifying source of spiritual power.
And Vahni said: "O Blessed One, for three years I have not obtained food anywhere; therefore, grant me food. (57)
Brahmā, having summoned the Brahmins,
joyfully offered a stream of clarified butter by means of the Vasordhārā rite for the very purpose of satisfying the Fire-god.
"Let them satisfy the fire," he said,
and they did so accordingly by offering the stream of wealth (vasordhārā) for the duration of an entire year.
Then, having attained supreme satisfaction, the fire reached a state of supreme nourishment,
because it became completely full through the stream of the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
Having thus manifested the fire, brought about rain, and performed the sacrifice, the deities beginning with Brahmā went to heaven; thereafter, Gaja and the others [departed].
Having seen the fire kindled in the wild hermitages of the sages,
they went to the refuge of the Purifier and prayed to the Lord.
"Wherever the fire appeared and by whomsoever it was beheld, the elephants and others declared it to be fire; O Lord, ward off this curse! (63)
The Fire-god said to the lordly elephant: "Indeed, let your tongue be capable of performing its function;
you shall have the form of a king's vehicle and you shall eat sweet food. (64)
And he said to the parrot, "May your tongue indeed be a praiser of kings! And he said to the frog, "May your tongue be a giver of indications of rain! (65)
And Matsya said to him: "May your lineage increase by one hundred and one in each generation, and may it reach a thousand in every single birth."
He said to the tortoise, "May your life-span be firm for more than a hundred years;
and may the Lord Śrī Hari himself be born in your lineage. (67)
Having taken birth by the force of his purpose, he will deliver those born of his lineage;
the Lord Śrī Hari himself became manifest as the Fish and the Tortoise. 68.
Gaṇeśa indeed had the face of an elephant, and Lakṣmī likewise had the face of an elephant;
they were both born in the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, while Śuka was the son of Vyāsa.
King Dardura was born as Hari, who could assume any form at will;
through him, the world in the city of the gods in Saurāṣṭra became truly Vaiṣṇava.
That king of Devanagara was indeed a supreme devotee of Viṣṇu;
and once Jājali went to the holy site of Someśvara.
Then, having established the Raivata holy site, he went to Dvāravatī;
from there, he proceeded to Camatkārapura on the bank of the Nāganadī river.
He fell asleep due to a defect in his sleep, and his semen was discharged;
rising up, he washed his loincloth in the water.
The female frog quickly swallowed him in the form of food;
while she was being tormented on the bank, a son was born to her. (74)
Having arrived, she met her death and was indeed held by the washerman;
moreover, the region of her belly had become torn open. (75)
There, having seen that beautiful boy and taking hold of his son while he was breathing,
the fisherman gave him, who was like the sun, to the excellent king.
By that miracle, the King of Gūrjara was raised up by the monarch;
he became a great devotee of Viṣṇu, a Vaiṣṇava who possessed the very form of Viṣṇu. ||77||
In whose kingdom all human beings and others were indeed Vaiṣṇavas;
[there was] the city of Darduraka on the shore of the ocean by Dardura.
A vast capital city was established, consisting of illusion, equal to heaven, and filled with prosperity in the southern region. ||79||
Then he gave a second boon to the frog:
"May your species live for a long time, and may you be ever renewed."
Indeed, every year a new body arises from its previous existence;
therefore, in the rainy season, he is born as a frog once again. (81)
Thus everything regarding the power residing in the fire has been told;
and Viśvāmitra [saw] that fire extinguished in an instant.
He cast away that impure dog-meat;
meanwhile, the great multitude there observed a fast.
Having dug into the earth and taken rice that had been stored in an underground cellar for three years,
he went by chance and gave it to that great seer.

Having bathed and attained supreme purity, and having performed the fire-oblation (homa) within the ether of consciousness (cidambara), he partook of the food provided by destiny while [the Lord] Kṛṣṇa, whose body is the void (ākāśavapuḥ), looked on. ||85||
Then, having completed his journey, he departed specifically for the sake of visiting sacred fords (tīrthas);
from hearing or reciting this [account], the burning away of sins occurs. ||86||
There shall be faith in the Dharma, and there shall be clarity within the fire;
having become a purifying mind, O beloved, it shall become fit for devotion. (87)

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Curse and Grace of Agni upon the Elephant, Parrot, Lotus, Fish, Tortoise, and Frog, Sent as Messengers by the Gods who were Searching for Him after He was Afraid of the Fault Arising from Contact with the Flesh Offered by Viśvāmitra during the Rainless Period Following the Coronation of the Younger Brother to the Exclusion of the Eldest, in the First Section on the Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā."
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī; there was once a great and illustrious king named Ajāpāla in the region of Sāketa, who reflected upon this again and again.
I must perform that deed which has not been done by other rulers here, nor will those who come after me ever do it. (2)
The constant protection of the subjects is indeed not possible without the collection of taxes;
through the collection of taxes, the maintenance of the army and other forces certainly comes to be. (3)
The collection of taxes causes agitation in the mind of the kingdom;
therefore, without me, [the king] shall protect his own realm through the power of austerity along with his army.
Reflecting thus on what must be protected, he spoke to Vasiṣṭha:
"I must perform ascetic penance out of a desire for the welfare of my subjects."
"O treasure-house of compassion, show me such a supreme sacred field.
Vasiṣṭha replied: "In Saurāṣṭra is the sacred field of Śrī Hāṭakeśvara."
O King, that place exists which swiftly bestows the attainment of the fruits of austerity;
become devoted to celibacy, pure, and intent upon your vows.
"Worship Pārvatī; she will quickly become pleased.
Having been told this, he went there and worshipped Pārvatī. || 8 ||
Pleased by his propitiation, the Mother said to that best of kings:
"Speak that which is in your heart, so that I may accomplish it all for you."
The king said: "For the sake of protecting my subjects, grant me weapons, the corresponding mantras, and indeed divine missiles that travel through the sky."
Those who know the offenses of all living beings—such as adultery, theft, and so forth—just like human beings, [are the judges]. (11)
Having gone there, those very [messengers] stationed by my side shall punish the offender and then return to my side, each to their respective place.
Likewise, grant us a collection of mantras for the suppression of diseases, so that the subjects may be free from illness, nourished, happy, and fearless. (13)
"An army of elephants and horses that sustains itself on my nails is not what I desire," Pārvatī said to the king of kings, "for your task is indeed difficult. (14)
Nevertheless, I shall bestow upon you weapons endowed with knowledge and a corresponding collection of mantras, which will follow as the fruit of your asceticism. (15)
All diseases on the surface of the earth shall become subject to your praise;
when you go to heaven, you must indeed place them within the water.
"These must never be given to anyone else," having said this, the goddess bestowed the mantras for the divine missiles and weapons. (17)
And he [taught] all the spells for diseases as requested by the king,
by which diseases are seized and likewise released at will.
Diseases that come within the range of his vision are easily kept at bay;
thus, by the grace of the Goddess, the king indeed obtains everything. 19.
He went to the city of Sāketa, gave gifts such as elephant-ichor,
dispersed his army, and likewise released taxes.
Even those very weapons serve to protect the subjects, by inflicting punishment according to the offense, whether openly or in secret. (21)
Even weapons that have not been seen bring about their effects at that very moment;
if even a hidden fault does not exist for anyone, how much less so an evident one? (22)
In this manner, everything within his own kingdom as well as in foreign kingdoms, and even in the realms of other monarchs, was secured in many ways through secret means. (23)
And when they committed offenses, he seized them with the Yamagraha;
and having diligently restrained all diseases by means of mantras, he [released them]. ||24||
Having personally assumed the form of a goat, he later protected them by taking up a staff;
when diseases were suppressed, the subjects attained supreme happiness. (25)
All hells have gradually become empty;
no man goes to hell, nor does any man tread the path of death. (26)
At that time, the subjects on earth were equal to the heavens and equal to truth.
Then, O virtuous lady, Vaivasvata went and petitioned Brahmā.
"O Brahmin, formerly I was appointed by you, out of a desire to observe dharma and adharma, for the sake of the restraint and favor of the worlds. (28)
O Lord of Creatures, King Ajāpāla rendered all that fruitless by propitiating the goddess Pārvatī through the power of his asceticism. (29)
Neither mental anxieties nor physical ailments prevail upon the surface of the earth; moreover, out of fear, the subjects commit neither sins nor offenses.
Thus has the true path of Dharma been established by that king;
let Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara obstruct it! (3.1)
Having heard this from Yamarāja, Brahmā remembered Śaṅkara and Viṣṇu; those two arrived, and the Creator of the Universe spoke to Śambhu.
"What should be done in this matter? Speak, O Śambhu; speak, O Lord!
Śambhu replied: "For one who is engaged in the true dharma and seeks auspicious results... (33)
How is he prevented there, and what is his punishment?
How long does his lifespan last? Tell me this, O Yama. (34)
Yama said: "By which means, when that time has arrived, shall I lead him to my own abode? His lifespan is sixty thousand years. || 35 ||
Five thousand years of his [reign] have now passed;
fifty-five thousand years remain for the future. (36)
Beholding that life-span to be so long, Śaṅkara assumed the form of a tiger and went into the presence of that king. (37)
Roaring repeatedly with a sound like the thundering of clouds, the goats, upon seeing him, fled in every direction. (38)
When they had all been devoured by the tiger,
that lord of the earth then discharged weapons empowered with mantras in order to slay the tiger.
Śaṅkara seized all those weapons, mantras,
and missiles with his own mouth, yet they did not come toward the king.
Due to the absence of weapons, he then quickly engaged in a duel;
at that moment, Śambhu became a three-eyed tiger, bearing a trident.
The king, immersed in bliss, praised Śaṅkara with joy:
"O Śambhu, you have been insulted by me out of ignorance; please grant me forgiveness. (42)
Śambhu said: "I have forgiven everything with complete satisfaction;
you have performed a great deed such as has never been done by others before."
"O best of kings, you have indeed performed superhuman protection for your subjects; therefore, go with me to Kailāsa."
Be happy together with this lawful wife of yours;
you must certainly not remain here in this world in opposition to Yama.
"You must not remain on the surface of the earth in opposition to the gods.
Thus addressed, that king said, "I shall do exactly as you have told me. (46)
Previously, the Goddess told me: "When you depart from the surface of the earth, then [you shall receive] all the missiles, weapons, and mantras. (47)
"O Śaṅkara, having given these to me and performed that [rite], you may depart.
Then Śambhu gave him those mantras for the weapons and missiles.
The king went to the sacred field of Camatkāra toward Śrī Pārvatī;
having offered everything to Pārvatī after placing it in the water and performing worship, he presented it. 49.
Having bathed in the Pārvatī-kuṇḍa on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha,
the king went to Sāketa, where Śambhu was waiting for him.
Having entrusted the kingdom to his son, the king departed for Kailāsa together with his wife and Śambhu; then Śambhu bestowed [the mountain] upon the monarch.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; obeisance!"—this mantra was bestowed, and a garland of tulasī was offered. (2)
Having become a supreme devotee of Viṣṇu, O Lakṣmī, he worshipped Śrī Hari along with his wife;
he departed for Goloka and became eternally liberated.
His son was King Daśaratha, who was exceedingly righteous;
by means of a celestial chariot (vimāna), he traveled to heaven and proceeded to the netherworlds (pātāla) and other realms.
He whose son was indeed Rāmacandra, Viṣṇu himself;
then, after some time had passed for that king, by the astrologers—
The planet Saturn will cause the destruction of Rohiṇī;
because of that, a famine will prevail for twelve years. ||56||
"In this way, the entire surface of the earth will become devoid of men.
Having heard this, the king went along that path where Śani was indeed located.
In the celestial chariot given by Śakra, he approached Śanaiścara;
having made his bow ready there, he spoke to Śanaiścara.
"Abandon this path of Rohiṇī, otherwise I shall kill you with a smooth-jointed arrow charged with the mantras of divine weapons. (59)
Having heard this, Śani said, "Who are you that blocks me in the sky?
The king replied, "I am a king; I am the son of Aja and the lord of the earth."
"Named Daśaratha, I have come here for the sake of protecting the subjects. Śani said, "I have no enmity toward you anywhere. (61)
"And how, O King, do you wish to destroy my path with a mere bow?
The king replied, "Slowly you proceed along the path of Rohiṇī. (62)
"For you shall indeed shatter the cart born of Rohiṇī;
when that has happened, there will be no new rain and no production of food. (63)
Because of that, there would be the destruction of progeny, the ruin of sacrifices, and the affliction of the gods;
therefore, having heard that the path of the stars was obstructed, Śani spoke to him.
"I am pleased with your valor, O King, for that which has never been accomplished by anyone else has indeed been achieved by you; choose a boon, and I shall grant it to you."
"Therefore, for the sake of the welfare of the subjects, I shall not cause Rohiṇī to be separated.
The King said, "On your day, whoever performs an oil massage [for me]," ||66||
For seven days, you must certainly not cause him any affliction whatsoever;
however, on that day, whoever performs the gift of sesame seeds and the gift of iron [shall be protected].
"You must not cause him any distress whatsoever for the duration of one year;
nor indeed should you cause distress to anyone within your range who performs rites of pacification."
"You must not cause affliction for seven and a half years";
"So be it," Śani replied, and the Lord of the Earth ceased speaking.
Having heard this, Mahendra quickly went to that place and said to the king, "I am pleased with your wonderful deed."
"Choose a boon from me today," the king said to him upon hearing this;
"O Mahendra, let there always be auspicious friendship between you and me. (71)
Indra said, "So be it; may there always be friendship between you and me.
O King, you must come to my abode every evening."
Having spoken thus, Indra departed; the king always goes to heaven.
Having heard the beautiful songs of the celestial nymphs in the assembly of Indra, [he remained there]. (73)
Having seen the dance accompanied by rhythmic beats and having heard the stories from the mouths of the celestial sages, he returns toward Ayodhyā every single day.
Immediately after he departs from the assembly hall of Śakra,
he always causes the sprinkling of water upon the chariot of Daśaratha.
Then one day, Nārada joyfully said to that king:
"O King, Indra indeed sprinkles you with water from his own mouth."
Then Daśaratha departed; having returned and settled upon his own seat, he rose up and looked toward his throne, which stood at a distance.
Then, by Indra's command, the servant sprinkled the seat with water;
seeing Mahendra there, the king asked him the reason for it.
Indra said: "O Lord, you have reached the limit [of my power] regarding the ancestors;
for one who is sonless, there is no goal, nor is there heaven beyond that. (79)
O King, when a man beholds the face of his son,
he thereafter attains freedom from debt toward his ancestors.
Having been addressed thus by Vasiṣṭha, that king, who was then deeply distressed on account of his son, returned home and performed a sacrifice for the sake of obtaining offspring.
Kausalyā, the eldest, gave birth to Rāma, a son who was like Nārāyaṇa;
Kaikeyī, the youngest, gave birth to her son Bharata.
Sumitrā gave birth to two sons in the middle, Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa,
and she also gave birth to one daughter, Lomapādā, who was a putrikā.
Indeed, the Savior (Tāriṇī) was given in the form of a daughter to one who was childless;
thus he attained freedom from debt and went to Vaikuṇṭha itself. ||84||
Then, after his residence in the forest, Rāma became king for ten thousand and one thousand years. ||85||
After the time of Sītā’s death, he ruled the kingdom;
at the end of eleven thousand years, a divine messenger arrived. (86)
The king of the gods said: "I have arrived, sent by him;
therefore, listen to his message and make your house uninhabited. (87)
"Afterwards I shall tell you," Rāma said upon hearing this;
"Lakṣmaṇa, make it private so that I may hear the messenger of the gods. (88)
While the conversation was still being carried on, others arrived;
thereupon, having observed the silence required for such discourse, the messenger of the gods spoke.
Just as a snake that has lost its fangs, or an elephant deprived of its rut,
so too a king who lacks authority is held in contempt by men.
Who are these who have gathered here even for this secret discourse, that you do not wish to hear even a whisper of suspicion in private? (91)
Having heard this, he then became deeply incensed and said to Lakṣmaṇa:
"Drive the others outside; do not let anyone else enter. (92)
If any man should come between us out of delusion, I shall slay him quickly with my own hand; of this there is no doubt. (93)
"I do not kill that which moves within my field of vision; at that time, there would be no transgression of the path of Dharma for me. Thus I declare: remain composed in this conduct.
Having said "Om," Lakṣmaṇa stood firm at the door of the palace;
the divine messenger also held counsel together with Rāma.
The destruction of Rāvaṇa has been accomplished, and Dharma has been established upon the earth;
his lifespan here has been brought to its full end, so it is pleasing that you go to Vaikuṇṭha.
In the meantime, Durvāsas arrived, overcome by hunger;
agitated, he said, "Where is Rāma? Inform me quickly! (97)
"Go quickly, Lakṣmaṇa; otherwise, I shall cast a curse upon you.
By that curse, I will surely consume the entire lineage; of this there is no doubt. (98)
Lakṣmaṇa, having shown humility, offered consolation to the great seer;
yet he, being unappeased, raised his hand to bestow a curse. (99)
Having heard that, Lakṣmaṇa quickly said to Rāma, "The sage has arrived.
Rāma replied, "Bring the sage Durvāsas in at once."
Then Lakṣmaṇa quickly ushered the sage inside,
and Rāma, taking the honey-mixture (madhuparka), went near him.
Having offered various kinds of arghya, he welcomed him, saying:
"I am blessed and I am graced that you have come to my home."
"This kingdom, these subjects, and this wealth are all due to your favor," he said;
thus addressed, the king of sages replied, "I am indeed fasting as part of my vow."
"I desire to break my fast here at the end of the four-month period;
therefore, O best of the Raghus, quickly grant me food," [he said] to the sage.
The Lord himself stood before him and fed him with sweet foods;
having eaten and bestowed his blessings, the sage departed as he had come. (105)
Then Lakṣmaṇa himself, taking up a sword, said to Rāma:
"Strike me down with your sword and fulfill your vow."
Reflecting upon this, Rāma said to him: "Exile is worse than death.
Go, Lakṣmaṇa; having been released by me, depart quickly for another land."
"Either the abandonment or the killing of the virtuous—both are equal to me.
O Lakṣmaṇa, you must not see my face again."
Thus addressed, he went quickly indeed to the very bank of the Sarayū;
having bathed and assumed the lotus posture, he departed through the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
Enveloped in radiance, he ascended into the sky; Rāma and all embodied beings beheld him.
Then they all departed and saw the lifeless body of Lakṣmaṇa fallen there.
The kinsmen and others wailed piteously;
having prepared a funeral pyre of sandalwood and other woods, they then laid the body upon it.
And a voice from the sky spoke: "O best of the Raghus, do not give me fire;
O Rāma, this kinsman of yours has gone to the abode of Brahmā."
Having taken with you Sugrīva’s devotee Vibhīṣaṇa,
who is full of devotion, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, you must indeed go to that very abode.
Then Rāma, having taken Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa with him, departed toward the southern direction by means of the Puṣpaka chariot.
Having returned to his own city with Lakṣmaṇa in that celestial chariot,
and having consecrated Kuśa and Lava in the kingdom, he departed for his divine abode.
And with his second form, the best of the Raghus protected Vibhīṣaṇa,
who was long-lived, in Laṅkā for the sake of the affairs of state.
"Because the bridge has been destroyed so that the Rākṣasas may not cross it,
O beloved, through hearing and reciting this, there shall be both worldly enjoyment and liberation."

Thus ends the four hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Subjugation of the Diseases of King Ajāpāla by means of the Goherd’s Circle, the Obstruction of Daśaratha’s Cart of Rohiṇī caused by Śani, and the Departure for Vaikuṇṭha according to Rāma’s Vow," in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
O Lakṣmī, listen as I proclaim the sixty-eight sacred sites on earth, which indeed purify embodied beings. 1.
Somanātha, the great holy site; Revatācala in Saurāṣṭra;
the holy site of Kuṅkumavāpikā, and also the holy site of Dvārakā.
Camatkārapura is a sacred site, as is Nārāyaṇasarovara;
Arbudadri is a great sacred site, and Puṣkara is the most excellent of sacred sites. || 3 ||
The great holy site of Hiṅgalājī, as well as the excellent Haridvāra;
the holy region of Kashmir and also Badrikāśrama.
The sacred ford of Kedāranātha, the purifying Kurukṣetra, the field named Śālagrāma, and Kāmākṣī in Kāmarūpa; || 5 ||
And in Nepal, there is Pāśupata at Kapilāśrama on the ocean shore;
likewise, the sacred field of Muktinātha, which is the abode of Mahālakṣmī.
The holy site of Hariharakṣetra, likewise the city of Jagannātha,
the field of Gayā, and the supreme pilgrimage site of the city of Sāketa.
The sacrificial pits of Paraśurāma, the region of Mathurā, Siddhapura as a great holy site, and likewise Prayāgarāja; || 8 ||
The sacred field of Kāśī, the Daṇḍaka forest, likewise Śrī Tryambaka, the Oṃkāreśvara Tīrtha, and the excellent Śuklatīrtha; || 9 ||
Bhṛgukṣetra, the holy site of Śrī, the confluence of the Narmadā and the ocean,
the birthplace of Kalki, the Saṃbhala-tīrtha, and the tulasī situated on the Candrabhāgā river.
Aruṇādri is a great sacred ford (tīrtha), and Śrīśaila is an excellent sacred ford;
the two Kāñcīs are auspicious sacred fords, and Cidambaram is purifying.
The sacred field established by Janārdana, the well-adorned Bhūtapurī,
the holy field of Kumārikā and Satī, and the purifying Dharmāraṇya.
The great sacred field of Rāmeśvara, the Mallikārjuna Tīrtha,
the Malaya mountain Tīrtha, and the purifying Tāmraparṇī river.
Ujjayinī, Mahākālavana, the Naimiṣa forest, Mount Mahendra—a great sacred site—and likewise the Viśālākṣī forest. || 14 ||
The great sacred field of Kālañjara, as well as the field of Gokarṇaka;
the holy ford of Amarakaṇṭaka, and likewise Sāptagodāvara. || 15 ||
The holy site named Trikūṭa on the Vindhya mountain, the Pakṣitīrtha, the Mahākailāsa Tīrtha, and the confluence of the Tāpī and the ocean. || 16 ||
The hermitage of Jamadagnya, the field of Paraśurāma, Sutīrthaka, the holy site of Pulaha’s hermitage, and also the Kāverītīrtha. || 17 ||
The sacred field of Vārāha-tīrtha, as well as Ṛṣabha-kṣetra;
the sacred field of Nṛsiṃhācala-tīrtha, and also Mīnākṣī-tīrtha. || 18 ||
O Lakṣmī, those sixty-eight great sacred fields of Padmanābha and these beginningless holy fords (tīrthas) truly exist upon the surface of the earth.
There are also thirty-three other crores of sacred fords (tīrthas), as well as stars, virtuous men, gods, seers, and sages.
Truthful and virtuous maidens devoted to their husbands, female ascetics and male ascetics dedicated to the vow of celibacy; ||21||
There were also most virtuous and wondrously marvelous excellent ascetics,
as well as cows, others who remembered their past births, and Vaiṣṇava devotees.
The Śaivas, Sauras, Gāṇapatyas, devotees of the Goddess, and the Śāṅkaras;
the Brāhmas, Cāndramasas, devotees of Īśa, and those devoted to Vahni. ||23||
Practitioners, mantra-experts, and those who enter the bodies of others—whosoever dwell there, they are accomplished ones free from passion. (24)
O Lotus-born One, those places where the peaceful ones, the supreme *paramahaṃsas*, and the practitioners of *sāṃkhya* and *yoga* dwell, are sacred pilgrimage sites (*tīrtha*). 25.
Even insentient objects become capable of destroying sins; indeed, sentient beings are true holy places, for they are the creators of insentient holy places.
Indeed, all temples are truly sacred fords (tīrtha);
and the hermitages of the guru and the gurus themselves are always sacred fords, O beloved. (27)
Having delivered them from saṃsāra, those sacred fords indeed establish them in the state of sovereignty or in liberation, washing away their sins.
