all women take on the form of Lakṣmī, and men become like me.

Thus ends the five hundred and eightieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Destruction of Kaṇṭha’s Sin of Brāhmaṇa-Slaughter at Soma-tīrtha, the Destruction of the Dānava Nalamegha at Jalaśāyi-tīrtha, the Becoming of the Fourteen Thousand Maidens the Wives of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Candrāditya-tīrtha, the Tīrthas Extending to the Edge of the Ocean, Śaṅkara’s Departure for Kailāsa, and the Explanation of the Means of Liberation for Impure Men and Women," in the first section on the lineage of the Kṛta-yuga in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. || 580 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, Lakṣmī, my form is composed of me, and I am indeed that very form.
All this is identical with Me; I am the form, the Supreme Person. (1)
Known as Puruṣottama, I dwell in the Puruṣottama field; indeed, I am the Lord of the worlds, a Person (Pumān) bearing a divine form.
There lies the divine field named Puruṣottama, supremely purifying,
where I, the Lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama, abide in a wooden body.
The Lord Jyotiḥprakāśa is Nārāyaṇa himself;
having become the eye of the worlds, though divine, he has come within the range of vision.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O Mādhava, how do you exist there as a wooden image?
O Blessed One, I wish to hear this for the sake of the welfare of the worlds. (5)
When, why, and how did you dwell there, and what was your state?
Out of compassion and grace, please let your devotees hear your story.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to this supreme secret that bestows great merit;
even by the mere recitation of it, the inner darkness is destroyed.
And I am the Lord of the World, dwelling in the secret cave of all beings; nevertheless, this field of mine is my supreme physical form.
I myself am present there in embodied form; by my name, this place, which extends for ten yojanas and possesses the beauty of a sandy grove, has been made famous by me.
In ancient times, having created the world of moving and non-moving beings, Brahmā, resplendent with the great mountain Nīlācala, indeed reflected upon it.
For the sake of liberating embodied beings, I shall indeed praise Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord;
and for my own liberation, I shall worship Puruṣottama.
Having reflected thus, he praised the primordial, glorious, and infallible Kṛṣṇa:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; obeisance to the Lord. (1-2)
Salutations again and again to the Lord of the syllables, the sovereign of the liberated;
salutations to You, the swan-like lord of Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Prabhā, and Māṇikī. 1.3.
Salutations to you, the Lord of Pārvatī, the beautiful Lord who possesses all attributes;
you are Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, and you alone are Nārāyaṇa.
You manifest as Bhūman, Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu, and Vairāja; you are the inner controller, the light, the perceptible, and likewise the imperceptible.
You alone are the essence of reality, the knower of both nature and its transformations;
you are the one who dwells within the sheaths, subtle as an atom, yet greater than the greatest.
You are substance, quality, and action; you alone are existence and non-existence; you are both illusion and the cause and the effect—salutations be to You!
In this saṃsāra, for those who are greedy for a self, you alone are the very essence; and even that which is essence-less appears to them as having the form of essence through their vision. 18.
Therefore, having abandoned passion, I shall become devoted to you as the Supreme Lord;
for what is the use of threshing husks that are devoid of essence?
And where there is emptiness at the end, a wise person should not undertake it;
O Keśava, I must certainly not perform a creation that ends in emptiness.
"Be gracious today and grant liberation to me who desires it.
Thus indeed was I, the one whose banner is the glorious Garuḍa, praised by Brahmā.
Then the four-armed Śrī Nārāyaṇa, radiant as ten million suns, manifested himself; desiring to enter that [lotus], he smiled and spoke to him.
O Brahmā, how did you attain detachment as soon as you were born?
O Creator, carry out my command: perform creation and practice meditation for me.
Beginningless ignorance is extremely firm and difficult to sever due to the bonds of karma;
yet, in the past, you performed the action that bestows the status of the Supreme Lord. (24)
Without enjoyment, that which incites new [beings] would not perish;
when that exists, how could death and birth be withdrawn from creation? (25)
Nevertheless, if your mind is firm in the path of devotion, then hold this in mind: wherever my mind is, there you are.
Knowing this, consider everything I have spoken as non-different from me;
O Brahmin, I abide forever within your heart.
I shall explain my ritual; perform it exactly as it has arisen in my heart:
on the northern shore of the ocean and to the south of the great river. (28)
Go indeed to that region on earth which bestows the fruit of all sacred fords;
there, human beings shall possess a mass of merit acquired through ten thousand births.
Indeed, those who are not devotees and those of little merit do not attain this abode;
[it extends] from the forest of Ekāmra as far as the shore of the southern ocean.
Beyond step after step lies my divine realm;
there, resting upon my throat, is the jewel known as Nīlama.
"Having rescued him, I established that Nīla mountain.
Brahmā then asked, having heard this: "How did the sapphire (nīlamaṇi) come to be there at that time? (32)
"O Lord, tell me the reason why Hari was established there by you.
Hari said: "Listen, O Brahmā; formerly, indeed, there were Madhu and Kaiṭabha."
The two Daityas who were destroyers of the cosmic egg have been slain by me with my discus;
though they were my devotees, they engaged in a fierce battle with me.
They both struck me in the heart with their fierce maces;
however, I removed that excellent jewel from my chest and held it fast.
As long as the battle lasted, he remained buried in that place;
there, my fierce devotees and the earth itself stood terrified. (36)
The maiden, having fallen into a state of terror, remains supported by the jewel;
protected by this gem, she awaits my arrival. (37)
Having slain the two Daityas, I then went there specifically to bring him back;
at that time, I, the Supreme Lord, was praised by the maiden Pṛthvī.
O Lord, you are my protector and guardian; you are my sustainer.
You alone are the lord of the earth, and you are the giver of life to me, O Lord. (39)
O Lord, O Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, O Master, protect me always!
O Hari, O Master, destroy my burden and annihilate my sins.
Thus addressed, I said to her, "Choose a boon; I shall grant it to you.
She replied, "You ought to always protect this sapphire here. (41)
By this, liberation shall indeed be attained through the destruction of the sins of embodied beings, and my protection shall also be secured by wearing the ornaments of Kṛṣṇa. (42)
Having heard this, the Blessed One said to her, "So be it.
And he presented this blue gem, which serves as an ornament. (43)
Held by the Earth upon her neck, he indeed always and certainly wears that supreme field which is of the nature of the neck and consists of Śrī Puruṣottama. 44.
And again, when I desired to depart from that place,
she requested once more that you should come here.
"And the Lord, intent on my deliverance, must always remain here.
"So be it," I said, and I went to Vaikuṇṭha. (46)
Then, O best of men, I received a command from the Lord, the Master of the Syllable, on the slopes of the Blue Mountain; indeed, I desire to go there.
"Under the influence of compassion for my devotees, I, known as Puruṣottama, have taken up residence here;
such indeed is the Blessed One, the primordial Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (48)
The Self of All himself dwells there upon the ground of Puruṣottama;
that Blue Mountain shines upon the shore of the ocean, illuminating the quarters.
O auspicious lady, this place is hidden on earth and unknown to you.
It is difficult for the gods and demons to comprehend, as it is concealed by my illusory power (māyā).
Endowed with all sovereign powers, I abide there in embodied form;
having transcended both the perishable and the imperishable, I exist as the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). ||51||
My field, the supreme among men, has not been overrun by the laity;
for in my abode, there is a man who bears all weapons, just as I am. (52)
There, on that ground of the Blue Mountain at the foot of the Kalpa-banyan tree, you shall likewise behold me, adorned with the emblems of the Supreme Lord. (53)
"You shall see me dwelling on the bank of the pool named Rauhiṇa;
go there openly, for as you meditate upon me, I will indeed appear."
Having thus instructed Brahmā, the illustrious Puruṣottama then vanished right there while Brahmā was looking on. ||55||
And Brahmā approached the place where Puruṣottama was;
he beheld Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, in that very form.
Then Jñānasāgara, thrilled by his recognition,
bowed to and praised Śrī Puruṣottama;
at that moment, a certain crow arrived there from the sky.
He fell indeed to drink water and, by fate, submerged himself in the pool. ||58||
Then, having been cast out from the sacrificial pit by that Brahmā, he rolled upon the earth and beheld the Supreme Lord of blue luster. ||59||
Having cast off his crow-body, he became possessed of a divine body, bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace, and stood there by the side of Kṛṣṇa.
Having witnessed the divine movement of the crow, which is difficult even for the lords of yogis to attain,
he was struck with wonder at Brahma and reflected upon it at that very moment.
Oh, how great is the majesty of this sacred field!
Even one who was tamasic and lowly attained the state of having four arms, even without spiritual practice. (62)
A human being was authorized for liberation, and even a bird attained liberation;
nothing whatsoever is difficult to obtain where Śrī Puruṣottama resides.
Where Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is present, there is indeed no distinction between a worthy recipient and an unworthy one.

Where the Ancient Person (Purāṇapuruṣa) is proclaimed by name by people, even those who merely hear it attain liberation; what then need be said of one who beholds Him? For the one who meditates upon Him and the one who serves Him, liberation is already within reach.
For the Blessed One, when directly perceived, grants liberation to his devotee;
such is the marvelous majesty of him who is known as Puruṣottama. (66)
In this place, even a crow attained Hari directly as the four-armed Lord; how much more so those who are constantly devoted to the yoga of meditation upon Kṛṣṇa? (67)
There, on the divine blue mountain in the sacred field of Puruṣottama,
even insects, moths, and the like attain liberation in every respect.
Having seen that, Yamarāja indeed arrived there quickly;
Brahmā beheld that son of Vivasvat, Dharma, whose fire had been extinguished.
Even Yamarāja, having prostrated before Śrī Hari on the Blue Mountain (Nīlādri), [beheld Him] sighing, dejected, and rendered his own office useless.
He praised Śrī Jagannātha for the firm establishment of his own authority:
"Salutations to you, the single reality, who appears as duality and who is infinite. (7.1)
Salutations to you, who are the source of all, whose every form is self-manifested, who bestows steadfastness and nourishment, and who is the presiding deity of all appearances.
Salutations again and again to you, the Guru who is the witness for the sake of faith;
salutations to you, the ocean of compassion, who transcend the Supreme. (73)
Salutations be to you, the destroyer of birth and death, the kinsman of the distressed; salutations to you, the self who presides over Māyā, clothed in yellow silk.
Salutations again and again to You, the wielder of the discus, for the severing of the wheel of illusion;
salutations indeed to the Supreme Lord, the giver of the staff and the supreme authority.
Salutations to you, who possess a body like a dark blue cloud, who dwell upon the Blue Mountain,
who are adorned by the lotus-eyed one, and who bear the mace.
To him whose chest is adorned with the shimmering beauty of the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem;
who is dark blue in hue, who dwells in the caves of the Blue Mountain, and who is the abode of compassion. (77)
I bow to the one higher than the highest, who destroys the suffering of those who take refuge in him;
by taking shelter at his feet, imperishable prosperity is obtained.
The eternal glory that bestows sovereignty upon devotees exists;
O Supreme Lord, that Prakṛti is dependent on another, by Your will. (79)
Enveloping you, it attains expansion for the sake of liberation from bondage;
and by your will, it bestows the state of nirvāṇa upon one whose enjoyments have been experienced.
You alone are the Supreme Brahman; you exist in the form of Brahman, and likewise you exist in the form of Bhūman and in the form of Vyūha.
O All-pervading Lord, you exist in the form of Yama and in the form of Rudra;
O Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, O Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! ||82||
O Great King Kāmbhareya, compassionate one, homage to you again and again!
O Lord Prabhā-Nārāyaṇa, Pārvatīśa-Nārāyaṇa, Haṃsa-Nārāyaṇa, Mañju-Nārāyaṇa, let there be salutation to you! 8.3
O Lord with attributes, I bow to your wife, the remover of suffering;
I bow to her who wards off anxiety for sons and who sustains all. ||84||
Having spoken thus, Yama ceased;
meanwhile, Lakṣmī, having herself become filled with compassion, was instructed by Nārāyaṇa— who was well-pleased by Dharmas’s hymn of praise— and spoke to Dharma.
O King Yama, that for which you offer praise is indeed difficult to attain;
this is the sacred field of Śrī Hari, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, known as Puruṣottama.
It bestows liberation upon all; they do not see Yama at all. Those who behold this sacred site shall not go to the abode of Yama.
Likewise, our Puruṣottama-kṣetra must not be abandoned;
here, the lordship of all guardians beginning with Brahmā is not praised. (88)
Indeed, the ripening of the karma of embodied beings does not occur here;
for by dwelling here, even insects [exhaust] their most grievous evil karma. (89)
Through the majesty of the feet of Puruṣottama, it goes to dissolution;
for those bound by the fetters of karma, no bondage exists here.

Since you have been ordained as Yama, the dispenser of punishment for those who commit evil deeds, why are you not the punisher of embodied beings who have become incarnations of Puruṣottama? || 91 ||
Here shines my Lord, the glorious Supreme Brahman Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself, who has made Mount Nīla his abode. 92.
Since even sinners are liberated upon seeing that Nārāyaṇa, your punishment does not apply to them; O Yama, you are the lord over others, but not over them.
O Yama, do not seek to punish those who have taken refuge in the Lord of the World;
even Brahmā was filled with wonder upon seeing the liberation of this crow.
For he abandoned pride born from the cycle of existence of embodied beings arising from karma;
you too, having likewise abandoned pride, should govern them. 95.
Except for those at the Puruṣottama-tīrtha, all embodied beings residing here are not subject to me; for they are under the control of their own master. 96.
In this matter, these four-armed ones are indeed liberated while living (jīvanmukta);
therefore, their falling into your hands has never occurred, nor will it ever occur.
By these means, O mind, attain composure and fulfill your duty;
do not grieve, O Yama, that this garment has not come into your own hands.
Thus enlightened by Viṣṇu in the form of Lakṣmī, Yama, feeling remorseful,
bowed again to Lakṣmī and, remembering Hari, spoke to her.
Where the glorious Anādiśrī Narāyaṇa resides as my mother,
I had indeed never before heard of the greatness of that sacred field.
"Struck down by ill fortune, how can I know the power of Hari?
Indeed, the will of the Supreme Lord proceeds unrestrained. (101)
In other places, that very same [practice] bestows bondage; here, it alone bestows liberation.
How vast is this sacred field, wherein living beings are untouched by "mine-ness"! 102.
Tell me also what kind of fruit results from abiding in this field, so that, having received your permission, I may wander in a distinct state. || 103 ||

Thus ends the five hundred and eighty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Narrative of the Blue Mountain in the Form of Nīlamaṇi in the Sacred Field of Śrī Puruṣottama within the Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the First Book of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; the Liberation of the Crow-Brahmā while he was watching on the bank of the Rauhiṇa Kuṇḍa; the arrival of King Yama there; and the fact that the messengers of Yama could not touch the living beings in the Blue Site (Nīlasthalī) created by Lakṣmī. || 581 ||
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
O King Yama, listen to the truth that you have asked, which is beneficial for you;
I shall describe the sacred field, its fruit, and likewise other auspicious things that grant liberation.
Just as I was formerly by the side of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa,
so too did I abide upon His chest during the dissolution of the universe.
And when this world had dissolved in every respect, I beheld both myself and this excellent field known as Puruṣottama. (3)
At that time, there were two of divine form: the sage Mārkaṇḍeya, whose lifespan spanned seven kalpas, and one who was submerged here in the ocean of universal dissolution.
Wandering in the ocean of waters at the sacred field of Puruṣottama,
he took refuge in the form of Puruṣottama on the Nīla mountain.
On the shore of the ocean, at a sacred field, he beheld a divine banyan tree;
there he saw the eternally manifest Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, brilliantly radiant.
[He saw] one who was laughing, beautiful, sixteen years of age, and four-armed;
that field is upon his chest, and he too is merged within the field. (7)
As he was speaking, [Mārkaṇḍeya said: "O Mārkaṇḍeya, why are you bathing in the water? Be firm!
Come here to my side, to this spot in the shade of the banyan tree. (8)
Having heard that and having seen the field, the banyan tree, and Hari, he was struck with wonder;
for it was not moistened by waters, nor was it consumed by fire.
This field is dried up by the Saṃvartaka fires and the like, yet it is not moved;
for it is seen to be like a boat in a single vast ocean. || 1.582.10 ||
And a divine, vast banyan tree, the body of the Lord, is seen;
even by the wind of the great dissolution, its leaf does not tremble.
There the Blessed One dwells even during the dissolution;
how indeed is this region of the earth stable even during the dissolution? (12)
Thinking thus toward Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the king of sages departed for me; seeing me situated upon his chest, he returned to himself.
Homage, homage to you, O Supreme Person; homage, homage to you, accompanied by Lakṣmī.
Homage, homage to you, who were within the range of my vision in the ocean of water, dwelling in the banyan tree.
Salutations, salutations to you who dwell here for the sake of the divine abode and for the sake of being the refuge of the world;
salutations again and again to you who, though immersed in dissolution, are endowed with a trace of compassion for those sinking [in saṃsāra]. || 15 ||
The supreme state, the abode of the Imperishable, the immortal realm of Vaikuṇṭha, Goloka, Hiraṇmaya, and so forth—
all these exist on earth wherever you have taken up residence.
And this divine [nature] is not consumed even by dissolution.

I bow to you, Viṣṇu—the all-pervading one, residing in the glorious Puruṣottama, possessing a vast form, established in the form of the banyan tree; who are beyond Māyā, the supreme Brahman, arisen from dissolution, and abiding in dissolution. 17.
In this world that has become a single ocean, what is this supreme state of yours, O Supreme Lord, wherein you shine as the manifest savior, the bestower of grace upon me? (18)
Save me, O Viṣṇu, Lord of the World, from this terrible ocean of saṃsāra;
for you are not separate from Mārkaṇḍeya, who beholds you at the appointed time.
Just as Lakṣmī is, so too is this Mārkaṇḍeya your follower;
why have you abandoned me and remain here while the ocean of worldly existence is being dissolved?
"O Lord, accept me here; grant me a dwelling under this banyan tree.
I shall perform your service here eternally and without ever departing."
Thus addressed, the Blessed One said: "Come here, O Sage;
stay here at this banyan tree together with Lakṣmī and likewise with me."
"In the morning, you shall see all my creations once again as they were before;
I have shown you this divine field, Śrī Puruṣottama. (23)
"Build a leaf-hut; dwell here within this circle of banyan trees, for it is on your account that I remain steadfastly here."
Then, having heard the command of the Supreme Lord, the sage Mārkaṇḍeya constructed an auspicious leaf-hut within the tangle of the banyan tree's roots.
He entered within, and there he saw Hari standing inside;
absorbed into that form, he beheld millions of cosmic eggs.
Within this egg, the Brahmin beheld the fourteen worlds, as well as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others—the guardians of the quarters who protect the worlds. (27)
The Siddhas, Gandharvas, Daityas, Rākṣasas, gods, and humans;
the Nāgas, Pitṛs, mountains, oceans, as well as the sacrificial altars. ||28||
He beheld Śeṣa, the sustainer of the worlds, adorned with a thousand hoods;
he also saw the Tortoise who supports Śeṣa, as well as water and fire.
He beheld the wind, the sky, and everything beyond the great ether;
and in the space of consciousness (cidākāśa), he indeed beheld Goloka and Vaikuṇṭha.
Then he beheld the imperishable abode of divine radiance,
where Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself, the Lord of Lakṣmī, resides.
There he saw a banyan tree and a leaf-hut built by himself;
there he beheld Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
The supreme king of sages beheld his own son Mṛkaṇḍu, the sacred field of Puruṣottama, the divine ocean, and the Nīla mountain.
Then, by the will of the Blessed One, in the very next moment,
I was again made to undergo contraction within that interval.
In his own leaf-hut, Hari beheld the Lord, accompanied by Lakṣmī, in his heart;
seeing Śrī Hari as before, he was struck with supreme wonder.
With supreme devotion, he praised Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama:
"O Supreme Lord, you are my beloved; what a wonder has been displayed! (36)
"And why, O Lord Śrī Hari, have you stayed at this spot? Tell me.
Then the Blessed One spoke of that ground of Puruṣottama.
Indeed, this very abode of mine was established by me forever;
it is that divine second form, Puruṣottama, together with the sacred fig tree (vaṭa). ||38||
This temple of leaf-huts shines with its virtuous inhabitants;
you are my imperishable abode, and Mārkaṇḍeya is another man [who has attained it]. (39)
And I have shown you the eternity of this abode of mine even upon the earth;
that sacred field of mine is indeed known by the name Puruṣottama.
Therefore, contemplate this field of mine as delightful and eternal;
here neither creation nor dissolution exists, nor is there the cycle of worldly existence.
Having known me here as the eternal Supreme Person, the Puruṣottama,
that pure-souled one enters the Field (kṣetra) and indeed goes to my own abode.
"Since he has entered into dense bliss, his birth shall not occur again.
Having heard this, the son of Mṛkaṇḍu chose to dwell there.
With a heart full of joy and filled with faith and devotion, he said:
"O Blessed One, please show your grace by residing in this sacred field of Puruṣottama."
O Supreme Person, may I remain such that I do not fall under the power of death, but rather become immersed in Your eternal abode and Your bliss. 45.
Then King Yama and Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa said to that sage: "I dwell together with you and with Lakṣmī."
I shall dwell here without a doubt for the sake of the welfare of the world, until the destruction of all beings and even during the final dissolution. (47)
At the end of the dissolution, I dwell again at the time of creation; even at the end of creation, I dwell here.
I shall always reside here; you, too, must dwell in Parṇapattana.
In this place, indeed, there shall be the famous city of Parṇanagarī;
it shall also be known as Puruṣottamapurī and likewise as Jagannāthapurī. (49)
In age after age, you shall attain renown by this name and shall dwell here;
and having become the remover of death, you shall remain in this place—of this there is no doubt.
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the Universe, vanished;
the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya then chose to dwell there.
And having established a purifying pit in the north-western corner of the banyan tree,
the Imperishable One himself conquered death through his intense ascetic heat.
The purifying hermitage of Mārkaṇḍeya is situated there;
this sacred field extends for five krośas, established within the ocean. (53)
Extending two *krośas* along the shore of the ocean, it measures seven *krośas* in total;
it is enriched with the beauty of blue mountains and strewn with golden sands.
Residing within the Supreme, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, even the ocean, which contains all sacred fords (tīrthas), has attained the status of the King of Tīrthas. 55.
O Lord of Yama, on its bank the Blessed One and Lakṣmī shine forth;
there I am, the goddess Kambharā, overflowing with the bliss of Brahman.
She who indeed shines in Kuṅkumavāpī and also in Saurāṣṭra as Gajānanā, and in Camatkāra, she is Kārṣṇavāllabhī in Kāśī.
She who is Jayā in the imperishable abode of Goloka is indeed Rādhikā;
she is Ramā in Vaikuṇṭha, and Prabhā Vinodinī in the golden realm.
In the realm called Śveta she is Māṇikī Lakṣmī; on Kailāsa she is Pārvatī;
in Satyaloka she is Haṃsā Mañjulā; and on Mount Meru she is my beloved Bhuvā Saguṇā. (59)
The wives of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa remain together with Him;
Śrī Jagannātha is in the east, and the Lord of Dvārakā is in the west.
To the north is Nara-Nārāyaṇa, and to the south is Janārdana;
these are indeed the forms of my Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In Jagannātha I am Lakṣmī; in Dvārikeśa, I am Prabhāvatī;
in Nārāyaṇa, I am Māṇikī; and in Janārdana, I am Pārvatī.
In the first kalpa here, I was a devoted wife to all;
likewise, in another kalpa and even in other manifestations, I was that same one.
By the will of Kṛṣṇa, I become enriched with manifold names and forms;
that which is my own desired duty is likewise my devotion to my husband.
My names and forms, as well as my manifestations,
shall indeed become women who descend as incarnations of Hari.
Indeed, hundreds of thousands of millions of women shall become the wives of my husband,
who is of unswerving valor and whose celibacy remains unbroken.
For Hari, who is endowed with immutable existence and is beyond number, women are excluded;
the field of that one of immeasurable splendor is Śrī Puruṣottama.
It is shaped like a conch, with the east and west aligned; at the western end is the one whose banner bears the bull.
At the eastern end, in the mouth of the conch, the blue-throated god shines resplendent.
The interior portion of Śaṅkha’s belly was flooded with the waters of the ocean,
extending from the lineage of the ocean up to the divine Nyagrodha tree as its limit.
The Blessed One is seen there, bestowing grace upon his devotees; whoever comes within the range of the Blessed One's vision becomes a partaker of liberation.
By dying while staying at my abode, or likewise by bathing there,
a human being indeed becomes freed from sins through the mere remembrance of this place.
At the region of the navel, however, reside Śaṅkha, Kuṇḍa, Vaṭa, and Hari;
there dwells the great power Vimalā, who bestows liberation.
She is the devourer of dissolution and the obstructor of the great dissolution;
he who, having seen her, bows down to her, enjoys eternal delights. (73)
The sacred field situated between the banyan tree and the ocean grants liberation even to insects and the like;
for the Antarvedī is the Bhāgavata field, and she indeed resides in its center.
Abiding in that [city], they indeed bear the conch, the discus, and the lotus;
there, Puruṣottama is the lord of three and a half crores of sacred fords (tīrthas). ||75||
Since the king indeed bestows liberation, he is called this "King of Tīrthas.
In the divine pool named Rohiṇa, in the water known as Kāruṇya, people [attain their goal]. (76)
Those men and women who bathe here shall certainly become Nārāyaṇas;
therefore, O Lord of Yama, you should have no concern regarding this place.
"O King of the Departed, you are not the Lord here for those who are qualified for liberation.
Having thus instructed Dharmeśa, Lakṣmī spoke to Brahmā.
Here, the guardian of the field named Kāmākhya always remains at the command of Nārāyaṇa; endowed with austerity, he worships Śrī Nārāyaṇa. (7–9)
And this Lord Nṛsiṃha resides on the right side of Hari;
by giving up one's life in the presence of Nṛhari, liberation will certainly be attained.
By the mere sight of Nṛhari, both worldly enjoyment and liberation come into one's hands;
furthermore, acts such as giving gifts and chanting prayers performed here yield millions upon millions of times their usual merit. ||81||
Both Nṛsiṃha and Vaṭa are Nārāyaṇas;
their shade bestows liberation, and within it, ignorance comes to an end. (82)
In Vārāṇasī, at the site of Avimukta, Śambhu whispers into the ear of the seeker of liberation the means for awakening; thereafter, he bestows the mantra. (83)
If liberation occurs through knowledge after practicing in stages, it happens gradually;
however, in this case, upon the cessation of the vital breaths, liberation occurs at that very moment.
Even whoever attains similarity [to the divine] without internal consciousness should bathe in the shadow of a banyan tree within the dark form of Kṛṣṇa, as if looking upon the ocean. 85.
Whether one dies here in this sacred field amidst dust, ocean waters, or rivers, there is liberation;
for the protection of Antarvedī, eight Śaktis have been created by me.
Maṅgalā is at the foot of the banyan tree, while Vimalā is in the west;
Sarvamaṅgalā is situated on the back of Śaṅkha. (87)
Lambikā is situated on the north, and Kālarātri on the south;
and behind Kālarātri, Caṇḍarūpā is established.
To the east dwell the Marīcikās, the female servants of the Lord belonging to Viṣṇu;
by the sight of these eight, there is the destruction of sins and the fruit born of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
Then the Lord Rudra, the highly fortunate devotee of the Lord, also offered his oblation:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; Svāhā! (1.582.90)
Chanting the mantra while remaining here, he worshipped the Supreme Person in eight ways;
having propitiated Kṛṣṇa through austerity, he requested an excellent boon.
O Lord, wherever you are, there I would dwell, constantly worshipping you;
O Beloved of Kamalā, apart from you, there is no other cause for liberation. (92)
You are my inner controller, the Lord; without you, whence could there be a body?
Resembling the stainless sky, I have gone to you for refuge. (93)
When this was said, Lord Kṛṣṇa created a devotee named Rudra there as the lord of the field-protectors (Kṣetrapāleśvara), the most excellent among the eight supreme devotees. 94.
And Kapālamocaneśa, Kṣetrapaiśa, Yameśvara, Mārkaṇḍeśa, as well as Īśāna, Bilveśa, and Nīlakaṇṭhaka. ||95||
And Mādhava established those eight, including Vaṭeśa;
by seeing, touching, and worshipping them, one is liberated. ||96||
For those who die in this field, Yama is not the ruler because of that;
if you have come for that purpose, then accomplish it elsewhere. (97)
The Sudarśana discus of Hari is the supreme cutter of illusion;
by means of it, no illusion shall exist here, so that the embodied soul may come into your hand.
Thus addressed, King Yama, having worshipped the Blessed One and bowed to Lakṣmī, departed for his own abode in the south, satisfied while meditating upon Hari. ||99||
Śrī said: Then the great king Indradyumna, a performer of sacrifices and a true Vaiṣṇava, [beheld] the Unborn One situated in the station of the Supreme Lord (Parameṣṭhin).
Before long, that devotee will appear in the Satya Yuga;
having come here, he will practice great devotion day and night. (101)
"For the pleasure of the Blessed One, he will perform a thousand horse-sacrifices here;
likewise, O Brahman, he will do so for the sake of your pleasure as well. (10.2)
Then, for the sake of bestowing grace upon him, the compassionate Blessed One will manifest in four forms, arising from a single block of wood.
Viśvakarman shall fashion the wooden image,
and you, having been propitiated by Indradyumna, shall be its installer.
Then, O Brahmin, you will become like these images resembling us here in Śrī Puruṣottama; they do not differ from us even by a particle’s breadth, O Lord.
"Because they are dissimilar, you shall establish them.
Now go, O Brahmā, to Satyaloka, the supreme field of the Puruṣa."
"Come again whenever I, the god, am remembered by you.
Having been addressed thus, the creator of the universe, having honored them both, went to the world of truth (Satyaloka).
The Lord Nārāyaṇa, a treasure-house of compassion, also said to Lakṣmī:
"Everything that you have spoken shall indeed come to pass in this very way."
To those possessing the eye of flesh, my form will appear as wood;
and to those possessing the divine eye, I shall appear as divine along with you.
Residing within a cave of the Blue Mountain, resembling a dark blue cloud,
he bore a wooden body and possessed the conch, discus, mace, and other [emblems].
Saṃkarṣaṇa shall dwell with me, Subhadrā shall be near me,
and likewise the Sudarśana discus shall reside together with me.
For my incarnations are many—divine, inanimate, and human;
as well as those born as animals and from the water—and among these, the divine ones possess the most excellent rites. || 11 2 ||
In the same way, my incarnation here as one made of wood is intended by me to cut through the sufferings of saṃsāra and bestow imperishable happiness. (113)
Therefore, though I am made of wood, I dwell as the Supreme Brahman;
for a wooden image never bestows liberation anywhere.
O Lakṣmī, the state of being uncreated is never found in that which is created;
for how could liberation—which is uncreated—arise from something created, such as wood?
Without a substratum, the divine sovereignty of Brahman does not manifest;
that substratum, the image of me, Nārāyaṇa, is this [the Śāligrāma]. 1.16
Even having made it supramundane, I shall employ it there as if it were mundane;
for where has it ever been heard or seen that a statue should speak? 1.17
To Indradyumna, he who bore a wooden body granted a boon:
"I am the sole refuge for the wretched and the helpless, and the means of crossing the ocean of worldly existence. (118)
O Lakṣmī, those men who shall come to me alone for refuge—Hari, who dwells on the Blue Mountain and is the deliverer from all sins—[shall attain liberation]. 11.9.
Not perceiving their faults even if they commit hundreds of offenses,
I shall forgive them with even the slightest devotion, assuming a body of divine wood.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord himself ceased speaking at the banyan tree,
while meditating upon his own form together with Lakṣmī within the circle of the Blue Mountain.

Thus ends the five hundred and eighty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Eternity of the Holy Puruṣottama-kṣetra to Mārkaṇḍeya," along with its measurements, the role of Śambhu through his eight forms and Pārvatī through her eight forms as guardians of the field (*kṣetrapāla*), the divinity of the *vaṭa* tree, and the future installation of the images by Indradyumna, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta-yuga in the glorious *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Now, O beloved, I shall tell you of a marvel here; listen.
I am the divine one in embodied form, the bestower of liberation, the giver of happiness, and auspicious.
Just as the elements such as earth are indeed the forms of the living self,
so too is my embodied image the abode for me who am formless.
The nature of the Self, which consists of a single reality, is not perceived by the physical eye;
therefore, I have not become an object of vision in the form of a material body.
I am one whose body is earth, and likewise one whose body is water;
I am also one whose body is fire, and likewise one whose body is air.
I am embodied as space and likewise embodied as the subtle elements;
I have the mind, intellect, and so forth as my body, and the Self and the Lord as my body.
I am the one who possesses the body of Brahmā, likewise the one who possesses the liberated body;
I am the one who possesses all bodies, and everything divine has me as its refuge.
In the matter of divinity, the ritual section of the Vedas, consisting of mantras and so forth, is the motivator;
therein, my installation is the primary cause for my entry.
Then, by means of that body, I perform everything like one possessing a body;
if one should know me thus, he who relies upon me becomes liberated.
Though motionless and possessing a body of wood, I perform divine sports and playful graces;
even with very little devotion, I can endure ten million offenses committed by my devotees.
Formerly, in Kurukṣetra, there were two— a Brāhmaṇa and a Kṣatriya—
who were both friends, devoid of dharma, fallen from their conduct, and deluded.
Living together with courtesans, they were devoid of the utterances of *svadhā* and *svāhā*;
indeed, the thought of the next world never occurred to them, even in their dreams. (11)
Once, however, a sacrifice to Viṣṇu was being performed at Kurukṣetra;
they went to the sacrificial enclosure and observed the ritual procedure.
As they heard the Vedic mantras, the evil of Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣa turned away; their minds became fixed upon dharma.
Discernment has also arisen for the sake of crossing the ocean of worldly existence and for the purpose of washing away the heaps of sins committed by the gods of the earth (the Brahmins). 14.

Having offered salutations and made known their own impurities— such as the consumption of liquor, meat, and sexual intercourse, as well as theft, the violation of women, and the killing of living beings— they questioned him.
Having heard that, the best of Vaiṣṇavas, the illustrious twice-born devotee of the Lord, [spoke].
Intent on divine rites, he spoke to the two of them with devotion:
"O twice-born one, O scion of the Kṣatriyas, if you both desire liberation from this most dreadful mass of sins, go quickly to Puruṣottama."
Having propitiated that Lord of the World, the Supreme Person who dwells there in that most excellent field made of wood—the husband of Lakṣmī and Rādhā—[one attains the goal]. 18.
Strive for the destruction of evil and likewise for liberation in the imperishable state;
do not delay, but proceed there with haste.
"In Utkala, on the Blue Mountain (Nīlaśaila) on the shore near the ocean"—
having been told this, those two sages bowed to the other ṛṣis and went to Puruṣottama,
both observing vows of pure diet while meditating upon Viṣṇu in their minds.
Having gone and bathed in the ocean, the refuge of all holy fords, [he returned] toward the temple. || 21 ||
Standing like staffs at the gate with a desire for a sight of him,
they gazed at the Blessed One; but when the two of them did not see him,
they became hopeless and then began the vow of fasting unto death.
Chanting the names of Hari, their minds became absorbed in Him.
Then, on the third night, they beheld a single light;
when that light vanished again, they remained steadfast and observed a fast.
In the middle of the seventh night, the two of them beheld Śrī Hari—
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Śrī Puruṣottama).
Four-armed and equipped with weapons, standing upon sandals rich with jewels,
lotus-eyed and with a smiling face, he draws Lakṣmī toward him with his left arm,
while holding the auspicious [object] from her hand at his side.
Betel was in her mouth, and her eyes were filled with a flood of love. || 27 ||
He was completely surrounded by a halo of radiance and encircled by female companions,
some holding jeweled canes in their hands and others holding chowries,
while others carried fragrant lamps; all were adorned with ornaments.
Puruṣottama was beautified by her who held a jeweled parasol;
Puruṣottama was perfumed by her who held an incense burner;
and he was looking at a certain woman with a smile, laughing most charmingly. || 29-30 ||
Thus he praised the gods, the Siddhas such as Sanaka and others, Nārada and the other Gandharvas, and the Vaiṣṇavas such as Prahlāda. || 31 ||
And they saw a host of Apsarases dancing before him for the sake of propitiating him;
having thus seen all this, the two of them became possessed of divine knowledge.
Having circumambulated that Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa three times with palms joined in reverence, they both repeatedly offered praise to Him who dwells within their hearts and stands before their very eyes.
We two, greedy for the objects of desire and practitioners of sinful sorcery, have indeed come here for refuge to you out of compassion for the sages. (34)
O Lord, have compassion for us, who are utterly wretched, who have come to you for refuge, and who, being deluded and performers of evil deeds, have fallen into the ocean of existence. (35)
Who else is a kinsman like you, the dispeller of great fear, the lord who is devoid of self-interest, whose sole object of meditation is the welfare of others, and the protector of the helpless? (36)
"Nārāyaṇa"—this is Your name, the sole means for attaining the four goals of human life.
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā! ||37||
For you, O Mantra, are the purifier even of the most sinful and the bestower of liberation;
indeed, when recited, you surely cause one to reach the further shore. (38)
Therefore, be gracious to us, O Lord of Gods; grant us firm devotion.
O Keśava, deliver us from this terrible and insurmountable pit. 39.
May our senses, mind, and intellect abide within Your form;
and may our self, together with its latent impressions, be offered at Your feet.
Be gracious, O God, the soul of all, with innumerable heads and arms;
with innumerable nostrils, eyes, hands, and feet—salutations be unto you! 41.
O Inner Self, you are the twenty-sixth principle; you proceed as the one beyond all phenomenal manifestation.
You are the embodiment of the four goals of human life; O Lord of the World, salutations be unto you! 42.
O Kṛṣṇa, through the worship of you, all perfections are attained;
salutations again and again to this Kṛṣṇa, even without the practice of yoga. (43)
Grant us firm devotion; there is nothing else to be prayed for.
As long as we maintain our lives, may our devotion to you remain steadfast. 44.
Therefore, O Lord Nārāyaṇa, grant your devotion even from beyond;
for us who are submerged here in the unfathomable mire of worldly existence, you are our ultimate refuge.
"O Lord, grant us eternal servitude; have mercy on us, O All-pervading One!
Thus praising Him, those two devotees fell upon the ground like a prostrate staff. (46)
Saying "Be gracious," they looked upon him again and again;
and having gazed thus with divine vision, they bowed down repeatedly. (47)
Just then, their lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa became invisible;
yet both of them [could still see] Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣa with their physical eyes. 48.
Through illusion, they perceived a divine vision as if seen in a dream;
then they beheld the Lord of Śrī once more, seated upon his throne. 49.
Having the form of wood, adorned with a crown resplendent with divine ornaments,
and bearing on the surface of his forehead an upward-pointing sectarian mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍraka) with golden-colored dots.
Resembling a fresh cloud, with eyes as long as blooming lotuses,
and radiant with golden earrings set with the finest of precious gems.
With red lips, a nose like a sesame flower, and wearing a forest garland;
bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus as weapons, and possessing a broad chest. ||52||
His face bears a gentle smile; his arms are adorned with divine golden bracelets;
his chest is enriched with the Śrīvatsa mark, the Kaustubha gem, and necklaces of pearls and other jewels;
his two legs reach down to his knees, and his forearms are graced with golden chains.
His hands, with fingers adorned by rings inlaid with excellent gems, display the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and hold a rosary;
he is clothed in saffron-colored silk garments and anointed with divine sandalwood paste. || 54–55 ||
His chest was graced by the Goddess Śrī, who shone like a garland of flowers;
his hand held a cluster of blossoms, his cheeks were perfectly rounded, and his two lips were as enchanting as the curve of a bow. 56.
His beard was slightly visible and his lower lip possessed fine lines;
his lotus-eyes were an ocean of love, possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids;
they beckoned with side-long glances and made known the longing within his heart. (57)
Her waist was encircled by a golden girdle consisting of twenty-seven strings;
her two feet resounded with a network of anklets and tiny bells, and their soles were richly colored with a crimson hue from the clinging lac and other dyes. (58–59)
It has a seat formed by a subtle moon, with elevated and rounded nails;
its hands bear the bow, banner, trident, svastika, fish, and other [auspicious] symbols;
and its palm is marked with upward lines, half-moons, thunderbolts, hooks, and so forth.
They both beheld their lord and master, Śrī Svāmī Puruṣottama, who was filled with fresh youth and was a thief of the heart;
and on the right side of Śrī Hari, they saw Halāyudha.
He is the Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa, Śeṣa, whose many excellent hoods support numerous cosmic eggs; he is Balarāma, adorned by a circle of thousands of hoods and jewels,
white-complexioned, wearing a crown, and graced with golden earrings.
Wearing divine garlands and blue garments, with lotus-like eyes, his lofty and broad chest is adorned with rows of jeweled necklaces;
he holds the conch, discus, mace, lotus, plowshare, and club. (64–65)
Then, between those two, they both beheld a lovely and auspicious young woman, radiant as a campaka flower, who had recently entered the bloom of youth;
her broad forehead shone, adorned with dots of saffron as red as the dawn.
[He saw her] with a forehead shining with golden streaks and saffron-sandalwood paste;
richly adorned by the beauty of her heavy braid, which was drawn into a *dhammilla* coiffure;
and decorated with ornaments for the ears, nose, neck, arms, forearms, and waist. (67–68)
She wears a shimmering sārī and bodice brilliant as lightning, and is adorned with tinkling girdles;
she is the eternal Lakṣmī, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, endowed with every beauty.
She is graced by betel, lotuses, and other ornaments, and attended by a female fan-bearer.
And they beheld [the chariot] which dwells in the bliss of celestial attire, beauty, and amorous charm;
which possesses a single wheel as radiant as a hundred suns,
has a thousand spokes, provides protection for devotees, and bestows final liberation.
Seeing Kṛṣṇa standing in four forms—a wheel fashioned from wood, as well as Hari, Bhadra, and Bala—the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya [were amazed]. (172)
In the morning, they were filled with wonder and believed in his divine nature:
"This is not a wooden image; it is Brahman itself that shines forth. (73)
The Blessed One, possessing a divine form, stands at the foot of a banyan tree on the bank of the Tīrtharāja, which is interspersed with wood; by seeing him, people are liberated. (74)
When the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, descends upon the earth, he manifests in four forms. ||75||
"Indeed, we two shall remain in the presence of Jagannātha," having thus resolved, the two devotees remained devotedly intent upon Kṛṣṇa. (76)
Remaining there for a long time, fully conscious and with their minds fixed on Kṛṣṇa,
they became divine and went to the imperishable realm of the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Thus, those who worship that beginningless Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the supreme abode of liberation characterized by non-return [to saṃsāra].
Men and women shall dwell in the city of Puruṣottama;
having become divine and four-armed, they shall go to my imperishable abode.
Even those such as insects and moths who are deprived of their lives shall,
by the power of Kṛṣṇa, go to the supreme abode.
Having their desires fulfilled, they shall go to the heavenly worlds known as Vairāja;
having enjoyed divine pleasures there, which belong to the Lord, thereafter—
"They shall go to my world, which is even higher than the Imperishable (Akṣara)," so said the Blessed One to Lakṣmī at Puruṣottama in Utkala.
On the shore of the southern ocean dwell my Vaiṣṇavas—men and women endowed with righteousness and devoted solely to me. (83)
Having reached the river Ṛṣikulyā, which flows toward the southern ocean, that region between the Svarṇarekhā and the Mahānadī rivers is Utkala. (84)
This very land, Śrī Puruṣottama, is heaven upon earth;
by taking refuge in Nārāyaṇa, it bestows dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. (85)
Where women are devoted to their husbands and men abide by their vows toward their wives,
there, among my devotees, the Kṛta Yuga prevails at all times.
O Lakṣmī, by the mere sight of them, eternal liberation occurs;
and by reading or hearing this, a person shall obtain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Thus ends the five hundred and eighty-third chapter, titled "The Description of Liberation through the Direct Vision of the Lord by a Brāhmaṇa and a Kṣatriya in the City of Śrījagannātha," within the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to my ancient narrative concerning its origin. In a former age, during the Kṛta-yuga, there was a great king named Indradyumna.
Mārkaṇḍeya does not know that time where he dwells;
neither the sage Baka, nor the sage Gṛdhra, nor Indra and the other gods indeed know him.
But the tortoise dwelling in Lake Mānasa knows that ancient one;
Lomaśa also recognizes Indradyumna as having existed in former times.
That fifth lineage of the Creator was indeed Vaiṣṇava upon the earth;
they were knowers of the supreme self, devotees of the Bhagavat, and perceived Brahman in all things.
He was all-knowing, possessed of excellent character, a performer of sacrifices, and devoted to the Brahmins;
he performed the Rājasūya sacrifice and a thousand Vājimedha sacrifices.
He resided in Mahākālavana, the capital city of Avantī;
there, he practiced devotion to Kṛṣṇa through his mind, speech, and actions.
The Lord himself, Śrī Svāmī Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, was personally present at the holy site of Kuṅkumavāpikā before the king.
Having reached the occasion of worship, he goes and accepts the offerings;
and after consuming the food offering himself, he personally instructs the king.
"O King, go to my field known as Puruṣottama;
there, cause a palace for me to be built, a mansion comparable to Mount Raivata."
Thus addressed, the king also said "Om" to Narayana;
and Hari, having received the worship offered by him, became invisible.
Then the king informed his own priest in the assembly hall:
"I wish to see that sacred field where the Lord of the World resides in person."
And we shall travel by celestial chariot together with learned men and poets,
along with astrologers and Vedic scholars, as well as male and female servants and others.
Having received this instruction from the side of the domestic priest,
a Brahmin ascetic then addressed the king.
O King, he who was known by the name Patnīvrata and whose sphere of influence extended throughout the cosmic egg said: "I know and I see it exactly as it is held in my hand."
That sacred field, which is the refuge of the Lord of the World, is indeed in the region of Oḍhra;
it is in Utkala, surrounding the Nīla mountain, by the southern ocean. 15.
That sacred field, known by the name Śrīpuruṣottama, exists both in the water and on the land,
where the Kalpaka-banyan tree stands and where the Rauhiṇa-pool is located.
There, in the eastern direction, resides the divine form of Kṛṣṇa made of sapphires; it bestows liberation through attaining His very form (sārūpya-mukti). (17)
To the west, indeed, there is a village of the Śabaras called Śabaradīpaka;
its path also leads to the abode of Viṣṇu.
There indeed resides Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in the form of a sapphire;
O King, I dwelt there at Śrī Puruṣottama for one year.
For the sake of pleasing the God of gods, the deities and sages, possessing divine vision and observing vows, assembled every night after having beheld him.
O King, this majesty of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa for the sake of his vision has never before been seen by me anywhere.
There, O best of kings, stories concerning the *saṃhitās* that deal with the meaning of other *kalpas* were heard; indeed, that place is worthy of being seen.
Just as the land of Raivata is, so is the region of Nīlagiri;
these two sacred fields have never existed before, nor will they ever exist again.
"Since you are a devotee of Viṣṇu, go and worship Śrīdhara.
Having spoken thus, that brahmin indeed vanished from sight.
Having attained a state of wonder upon hearing these superhuman words, the king now spoke to his domestic priest.
Buddhi is eager to go there where the Lord of the World resides;
O Purohita, my virtue, wealth, and pleasure are all dependent upon you. (26)
"Now you go before him; my desire will be accomplished.
Having heard this, the brahmin said, "Certainly, O King, you shall see Keśava."
"By whatever means you [suggest], I shall likewise act for your benefit;
we shall all dwell there, in Puruṣottama. (28)
What greater success is there in this world than the vision of Hari?
Therefore, the proximity of the Blessed One in that sacred field is pleasing to me. (29)
"First, let my younger brother go to that region accompanied by spies;
likewise, let Vidyāpati go to Jagannātha, Nīlādri, and the banyan tree."
Having carefully examined the region of the earth and measured the ground, let him come, knowing that field to be the refuge of Nārāyaṇa. ||3 1 ||
Upon hearing this, King Indraka commanded him, saying, "So be it," and the domestic priest likewise informed his younger brother accordingly.
Having performed rites for his welfare by means of the twice-born, he sent him forth;
then, standing upon the Puṣpaka chariot, he spoke to his companions.
"Oh, our birth has become fruitful and this night is auspicious for us, since we shall behold the lotus-face of the Blessed One, which bestows liberation! (34)
And we too shall behold that Lord of Śrī, who dwells on the Blue Mountain (Nīlācala), whom the supreme masters of yoga constantly perceive within their hearts. (35)
Having beheld that which is invisible, we shall cross the ocean of worldly existence;
we shall behold that Source of Beings, the remembrance of whom is the washerman of our feet. 36.
"Today, oh, a mass of former merit has arisen that bestows the Lord; we shall bring the Protector, who grants liberation in his own form, within the range of our vision. (37)
"Let us all search for Hari with leather-bound eyes";
speaking thus, he went through the sky at midday to Puruṣottama.
He saw people bearing conchs, discs, maces, and lotuses in the land of Oḍhra, at the ocean, at the banyan tree, and on the Blue Mountain (Nīla-parvata). ||39||
Then, in a most wonderful and beautiful divine place near the Blue Mountain, there was the actual abode of Hari in embodied form.
He brought his own celestial chariot down there onto level ground;
having ascended the mountain slope, he was eager for a vision of Mukunda.
There, on the mountain, he repeatedly heard conversations concerning devotion to the Blessed One;
and having arrived there, he indeed beheld the dwellings of the Śabaras.
Having seen the Śabaradīpaka and those marked as devotees of Viṣṇu, he stood with his head bowed in salutation for as long as he remained there with his retinue.
At that time, a Śabara named Viśvāvasu, having worshipped the Supreme Lord,
arrived there together with his wife and questioned him.
"The Blessed Viṣṇu, the Lord of the World and Great Master, resides here;
for his sake I have come from afar, so grant me an audience here. (45)
I am the younger brother of the family priest of King Indradyumna, a resident of the city of Avanti, and my name is Vidyāpati. (46)
He was sent here by that king, who, desiring to go and wishing to see Hari, sought to find the path leading eastward from Nīlamādhava.
"O virtuous one, having seen all the news of the king, I too shall certainly remain without food; therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, show him to me. (48)
Having heard this account from the Saṃhitā as previously heard, that Śabara also remembered how King Indradyumna there was indeed a devotee of Viṣṇu.
Having arrived here, he will establish the Lord of Gods in four forms,
and he will perform a thousand horse-sacrifices upon this earth.
When Mādhava has dissolved and merged within the earth, O Nīlamādhava,
the king will come again and install him in a wooden form.
This very time has arrived, should this verse prove true:
the Lord, composed of sapphire, shall become invisible. (52)
The power of invisibility has appeared in the presence of the Blessed One; therefore, I shall indeed show him this Acyuta, who is like a sapphire gem. (53)
Having reflected thus, the Śabara spoke the thought within his heart to the Brāhmaṇa:
"We have heard the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. (54)
In this regard, news has arrived that King Indradyumna will make his own residence in the great sacred field of Jagannātha.
"O Brahmin, the vision of you as a blue-stone image arises;
therefore, you are indeed more fortunate than Indradyumna in this matter. (56)
But for this king, who possesses the luster of a sapphire, there shall be no vision [of the Lord];
behold with your own eyes that dark Mādhava dwelling upon the Blue Mountain.
"Come, let us go to that mountain plateau whose body is like a sapphire," he said;
and having spoken thus, he took him by the hand and proceeded along a dense path.
Ascending higher and higher upon a desolate and inaccessible place, abounding in stones and thorns, where one can pass only singly and which is devoid of people; (59)
Having led him to a place mostly shrouded in the darkness of tree-shade,
that Śabara showed him the most purifying holy site, the Rauhiṇa pool.
To the east of that place is this great banyan tree named Kalpachāyā;
between these two, O Brahmin, it stands within a grove.
"Behold Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the World, Śrī Puruṣottama himself!"—
thus did he show him Hari in the form of the Blue Stone.
Having bathed there in that pool, that brahmin prostrated himself with his whole being before Hari from afar, and with a single-minded heart, he praised Him within.
O Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Blessed One who transcends the imperishable;
O Supreme beyond the supreme, the heart of the liberated souls—salutations be unto You!

Salutations be unto You, who are to be propitiated through all ritual actions and accomplished through yoga; salutations again and again to You, whose self is the object of the noose of love and whose self is the sacred ford.
Salutations to you whose nature is splendor; salutations again and again to the purifier.
Salutations to you, the god who is the consumer of oblations, and who dwells within the heart. 66.
Salutations to you who abide in the mantra, who grant life and liberation;
salutations again and again to you, the Brahman-Lord, the bestower of all bliss. ||67||
Salutations to you, the wielder of illusion, the essence of reality, the one possessing form, the witness of all faith, the victorious one with many heads, the Lord of Kamalā.
O ocean of compassion, lift me up; protect me who am possessed by latent impressions (vāsanā).
Fulfill the resolve of King Indradyumna as well. (69)
Having thus offered praise, Vidyāpati recited the mantra "Om.
Then that Śabara said, "You have now achieved your purpose."
"Let us go home; you are hungry and ill-suited to life in the forest.
This region is perilous, filled with predatory beasts that stalk on foot. (71)
Having spoken thus, the Śabara led the Brahmin to his own home;
even on the rugged path, he felt no fatigue, for he was beholding Kṛṣṇa.
The Śabara honored him exceedingly with food, drink, and other offerings, and said:
"O twice-born one, are you satisfied with these Śabara articles? (73)
"By pleasing you, Indradyumna will be satisfied.
The Brahmin said, "This is a marvel; there are divine splendors in your home. (74)
"And since these have passed beyond the kingdom, tell me now, from where do they come?
The Śabara replied: "O King, these are indeed the gods who come daily to Hari. (75)
Taking divine offerings for the worship of the Lord of the World, they praise him, honor him, present their offerings, perform dances, and then depart. (76)
For these indeed are divine provisions;
by means of them, we dwell free from disease and with a lifespan of one hundred billion years.
Having heard that the destruction of sins and divine status result from enjoying the grace of Viṣṇu,
the brahmin, filled with wonder, considered himself to have achieved his life's purpose.
"Aha! I must dwell right here, forever in the refuge of the Blessed One;
and I must become just like this devotee of Viṣṇu. (79)
"What is there for me at my own home that I must go there?"— having reflected thus, she said to him,
"If you have favor toward me, I shall serve as a maidservant to Kṛṣṇa."
"What need is there for service to others in this world? I shall perform service to my own master.
If merit from a previous life exists, one obtains service to a master. (8.1)
Excellent, O friend! Since I have this meritorious meeting with you, through association with the virtuous I shall cross over this difficult and treacherous cycle of existence. (82)
"Sitting together with a Vaiṣṇava is merit more essential than the most essential;
the Śabara then said, 'So be it'—listen further. (83)
"O twice-born one, take Indradyumna with you and reside here;
by that means, the image fashioned from the Blue Mountain (Nīlaśaila) will attain dissolution."
The king shall not behold this ancient image;
Hari will soon disappear into the sands.
And that king, having arrived and not seeing Puruṣottama, the Lord of Śrī,
while remaining in a fast unto death, shall behold Mādhava in a dream.
At the command of Hari, he will install four wooden images of Hari through the rite of consecration (vedha) and worship them with devotion.
He will cause a palace to be built for Your Majesty that reaches to the heights of the sky;
our lineage shall endure as long as this wooden image remains. (88)
Having remembered that [place] made of sapphire and having bathed in the Sindhu thereafter, proceed to Indradyumna and bring that king here. (89)
Thus addressed, the brāhmaṇa bathed, bowed, and ascended a celestial chariot;
in the evening, he went to Avantī and described what he had seen to the king.
Then, at the time of worship in the evening, a wind of fierce velocity blew throughout the field of Jagannātha, scattering golden sands all around.
Covered by them, that Mādhava was carried aloft by the wind;
even though Rauhiṇakuṇḍa was covered, it became a mountain of sand. ||9.2||
The gods and the others saw only a heap of sand and did not see Mādhava;
likewise, in the next moment, they did not see Rauhiṇa or the pool.
They all entreated for forgiveness regarding their own offenses:
"Why do you not appear to us simultaneously, having abandoned us, your servants? (94)
Having assumed this physical form and body for their sake, how is it that you have now vanished from the earth, abandoning those who are without a protector? (95)
There is no palace, nor a place, nor a path, nor even you;
nor is a sacrificial pit seen here—how can you have such anger? (96)
"And even us, draw along with you here at this dissolution,"—
such was the voice from the sky that arose while the gods were thus lamenting.
O gods, do not grieve; for when my will ceases, [the world] is certain [to vanish].
Therefore, my vision has withdrawn, and a transformation is desired. (98)
"Brahmā will declare my entire other incarnation.
Having heard this, the gods went to heaven, while the Śabaras fell into grief.
The Blue Mountain became covered with sand on all sides, so that it was seen [only as such],
because this longing for Nīlamādhava had itself vanished.
Then the Śabaras thought thus, and the twice-born Vidyāpati traveled by means of a celestial chariot to the abode of Indradyumna in Avantikā.
He gave the garland of remains from the worship of Mādhava, known as Nīla, to the king;
the king was delighted, wearing the garland of remains upon his head.
Indeed, I behold here Mādhava in the form of a garland;
I bow to the divine garland that fulfills the hearts of devotees. (103)
Having spoken thus, he placed the garland upon his neck by the hand of the brahmin;
the king then praised Śrī, the supreme goddess who is the very essence of the garland.
"Lead me, O Mahālakṣmī, to where my lord, the Blessed One, resides.
Having spoken thus, the king sat down in the assembly of the inhabitants of Avantī.
Then, having been questioned, the Brahmin described in detail and with full clarity before the assembly the events that had occurred at the sacred field of Puruṣottama.
Also the sight of Bhilladvīpa, the bathing in the ocean, the ascent of Mount Nīla, and the vision of Nīlamādhava. (107)
He described in every detail the excellent bathing at the Rauhiṇa pool, the sight of the divine banyan tree,
and the dwellings of the Śabaras.
And the description of the form made of sapphire is given exactly as it is;
the ancient image is fashioned from a stone of blue sapphire. (109)
This garland, made of shimmering gold and highly honored by the gods, was offered to her by the deities; it never withers.
O King, this [garland] upon your neck cannot be surpassed by any fragrance;
I shall describe to you the divine worship and other rites performed there. 111.
O King, both enjoyment and liberation exist there simultaneously;
indeed, no suffering such as old age, disease, or grief is found there.

Thus ends the five hundred and eighty-fourth chapter, titled "The Direct Vision of Śrī Puruṣottama by Indradyumna, the Dispatching of the Priest’s Brother Vidyāpati to the Field of Jagannātha, and the Description of His Return and What He Saw, Including the Blue and White Circles in the Sand Created by a Gale," in the first section, the Kṛta-yuga lineage, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī; then Vidyāpati spoke in the midst of the assembly:
"I shall describe to you exactly the divine nature of that sacred field."
At midday, the Brahmin spoke, and a wind of divine fragrance blew; the gods arrived by way of the sky to offer the gift of *naivedya*.
Then there were instrumental music and songs by celestial nymphs;
a thousand services were offered to him by the gods. || 3 ||
Having worshipped him, those gods then departed for heaven with cries of victory;
Viśvāvasu, the Śabara, [attained] grace from Mādhava. 4.
"O King, let pure food and garlands be given, as well as that which was taken away by me here; let the gift consisting of sugar be bestowed upon the assembly. (5)
The field named Nīlādri is surrounded on all sides by dense thickets;
it lies on the shore of the king of holy fords and is covered with golden sand.
The sights there are wondrous even for the gods; what need to mention humans?
On the peak of the mountain stands a great, lofty banyan tree that lives for an entire kalpa.
Long and extensive, devoid of flowers and fruits, yet radiant with young shoots;
behind that is the Rauhiṇa pit, situated to its east upon a sacrificial altar.
Cool with the shade of a banyan tree, the Lord Hari, made of sapphire,
sits upon a golden lotus, bearing the discus and the mace.
The Lord’s face, shimmering with a gentle smile, measures eighty-one finger-breadths;
his eyes are as lovely as lotuses, and his countenance is filled with nectar.
Although her body was composed of stone, her lower lip was bright as the moon;
with her cheeks blossoming with smiles, her chin and jaw were most beautiful.
His chest shone with two earrings upon his ears and with a garland,
as well as with golden neck-ornaments set with jewels and brilliantly radiant.
He has a pair of thick, broad shoulders and four long arms reaching down to his knees;
his eyes have corners extending to his ears, and he casts side-long glances from them.
Adorned with the Kaustubha gem, bracelets, rings, and finger-rings,
it possessed a deep navel and was beautiful with a fine line of hair below.
His waist was radiant with a girdle of precious gems, his silken lower garment was washed clean,
and his lotus-like feet possessed red soles enriched by the tinkling sound of small bells.
Her hips were beautiful, divine, and a lovely abode of desire;
her phallus was radiant with splendor, charming, and the vessel that draws all things toward itself.
The God who illuminates all desires resides upon the Blue Mountain;
Lakṣmī is on his left side, embraced by the Protector of the Lotus.
Intent on playing the lute, her eyes fixed upon the face of the Blessed One, she was enriched with the beauty of all loveliness and adorned with every ornament. (18)
Resplendent with every ornament and in the full bloom of fresh youth,
Śeṣa was seen behind her, his multitude of hoods serving as a canopy.
He saw him standing at the front, bearing a beautiful form, with his palms joined in reverence; behind him was Garuḍa, seated upon his back.
O King, those who show favor to their devotees appear as if they were truly alive; my heart runs toward them with great intensity.
Indeed, it is through the ripening of merit from many thousands of births that one beholds [the Guru];
for that which is attainable through all other means is attained simply by seeing him. 22.
By him who has beheld you, O King, every means for achieving liberation has been accomplished; therefore, look upon the Lord of the World with all haste.
I do not know whether you will be able to see the sun tomorrow or not;
therefore, for the sake of liberation, one should perform today that which is to be done tomorrow regarding the Supreme Lord.
Thus addressed, Indradyumna attained abundant joy and said,
"I have accomplished my purpose," because he had received the garland of grace.
"By her, the state of being a worthy recipient for the vision of Hari has been attained by me today;
therefore, I must certainly go along with my entire self and my kingdom. (26)
Having made my permanent residence there, I shall perform horse sacrifices;
day after day, I shall worship the Lord of Śrī with every form of service.
"I shall please Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Ramā, through service as a servant.
While the king was speaking thus, Nārada indeed arrived.
Honored and saluted by the king, he spoke to the king:
"We have descended to Badarī to behold Nara and Nārāyaṇa. (29)
Having heard of your fame from the deities, he has come here in truth,
having made a special resolve to go to Śrī Jagannātha.
Having known this, I have become pleased with you; go and serve Him.
Through the practice of a thousand births, devotion toward Mādhava arises.
Having propitiated that Lord, Brahmā obtained the station of the Grandfather;
I am his son and you belong to his lineage—indeed, through devotion, glory always belongs to us.
Supreme devotion is capable of destroying beginningless ignorance;
it is a boat in the ocean of worldly existence and a medicine for the disease of birth. 33.
Like a mother, she protects her devotees, and by her the virtuous indeed flourish;
through her grace, the state of Brahman and liberation are attained.
To many locusts, the beloved of Hari is like a forest fire;
she bestows the fruit of all sacred fords and is the savior of those who are sinking. 35.
Austerities, sacrifices, gifts, vows, and religious observances—
even ten million times ten million of these do not equal one ten-thousandth part of devotion.
That [devotion] is considered threefold according to the distinction of the qualities (guṇas), while the fourth is held to be devoid of qualities (nirguṇa).
That which is joined with the pursuit of one's own self-interest is declared to be tamasic devotion.
That which is mixed with both one's own interest and the interest of others arises from passion (rājasa) due to the desire for enjoyment;
that which is to be directed solely toward the interest of others is characterized by goodness (sāttvika) and is a vessel of happiness. (38)
In Śrī Puruṣottama, that [devotion] is devoid of fruits and free from the material qualities;
devotion to Hari, consisting of loving service, is declared to be free from qualities for the sake of liberation. 39.
Through the *sāttvika* [nature] one goes to the abode of Brahmā; through the *rājasa*, to the world of Śakra;
and through the *tāmasa*, to the worlds of the ancestors and so forth, and then returns again to birth on earth.
One should perform the highest rite after the highest; through that, liberation may sometimes occur.
Even one who is devoid of family traditions and the like is highly praised if he possesses devotion. ||41||
Even one who has mastered all branches of knowledge is censured if devoid of devotion;
however, that by which one knows the Supreme Brahman is considered the supreme knowledge. 42.
That by which one pleases the Blessed One is proclaimed as *satkriyā* (reverential service). One who is endowed with both of these is indeed a devotee, the most excellent of *bhāgavatas*. ||43||
By the dust of his feet, the entire universe, including all that is moving and unmoving, is purified;
likewise, when there is devotion to Vāsudeva, equanimity always arises.
Between those two, there is indeed no difference whatsoever in their sovereignty, form, and so forth;
for he is one whose mind is tranquil, gentle, with senses conquered, and non-violent.
He who is free from malice, endowed with compassion, and non-critical;
who perceives virtues, follows right conduct, and is filled with joy at the happiness of others—[he is a true friend]. (46)
Everywhere he beheld Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, free from envy; compassionate toward the wretched, acting for their benefit, and possessing ten million times the love for Hari. ||47||
Devoted to the service of the virtuous, worshipping the gods, and offering libations to the ancestors;
knowing that everything is pervaded by Viṣṇu, both in its collective and individual aspects. (48)
Indeed, perceiving [the Lord] as non-different [from himself], he performs service to Hari;
and he who exists as a servant through the relationship of master and servant [also serves]. (49)
He meditates upon Hari, glorifies Him, and offers salutations;
he constantly worships the Lord alone and does not direct his attention to anything else.

Possessing the meditative absorption of equanimity toward stones, gold, objects, clods of earth, women, falsehoods, thorns, and so forth; and toward friends, enemies, kinsmen, and those who are neutral or otherwise divided. //51//

Devoted to the meditation on the name of Viṣṇu and always delighting in the victorious speech [of the scriptures], he was renowned as a lover of divine symbols—a devotee and the best among the Bhāgavatas. (52)
Adorned with the conch, discus, mace, lotus, and the moon-tilaka; wearing a necklace and a garland of forest flowers, he is further embellished by a wreath of Vṛndāvana blossoms. ||53||
Free from passion, hatred, intoxication, and pride, with the exhaustion of craving, the devotee becomes devoid of desire and the like, his latent impressions having been destroyed. ||54||
Having been addressed thus, Indradyumna, filled with joy toward Nārada, said:
"By my good fortune, the company of the virtuous has presented itself to me today. (55)
"Therefore, let us mount a vehicle and behold Nīlamādhava.
Having thus resolved on the fifth lunar day, under the constellation Arjuna (Kṛttikā), during the month of Jyeṣṭha, on a Wednesday; ||56||
In the month of Puṣya, Indradyumna caused a proclamation to be made by his armies, subjects, kinsmen, and others, each according to their means.
Having dedicated [myself] for as long as I live, I must go to Mount Nīla;
and whatever livelihood is cut off here, by that very means may he live there as well. (58)
The kings, together with their harems, ministers, and retinues, [departed] with chariots, elephants, horses, treasuries, and foot soldiers. ||59||
Let the Brāhmaṇas who maintain the sacred fire-grove set out there prepared;
let the merchants go with their wares, and those who live by trade with their merchandise.

Those skilled in the arts of dance, song, and instrumental music; those proficient in the science of astrology; physicians; storytellers; learned scholars; virtuous men; and courtesans—[all these gathered there]. (61)
Let the cows, the bird-keepers, the fowlers, the male servants, and likewise the female slaves, go to the field of Śrī Puruṣottama. (62)
On the sixth day, the king himself performed auspicious rites for his journey;
having bathed in the waters of sacred fords, he caused the *nāndīmukha* ceremonies to be performed.
Then, having performed the oblation, he circumambulated the fire;
thereafter, he began the preparation of auspicious attire.
Having worshipped Hari upon the golden pedestal, the king first took up a garland of His grace, meditating upon Śrī Puruṣottama. (65)
Having declared his intention for a journey, he raised his right foot;
he bestowed gifts upon the brahmins with his right hand, while his left was fondled by a courtesan.
Beholding white horses, elephants, doves, swans, and jasmine flowers, as well as a full water-pot adorned with mango sprouts, the king proceeded on his way.
Having gone to the temple of Nṛsiṃha and having worshipped Hari,
Satī arrived at the gate, where there was a great celestial vehicle.
The sage, together with the women of the inner apartments and others, ascended;
and by means of thousands of other vehicles, they set out toward the city.
Shouts of victory, the sounds of musical instruments, and showers of flowers arose; then, millions of people mounted upon various vehicles [proceeded].
Accompanied by their provisions and their families, they all went to Śrī Puruṣottama;
within half a day, they reached the land of Utkala.
Staying within the boundary, they worshipped the sovereign goddess named Carcikā;
having gone to the river Citrotpalā, they performed the drinking of water and other rites.
And they all partook of delicious foods as was fitting;
then they rested there on the riverbank at the encampment of the army.
They performed their evening rites and took pleasure during the night;
then, having bathed in the morning, they performed their daily worship, consumed water, and so forth.
Having done so, they remained there for that long when a servant of the King of Oḍhra arrived before Indradyumna and spoke with words of salutation. (75)
And here King Utkaleśa desires to see you,
having learned that you, O Lord, have arrived as a sovereign emperor.
Provided with a means of access, he waited on the riverbank for instructions;
having heard those words, the king summoned the lord of Oḍhra.
Accompanied by his Vaiṣṇava ministers, the lord of Oḍhra inquired after his welfare and prosperity; he bowed to him and placed gifts before him. (78)
