Then those asuras, having observed that festive occasion of milking the cow,
assumed the forms of cows and approached for the purpose of giving milk.
Arjanyā and the others were their wives, who had assumed the forms of cows;
they were tawny, reddish-brown, red, dark-complexioned, and others were brindled. ||33||
Then, having appeared, they came into the presence of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa;
at that time, the poison collected within the waters was like white milk.
Having understood that deed of the rākṣasas, the goddess Vasundharā herself became a cow and first approached Śrī Hari.
She said to the young Gosvāmī, "O Lord, drink my milk;
drink all my milk as much as you desire so that you may be satisfied. (36)
"These cows, dwelling in the forest, have come with a desire for liberation;
having drunk their milk up to their throats, grant them liberation. (37)
Having heard this, the Blessed One, Śatarūpa, who was filled with affection for that Vasumatī,
said "Om" and once again became a child through his divine play.
The Blessed One firmly grasped their garments with both hands; placing their breasts against His face, He drank the milk that surpassed even the nectar of immortality.
O Blessed One, he forcibly drank all the nectar that had reached his mouth, along with the breath itself, as if it were milk. (2.8.40)
When this was done, those Daityas and the wives of the Daityas then cried out:
"Save us! Save us! O ocean of compassion! Release us! Release us! Protect us! (41)
Then, having assumed the forms of Daityas, they sought forgiveness;
the mother, the father, and the daughters were overcome with fear and agitation. ||42||
Seeing the Daityas weeping due to the evil deed of Tṛṇabindu and his act of attempting to kill Kṛṣṇa, Lomaśa consoled them.
Arjuna and the other rākṣasas praised the Supreme Lord:
"Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods; O Supreme Lord, let there be salutation to you! (44)
"O compassionate one, we are your sons and these women are your slaves;
a virtuous person does not give way to anger at the misconduct of scorpions. (45)
O Acyuta, do not yield to anger toward the nature of the Asuras;
protect your life, O Lord of Liberation, for by you poison has been turned into nectar. (46)
Likewise, ordain for us those who take refuge in [the Lord], as well as the deceased;
and likewise the incarnations, the liberated ones, the lords, the sages, and the gods. (47)
Sages, ancestors, mortals, piśācas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kinnaras, cāraṇas, sūtas, and kimpuruṣas—these are the followers of Yama. ||48||
Animals, domestic beasts, trees, creepers, reptiles, wild deer, shrubs, grasses, birds and the like, insects, and species of mosquitoes; ||49||
The Daityas, Dānavas, those of mixed castes, Asuras, rogues, Nāgas, serpents, the dull-witted, Caityas, men, and women—all these are your offspring. (2.8.50)
"O Lord, all your sons are endowed with the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas;
O Kṛṣṇa, may your affection be equal toward them all. (5.1)
The affection of a father and mother is equal toward their children, even when they have fallen into adversity;
protect, protect us, O Great King, do not deprive us of our lives! 52.
We were born as killers of our father, givers of poison, and evil-minded;
do not take account of the offenses of us who were ignorant and performers of cruel deeds. (53)
Again and again we bow down, placing even blades of grass in our mouths;
protect us, O Lord, give us life, do not deprive us of our breaths! 54.
Having thus entreated Hari, the Daityas fell at the feet of Hari;
and Hari, wishing to liberate them, descended near the earth.
Through the excellent union with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, their sins were consumed;
yet Arjuna, the best of Daityas, remained the cause for his birth from a Rākṣasa womb.
Having understood this with a pure and heartfelt mind, he described it:
"In former times, we were staying at the hermitage of Gālava in a desert region. (57)
The Brahmins were masters of the Vedas, devoted to pure sacrifices, following the dharma of non-possessiveness, and subsisting on bulbs, roots, and fruits. ||58||
They subsist on wish-fulfilling trees, wish-granting creepers, and wish-fulfilling gems; they assume forms at will, travel through the sky, and possess the brilliance of the sun. (59)
We were performers of pilgrimages and free from worldly possessions;
nevertheless, by the power of a Śūdra’s asceticism, we came to dwell upon the desert land.
There was a drought, by which roots, fruits, and other provisions were destroyed;
consequently, we all became mendicants, yet we remained possessed of property. (61)
Greedy for food, they became snatchers of wealth by force;
indeed, those sinners, being hungry, became eaters of what is unfit to be eaten. (62)
The trees have perished, as have the wish-fulfilling creepers;
therefore, let us roam through the forest as we please, acting contrary to dharma.
Whoever we meet on the road— be it their wealth, clothing, and so forth, or their food and water— we seize all of that from them at that very moment.
While those fifteen householders were living in this manner,
once a pair of brahmins arrived in their presence.
Endowed with righteousness and compassion, likewise devoted to the path of Brahman,
perfected in the study of the Vedas, and fully intent upon the six duties.
His wife was devoted to her husband, dedicated solely to him; she was a virtuous woman who performed service to her husband and engaged in ritual bathing, worship, and other such duties. (67)
The vow of eating once a day and likewise staying awake during the two watches of the night—these two, when used for the worship of Brahmins, are pleased and bestow all things. (68)
Endowed with faith and devotion, and devoted to their guru and father, those two arrived at our hermitages and rested near us. (69)
Before them there were parched barley flour, barley grains, and likewise unbroken rice;
these were taken away by us, as was their food.
Their clothes were stripped away and their wealth was plundered;
at that time, only enough clothing for two loincloths remained.
Even while his wealth was being carried away, her husband kept remembering Hari;
and that virtuous woman did not speak a word, but repeatedly chanted the name of Hari.
Thus, those two Brahmins were then forcibly plundered there by us, who were devoid of compassion and acting like thieves in the guise of Brahmins. (73)
Seeing those two most righteous ones afflicted, an earthquake occurred;
there was a shower of stones and a rain of dust at that time. (74)
These two remained taking refuge in the tree, mindful of Hari; she, being devoted to her husband, thought that everything was by the will of Hari.
She caused her husband to be carried along and crushed his body;
even when there was a true rain of stones and a downpour of dust, [she remained unharmed].
The two of them felt no sorrow, nor did they harbor any desire for protection.
*Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā* ||77||
Thus performing their recitation, they both remembered Hari, their Guru;
at that moment, he arrived there, accompanied by an umbrella, garments, and food.
Another Brāhmaṇa, marked with a tilaka on his forehead and adorned with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, radiant like the moon, gave him excellent food after making inquiries. (79)
He gave garments and likewise an umbrella to that couple;
and we witnessed that while the rain was falling.
Having gone there, that too was taken away entirely;
then the giver vanished, being either a divine deity or a sage.
"The sons of Brahmā, you have cursed us, saying: 'Since you are cruel, merciless, and eaters of your own kinsmen, therefore become Rākṣasas! (82)

Those who possess not even a trace of compassion toward women, men, or indeed toward a twice-born, have already obtained what was previously attained—namely, that barley, clothing, and so forth. || 83 ||
Due to the disparity of place and time, the turning back of sin was endured;
yet when [the opportunity] was regained, it was seized once more by merciless and evil-minded men. (84)
Therefore, having met their death by showers of stones, let the Rākṣasas become subject to the nature of the wind and dwell upon the parched mountain. (85)
"May those who eat the flesh of animals be deprived of happiness!"—thus indeed were we cursed by him at that time through a voice from the sky. (86)
They entreated him who was cursing them for forgiveness, liberation, and happiness;
then that sage Gālava himself manifested his true form. (87)
Our former guru spoke again out of compassion:
"In Saurāṣṭra, there is the supreme self, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (88)
"Liberation will come to you through yoga; go to him.
Then we paid homage to that sage and likewise to that couple. (89)
The wealth requested for the sake of atonement was surrendered and duly honored;
clothing and food were returned, and thereafter we were indeed rained upon.
"Indeed, having died there by that curse, we have all entered the womb of Rākṣasīs;
today we are all Rākṣasas with families. (91)
Having made our dwelling on a mountain or similar place, we meditate upon the Lord Nārāyaṇa, thinking: "When will the Blessed One become the bestower of liberation? (92)
Indeed, through the words of Tala, we have all become rememberers of our past births;
thus, possessing knowledge, the Supreme Brahman, the bestower of liberation, shines here. (93)
Thus we have accomplished our purpose, being liberated from the state of demons;
O Lord of Gods, through your yoga, our sin has been utterly consumed.
O Lord, we who were evil-natured Brahmarākṣasas have been delivered;
for us, the poison has become nectar, yet it remains poison for those who are offenders. (95)
There is no limit to Your compassion, nor is there any limit to our suffering;
may He who brings others across indeed make us, who are dependent on others, cross over the ocean of existence. 96.
Having spoken thus, the Daityas, remembering their former births, wept again and again;
they prostrated themselves like a staff before Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and sang his victory.
The Blessed One looked upon them with compassion and quickly caused them to abandon their bodies and caused the deities to take them [to heaven]. ||98||
Then those maidens became endowed with two forms;
numbering one hundred, they were protected as virgins in the hermitage of Lomaśa. (99)
Divine goddesses were dispatched by means of celestial vehicles to the abode of Brahmā for those practicing yogis among the brahmins who had attained that state through yoga.
By His grace, liberation was indeed bestowed, and Pṛthvīgau vanished;
Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa became a child. (10.1)
Well-tended by young maidens, he played upon the swing of delight;
and during that festival, the true nature of the earth was explained there by the Cow.
"O Rādhā, the deeds of Kṛṣṇa have been known by His mother, father, and sisters;
I have related them to you, which grant liberation both when read and heard.

(103) Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how, at the beginning of the second month of the boy Kṛṣṇa, during the festival of drinking milk, the Lord drank the milk of divine cows in many forms, and how He brought about the destruction and liberation of the deceitful demons who had assumed the form of cows and their wives who were likewise in the form of cows, by making the living milk flow away," from the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the second section, the Tretā-Santāna.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen to another account of the Supreme Soul, O Rādhikā;
when the second month had passed, it was the third month, during its bright fortnight.
The mother indeed brought her son out from the house;
there, the proclamation of an auspicious day (*puṇyāhavācana*), the *nāndī-śrāddha*, and other such rites were performed. (2)
The father had him consecrated with blessings by the brahmins;
having gone to the hermitage of Lomaśa,
he indeed touched his feet and applied a tilaka of saffron-moon upon his forehead.
Having joined his own hands together, he placed them at [the child's] ears and gave him the mantra:
"Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is my refuge; obeisance!
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā! || 4-5 ||
Having heard it, the boy repeated the mantra three times;
Lomaśa Ṛṣi, his mother, Janaka, and the others were filled with joy.
He placed a garland of Tulasī around his neck, which was wound twice.
The sage Lomaśa placed a garland of flowers around Kṛṣṇa’s neck;
with his hand, Lomaśa placed a grain of sugar in His mouth,
made Him drink milk, and repeatedly touched Him with his palm.
Then the mother gave the boy to the maidens staying in that hermitage, who were the beloved consorts of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, for them to play with.
They kissed him again and again, and being eager, they made him laugh;
they led him to a garden nearby, to a bower of flowering creepers.
Then there arose a quarrel, each saying, "I first! I first!
regarding which single beloved youth they, the maidens and the women, should delight. (11)
Having beheld ten million maidens,
the Lord manifested ten million forms within that garden in particular.
Just as the young moon might bring them happiness,
so did Kṛṣṇa, the beloved, always remain under their control;
one woman delighted Kṛṣṇa and kissed him again and again.
But one woman, placing him upon her breast and bestowing a weight of affectionate words, [spoke].
Another, placing her own charming child-form upon her lap, makes her beloved laugh by scratching his cheeks with her fingertips.
Touching her beloved again and again, a certain woman steadily delights his heart;
placing the finest fresh butter upon his head,
she gently rubs it with the palm of her hand as he takes the form of a child.
One [woman] applies a reddish drop of collyrium to the forehead with a small stick. || 17 ||
One woman applies a red *tilaka* with a golden rod—
a saffron mark that is passionate, captivating, and draws the Lord toward her.
Another applies a charming [mark] upon her cheeks and chin.
Another makes a red garland of *bindū* flowers, which brings joy to the mind;
yet another, having fashioned a soft, fresh garland of land-lotus petals with a peaceful fragrance, places it around his neck. (2.9.20)
But another woman, beautifying him, applied auspicious collyrium made from ghee to his eyes for the sake of brilliance and for the sake of beauty. 21.
Another indeed raises the child up into the air with her hands;
another likewise presses him repeatedly against her chest and her belly. (22)
With her mouth, lips, and breath, she makes the sound "bhaṃbhaṃbhaṃbhaṃ," while another gently plays upon her throat and utters the sound "kilkilā."
One woman rejoiced, placing his feet upon her own chest;
another, having placed him upon her hip, held the Lord with her arms. 24.
And she indeed displayed a dancing peacock through her gestures,
while the other [displayed] something charming at his feet and hands.
Sudarśanā adds a small amount of coloring substance; another [woman], however, [treats] this cuckoo-like you who is already warbling, as if he were merely associated with a mango tree.
One girl shows her nose to Kṛṣṇa, another coos at him, and yet another makes Hari laugh; while another adorns Kṛṣṇa’s nose with a cloth.
One woman quickly brushed away the dust clinging to her from the wind;
another pointed out with her finger a monkey perched upon a tree branch. (28)
Likewise, another girl, holding fresh clusters of white flowers, respectfully offers their fragrance to Bālakṛṣṇa. ||29||
Another makes him hear a faltering sound and rejoices;
yet another indeed offers a sweet taste, like honey.
Likewise, one sings a song, another dances upon the ground;
another whirls a child like a wheel and herself also spins around. ||3 1 ||
One woman was even grinding *saugandhika* flowers with *viṣṇutaila*, while another was swinging upon a swing made of creepers. ||32||
The second also gives a woolen blanket for the sake of dispelling the cold;
another, having kindled a fire, stands by its side.
Another beloved woman causes him to mount the back of a deer, while yet another leads her lover and places him before a fawn. (34)
Having led the calves toward the cows, she shows them their beloved mothers;
then, holding up two rabbit ears, she points Kṛṣṇa out in the sky.
And his beloved likewise shows him his face in a mirror, while others announce to him other signs as well. (36)
And new arrivals, having come together, behold them with joy;
and Śrī Kṛṣṇa, seeing the garment, exclaims "Kilkile! (in delight).
To some, she opens her own mouth and shows them the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), and to others, the primordial Goloka and the imperishable Vaikuṇṭha. 38.
There, the Blessed One displays his own form even within their own bodies;
thus all the maidens rejoice in the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. 39.
Having attained the bliss of Brahman, they became fulfilled;
then the Blessed Lord withdrew those forms.
He who had four arms became one with Lakṣmī in her hand, and likewise, he who had two arms came to rest upon the lap of Māṇikyā. ||41||
Then, from the waist of the illustrious Kambharā-Lakṣmī, Ekalaka was born;
having beheld all his prowess, they became satisfied, and thereafter the father [was pleased]. ||42||
He worshipped the sage Lomaśa, his preceptor, according to the prescribed rites;
he honored him with sandalwood paste and applied a tilaka mark upon his forehead.
They caused a canopy to be made with unbroken grains of rice, parched grain, beautiful flowers,
necklaces, sandals, fruits, leaves, and fragrant roots.
With roots, the finest skins of deer, milk, clarified butter, rice,
garments, and bark— substances employed for the sacrifice.
He gratified Lomaśa and accepted his blessings;
and the mother gave auspicious articles of good fortune to the young girls.
Garments and bracelets, as well as various utensils;
foods to be chewed and eaten, drinks, savory dishes, and clarified butter.
Then the mother indeed gave the ornaments for the hair;
she gave all those infinite things that were dear to him. ||48||
The mother protects them in childhood, just as she protects all her daughters;
indeed, the great stage of student life (brahmacarya-āśrama) therein is like a second heaven. 49.
By the grace of Hari, Lomaśa’s hermitage became like Vaikuṇṭha, free from illusion (māyā) and other such defects,
and was resplendent with liberated maidens.
Day and night, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa were meditated upon here;
all were beloved of Nārāyaṇa, and none were otherwise.
Lomaśa remains eternally liberated, free from illusion;
he is indeed imperishable and immutable, a soul emancipated who has reached the further shore of Brahman.
When there is no desire in the hermitage, nor does anger prevail;
when there is neither greed nor delusion, how then could pride and the like exist? (53)
Where there is no transformation of gender, where there is no sexual union,
and where desire indeed does not exist— such is the hermitage of Lomaśa.
The syllable *lī* is the head; it is the great station where eternal peace resides. Furthermore, the four syllables beginning with *lo* indeed possess auspicious meanings. (55)
When the father honors such a knower of Brahman, then his daughter named Prabhā [honors] Bālakṛṣṇa, her beloved Lord. (56)
Having led her there to sport and delight, he went to a tree growing in the garden;
his beloved’s friend took refuge beneath that royal campaka tree.
The young woman sat down and indeed offered all her means of subsistence to Hari.
Just then, the Asura Krodhanaka arrived there through the sky—
he who was born from the forehead of Rudra in the midst of the waters.
O Brāhmaṇas, when Rudra was manifested from his own forehead,
he was then addressed for the purpose of creation; however, with a troubled mind,
he remained within the water there, overcome by agitation as he reflected for a moment.
From that, a drop of sweat from Rudra was produced upon his forehead;
from that drop was born the cruel Asura, a hater of the gods.
This man was wrathful and powerful; he performed most rigorous penance.
Having attained perfection through his asceticism, he became capable of traveling through the sky and assuming any form at will.
Having indeed recognized him through yoga on the grounds of Kuṅkumavāpikā—
[He meditated upon] the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the adversary of the Daityas. ||63||
Thinking at that time, "A maiden is present in the garden," the Asura Rabhasa arrived there with the desire to seize the boy. ||64||
Having assumed the form of a maiden, she arrived to delight him;
then, without taking leave of Kṛṣṇa, who held the light in his hand, she took it.
Bālakṛṣṇa, having indeed perceived his wicked intention,
placed his hands upon his hanging arms for the sake of his destruction.
And for the sake of granting liberation, the Lord came into her hand;
Prabhā, having understood this, gave a certain friend to him along with the boy.
That wrathful maiden, having taken the child, vanished instantly within a moment among the trees and creepers, becoming invisible. ||68||
But Prabhā did not see her; then, having summoned her, the wrathful goddess took her into the sky and quickly departed along the path of the clouds.
Making repeated efforts to kill that child, she placed a noose around his neck; however, at that moment, it remained instead upon her own two hands.
Being consumed by fire, she released the throat of the boy;
situated in the sky, her body was then scorched by the flames and enveloped by the cresting fire.
Her physical form was burnt by the tongues of flame arising from the body of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Crying out "Alas! Alas!", she then threw herself upon the ground at Kṛṣṇa;
yet the fire arising from Kṛṣṇa’s body did not leave her, blazing in many ways like a smoke-bannered comet in the sky.
The cruel fire consumed that maiden; there was no protection to be found.
Then, she quickly leaped up and descended after the boy. ||74||
But Prabhā, having gone there, quickly seized the boy by the hand.
Having caught Hari as he arrived, Prabhā ran toward Lomaśa.
Then that angry woman said, "Extinguish the fire that is equal to yourself."
I am burning because of my own karma; protect me here, for I am wicked and sinful.
Having spoken thus, he blocked the path before him and praised the Child:
"O Lord Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, deliver me from this distress! (77)

"I am indeed the son of Śaṅkara, and my name is Krodhanaka. I am the one who sows enmity among the gods; sent by the asura named Tāla for the purpose of your destruction, I have accumulated this sin."
"Since my mind has resorted to the means of killing one who is not to be killed, I therefore beg for forgiveness; protect me and grant me liberation.
Thus addressed, Bālakṛṣṇa, the ocean of compassion, [spoke].
Then, filled with innate compassion, he spoke to the angry one:
"O proud woman, how is it that you have been born as a girl for my destruction?
You do not know me at all—I am the Supreme Lord, the inner self of all. (8.1)
The channels and vital breaths are in my hand; they belong to both creation and liberation. ||82||
"Tell me, O beautiful one, what offense you have committed against me;
tell me what punishment I should impose upon you for it, and I shall do so.
To her beloved husband Kṛṣṇa, the charming Lord, the angry woman replied:
She said to me: "O Lord, pacify this burning of my body in that manner;
O Lord of Gods, become my beloved, for I choose you as my husband.
O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, my heart runs toward you. (84-85)
"Grant me liberation and likewise destroy my demonic nature at the end.
Hari said, "So be it; all this shall come to pass for you.
By my touch, your body shall forever be divine and eternally youthful. ||86||
"For my sake, let there arise a beautiful hermitage inhabited by Lomaśa;
and you, O beautiful lady, should remain among the maidens in the form of a maiden.
Let your second [self] likewise attain liberation to the imperishable state."
Your third form shall likewise be of a human nature, resembling fire;
it shall be wrathful, entirely cruel, and known as Krodhana on the surface of the earth.
Let it indeed take the form of a sage, and you shall always remain as Krodhana.
In this way, Kṛṣṇa indeed bestowed these three forms upon Krodhana.
And in another birth, this Krodhana will become Durvāsas;
he will always be the foremost of Vaiṣṇavas, equal to Nārāyaṇa in virtue.
"O Rādhā, this shall be the cause for my incarnations as Nārāyaṇa," having said this to the auspicious girl Krodhanā,
the Blessed One made her an eternally beautiful maiden and likewise fulfilled her desire.
The second form of hers is Kānyaka, which also leads to excellent liberation. || 93 ||
Having performed this, he instantly dispatched his third form, the Puruṣa-form characterized by tamas, from his abode to the Imperishable (akṣara) through his celestial vehicle. || 94 ||
He performed supreme austerity in the vicinity of Lomaśa’s hermitage,
and at the bank of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, he visited the great holy site named Krodhana.
O Rādhā, it should be known that what was born is auspicious and bestows liberation. Then Prabhā and the maiden Krodhanā [approached] Bālakṛṣṇa. (96)
Having led her there, they then brought her to the place of Lomaśa’s worship;
when asked, "Who is this new girl?", Prabhā replied.
Having heard of the wonderful miracle of Nārāyaṇa, they were indeed filled with amazement;
and having performed the worship of Lomaśa, the mother, the father, and Hari [departed]. (98)
That maiden went to the house of the girls with a longing for Hari;
she made her constant residence there and became the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. 99.
Then, at the time of dusk, his father or mother performed the worship of the moon according to the prescribed rites and caused the Vāmadevya hymn to be sung.
The mother caused her son to assume a gentle appearance like that of a flash of lightning;
likewise, the wives of the Moon and the Moon himself rejoiced upon beholding Mādhava.
Upon seeing Hariścandra, he then pointed with his finger and said to his mother,
"O Mother, bring the moon here into my presence," thus thinking in his heart.
Having understood the intention of Hari, Candra, accompanied by twenty-seven [wives],
arrived joined by the chariots of his twenty-seven wives.
When the moon departed, the Kuṃkumavāpikā field became entirely divine, resembling the lunar orb.
Candra, moreover, brought various kinds of jewels,
as well as divine garlands endowed with celestial luster that bring forth cool nectar.
There, the offerings intended for Hari were presented by Mātṛkā, and likewise, a gracious welcome and other hospitable honors were performed for the wives of Candramas.
Having offered water for the feet, the respectful oblation, the honey-mixture, food, and drink,
and having worshipped Hari, Candra bestowed his blessings.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa went to his own abode in heaven and became joyful;
then all the others, beginning with his father, [honored] Lomaśa, the best of sages.
And having prostrated like a staff with devotion and offered the gifts,
he received His great favor as well as His blessings.
Having given blessings to the maidens, they departed toward their own abodes;
thus indeed, O Rādhikā, was it for the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
This sacred narrative is wondrous and brings happiness;
it grants liberation to those who hear it and bestows prosperity upon those who remember it. (111)
For those desiring worldly sons and wealth, it bestows heaven, progeny, and riches;
for those longing for knowledge, sovereignty, and the like, it is the supreme bestower of the perfection of knowledge.
O Rādhā, I have described to you this purifying form of the Child, which bestows enjoyment, liberation, and even good fortune for women. (11.3)
By merely thinking of this, one shall indeed obtain the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas),
and likewise, one shall acquire the merit born from the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) of all sacrifices.
O Rādhikā, both the fruit of all acts of giving and likewise the fruit of all yogic practices reach their completion upon attaining the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the second section on the continuity of the Tretā age, during the third month of Lord Bālakṛṣṇa’s life, on the bright fortnight, while the rite of the first outing (*niṣkramaṇa-saṃskāra*) was being performed by women for His playful fondling, [the Lord] manifested many forms and a divine vision appeared. Then, Prabhā took Kṛṣṇakānta to the hermitage of Lomaśa; there, the demon Krodhana, having become the maiden Krodhanā, abducted Hari.

In the sky, she was consumed by Hari; he released her, having made that divine being three-formed in the hermitage of Lomaśa, at Mokṣa, and in the birth as Durvāsas, manifesting her in the form of a servant-woman. This is the ninth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Vidhudarśana, Camatkāra, and Others."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhā, listen as I relate another account of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul, which bestows the essence of the bliss of Brahman.
And in the fifth month, on the earth, he performed for his son the sacrament of sitting up (upaveśana), and at that time he bestowed gifts.
On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight, having risen early in the morning, the father indeed bathed, performed his daily rites, and stood near the courtyard of the palace.
He caused a pavilion to be constructed, adorned with plantain leaves and auspicious archways made of the foliage of aśoka, clouds, and other trees.
He tied the water-pots and placed them upon [the pole];
he hoisted the banner and wrapped it with cloths. || 5 ||
He caused a canopy to be fixed and fastened small banners;
he also had creepers fashioned all around the pillars of the sacrificial pit.
Then he caused fruit-bearing and flowering trees to be placed within the pavilion,
as well as lamps and luminous gems.
He placed inlaid ornaments upon the pearl garlands,
and likewise suspended various paintings upon the canopy.
And upon the pillars, in the middle, and in the corners, he fashioned beautiful,
embodied forms of the Goddess and the gods in their iconic shapes.
Having made the floor beneath that soft with golden sands,
he arranged pleasing and unsurpassed seats.
Having spread around there beautiful, multi-colored rugs made of wool and silk, as well as small and long mats, he arranged them.
And the excellent father placed a cushion upon the lion-thrones;
it was a seat for Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa upon the earth.
He established a divine [pedestal] in the center, rich with a golden core,
and likewise prepared a divine ground made of black clay within the pavilion.
And for the purpose of seating the children, he protected Śobhanā;
he had a sacred, four-cornered altar constructed.
Having placed there a long golden band adorned with the essence of excellent jewels, and upon it a linen and woolen cloth that was white; || 15 ||
Having placed a red garment over the wheat,
one should set a water-filled pitcher at the side, along with rice grains, saffron, and other such items.
Flowers, sandalwood, camphor, garlands, collyrium and the like; various kinds of food offerings, drinks, as well as betel-leaf with cardamom and so forth—(17)
The five vessels, the cooking pot, the water for sipping, the fruits, all the implements for worship, and those made from tulasī leaves. || 18 ||
The father indeed established all the objects of worship for Dharādevī,
for Suvarṇa, and likewise for the Lord Varāha.
And he had two images fashioned, beautiful in all their limbs,
adorned with ornaments and garments, gentle, divine, and possessing the very form of a god.
He saw the goddess Pṛthvī, beautiful in form, possessing the appearance of Lakṣmī, most splendid, seated comfortably in the svastika posture. ||21||
Her two feet were Pātāla, her two calves were Rasātala, her two knees were Mahātala, and her two thighs were Talātala. (22)
At the base of her thighs is Sutala, and likewise Vitala at both her hips;
Atala is at her loins, and her womb is Bhūtala.
Her belly is Bhuvarloka, her auspicious heart is Svarloka, her throat is Maharloka, her mouth is Janaloka, her eyes are Tapoloka, and her head is the highest world, Satyaloka. (24)
He likewise fashioned the forehead and Satyaloka within the form;
there, indeed, the earth with its oceans, mountains, and forests was seen directly manifest.
Likewise, one should visualize the form of Vārāhī with two feet, seated upon her throne, white in complexion, and radiant with firm body hair. ||26||
With a long nose, tawny hair, and fine eyes, and possessing a mane,
she stood on the ground with her two feet bent at the hips.
And with her two foremost hands, she holds a mace and a discus;
she is most excellent, wears a garland of forest flowers, and likewise has lifted up the earth with her supreme tusk.
Wearing a crown, bracelets, earrings, a sacred thread, a sacrificial cord, and a waist-belt, she stands poised upon the water. ||29||
Gopālakṛṣṇa likewise had a beautiful and charming golden image of Varāhikā fashioned;
he then established the ritual services for its worship and other offerings within the pavilion.
Then, when an auspicious and beautiful moment had arrived, his father [addressed] Lomaśa.
He respectfully invited the great sage with the sounds of musical instruments and other offerings;
having brought him and seated him on a throne, he performed worship for him.
Then auspicious words and the songs of women were set in motion,
and musical instruments were played on all sides.
Having brought together milk, curd, clarified butter, water, sugar, and fresh honey— the five nectars (pañcāmṛta)— the father established [the image] before him.
Having had her son purified and having summoned his mother, she stood there in that most excellent empty space within the pavilion, holding him on her lap. (35)
Lomaśa caused the auspicious worship of Gaṇeśa, the Mothers, the gods, the Brahmins, and likewise the virtuous ones to be performed. (36)
Then, with Vedic mantras, Lomaśa caused the auspicious worship of the Earth-Brahmā and the Boar to be performed by the couple. (37)
The young maidens sang songs of the virtues of Bālakṛṣṇa;
then the goddess Pṛthvī, a divine maiden, approached Hari. 38.
Having bowed down, she became fixed in the invocation within her own image;
and when the invocation was completed, Hari assumed his four-armed form.
Then, having approached the Lord who was situated within the Boar,
Lomaśa brought them both there and offered them the pleasing water for sipping (ācamana).
He offered the *argha* water, the water for the feet (*pādya*), and a seat that brings auspiciousness;
he also performed the bath with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and the bath with pure water.
Having performed a thorough cleaning with garments, he then offered fragrant incense;
he presented clothes enriched with mineral-dyed threads and precious ornaments.
He gave him the sacred thread (upavīta), a lunar mark (candratilaka), and likewise saffron (kuṅkuma);
he then gave him collyrium (kajjala), vermilion (sindūraka), and Viṣṇu-oil (viṣṇutaila). ||43||
She gave him lac-dye, saffron, sandalwood, flower petals, tulasī leaves, garlands, and beautiful necklaces. ||44||
He offered all kinds of erotic ornaments and excellent unguents for good fortune;
he also gave him chains, gentle bracelets, rings, and so forth. (45)
Having offered saffron, *abīra*, unbroken rice grains, and *gulāla* powder,
as well as incense and a lamp, he presented an offering of milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
He gave all kinds of grains, most delicious food, water mixed with sugar for drinking, betel leaves along with cloth and cloves,
fragrant substances, fruit, and a beautiful golden seat.
The sage Lomaśa gave as a sacrificial fee gold, silver, and other riches. ||48||
And he performed the waving of lights (ārātrika) for the goddess Dharā and the god;
he offered salutations, hymns of praise, circumambulations, benedictions, and handfuls of flowers.
He prostrated like a staff, offering prayers and requesting forgiveness;
having thus worshipped the God and the Vedic Brahmins at that time.
Then the father honored those who were seated in his presence;
at that time, musical instruments were played and there was exceedingly beautiful dancing.
The goddesses and the Kinnarīs sang beautiful songs;
then, at the conclusion of the worship, the mother [honored] her son according to the procedure prescribed by Lomaśa.
On a spot consecrated by sprinkling in the presence of the worshiped Earth,
which had been honored, saluted, and entreated for forgiveness, he placed [the vessel].
Then the goddess Earth appeared in personified form;
placing Hari Kṛṣṇa upon her lap, she honored him with a blessing.
Then the other goddesses and the maidens worshipped and honored Hari with saffron and other substances, as well as with sweet milk-rice (pāyasa). 55.
Dharādevī placed her cupped hands in supplication before Śrī Hari to ward off his sorrow;
she then placed them upon her own head. (56)
Then Viṣṇu himself appeared as the divine four-armed Vārāha, manifest before the eyes of all, and he bowed down to Bālakṛṣṇa.
Sūkara gave a golden lion-throne to Bālakṛṣṇa,
while Dharā gave him the eternal Earth as a golden bed.
Then, having established Bālakṛṣṇa there by those two,
the sage Lomaśa performed the gradual dismissal of the worship.
Then indeed Kambharā Lakṣmī fed Lomaśa, as well as the brāhmaṇas, the foremost of ṛṣis, the virtuous women, and the maidens. (2.10.60)
Having given all kinds of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās), having bowed down and performed salutations,
he dismissed everyone and laid his son to rest.
Thus the father held a festival for his son’s sitting upon the ground;
thereafter, the son, being peaceful, made an exemption, saying, "I am sleeping. (62)
Then, at that time, a female mendicant arrived there desiring food;
she was of wretched appearance and miserable voice, yet she imagined herself to possess a divine form.
She, whom he had never seen before, desired to see her son.
Questioned by his mother, "Who are you? What do you desire? I shall give it to you," (verse 64).
She said: "If you are truthful, give me here your son;
[I am] a cave-dweller named Siṃhikā, a maiden and daughter of the Earth. (66)
"I dwell upon the mountains and I roam even in the forests;
today, on this day, my mother, the goddess Earth, has been honored by you. (66)
Having learned this, I have come here for the sake of seeing your son;
this charming boy is the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. As soon as he was seen, he took up residence in my heart, destroying my sorrow.
Enveloped by darkness, I burn in the forests for the sake of my beloved.
Without food, lacking luster, and unadorned,
there are thousands of other sisters of mine upon the mountains;
for they are all maidens performing penance to obtain a beloved husband.
"If you so intend, O Mother, give me back your little son."
"Having attained peace and joy here, and having obtained the supreme fruit of my asceticism, I shall delight your son and then, having restored him to you,
I shall go to the place pointed out by my beloved and dwell there. (71)
O Mother, if you have favor toward me, speak and grant me your son.
"I swear by the truth that I am Dharāputrī, who considers her husband her own;
having heard this, the mendicant mother Kandarā said to the two maidens: (73)
"If it be so, O daughter of the Earth, delight him and take him as your husband.
Having heard this, Kandarā was satisfied, gracious, and filled with joy.
She quickly took the sleeping boy by the hand to lead him away;
seeing him still in sleep, she touched him and kissed him repeatedly with love. (75)
The girl ate the food given by her mother,
and she placed Bālakṛṣṇa upon a swing and rocked him.
The beautiful woman repeatedly showed herself;
then, out of affection for her sister, Kambharā bowed to the virtuous Satī.
Then, having received the command, her sisters went to bring her—
those who resided on Mount Meru and other mountains, wherever they had been.
Having summoned the female ascetics and gathered them together, she returned once more; all the auspicious female ascetics from the caves and the foremost of the mountain glens had assembled. (79)
Ten thousand maidens arrived to behold the Supreme Lord and the Mother Satī, the presiding deity of Kuṅkumavāpī.
They praised Kambharā with love and entreated Acyuta; they requested Acyuta, saying, "O Mother, grant us [this]. ||81||
Having heard those sweet sounds, the child quickly awoke;
his mother, having given him milk to drink, then gave [the milk] to them, she who is a treasure-house of compassion. || 82 ||
Until then, there was for me the grasping of those [forms] as "mine" and "for me"; yet, in the act of grasping this or that, this one possessing a second form appeared repeatedly. || 83 ||
While the lover remained thus with the girl-giver, he fell into the hands of the seizer in her second form. (84)
And that multitude of caves, accompanied by Bālakṛṣṇa, became peaceful;
and they took delight with him. ||82||
Then all those maidens considered their birth to have achieved its purpose;
they worshipped him, the youth who enchants the mind. ||86||
Then Hari, smiling, spoke to them for the sake of granting a boon;
they then requested the service of this very Lord, which is ever sinless.
Hari granted him service, fame, renown, devotion to the virtuous, and the state of being beloved by Kṛṣṇa; and he likewise granted him a dwelling in the hermitage of Lomaśa, saying, "So be it."
Hari gave them to those maidens and spoke to them again:
"In all the caves that always take the form of active duties," ||89||
"Virtuous practitioners of yoga, free from passion, will dwell with me;
you shall always have the company of the righteous. Fame, renown, and service to the virtuous shall be yours forever."
Through devotion to the virtuous, my own devotion and purity shall arise.
And for you who always remain here in these mountain caves, may there be constant union with me; I shall grant you eternal liberation.
"And I, O virtuous lady, shall dwell in your cave;
that cave shall become known as Siṃhagahvara. (93)
In that deep abyss where eleven maidens shall take birth, your daughter Ekādaśī shall by all means perform that very vow. 94.
They will frequent caves, sacred fords, and mountain clefts;
by my grace, they shall always become saviors.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed them in the presence of his mother,
summoned the Guru, and gave them to Lomaśa.
Having bowed to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and having eaten and drunk, they departed for the hermitage.
Kṛṣṇa remained in his singular form, and his mother was filled with wonder. ||97||
And she considered them to have performed meritorious deeds and fulfilled their purpose regarding their own selves;
for when that which is to be attained—the Supreme—is attained, what else remains?
O Rādhikā, the Lord of Compassion surely meets one only after bestowing His grace.
The Supreme Self manifests for the sake of obtaining compassion and grace.
By reading, hearing, remembering, or even causing others to hear this,
one shall obtain enjoyment, liberation, the fruit of ten million sacrifices, and a beloved wife.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Earth’s Ten Thousand Daughters, Siddhikā and Others, Attaining Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa as Their Lord during the Rite of the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa’s Seating upon the Earth," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; indeed, Hari, the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, being constantly nourished by His mother and others, grows like the young moon.
And that Supreme Person, the stainless Self, pure of heart and without support, is constantly served by those maidens. || 2 ||
Bringing joy to his mother, with eyes as radiant as the reflection of his father,
he gazed upon that dark boy who was the very embodiment of all forms.
Indeed, the subjects, by beholding him, considered it their own merit;
and the yogis, having seen him, considered him truly to be the Supreme Lord. || 4 ||
Once, having summoned Lomaśa, his father Gopālakṛṣṇaka had the piercing of the ears performed with a silver needle in the sixth month.
With a thread twice the length [of the child's height], for the sake of increasing nourishment, longevity, and prosperity,
the father Gopālakṛṣṇa bathed early on this day.
Having had a silver image of them fashioned, he then performed the worship of the Aśvinīkumāras through the hand of Lomaśa.
Then, while the father was worshipping the physician of the gods after having invoked him there,
he appeared in person, resembling the sun and adorned with earrings.
Having accepted the performed worship, he touched with his hand Hari’s two ears,
which were very soft, beautiful, adorned with the circular shape of ear-rings, the eternal abode for the attainment of all powers of hearing and the like,
and which were first anointed with the essence of oiliness.
Then, having honored a fine, new, golden needle,
her ears were pierced at the proper spots with that firm instrument.
But by the physician of the gods, through his gradual, light, and gentle touch,
the prick of the needle was not felt at all by the child, owing to the power of that elixir.
Then, as the two ears were pierced according to requirement, there appeared a needle;
it became a goddess in embodied form, adorned with divine garments and ornaments. (13)
Then that goddess, rich with the beauty of every limb, radiant as the moon, and tender,
spoke joyfully to her mother and father.
For her who has touched Nārāyaṇa, the destruction of Māyā is certain;
my Māyā is destroyed today—protect me in the presence of Kṛṣṇa! 15.
Having heard her, the mother said to her: "Whose daughter are you?
Tell me here, O goddess Kānakī; what you desire shall come to pass. (16)
Having heard this, Sūcī told her own account exactly as it had occurred:
"I am indeed the mind-born daughter of Brahmā, born from him."
My task was to reach the far shore and create a breach;
likewise, while alone, I brought about the destruction of the Daityas, beginning with Kaṇṭaka.
My father-in-law was a weaver, and he was the son of Viśvakarman;
[the garment] was entrusted to Doraka, the son of that weaver. (19)
My task is indeed the reunion of us two who have been separated, along with my beloved;
I am both the insentient form of the Creator and the conscious deity.
My family is likewise always twofold: the cause and the effect;
the cause is of the nature of the deity, and the effect is also material. (21)
Thus have I told you here that I am the beloved of the wrist-thread;
O Mother, from this day forward, I have become devoted to your son. (22)
Having manifested here specifically as divine and of divine form for the sake of serving your son Nārāyaṇa, protect me! 23.
Having heard this, Kambharālakṣmī then spoke to her again:
"O Queen of the Gods, dwell here in this hermitage of Lomaśa together with your husband."
Together with your husband and family, dwell here on the banks of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake, full of joy in your heart to serve Kṛṣṇa. || 25 ||
Having been addressed thus, she rejoiced; having bowed to the twin Aśvinikumāras and her mother, Śrī Hari, she quickly went to the house of her father-in-law. || 26 ||
Having consulted together, she quickly arrived with her family at the eastern site on the shore of Lake Aśvapaṭṭasara. (27)
Indeed, she dwells there with her family, devoted solely to the worship of Kṛṣṇa;
the young maidens take Kṛṣṇa with them and go to that place to play. (28)
Then, on the eastern bank, there was the holy ford (tīrtha) called Tunnavāyāśrama.
Once, she took Kṛṣṇa upon her hip and rejoiced.
"My Lord, when will the Blessed One consider me?
Knowing what was in her heart, Kṛṣṇa spoke to her while smiling. (2.11.30)
And I grant you success, which consists of assuming many forms;
become a maiden in appearance and dwell indeed in the hermitage of Lomaśa. 31.
"O sinless one, my attainment shall come to you at the proper time.
As soon as this was said, that goddess indeed became a maiden of divine form.
Possessing the beautiful hue of the campaka flower and assuming a second form,
she appeared in the presence of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa on the bank of the lake.
She went with her beloved Kṛṣṇa to the hermitage of Lomaśa;
she, known as the wife of Doraka, remained in the house of Doraka.
And she, having attained perfection through the worship of Kṛṣṇa, assumed the form of a crore;
appearing as a needle, she pervaded the worlds with equal clarity.
Thus, through the gain of his grace, she always obtained Kṛṣṇakānta;
the two Aśvinī-putras were indicated as the physicians for the granting of the boon.
They both also requested a dwelling for the sake of propitiation; and Kṛṣṇa, with a gracious mind, said to them, "So be it. (37)
And that sacred bathing place (tīrtha) became known by the name Aśvinīputrārāma;
it was situated among the trees on the eastern shore of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake.
In this manner, Lord Kṛṣṇa gave them and her a dwelling;
then, supported by the girls, he himself went to his own palace, the abode of the Supreme Lord.
The sage Lomaśa also received worship and abundant sacrificial fees from Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa there at the excellent shrine named Karṇavedha;
thereafter, the divine king of sages, Lomaśa, departed for his own hermitage.
On the full moon day of the sixth month, in the bright fortnight of Caitra. ||41||
When they had assembled there, the father summoned Lomaśa and performed the auspicious annaprāśana ceremony according to the prescribed rites.
Having first performed the auspicious bathing of the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa with curd, ghee, and honey mixed together, one should perform the worship of the Mothers (Mātṛkārcana). 43.
Having established the pure fire, he performed the oblation of sacrificial porridge (caru-homa);
he conducted the worship of Brahmā and the other deities, and also fed them with excellent food.
He likewise gave wealth to the virtuous Brahmins, as well as to the poor and the blind, and also to chaste women, maidens, and young boys.
Then he gave mouthfuls of food to the cows and deer, flour to the insects and such, and grains to the leeches, tortoises, and fish.
Then the father gave grains to the crows, pigeons, and others;
then he offered water to the trees, creepers, grasses, and so forth. (47)
Then he gave to the ancestors, the gods, and human beings whatever foods they desired, as well as all necessary utensils.
To all the maidens, [he gave] ornaments, garments, and materials,
as well as articles for adornment suitable for the body and implements for their practice.
Food, seats, vehicles, leaves, and coverings, as well as books for the practice of spells and those for the practice of devotion. || 2.11.50 ||
The father gave him various divine objects of enjoyment;
then the medicinal herbs on the earth, in the form of grain, yielded their seeds.
They are givers of oblations, givers of fruits, givers of roots and tubers, and givers of wheat and other grains;
they are givers of juices, sweet, givers of the essence of sugarcane, and providers of sugar.

The trees, shrubs, creepers, and other plants—givers of leaves, flowers, and foods to be chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked; destroyers of disease and bestowers of nourishment—took up the various edible items produced by each of them, consisting of young girls, and placed fresh grains and all other provisions into platters. (53–54)
Adorned and resplendent with the brilliant hue of fire, they arrived to feed Kṛṣṇa while making proclamations accompanied by musical instruments. (55)
In the Kuṅkumavāpikā garden, extending for one yojana to the west,
they remained guarding the vessels and meditated upon the Lord Śrīpati.
Knowing that they had arrived at Kalpodyāna, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa assumed a hundred thousand forms and stood before each one of them. ||17||
Having seated her beloved lord upon a golden throne, she fed him, honored him, delighted him, and kissed him again and again. (58)
Then the Blessed One, having assumed youthful forms,
ate the delicious foods with affection.
And his own grace was bestowed upon all of them, filling their bowls;
whatever they ate at that time, all of it came through the power of Śrī Hari.
Nothing whatsoever was seen to be lacking, as it had been increased by Lakṣmī;
they all fed their lord and husband with their lotus-like hands. 61.
And the Blessed One ate again, bound by affection for them;
he was fed and given drink repeatedly, and likewise honored.
Assuming a divine form, he fulfilled their desires;
and on the very first day of the annaprāśana ceremony, he ate various foods.
Beholding all that sovereignty, they were struck with wonder there at Keśava;
and the Blessed One, having drunk the water, assumed the form of a child.
He repeatedly took up the belching that bestowed satisfaction and rejoiced;
then Hari was there saluted by them for the sake of service.
Act in such a way that we may constantly perform service unto you;
for you are our own self, you are the supreme self, you are our essence, and you are our strength.
You are the fruit, you are the leaf, you are the flower, you are the inner core, and you are the bud;
you are the root, you are the central trunk, and you are even the branch and the sprout.
You are the vital breath and you are life; you are the food and you are the eater as well.
You are the enjoyer and you are the very object of enjoyment; likewise, you are our inner self.
You alone are the creator, the protector, the guardian, the nourisher, and likewise the place of dissolution;
you are the Supreme Brahman, the Lord, the one dearer than life, and the Master.
O Supreme Person, accept that which is within our hearts;
O Lord, protect us in our service so that we may perform service unto You. (2.11.70)
Thus addressed, Viṣṇu, seated upon his lap, laughed and said to the deities:
"O forest goddesses, you should dwell here in the hermitage of Lomaśa."
Likewise, they certainly appear in the form of maidens, as well as in the form of trees and creepers;
they take the form of vines and trees, bringing auspiciousness to their dwellings in the gardens.
"Let them remain forever for the purpose of serving me with fruits, flowers, and other offerings.
Having been addressed thus, they indeed recognized the supreme love of Nārāyaṇa.
Having received this supreme favor, they became double-bodied;
possessing the forms of trees and creepers, they dwell in the Kalpa-grove.
Then, as those girls in the form of maidens looked again and again at Keśava who was upon their laps, Lomaśa withdrew him.
And assuming a single form, he stood upon the lap of the maiden Śrīvallī;
smiling, he remembered the sage Lomaśa, his eternal preceptor. (76)
As soon as he was remembered, he appeared with a divine body;
he praised the Supreme Lord and said, "O Lord, tell me, what is your command? (77)
Hari joyfully gave those maidens, who were like forest goddesses, to him;
Lomaśa, having paid homage to those deities, led them to his hermitage.
The female attendants became devoted to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and attained the nature of Brahman; thereafter, Hari vanished and returned to his own abode.
And having been informed by Lomaśa, his father learned of all his son’s prowess and incomparable sovereignty, and attained great joy.
Then Gopālakṛṣṇaka spoke to Lomaśa:
"This one appears to be a child, yet in reality he is not truly a child. (8.1)
Marvels occur which are the deeds of a divine person;
therefore, there must exist some inconceivable Lord and Master of all.
What primary livelihood or primary action will be possible for him—whether he be a king, a preeminent deity, or even a renunciant teacher? (83)
"Tell me, what single, certain practice should be cultivated as a virtuous support?
Thus addressed, Lomaśa replied: "Clothing, alms-bowls, wealth, and so forth... (84)
"Place something before him, and know whatever he might take.
Thus addressed, the father quickly placed a means of subsistence before him.
Clothing, a bowl, a weapon, wealth, a book, a pen,
a staff, *darbha* grass, a diamond, a garland, and a handful of grain— ||86||
A sacrificial ladle, a betel nut, a thread, a fruit, a conch shell, a cowrie shell, a water vessel, a mirror, grain, and an artificial swan. ||87||
Furthermore, he placed a lamp, an umbrella, a stone, ghee, wood, as well as medicine, a flower, a clod of earth, sandals, a needle, and a sword. 88.
Having observed those thirty-two objects, the Blessed One, the Lord, also assumed thirty-two arms and touched them all simultaneously. (89)
The treasury of all arts knows every single thing;
for what is there that remains unknown to the Supreme Self, who consists of all modes of existence? (2.11.90)
"What indeed is impossible for Hari to accomplish, what is there he cannot do, or what is unknown to him?
His father was struck with wonder, and Hari indeed laughed then. (9.1)
And Lomaśa said: "The sixty-four unsurpassed arts exist here alone, in this Lord of Gods, the ancient Person, the Guru."
He shall be the creator of all, the giver of all states of existence, and the nourisher;
this eternal Supreme Self is the performer of all actions. ||93||
The mother rejoiced upon hearing and seeing her son’s splendor;
meanwhile, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, smiling, watched as many as were looking on.
Holding a book and a rosary with two hands, and a pen and kusha grass with the other two hands, he became four-armed.
Then, holding a garland and a book, he became two-armed;
placing the book upon his lap and casting the garland around his neck. (96)
Taking the lock of hair with his hand, Hari, who possessed the form of a child, laughingly placed it upon his own head and smelled the flower.
At that time, he was indeed seen as a mere child, yet bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
especially as these were held by those [deities] themselves.
Lomaśa informed his father and the others of each of those specific events; being pleased and receiving worship and hospitality,
he departed for his own hermitage, where he constantly worships that Narāyaṇa.
O Rādhikā, the beginningless wonder of Kṛṣṇa has been repeatedly experienced by me.
"He has been described as accessible through devotion, and he grants liberation even from hearing his recitation.

By me, through divine vision, those pastimes were witnessed directly. (101) Thus ends the section on the *karṇavedha* (ear-piercing) sacrament of Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the manifestation of wonders by the needle, the *Aśvinīkumāra-tīrtha*, the *annaprāśana* (first-feeding) sacrament, the feeding performed by the forest deities, the display of many wonders by the forest deities in various forms and the attainment of the beloved, and the objects such as garments and weapons held before Hari for the purpose of testing his knowledge of their functions.
The eleventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Multiformity and Divinity [of the Goddess] for the Purpose of Seizing," is concluded. || 11 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen to another purifying and delightful narrative concerning the sovereignty of Śrī Hari, which pertains to the eighth month.
In the southern part of Saurāṣṭra lies the great and supreme Vyāghrāraṇya;
to the south of that is Siṃhāraṇya, and beyond that is the ocean adorned with islands.
There was a king named Damanaka on this island, who was exceedingly cruel;
he came from the western region of Avrikta, possessing the nature of an asura.
That exceedingly cruel one forcibly took possession of the kingdom;
being powerful, he indeed paid no heed to dharma, heaven, or rebirth.
Strength is dharma, strength is sovereignty, strength is heaven, and strength is happiness;
by strength a kingdom is enjoyed, and by strength heaven is attained.
The fire, when not offered oblations, does not grant anything else but causes the depletion of the clarified butter;
sovereignty is not obtained through recitation, but sovereignty is indeed obtained through the sword.
Prosperity is not attained through praise, and fortune is acquired through battle;
a maiden is not won by wretchedness, but even a maiden is obtained through abduction.
The subjects do not follow through conciliation; they follow out of fear born of punishment.
But the gods are mere mental constructs; they neither come nor do they shine.
The food of Brahmins is in vain, as is the worship of the virtuous;
the knowledge of storytellers is false, but for those seeking the goal of man, it is truth.
The earth hangs upon the strong; servants and maidservants seek him out.
For one devoid of manly effort (puruṣārtha), there is neither wife, nor home, nor wealth. 2.12.10
That which is obtained through strength is one's own and truly ethical; that which is devoid of strength is rich in unrighteousness. Therefore, one should make strength supreme. 1.11.
Dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, as well as power itself—and nothing else—consist of sin and merit; power is everything, for there exists no other purpose for it.
The strong are happy, while the weak are poor;
moreover, fortune and prosperity, being fickle, attend upon the powerful. (1.3)
Food does not enter the mouth of a hungry, weary man;
yet for a lion roaming in the forest, food is provided.

"This one may be harmed, this one not"—such is the law established in the world; yet that is not the primary standard for heroes, for in the case of the truly preeminent, power prevails over such considerations.
Among various classes of beings here, he shall be powerful and preeminent;
among beasts, birds, and winged insects, he shall be strong and vigorous.
One who possesses strength enjoys heaven; fortune is established in strength.
It is heard that here on earth, in the region of Saurāṣṭra, there is one who is strong. (17)
The father of Kṛṣṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, was named Gopālakṛṣṇaka; he was very prosperous, exceedingly powerful, and resided in the field of Kuṅkumavāpikā. 18.
The Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, though remaining here in his childhood state,
dwells in the presence of Lomaśa, accompanied by many thousands of forces.
In the hermitage of Lomaśa, there were maidens such as Talārjantā and others,
as well as the daughters of Rākṣasas, gods, and forest-dwellers.
Furthermore, young women of exceeding beauty and wealth are protected there by the power of Bālakṛṣṇa; for they are indeed suitable for me. (21)
"Having indeed slain Lomaśa, having slain Gopālakaṛṣṇaka, and likewise having slain Bālakṛṣṇa, I shall bring them under my control. (22)
Having reflected thus, the great asura Damana summoned his own warriors and openly disclosed his heart's intention in the assembly. (23)
Mārtaṇḍa, Pracaṇḍa, Kūṣmāṇḍa, and likewise Bhāṇḍaka;
Duṣṭāṇḍa, Kaṭāhāṇḍa, Gartāṇḍa, and likewise Tāṇḍava. ||24||
Bhaṇḍa, Ṣaṇḍa, Kubhāṇḍa, Śailāṇḍa, Bhramarāṇḍaka, Harjāṇḍa, Garjāṇḍa, Jaṭhrāṇḍa, and Gṛdhrakāṇḍaka. ||25||
Gokrāṇḍa, Ghurghurāṇḍa, and Māyāṇḍa spoke to all the commanders of the army and the lords of the Dānavas, saying, "O Vīravatī! [26]
"Accompanied by an army of one hundred thousand, you must indeed be ready for battle here;
and in Saurāṣṭra, there are crores of heroic maidens at the hermitage of Lomaśa. (27)
For the sake of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, they remain protected;
Talajā resides there, as do thousands of others. (28)
They must be brought by force, for power indeed is called sovereignty;
among them, the boy most beloved shall enter in the eighth month.
It is heard that he is always endowed with great sovereignty and is not a mere child;
therefore, you practitioners of the *astras* and other weapons must remain vigilant.
"Having fully equipped the fourfold army, proceed ahead with palanquins shaped like lotuses and vehicles that travel through the sky."
"Go ahead with all your weapons to Kukumavāpikā;
the three tasks that must be accomplished must be performed even at the cost of your lives."
Those maidens must be recovered at any cost, even by means of life and wealth;
a battle must be waged against Lomaśa for his destruction.
If Kṛṣṇa, having assumed the form of a calf and grown large, should engage in battle, he must certainly be slain; this would be a most significant task.
"Thus, the three tasks to be performed have been promised at my feet.
When this was said, Kūṣmāṇḍa spoke there with humility: (35)
The beneficial words spoken by a servant should be considered, even if they are harsh;
for I am among the very hosts of Kūṣmāṇḍakas belonging to Śaṅkara. || 36 ||
Having indeed previously heard [this], Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Hari, the Supreme Self, the slayer of asuras, the slayer of daityas, and the destroyer of dānavas, remained [there]. ||37||
In the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā resides the one of divine form,
the teacher of the teachers of the destroyers of Hiraṇyakūrca and others.
Indeed, upon each single hair of his, there exist ten million times ten thousand lotuses,
wherein dwell all the deities who are the destroyers of powerful Daityas.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and others, as well as the Rudras, Vidyādharas, and so forth—
the Nāgas, Sarpas, and those stationed in the ranks of foot-soldiers— are indeed considered his servants.
If those maidens belong to that Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa as his very wealth, they must never be touched by you under any circumstances. ||41||
In that regard, I see death as the only refuge and nothing else superior;
one who desires eternal happiness should not practice excessive greed. (42)
One who desires a long life should not steal the property of others;
that which is obtained by one's own destiny cannot be taken away by anyone. 43.
That which arises for the sake of another is certainly not born for one's own sake;
once that human purpose has been accomplished, the opposite state occurs. ||44||
Women, wealth, and land nourish their own refuge;
if obtained through merit, they are beneficial, but if otherwise, they are destructive.
Longevity, fame, strength, wealth, progeny, and even sovereignty—if these should become their opposites, they will destroy [the person], without a doubt. (46)
O King, you have many wives, wealth, subjects, male and female servants, and elephants; why do you not abandon your craving? (47)
Many have perished through craving, like bees at night over a lotus;
yet many rejoice in their own possessions through contentment. (48)
"O lady, what I have spoken may indeed be bitter, yet it is sweet;
in brief, I know that nothing other than that which is consistent with the scriptures leads to happiness. (49)
Nevertheless, O King, you think that we, as your followers, must act;
for we shall certainly carry out whatever you command, even unto death.
Having spoken thus, that Kūṣmāṇḍa then ceased;
and Mārtaṇḍa and the others, having reflected upon the truth, spoke to their own lord.
O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, you desire a jewel in fire, a flower from the sun, a gem from the depths of the ocean, and blood residing within the heart.
What has been gained does not bring happiness, and what is yet to be gained will end in misery;
nevertheless, the royal command of the Supreme Lord must not be transgressed by his servants. (53)
Then Javrāṇḍa, who was aged, and his companion Maghrāṇḍa, both spoke to those truthful ones with force and the appearance of valor. (54)
But people are born and act as they do because they reside within the mind;
otherwise, if they were inactive, they would become like withered flowers in this world. (55)
Who would exert themselves toward an object that deserves investigation?
For the brave, death in battle is the goal; women, wealth, and the like are mere incidental motives. (56)
In victory there is success, but in defeat comes destruction;
death in the midst of battle is the supreme gift that grants the higher world.
Thinking exactly thus, the brave ones must go to wherever jewels are found and obtain them by means of surrendering themselves. //58//
Therefore, war must be waged and those maidens must be won;
[so too must be won] Lomaśa, Bālakṛṣṇa, and Gopālakṛṣṇaka.
"Those others who are their companions must also be slain, for they are indeed obstacles to us.
Having heard this, Jāgṛtāṇḍa reflected and spoke to the members of the assembly.
Hari alone exists as a child; Rudra and the others are not children. The thirty-three million gods who worship Kṛṣṇa are not children.
O cowards, if you wish to witness an untimely dissolution, then achieve victory and go to provide hospitality for the King of Dharma! 62.
Then Damanaka, hearing that everyone was devoid of strength,
said, "I shall go first," and took a sword in his hand.
"Let those who are greedy for life depart, leaving me and going to their own homes;
let the heroes of battle come quickly, accompanied by their armies. (64)
Thus King [Damanaka] and Damanaka spoke with wrath and valor;
then all, both those without minds and those with minds, became ready. (65)
Furthermore, as they proceeded, inauspicious omens arose for them again and again:
the sight of black snakes and even the sight of owls.
The falling of crowns and weapons, the breaking of vehicles, the sight of poverty, and likewise the sight of empty vessels; ||67||
The washerman went ahead and the barber followed him;
a crow cawed upon a dry log, and even an earthquake occurred. (68)
Flowers fell from the hair of those women,
their menses appeared even out of season, and fire consumed their home.
And at that time, the cries of beasts and birds became terrifying;
indeed, this was impelled solely by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
"Everything happens at its own time; what need is there to mention Damanaka?"—even as such ill omens were arising, O Rādhikā.
Accompanied by his army and filled with longing for Kanyakālālasā,
Damana arrived at the field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, at the hermitage of Lomaśa.
He made a sound like a conch shell and caused the drum to be beaten;
he had the battle-instruments struck in many ways by his men.
He dispatched his own messenger to the village of Lomaśa;
and Kharvaṭa, having arrived, bowed at the feet of the sage. (74)
By means of Damanaka’s counsel, he delivered this message:
"O Sage, King Damanaka is the ruler of the coastal kingdom. (75)
He announces his bowing at the feet of the venerable and worshipful one:
"In your hermitage there are tens of millions of maidens worthy of a king. (76)
"Give us [wealth] out of compassion, whether through peace, diplomacy, or war!
Lomaśa said to that village chief, "This wealth is not mine. (77)
But how can I bring myself to give wealth to Bālakṛṣṇa?
He is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord Śrī Parameśvara. ||78||
How indeed could I give up my eternal deposit?
Or rather, let him go to Bālakṛṣṇa and do as he pleases.
Thus addressed, that Kharvaṭa bowed and went toward the king;
having heard his words, Dama then spoke these sequential verses.
She urged her army to seize all the terrifying Daityas;
the host surrounded the region of Lomaśa on every side.
"Let them seize, carry off, and crush the maidens;
let the soldiers of the army return after repeatedly taking them away"—thus [he spoke] at that time. (82)
Cursing and roaring at one another, they ran toward where those maidens were; having seen them, they rushed close.
Seeing that tumultuous uproar, the girls became terrified; they remembered Hari and Lomaśa, and reported their great fear. (84)
Established in meditation there, Lomaśa, having remembered Lord Hari Bālakṛṣṇa, cast the paralyzing mantra in a mere moment. ||85||
Meanwhile, the army became as motionless as tree trunks;
everything was entirely devoid of movement, like wooden puppets. (86)
A great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose among Damanaka’s soldiers;
their leaders were utterly terrified, as if they had entered the jaws of death. (87)
Then the child Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, perceiving that extremely terrible distress of his beloved ones, went toward the maidens. 88.
Having bowed to the sage Lomaśa, the Lord, bearing the conch and discus,
gazed upon his beloved with a gentle look and stood before her for a moment, smiling.
He sat down upon the seat offered by Lomaśa;
and the maidens, agitated by fear, cried out, "Protect us, O Lord! (2.12.90).
Then Damanaka and the others, having become as motionless as stones,
took refuge in their minds with the supreme lord Lomaśa.
The offense was committed by the forces of war, not by our own strength; have mercy!
By a mere fraction of a portion of our own strength, our power has gone to ruin.
O Lord, we women are weak and powerless; therefore, having discerned us as such through our state of dullness, grant us our livelihood. (93)
Thus, with their hearts, they sought refuge at the feet of the sage Lomaśa; then the sage, full of grace toward them, [acted].
In the presence of Hari, he released the state of stupor and the paralysis;
then, they were urged on by Damana, who was of a wicked nature. (95)
Then, in order to seize the maidens again, they swooped down like hawks;
seeing their offense, the Blessed One released the Sudarśana [discus].
Consisting of flames of fire and assuming many forms,
it cut down the Daityas there by the hundreds of thousands with great speed, like grain in every direction.
In a mere instant, that army, as well as its leaders and Damaka, were all cut in two; not a single one remained.
All of them were consumed right there by the Sudarśana fire;
having brought the Sudarśana back to himself, it returned to the hand of Hari.
O Rādhikā, those whose essence is the self have attained dissolution into the form of Kṛṣṇa;
and the Blessed Lord, taking up his discus and bowing to the sage Lomaśa, [departed].
Having gazed upon and spoken repeatedly to all his dear daughters,
he indeed assumed the form of a child and came to the small couch.
In this manner, the Blessed One brought about the destruction of a hundred thousand Daityas;
for what indeed is impossible in an instant for the Lord of Śrī, the Lord of Śrī Rādhikā? 102.
There, where those asuras had perished, having been slain by the discus,
that ground on the shore of the lake became famous as Cakrakhātā.
Thus, that Cakratīrtha was born at the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake;
in this manner, the Lord brought about the removal of the earth's burden there.
For the listener, the reciter, the rememberer, or the one who causes others to recite, there shall surely be wonder; there shall indeed be liberation, or even the fulfillment of every desire. (105)

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of the Stupification of the Daitya Damana residing on the Southern Ocean by Lomaśa when he came to Lomaśa’s hermitage to abduct a maiden, and the Destruction and Liberation of him along with his army by Bālakṛṣṇa using the Sudarśana [disc]," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhā, for Śrī Narāyaṇa is indeed the purifier of the asuras;
having caused all the Daityas to merge into Himself, He led them to His own abode. || 1 ||
In this manner, the illustrious Blessed One, Puruṣottama, performed the removal of their sins for the Daityas, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, and those who were hostile and antagonistic. || 2 ||
For he is indeed the remover of the distress of those who have sought refuge in him and the bestower of liberation;
this is the grace of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Self.
For this liberation is achieved through compassion and is considered like a reward;
listen, O Rādhikā, that the demons went to liberation when they died.
And having heard this, Damanaka’s wife named Śīlahā and others [performed] the rites of piercing the rays of the heroes, such as Mārtaṇḍa and the foremost among them. || 5 ||
Dhībhakṣyā, Vānasī, Śauṇḍī, Mātīryā, Kaṇḍikā, Hṛti, Kuṇṭhā, Kāluṣikī, Dhūmrā, Pādhūlī, and Rajo’ṇḍikā. || 6 ||
Karaṃdhamī, Vikaṭī, Datkaṭī, Dāmanī, Rukhā, Dāminī, Tālajaṅghā, Dīrghikā, Daṇḍikā, and Ghaṭī. || 7 ||
Horā, Āyā, Damā, Diṣṭi, Piṣṭi, Pāmpī, Prakuṇḍikā, Karaṇḍikā, and others—these are indeed dear to the foremost [of women]. || 8 ||
Upon hearing of the death of the Daityas, they wept with loud cries;
with disheveled hair and fainting, they wailed, "Alas! We are destroyed! (9).
All their finery destroyed and deprived of all their good fortune,
more than a hundred thousand women were afflicted by the pain of widowhood, as if they were devoid of life.
Then, indeed, their venerable preceptor Śukrajīvana arrived there;
he consoled them with wise instruction and likewise explained the means of avenging their enmity.
"We shall all go and kill Lomaśa;
having slain this boy, we shall leave all the maidens without a protector. (12)
"Prepare yourselves all, you who grant life to your husband;
we shall go upon our master's path, having satisfied our enmity. (13)
She who has not perished for the sake of her husband is indeed dead even while living;
for the husband is the wealth of women, and when he is gone, all wealth is lost.
The husband is one's deity, the husband is one's fortune, and the husband alone is one's good luck;
the husband is one's master, the husband is honor, and the husband is beauty—stability resides in the husband. (15)
The hair, the bracelets, and the full curves shine when they sustain their husbands;
but upon their loss, the life of women is lost, and with it, their very birth.
Death thereafter would be meaningless; it should be meaningful. One must die while still possessing the form of virtue, without having avenged one's enmity. (17)
Death here is meaningless; it does not bring peace to the husband.
Only by avenging the enmity can one find the path that grants peace to the husband. 18.
Therefore, all of you come together, having reached a firm decision;
having fully armed yourselves, we shall fight and we shall slay the maidens.
We shall indeed tear out the matted locks of Lomaśa;
we shall carry off Bālakṛṣṇa, or even kill him.
Having thus addressed him, then hundreds of thousands and tens of millions of Daitya wives,
led by Śīlahā and others, equipped with weapons, flew up into the sky.
Spears, javelins, swords, scimitars, bhūśuṇḍīs,
mallets, iron clubs, flat-headed maces, pestles, staffs, dantaras, and tridents.
Spears, white swords, discs, battle-axes, arrows,
hair-tufts, daggers, piercing weapons, stones, staffs, and whips.
Pikes, hooks, spears, bamboo lances, fire-mouthed missiles, projectiles, fetters, nooses, reins, serpent-fetters, and leather straps. (24)
Holding axes, hatchets, wooden blocks, stones, feet, and chains—various such weapons and missiles—the Asura women [attacked]. (25)
Equipped with armor and leather, with their hair concealed by helmets, they had side-flaps, secured waistbands, and were firmly girt in their garments. (26)
Accomplishing their purpose by means of vehicles through the sky and with the sounds of musical instruments,
they arrived at Lomaśa’s hermitage, terrifying the entire world.
With eyes reddened by the drinking of liquor, heedless from the consumption of meat,
and prattling like those who are insane, they descended toward the earth.
At that time, their faces were decorated with black collyrium, horns, and other ornaments; they were terrifying, with red moons, discs, and other such marks upon their breasts. ||29||
"Cut him! Kill him! Pierce him! Eat him! Crush him! Chew him up! And destroy his life-breaths with poison and other such means! || 2.13.30 ||
Let them pull out their entrails and grind them upon the surface of a stone;
let them split open their heads and drink their blood.
"O friends, let them chew the flesh of the maidens and likewise that of Hari; O ladies of Vraja, let them tear Lomaśa into pieces! (32)
"By this, our master has indeed been killed; his ashes are here.
Let them first kill Lomaśa with their blows."
Then let them drag him through mud mixed with urine and filth, and let them cast that mud into his mouth and into his eyes. (34)
