Let them pluck out his eyes and impale him on stakes;
let them crush him between their feet and split him into two pieces.
Speaking thus, those fierce women went to the hermitage of Lomaśa and destroyed the forest trees and other things all around.
They destroyed the creepers; the tax-collectors seized [the produce], while the cruel men killed peacocks, parrots, swans, and deer.
Lomaśarṣi did not even look at those groups of women;
a man should never, under any circumstances, allow himself to be overcome by women.
Even there, the Sage did not deliberate thus, nor did he give or take [anything];
meanwhile, they arrived with weapons, intending indeed to seize him.
All the maidens set about trying to destroy the sage;
seeing this, the sage took up water from all sides.
At that time, he protected himself as well as the maidens;
however, the water he discharged took the form of fire, which burst forth and consumed them. 41.
Then the king of fires, assuming a circular form,
surrounded the great army of the Daitya women on all sides, acting as a protective wall.
Assuming the form of a canopy above, he obstructed the rākṣasīs;
burning with pain, they fled toward the abode of Bālakṛṣṇa.
Then all the maidens, as well as the eminent sage Lomaśa, said to one another: "These rākṣasīs are indeed going toward Hari."
They will kill that fool, or even his mother and father;
therefore, one must not fight with women, for men [are the ones who] always [do so]. (45)
One must indeed fight with women according to the law;
for you are all maidens, so you must wear this armor.
Let them all take up these weapons according to their respective positions;
let them hold the divine mantras and swiftly destroy those [enemies]. 47.
Having spoken thus, Lomaśa then quickly caused the maidens—who were protecting the life of their husband—to hear the *Śrīsvāmika-vaktra* (the armor of the Lord). 48.
Having sipped water three times, meditated upon Hari, and likewise performed the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma) three times, [one should pray]:
"May the head of Hari be upon my head, and his face upon my face. (49)
May the eyes of this Hari be in my eyes; may His ears indeed be in my ears; may Hari’s throat be in my throat; and may Hari’s hands be in my hands.
On my chest are his two breasts, and likewise on Hari’s chest are mine;
on my belly is Hari’s belly, and on Hari’s waist is my waist. (51)
Back upon back, my hips upon the hips of Hari;
likewise, the private parts upon the private parts, and the thighs upon the thighs, and the feet upon the feet. (52)
"May every form of Hari reside within me, who am composed of all forms.
Having performed the nyāsas in this manner, one should recite the Svāmika-vacana.
Oṃ, may the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the possessor of all power, who has ascended his divine celestial chariot, grant us protection from everything. ||54||
May Hari, who holds the conch, discus, mace, lotus, shield, sword, bow, noose, bow, trident, and arrow, protect us from all weapons. 55.
May He whose divine stride is in the sky protect us; may Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa in fire protect us;
may the Lord of Prāṇa protect us in the wind; and may the Master, higher than the highest, protect us in the water. (56)
May Bālakṛṣṇa protect us on the earth; may Puruṣottama protect us in battle;
may the Lord, established in his fruitfulness, protect us from the discharge of weapons, missiles, and mantras. (57)
May the Lord of Śrī, the Inner Self, protect [us] from the illusions of Indra’s net and the like; may Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the beloved Master, protect [us] from the force of time. (58)
May the Beloved of Kṛṣṇa protect us from Rākṣasīs through his vigilance;
may the Lover of Kṛṣṇa protect us from diseases, anxieties, and inconceivable fears. (59)
May the Lord, whose abode is the Imperishable, protect us from material transformations;
may He, who dwells within, protect us from all things in all conditions. (2.13.60)
Withdraw the army of rākṣasīs, protect the multitude of maidens, gladden us, and then grant us victory, O Supreme Lord! (6.1)
May Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa of Oḍra protect him;
salutations always to Lomaśa, the sage of Svāmikavaca. 62.
May there be salutation to Kambharā Śrī Mahālakṣmī, the protectress;
may there be salutation to Nārāyaṇa and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa. May it be auspicious.
Thus uttered, this armor,
assuming a form of ten million [rays], instantly became blazing like a circle of ten million suns.
Those maidens held [the child] along with you, O Rādhikā—Mañjulā, Pārvatī, Lakṣmī, Prabhā, Haṃsā, and Māṇikī. (65)
Tens of millions [of beings] donned golden-hued armor that was free from cuts, unblemished, inseparable [from them], and filled their bodies.
Having held that which was both soft and harsh, pleasant to the touch and protective,
they drank the mantras of weapons and missiles along with water.
Through compassion, they simultaneously became enriched with the mantras of Kanyākāvarman:
"Oṃ kṣaḥ phaṭ svāhā! May the beloved of Kṛṣṇa devour this for the sake of his beloved. (68)
Then they chanted this mantra one hundred and eight times;
for he who is remembered is indeed the protector in all battles and in other circumstances as well.
After that, Lomaśa gave those two women this mantra, which they held and recited; he likewise bestowed upon them the supernatural powers beginning with atomization (aṇimā).
All sovereign powers, even those that are invincible,
as well as Sandhinī, Yojinī, Kṣatavāriṇī, and Śūlahāriṇī— [these he bestowed].
He indeed bestowed thousands of sciences along with the ritual rinsing of water;
[he is] the abode of manifold forms and the upholder of both the false and the true.
Then he bestowed upon him the power of invisibility, rebirth, and all branches of knowledge,
as well as ten billion maidens dressed in military attire, all arriving swiftly.
By sprinkling drops of water, the sage Lomaśa caused musical instruments, vehicles, and [the forms of] elephants, lions, and horses to appear. (74)
In an instant, he turned the vehicles of the swans and Garuḍas into water;
meanwhile, musical instruments were sounded and young maidens flew up into the sky.
Where the blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, the infant master, was staying within the house; having gone there in a moment's meditation, they reached the sky and stood before him. 76.
To ward off the armies of the rākṣasīs, Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Śrī, Pārvatī, Māṇikī, and Prabhā stood ready. (77)
Maṅgalā, Manasā, Revā, Bhārgavī, Sarasvatī, Gaṅgā, Mañjulā, Bhakti, Muktikā, Ekādaśī, and Rati. (78)
Haṃsā, Saguṇā, Tulasī, Kamalā, Virajā, Satī, Mūrti, Gomatī, Svarṇarekhā, Jayā, and Nandinī. (79)
Durgā, Lalitā, Sāvitrī, Dolā, Puṣpā, Kalāvatī, Badarī, Mādhavī, Pampā, Ṣaṣṭhī, Prīti, and Ṛtadhvajī. (2.13.80)
Mauktikā, Lāḍakī, Devī, Manu, Kastūrikā, Sitā, Haimī, Śānti, Praśāntā, Campā, Godāvarī, and Yamī. (8.1)
Ojasvatī, Savitrī, Ratnā, Miṣṭāmṛtā, Dhani, Caturā, Vajrikā, Muktā, Suśīlā, Śyāmikā, and Amalā. (82)
Santuṣṭā, Candrikā, Kānti, Kuṃvarī, Śivā, and others—these and another hundred and forty who were foremost among them [were there]. (83)
At that time, millions of powerful beings stood at the forefront in the generalship;
they raised shouts of joy, crying out, "Victory to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! (84)
Victory, O Beloved! Victory, O Great Beloved! Victory indeed, O Supreme Lord!
Victory, O Master! Victory, O Protector! And may Lomaśa also be victorious here! 85.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā!
Thus chanting this mantra, the demonesses restrained [the enemy]. (86)
Having swallowed this, Kṛṣṇakānta [uttered] "Oṃ kṣaḥ phaṭ svāhā" for the sake of his beloved; then, performing the recitation of this mantra, he warded off the demonesses. (87)
Seeing the army of rākṣasīs suddenly arrive from the path of the sky, the parents, the residents, and others [were struck with fear]. (88)
Then, having become a young calf, Bālakṛṣṇa spoke to his parents: "There is no need to fear at all, not at all, indeed not at all. (89)
The Rākṣasīs have come to fight out of enmity toward the widow who has departed;
yet, women must never be slain by me, nor indeed by any man anywhere. (2.13.90)
Lomaśa was never, under any circumstances, to be killed, because that king of gurus had established protection for the hermitage through fire. 9.1.
Frightened by that, they have indeed come here to kill me;
let these maidens, sent by Lomaśa, fight against them.
Armed with mantras as their weapons and missiles, and strengthened by the power of battle and other arts, these [energies] exist in the sky in the form of armies by the millions. 93.
"O Mother, it is not at all surprising that I desire to fight out of my own will," Kṛṣṇa said; and upon these words, [he mounted] Garuḍa, whose horses are swans.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara gave divine elephants, celestial vehicles, chariots, and aerial palaces to the maidens in the sky. 95.
While the great army of heroic maidens was being adorned with mounts,
the Rākṣasa women sprang up from all sides.
Then they struck that group of heroines most fiercely;
those maidens, fierce in battle, returned the blows.
The trumpeting of elephants, horses, swans, and Garuḍas,
along with the roaring of lions and the celestial chariots, completely overwhelmed the fierce thundering.
Likewise, there arose cries of donkeys, camels, and cocks, as well as of Rākṣasas, dogs, and jackals, directed against him. 99.
Indeed, there were frequent collisions of missiles, weapons, and arrows, as well as of murderous women, against one another’s bodies. (2.13.100)
Some struck them with javelins, others slew them with swords;
some, seizing them by the hair, threw them down upon the surface of the earth. || 10.1 ||
Some struck them with maces, others with clubs, still others with slings, and yet others struck them with swords. (102)
Others [assailed] with swords, others with stones, rocks, and slings;
likewise others with chains, staffs, iron arrows, and shafts.
There, the rākṣasīs were slain, but not the maidens while they were still alive;
some were killed with spears and mallets, and others likewise with bhūśuṇḍī weapons.
Burning with the fire of anger and enraged by the gnashing of their lips,
they strike with clubs, teeth, tridents, mallets, and sharp-edged spears.
The foolish Māras fell indeed, struck by white swords, spears,
lances, arrows, discuses, and pestles.
With knives, stones, clubs, and piercing instruments,
their cranial apertures are pierced and their thighs and arms are cut asunder.
Their hearts, breasts, and heads are torn asunder by spikes, kusha-grass arrows, bhalla-javelins, bamboo shafts, and fire-tipped missiles.
They are bound with nooses of light-rays and cast down by anklets and other ornaments;
headless trunks are split asunder by axes and hatchets.
Then they were beaten with chains and burned by fires;
the Rākṣasa women struck the maidens against one another with blinding blows.
Thus, indeed, a tumultuous battle broke out there;
amidst the roars of the combatants, not a single word could be heard. (111)

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Commencement of the Tumultuous Battle between the Rākṣasīs and the Maidens in the Vicinity of Aśvapaṭṭasara," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 13 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen to the terrifying battle of the fierce women,
the rākṣasīs who were the wives of the jackal-king.
It was terrible, causing total destruction and consisting of the surrender of one's life;
since their husbands had died there, they resolved to die there amidst the ashes.
Thinking thus, they fought as if their lives were at stake;
having cast aside all fear upon seeing Hari, they cried out, "Kill him! Kill him! || 3 ||
"Let them be cut into pieces and portions for the ritual brooms! they cried out, like the surging flood of the ocean on the day of the full moon.
Likewise, the army of the Rākṣasīs fell upon the house of Bālakṛṣṇa;
the great host of maidens was mingled with them at that time, not separate.
And because those cruel ones shone forth even after death, in order to rescue Bālakṛṣṇa as before, by force and however it might be.
"He must be captured or killed; while he lives, he shall not remain alive!
Thinking thus, they rushed forward to slay him, making his death their primary objective.
Just as locusts fall from the sky onto the surface of the earth at the time of universal dissolution,
so did all those Rākṣasīs fall upon the child’s bedchamber.
Having thus observed this reversal, the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa then,
smiling, caused the field of Kuṅkumavāpī to vanish.
Seeing everything there— on that site of the house in the forest— to have suddenly become composed of water, the rākṣasīs departed into the sky in despair.
Filled with intense rage, they waged a great battle against the maidens;
those maidens of divine bodies were struck down by millions of weapons. || 11 ||
And their bodies do not break apart like lumps of iron heated in fire;
nor do sufferings arise, nor do they undergo any severing.
Protected by the armor of their Lord and guarded by protective mantras, the wives of Kṛṣṇa do not die; the wives of the Daityas, however, do die.
At that time, the daughters were cut into many pieces by the fierce weapons;
having become divided in two, that Rākṣasī was no longer one.
She who was alive has been slain; she has departed and gone, and will surely not return again.
The sky is completely pervaded by battle and adorned by the fierce warrior.
He became filled with joy and granted many spaces;
indeed, at a distance of a thousand krośas away, there was then space for battle.

Throughout the entire land of Surāṣṭra, there was not even a single man to be found at that time who would venture into the fray amidst those women numbering in the tens of millions, billions, and trillions.
The headless trunks, heads, arms, breasts, thighs, and hips of the Rākṣasīs fell from the sky, descending from the heavens.
A rain of blood, a rain of flesh, and a rain of lumps occurred;
indeed, there was a rain of hair, a rain of weapons, and a rain of corpses.
A rain of limbs and a rain of moon-like fragments occurred; their bodies, exceedingly tender and like fresh butter, were torn asunder.
For the sake of their god-like husbands, the beloved groups of women threw themselves at one another;
hearing this, King Yama arrived to witness the battle for a moment.
The gods, who move through the sky, observe the battle but do not originate from the elements;
when it was realized by the hosts of Daitya women that their own destruction was at hand. || 22 ||
Then, having consecrated the Kanyakās with mantras,
he released divine missiles capable of destroying all beings.
Then the rākṣasīs first discharged the weapon of tears;
that vapor rose into the sky, and it was not even known whether it were grass or anything else.
The ray-weapon discharged by Lakṣmī became the destroyer of tears;
then Śukrajīvanī indeed released the smoke-colored weapon (dhūmrāstraka).
Her garment was shrouded in smoke, and a flame indeed arose from her eyes;
then Añjanī performed the entire ritual of inhaling the smoke.
There he released the Vahni weapon, which causes the destruction of the Rākṣasa's form;
Śukra, for his part, released the Megha weapon there, which restores life.
Then Vṛndā discharged the great Śālagrāma weapon;
indeed, the Śāla-mountain peaks struck the rākṣasīs in the sky.
Then the Rākṣasī Koṭarā swallowed the Śālagrāma weapon;
thereupon Śukrajīvanī discharged a weapon of dust, thick with powder.
Then Añjanī discharged the Vāyumantra weapon,
and Ṣaṇḍikā launched the Nāgāstra in every direction.
Then Kamalā discharged the Gāruḍa weapon, which brings happiness,
and the Rākṣasī Vikhātā then discharged the scorpion weapon.
Then Garuḍī again released the cillikā weapon;
it brought about a rain of fire-atom arrows that was life-destroying for some and life-giving for Śukra.
Then Śāradā effortlessly swallowed the shower of fire;
thereafter, those wives of the Rākṣasa engaged in illusory combat.
The Maruts created stones, trees, flesh, blood,
and pus, as well as streams of liquor, arrows, and weapons in every direction.
They rained down extremely fierce weapons from all sides— crushing powders mixed with fire,
as well as sharp missiles consisting of excrement, urine, and the like.
Then a cry of "Alas! Alas! arose among the groups of maidens on the earth;
at that time, the circle of Yoginīs consisting of sixty-four groups [was present].
Having assumed forms equal to mountains, all those illusions born of falsehood repeatedly swallowed [him]. (37)
Then, those Māyās, whose nature is like a shower of rain and who had been overcome by the power of the Yoginīs, dissolved once again, reaching their dissolution back to the very root.
A shower of corpses was brought down upon the city named Pherucita;
indeed, millions of corpses, as well as those of women, fell from the sky. (39)
And likewise, the corpses of female hens, vultures, crows, female parrots, female hawks, female vultures, and female pigeons. || 2.14.40 ||
Flesh-eating female owls, hawks, and crows fell there from the sky, and the surface of the earth became completely covered. (41)
Then, beholding Śambhu, the great chaste Bhairavī indeed assumed her own form, ten yojanas in length.
He simultaneously seized all one hundred thousand rākṣasīs who were emitting corpses from their hundreds of thousands of arms, and then he crushed them.
Then, with hundreds of thousands of feet, those fools created a great tumult;
the creation of corpses came to an end, and false illusion vanished into dissolution. 44.
Then, at that time, the wives of the Daityas fell into the hands of Bhairavī; in order to deceive her and escape from her grasp, they made an effort,
and each one of them assumed countless forms within her hand.
Some were ten, some fifty, and others a hundred. ||46||
Just as the beads were not on her hand, so did those digits move about;
then Bhairavī performed the increasing of her own hands. 47.
Likewise, those rākṣasīs then assumed their own growth;
thus, there was indeed a great burden in the creation of countless bodies.
Having emerged from the fist of Bhairavīkāra, they stood in the path of the sky and roared repeatedly at the head of Bhairavī. 49.
Countless Rākṣasa women beat him excessively; standing in a life-threatening situation, they did not even consider the fear of death.
Then Mahālakṣmī beheld those innumerable rākṣasīs, who possessed countless forms and assumed infinite manifestations.
Mahālakṣmī herself, remembering Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
assumed a form equal to the universe and endowed with ten million arms.
The planets, constellations, stars, and so forth indeed hang from her hair;
she is truly most terrible, striking with all kinds of weapons. (53)
Seizing them again and again, he repeatedly slew the rākṣasīs;
others had four hands, and still others had eight hands.
Others are sixteen cubits long, others are endowed with thirty-two cubits, some possess sixty-four arms, and there are those with hundreds of thousands of excellent hands. ||55||
And ten thousand hands were created by Mahālakṣmī;
leaping up again and again into the sky, they struck down those rākṣasīs.
Many there were slain, lost, and fell lifeless, tormented;
but those who died remained truly dead, deprived of any further rising.
Then they entered into the being of Mahālakṣmī;
however, all the strength of the Rākṣasa women, exceeding half [of their original power], was destroyed.
Then, for a moment, Mahālakṣmī, Bhīrulakṣmī, and the other Lakṣmīs,
having beheld their own victory, sounded the war-trumpets.
Then the maidens, together with Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, attained great joy.
Now, there was a certain Rākṣasī named Rūḍhikā there, who had the form of a mountain.
Having become so, she quickly fell from the sky upon Bālakṛṣṇa;
at that moment, the grains of rice became like a great mountain-cave.
The sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, protected by the Talāja mountain, became pregnant with a maiden; from that, all fear departed far away.
Rūṇḍhikā, by her speed, fell upon the mountain of parched grain;
cut, shattered, and split apart by its peaks, she died. (63)
Then another [form], consisting of the earth itself,
entered the surface of the ground and became long in shape, indeed extending for a hundred yojanas.
Having assumed the form of a female frog, ten yojanas in height,
she made the lower lip of the earth exceedingly beautiful, appearing like its very foundation.
The upper lip was made to be like heaven, endowed with all stars and the sky,
where indeed no confusion of any kind could cause fear.
Having acted thus through deceit, all the maidens likewise [reached] the sacred field of Kuṃkumavāpikā and the Aśvapaṭṭa lake.
She also placed the hermitage of Lomaśa in the middle of her mouth;
meanwhile, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, having understood that wicked deed, [acted accordingly].
For the sake of destroying the Rākṣasī and likewise to manifest a wonder,
he himself indeed assumed the form of a maiden among the maidens.
Then, for a moment, Kṛṣṇa shone with the divine Sudarśana discus held in his hand, while the maiden named Kṛṣṇā stood at his throat.
He released the Sudarśana, endowed with great splendor and fire;
with that wheel joined by fire, he [severed] her neck, mouth, and belly.
In an instant, he indeed cut that Maṇḍūkī Rūṇḍhikā into pieces;
from her fat and bones were born the Cākacakyas and Ciroṭikas.
Then another rākṣasī named Dāminī, seeing that Dardūrikā was indeed dead,
herself assumed a form composed of radiant energy.
Then, opening her mouth wide, she swallowed the Sudarśana discus of Viṣṇu, which pervaded the sky and was filled with garlands of great lightning-flames.
Having pierced through that [city], the Sudarśana [cakra] emerged instantly, falling upon the earth just as flashes of lightning descend. (75)
The Rākṣasī Dāminī fell to the earth in pieces;
then another, Dyuhanā, manifested there a body like that of the sun.
Placing Bālakṛṣṇa in his mouth, he leaped up toward the sky and heaven;
meanwhile, Vīraśi beheld the sage Lomaśa there.
Having placed [the child] in his mouth, he leaped upward and went far into the sky,
where the boy Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and Lomaśa, the king of yogis, were also present.
Both of them were born there in the womb in the form of fire; indeed, they were terrible.
They blazed up with fire, and the two Rākṣasīs likewise perished.
Having split open her belly, the two—Lomaśa and Acyuta—emerged;
then another lightning bolt, in the form of fire, appeared in that hermitage.
He quickly burned the entire hermitage of Lomaśa and the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā with fire, until only a small remnant remained.
Bālāhakī Mahālakṣmī indeed assumed the form of rain;
she obstructed the fire and extinguished it with her showers.
Having seized Dāminī there, the virtuous woman struck her with all her might;
Dāminī died there, her hands and feet outstretched.
Then another rakshasi woman, named Dhībhakṣyā, who was enamored of the demon,
took the goddess Kambharālakṣmī upon her shoulder and flew into the sky.
Upon seeing her, that virtuous woman then struck the devourer of intellect with her fist;
the devourer of intellect died and quickly fell from the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head).
As Śauṇḍī, assuming the form of a tigress, was about to seize her father Gopālakṛṣṇa, Pārvatī became a lioness. ||86||
Having become a tigress, she devoured her; then her father became healthy once more.
Then, by other maidens who were fierce in battle and possessed of strength on all sides, [she was consumed]. (87)
There, all those who were struck down died, with only about a hundred remaining;
at that time, Kuṇṭhā, Iṣṭidā, and the others sought refuge.
Those widows, stripped of their weapons and bound in fetters by the maidens, remembered Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and prostrated themselves before him. ||89||
Immersed in fear, they wept and entreated the Lord:
"O Kṛṣṇa, our protectors have indeed been slain; we have come to you for refuge. (2.14.90)
O Supreme Lord, O Great Sovereign, deliver me from this great suffering caused by hundreds of thousands,
millions, and tens of millions of women, both natural and artificial.
"Perform the funeral rites for the deceased Rākṣasīs;
but we, O Kṛṣṇa, though your beloveds, are indeed weak and have been slain. (92)
"Where are we going, O ocean of mercy? Make us your own servants!
[Make] Lakṣmī, Ramā, Rādhā, Śrī, Satī, Pārvatī, and Prabhā likewise. (93)
O Lord, make Māṇikyā, Mañjulā, and their maidservants Nainjas;
or else, O Mādhava, ordain maidservants for those maidservants as well. 94.
Without you, no other home is considered to grant happiness in the future;
we, however, are deprived of both, so how indeed shall we obtain happiness? (95)
Therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, forgive our most terrible deed; having consumed it with your own power, protect us and grant us a divine state. 96.
The gods, the enjoyers, the Daityas, the Dānavas, the Rākṣasas, the birds,
the sages, the seers, mortals, trees, and so forth— these are their offspring.
Born in your lineage and having attained your yoga,
how can we live in sin, having come to this unattainable state?
"Make us all purifying [rivers], entirely free from the nature of rākṣasas"—thus was the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa entreated by them. (99)
All of them [were overcome] by divine vision, by divine sprinkling with water,
by feelings of hatred toward him, and by his constant remembrance.
Then she rendered those cows free from sin and devoid of fear,
having placed them inside the mouths of the Kāmadhenu cows from within the belly of the cow.
Having been expelled right there by Lomaśa through the urinary passage,
they became fit for Brahman, possessing divine bodies like those of Ramā.
Then they forgot their own births, purificatory rites, and bodies;
they became like divine goddesses, as if born from the digits of the moon.
All those maidens, desiring Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
were gentle, twelve years of age, devoted to Viṣṇu, and adorned with sectarian marks.
O Rādhikā, by the power of Kṛṣṇa, who acts in such a wondrous way,
those who were then slain in battle became absorbed into the form of Kṛṣṇa.
And all those divine maidens emerged from the body of Kṛṣṇa;
numbering one hundred thousand, they were stainless and wore garments as radiant as the sun.
Adorned with bracelets, crowns, armlets, earrings,
and girdles, the beloved wives were born in an instant from the horse of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā!
Śrī Lomaśa bestowed this mantra upon them in the presence of Śrī Hari. (1.08)
Having caused the oblation to be performed for them and for others as well, Lomaśa gave them sacred threads, yellow garments, and garlands.
Then he gave him garlands of tulasī and rosaries for his neck;
he also gave him the marks of the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus.
All those who were there in the battle—Ramā and the others, numbering ten million maidens—were fed, initiated, and protected at the hermitage of Lomaśa. || 111 ||
There, the Lord of Kṛṣṇa gave them supreme bliss beyond the beyond;
embracing them with his arms and pressing them against his own chest. (11.2)
Then the Lord gave words of blessing and benediction, as well as kisses;
meanwhile, the exhaustion from battle and the fatigue from handling missiles, weapons, and the like vanished.
In an instant everything ceased, and not even a hair’s breadth of injury occurred;
there, a great cry of victory arose for all of them.
All were fed, honored, and embraced by the compassionate one;
they were kissed upon his chest, pressed close, and made immortal.
A great festival was held there on account of the victory, and the gods and others arrived; they were honored and fed.
Having departed just as they had come, Lomaśa, the king of sages,
then indeed bestowed new names upon the hundred thousand maidens.
The sage Lomaśa gave her auspicious names such as Suśīlā, Susahā, Vidyut, Kiraṇā, Candrikā, and Dyuti.
By the command of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, he led them all to the hermitage;
then Pṛthvī was summoned by Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Then the Earth herself leveled the battlefield;
she removed all impurities and made the ground pure.
Then that auspicious ground was washed by the rain from the sky;
thus it became known as Lakṣatīrtha, honored by Kṛṣṇa.
The Lord preserved in his own palace those weapons—
both divine and material— which had fallen there during the battle.
Thus indeed, O Rādhikā, did that battle take place there in ancient times; it was never before, nor will it ever be again, a battle that grants women such a divine destination.
By the will of Hari, two forms of each of the hundred thousand maidens were produced,
and each of them ascended a celestial chariot.
Having become so, she was led by her attendants to the supreme state of the Absolute (paramākṣara);
and she appeared in a second form as a maiden, residing in the hermitage of Lomaśa.
Thus, O Rādhikā, this most wonderful and supreme divine narrative of Hari, consisting of a battle between women, has been told to you here. 126.
By reading this, by hearing it, by reflecting upon it, and likewise by offering it [to others],
one attains the state of being beloved to Kṛṣṇa and shall find a destination in the world of Brahmā.

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Rakshasis' Defeat and Imminent Destruction in Battle with Countless Warrior Maidens, and Ultimately Their Seeking Refuge, Attaining the State of Liberation and the Status of Maidens through the Grace of Bāla-Kṛṣṇa," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to the most purifying account of those women who attained the state of Ramā through union with the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa entrusted them to Lomaśa for the purpose of their residence and protection in his hermitage. || 2 ||

Having attained their divine forms and having reached the state of perpetual youth, they nevertheless had not yet obtained the lamp of knowledge; for this very reason, [the following] occurs in the narrative.
Or during an exposition, those whose intellects have not been revealed remain devoid of aesthetic flavor;
indeed, in the assembly, they behave like fools through their silence.
They did not know self-knowledge, nor did they know the bull-like austerity;
being ignorant of the dharmas of liberation, they were like lamps hidden beneath a cover.
But all of them, rich with the desire for liberation and devoted to the dawning of knowledge, O Rādhikā, questioned Lomaśa, the sun of wisdom.
Just as a female bee makes insects her own through her sting,
so too does the man of knowledge, bestowing wisdom, make the blind possessed of sight.
O Guru, grant us that knowledge which bestows liberation and grants peace from suffering;
for the female form is always devoid of true knowledge and is merely a locus for latent impressions (vāsanā).
Liberation arises precisely from that which is the locus of the defects; therefore, it is not produced [from elsewhere].
[This is taught] so that liberation may come to be, and so that the destruction of the defects may occur. (9)
In such a way that Kṛṣṇa may be pleased,
please instruct us— us who are straightforward, who bear the burden of our duties, and who are but women.
Thus requested, Lomaśa, on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, instructed all of them in the auspicious duties of the vow.
"O daughters, the Ekādaśī vow is supreme and removes all sins;
it was observed by me without water, without food, and likewise with a night vigil. (12)
That śrāddha which includes the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is accompanied by the propitiation of Kṛṣṇa,
involves association with the virtuous, and entails the restraint of the senses, is indeed a destroyer of sins and a bestower of liberation.
It bestows the grace of Kṛṣṇa and likewise grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
today, at dawn, perform the worship of Hari as Bālakṛṣṇa during this vow.
Go and perform worship with flowers and other offerings, fruits, water, and sandalwood; offer yourselves through circumambulations that arise from the heart and are most enchanting.
By the giving of food and the giving of drinks, by swinging on hammocks, by dancing and singing, by gestures and expressions of love, and by constant pleasing services; (16)
By restraining the senses and observing silence, perform a vow dedicated to Kṛṣṇa, entirely free from worldly objects, solely for the sake of his grace. (17)
Thus addressed, those young maidens observed the vow consisting of fasting from water,
beginning on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, accompanied by a vigil.
The gracious Bālakṛṣṇa caused them to behold Vaikuṇṭha and revealed his own form with four beautiful arms.
He bestowed [them] attended by the splendors of numerous retinues and other riches;
and those beloved consorts of Śrī Hari considered themselves to have fulfilled their purpose.
They kept a vigil at night and performed the breaking of the fast in the morning;
then they questioned Lomaśa, as he sat, regarding the compendium of dharma.
What should always be served that destroys sin, bestows merit, grants liberation and heaven, and wards off the hardships of Yama? (22)
Then Lomaśa said to him: "Such cows as these should be served;
cows consist of all the gods, they are goddesses, and they are oceans of nectar. (23)
The Tārikās are in the form of sacred fords; they are pure and bestowers of nourishment.
Their service should always be performed, as it grants all gains. 24.
By the offering of a single cow, the deities and others are gratified;
for all the thirty gods are pleased by curd, and Maheśvara by milk. (25)
The Purifier (Agni) is always pleased by clarified butter, and the Grandfather (Brahmā) by milk-rice;
by giving a cow and drinking cow's milk, a man becomes pure and gratified.
The five products of the cow (pañcagavya) are supremely purifying and bestow the fruit of the horse sacrifice (vājimedha).
Among the teeth of the cow are the Maruts, and on her tongue is Sarasvatī.
The Gandharvas are in the middle of his hooves, while the Pannagas are on the tips of his hooves;
the Sādhyas are in all his joints, and the Moon and Sun are in his two eyes.
All the Kṣatriyas are in its hump; Dharma is established in its tail;
all sacred fords are in its anus; and the river Gaṅgā is in its urine. (29)
The oceans reside in her udders, while the great sages dwell in the pores of her skin;
Lakṣmī resides in her dung, and all powers abide in her hair.
Fortitude, steadfastness, peace, nourishment, growth, as well as memory, intelligence, modesty, physical form, fame, learning, intellect, and progeny; || 31 ||
The cows, who are the wives of Dharma and the embodiments of devotion, always abide within cattle; when given to a worthy recipient, they follow the deceased. (32)
Where there are cows, there is prosperity, righteousness, knowledge, and the deities;
even the immortals were brought into being by means of cows that had been given away. 33.
Therefore, worship the wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenus) in the hermitage;
this great and auspicious dharma has been proclaimed by me here in the forest. ||34||
Having heard this, those young maidens performed auspicious service to the cows;
then they questioned another upholder of dharma regarding what brings welfare.
Is there any other service comparable to the service of cows, by which both worldly enjoyment and liberation may bring auspiciousness to women? (36)
Lomaśa then said: "Such is the service of a husband;
indeed, through service to one's master, heaven, liberation, and happiness are obtained. (37)
Having drunk the water from her husband’s feet, she is glorified in the world of Brahmā;
for the husband alone is the Supreme Brahman, and the husband is the gift, the vow, and the sacrifice. (38)
Obedience to the husband is the supreme duty; through that, women indeed attain liberation.
For all the gods and all sacred injunctions reside within the word of the husband. (39)
But for those whose husband is their god and is pleased, the Supreme Lord is pleased;
she who sleeps when he sleeps and certainly wakes when he wakes. (2.15.40)
She who eats only after her daughters have been fed certainly conquers death;
she who remains silent when [others] are silent, and she who remains standing when [others] are standing. (41)
A daughter who possesses single-minded vision, a focused mind, and who carries out the commands of her husband, conquers death; there is nothing else that brings victory over death. 42.
The messengers of Yama fear her; that virtuous woman is honored by the gods.
Addressed with love by her husband, she would not refuse him. (43)
A woman who is dear to her husband never goes to another deity other than her husband;
that devoted wife, equal to Lakṣmī, does not enter the mouth of death. 44.
"He is my mother, he is my father, he is my kinsman; he is my supreme deity.
She who serves him in this manner certainly conquers death. (45)
Meditating upon her husband, following after her husband, and thinking of her husband, she never beholds the realm of Yama at any time. (46)
She who does not look upon another with her mind while bathing, sitting, traveling, or during such acts as grooming her hair, never beholds Yama.
She who does not abandon her husband when he is worshipping the deities, eating, or sleeping comfortably shall conquer death and time. 48.
That woman who always sweeps the house before the sun has risen, and remains devoted to the service of her husband, does not behold the world of Yama. ||49||
Endowed with purity and proper conduct, she who gazes upon the face of her husband does not behold the door of death for her husband. 2.15.50.
Devoted to their husbands, truthful in speech, unconquered, and serving their lords,
those who are free from violence never go to the world of Yama.
Maidens devoted to celibacy, widows who have maintained their dharma,
devotees of Hari, and female servants of the virtuous do not go to the city of Yama.
Likewise, those who are established in knowledge, who have attained supreme wisdom, who are composed in meditation,
and who give up their lives for the sake of their master, do not go to the city of Yama.
Those who give gifts, those who serve their mother, father, husband, and true guru, and those who bestow sesame, cows, and gold, do not go to the abode of Yama. (54)
Those who observe the four-month vow, who follow the mind of their guru,
and who constantly listen to sacred discourses do not go to the abode of Yama.
Through austerity, heaven is attained, as well as fame, long life, happiness, and so forth;
likewise, knowledge, realization, health, beauty, good fortune, and prosperity. (56)
Enjoyments are attained through austerity, and the supreme state through devotion to Viṣṇu;
those who subsist on water go to heaven, and those who give wealth attain abundance of riches. (97)
Through service to the guru, they attain worldly enjoyment and liberation through meditation;
through the ancestral rite (śrāddha), they obtain progeny, and for those who subsist on leaves, heaven shall be attained.
For those who subsist on fruits and roots, sovereignty shall come; for those who serve cows, liberation shall arise;
and by the gift of flavorful juices, good fortune is produced.
Through the gift of food and drink, eternal satisfaction arises;
through the offering of fragrant scents, one is fully gratified by sensual enjoyments. (2.15.60)
Through fruits one obtains a son; through flowers, supreme good fortune;
and by the gift of fearlessness, one shall attain all desires.
He who grants fearlessness to a living being gives them freedom from fear;
by means of that worthy recipient, the deliverance of both [the giver and the receiver] shall come to pass.
Through association with the beginningless Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa and by service to the virtuous, all that is inauspicious comes to an end; therefore [one should pursue these]. ||63||
A virtuous intellect arises that bestows liberation and the fruit of the Self;
likewise, auspicious action is born which destroys afflictions and removes evil. (64)
Heaven is the attainment of auspicious fruits, while hell arises from sin;
one should always strive for that which is excellent and fruit-bearing, never for that which is inauspicious.
Non-violence toward all beings, free from craving and anger, and devoid of harmful action—this universal quality certainly delivers one across [the ocean of existence]. //66//
A woman who remains forever free from desire, who is not greedy for desired objects,
and who, through detachment, is fixed upon Hari, crosses the ocean.
A woman who is faithful and free from malice, devoted to serving her teacher,
of noble character, and rich in dharma, crosses the ocean.
She who performs what is praiseworthy and avoids what is blameworthy, remaining ever engaged in auspiciousness, is liberated from all evil. (69)
She who, with a pure mind, frequents sacred sites—both stationary and moving—and constantly serves the virtuous, attains the supreme goal. (2.15.70)
The illustrious young maidens said: "Tell us that which involves little effort and is easy in every respect, [to counteract] the various births arising from inauspicious actions. (7.1)
"O one rich in asceticism, tell us that which is capable of shattering [this doubt].
Śrī Lomaśa said: "When Hari, the bestower of liberation, has arrived, and when the virtuous people and the guru have arrived... (72)
Whatever service one may perform with a pure inner self, that service is indeed a straightforward means for the destruction of unwholesome karma. //73//
Having seen holy men, she who bows down to them is liberated from sins—whatever impurity has been committed through thought, deed, or speech. (74)
Having offered [the image] to Kṛṣṇakānta, she becomes pure and attains liberation.
One should worship Kṛṣṇa during the sun and Kṛṣṇa during the moon, and Janārdana among the cows. (75)
She who beholds Kṛṣṇa in her guru shall be liberated from bondage—
[he who beholds] the saintly husband, the guru, the deity, the cow, the parents, the chaste wife, and the twice-born.
Having seen [it], one should bow, meditate, and perform circumambulation;
by doing so, one quickly abandons misdeeds and is liberated from bondage. (77)
Cows are purifying, auspicious, and even the deities of the gods;
she who serves them with devotion is liberated from all sins. (78)
She who drinks the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) during an auspicious moment is liberated from all sins committed throughout her life at that very instant. ||79||
That virtuous woman who receives upon her head the water drawn up by the tail is liberated from all sins, having obtained the fruit of all sacred fords.
She who receives upon her head the stream of milk flowing from the udder of a cow is liberated from all sins. ||81||
Having properly attended upon a virtuous person and having fed them according to the rules, one should worship them;
indeed, all of that person's sin perishes at that very moment.
Having spread out *kuśa* grass with its tips pointing eastward and having placed a bull before him, she who bathes in the water from its tail becomes pure in every respect. (83)
One becomes pure by bathing with water contained in a right-spiraling conch;
by bathing with water mixed with black sesame seeds, one becomes pure at that very moment. (84)
Having bathed with the water from the unwithered lotus petals, with water containing all kinds of jewels,
and even with the water used for washing the feet of the virtuous, one is liberated from sins.
Having observed the Bodhinī fast and likewise the Dvādaśī fast in the month of Kārtika, the observer of the vow quickly destroys the sins committed over ten million lifetimes. (86)
O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Lord of Lakṣmī, O Master!
Through the chanting of the names Māṇikyeśvara and Haṃseśa, one shall attain absorption into Him. 87.
Having propitiated the Supreme Lord over thousands of other births,
when all sins have been destroyed, someone may attain the status of a Vaiṣṇava.
O daughters, by receiving the grace of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, you have indeed attained that rare status of being Vaiṣṇavīs, which is obtained through His mercy.
For the Vaiṣṇavas, O fortunate ones, purify the entire world;
whether remembered, praised, seen, or even touched, O sons. (2.15.90)
The Blessed One, who purifies a thousand births, purifies instantly;
knowing this, you should worship him with special care. (91)
"Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who possesses the form of a child," having spoken thus, he gave the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and bestowed the radiant knowledge of the Self.
Lomaśa ceased speaking, and those young maidens also desisted;
having abandoned both dharma and adharma, they remained established in eternal wisdom.
Free from fear and beyond reproach, they undertook various religious observances, filled with supreme affection and constantly thinking of Kṛṣṇa.
Lomaśa, too, would always in the evening cause those stories— which bestow devotion such as conjugal fidelity— to be heard by Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
And he caused them all, who were established in the vows of the Cāturmāsya, to hear the entire Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā from every side. ||96||
The newly arrived Lakṣa-kanyās, as well as all the others, constantly chanted the name of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa with great reverence. (97)
Whether awake, asleep, or even in deep slumber, they longingly held Hari, their husband and lord Śrī, within their hearts. (98)
With their hearts, they chose Bālakṛṣṇa, the delight of Yaśodā;
they took refuge in Him as the beloved Lord who dwells within the self as the Inner Self. 99.
Thus, O Rādhikā, those divine women, though born of darkness (tāmasa), became so through union with the Supreme Lord; what wonder can I tell you? 2.15.100.
This Kṛṣṇa, who has taken birth solely out of compassion and is possessed of grace,
destroyed the fierce sins of the wicked and made them his own.
He indeed likewise makes men, women, animals, trees, creepers, Daityas and others,
as well as the readers and the groups of listeners, his own.

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of the Ekādaśī Vow, Chastity, and Service to Cows, Gurus, and Others, as Revealed by Lomaśa to the New Maidens," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, you have not previously heard this divine narrative. I shall tell you of its wonder; listen to me with attention.
In the month of Āṣāḍha, all the maidens indeed performed the Cāturmāsya vows as instructed by Lomaśa for the pleasure of Bālakṛṣṇa.
On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha,
having bathed early in the morning, they meditated upon Kṛpānātha, bowed down, and worshipped Lomaśa.
Sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, flowers, saffron, garments, and garlands; cow’s milk, as well as a decoction enriched with sugar, cardamom, and saffron filaments. || 4 ||
Having led the Lord, who is adorned with ornaments, garments, and necklaces, they approached to behold the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. || 5 ||
With their minds fixed on the glorious Lord, they sing songs with sweet voices, bearing upon their heads jars adorned with pearl-encrusted golden bands.
Holding vessels for worship filled with fruit in their hands, with Mādhava as the foremost object of their vision,
they held Kṛṣṇa within their hearts and performed the auspicious marriage rites.
The foremost among them remembered the Lord of Śrī with a spirit of competitive emulation;
then, in the morning, a miracle was displayed by Bālakṛṣṇa.
"Ten million maidens will come to my house for the sake of worshipping me;
there will be a great crush here, so I must go to the edge of the lake."
"Receiving the worship and the crowding must occur simultaneously so that there is no disorder"—
having thus resolved, the Blessed One instantly assumed ten million forms.
Smiling, the youthful soul proceeded along the path holding them;
one girl saw him alone, while another did not see the other.
Only one woman knows me thus: "The Lord approaches me with a smile out of an excess of love for me; he did not go toward the others. (12)
One woman recognizes me alone and approaches me, while the others do not;
another sees me coming toward her as one who is truly compassionate toward her.
Thus, indeed, each one perceives her own beloved; thinking him to possess incomparable beauty, they quickly unite at his chest.
Śrī Hari bowed to Lomaśa, and Lomaśa also joyfully bowed to Hari;
then, with those two crores [of attendants], the earth became like the heavens.
Kṛṣṇa goes ahead, inquiring after news rich in welfare,
while the maiden walks slightly by his side, at his side, behind him, or to his left.
On the vast bank of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake, extending for many yojanas,
shaded like a cloud-canopy and adorned with flowering trees and creepers.

On ground covered with auspicious, tender crops and endowed with cool, fragrant breezes, having arranged the vessels for worship and having made the seat pleasing before him, [one should proceed]. (18)
They all worshipped [her] with sincere devotion, using various materials and substances; they applied fragrant sandalwood paste as decorative marks upon their foreheads.
They applied collyrium to their eyes and a tilaka mark upon their foreheads;
having placed a drop of blood on the right cheek, they eagerly kissed them.
They placed a flower crown with a crest of peacock feathers upon his head, clusters of flowers on his ears, and various kinds of floral wreaths.
They bore for the Lord garlands of flowers from the Tulasī plant, as well as bracelets, waistbands, and garments with floral patterns.
They applied lac-dye and saffron to his feet and hands; they also gave him anklets with small bells and bracelets for his wrists.
They gave him yellow silken garments made of linen and silk;
they also gave him a flute and two clusters of blossoms for his ears.
They placed a lotus petal in his right hand and gave him fragrant sprinkling water;
they offered cool, sweet water, food, fruit, juices, milk, and curds.
Cardamom, cloves, and seeds provided purification for the mouth.
Having thus worshipped that Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa again and again, [he offered these]. (26)
They performed the nightly lamp-offering, the ritual water-sprinkling, and the wiping with cloth;
they offered salutations, hymns of praise, prostrations like a staff, circumambulations, and the gift of honoraria.
They offered themselves as a handful of flowers, performed a request for forgiveness, drank the water used for washing his feet, and placed it upon their heads. (28)
Placing the feet of Kṛṣṇa upon their breasts, they attained supreme bliss;
being fully satisfied, they requested vows from their own Lord.
Some for four months requested a diet of fruits; some a diet of roots; some a diet of leaves; and some a diet of milk. (2.16.30)
One [woman] ate only once a day; another consumed the food of sages; one ate only barley, and another took nothing but wheat.
One [woman] [offered] mouthfuls of rice; another, food devoid of flavor; another, food without salt; and another, food devoid of sweetness. ||32||
One [portion] was devoid of bitterness, another was free from pungency;
one was uncooked by fire, while another was dry and roasted. ||33||
Some [women] ate only without rice; some were deprived of vegetables;
some avoided pulses, while others avoided even water with husks. ||34||
One [vessel] was devoid of meat, another was destitute of milk; one lacked food to be eaten, and yet another was without oil. (35)
Another [practiced] eating once at night, another every fourth period of time, another eating only at six times [per day], and yet another eating only once every seven days. (36)
Likewise, eating once every fortnight, eating once every month, the Cāndrāyaṇa and other penances, as well as the various types of Kṛcchra lasting one, two, three days, and so forth; (37)
Thus they undertook the vows with the desire to please Kṛṣṇa.
Having heard this, the venerable Lomaśa said: "Listen, O maidens, to what is for your benefit. (38)
Whatever vow is most excellent for the sake of which Kṛṣṇa may become pleased— whether by that vow, or by austerity, or by propitiation through self-restraint and other such means.
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is to be propitiated by millions of spiritual practices;
yet He may become gracious even toward one who observes no vows—for such non-vow is indeed a vow itself.
If He is not pleased despite one's observance of vows, then that vow is merely a non-vow.
"Therefore, daughters, you must ask that by which Hari may be pleased.
Having learned what bestows satisfaction, perform that vow during Cāturmāsya.
Thus addressed, those delicate girls [asked] Hari Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Seated comfortably, they asked: "Tell us that by which you are pleased.
Hearing this, Hari smiled and said: "I am pleased by devotion alone, and not otherwise—not by vows, nor by gifts, nor likewise by restraints or observances. (43)
Neither by sacrifices nor by sacrificial fees, nor likewise by the emaciation of the body.
I am not pleased by deliberations, nor by wealth, nor by notions of delicacy;
rather, I am gratified by love that is sincere and unswerving. (45)
The vow of love for my sake must indeed be fulfilled by you yourselves;
out of love he is to be honored, saluted, and remembered. (46)
With love, one should perform service characterized by servitude unto me in every way—during bathing, meditation, eating, and even in all bodily functions. (47)
I am Kṛṣṇa who should be invoked; that vow shall be the giver of liberation.
I am the strength of the weak, and I am the portion of strength for the young.
"Whom among the maidens shall I make happy? I am Nārāyaṇa, the giver of liberation.
During the Cāturmāsya, for my sake indeed, there shall be circumambulation and prostration. (49)
My garland and my chanting, my meditation and the beautiful recitation of My names; My verses and My stories—O dear ones, life for the sake of Me is dear to you.
Indeed, I have performed this supreme vow, the offering of everything to Kṛṣṇa,
which is divine and directly produced from my yoga, for your sake.
This other vow is not equal to that [previous one] by which the bliss of liberation would arise;
indeed, I have attained in every way that very state which is to be reached through vows. (52)
"What is that vow, and what other vow is there? Remain thus while I am established in my vow.
Having said this, the Blessed One took the articles for their worship.
Assuming ten million forms, he bestowed the pleasure of seeing and touching upon them;
then, having bowed to Hari, they all spoke to the Supreme Lord. (54)
"O Lord, we shall always perform worship to you here, gathered together;
likewise, grant us happiness through the grace of accepting this worship. (55)
"So be it," Hari replied; meanwhile, O Rādhikā, listen, my dear, as I tell you of the wonder that has occurred here. (56)
Indeed, the mountain named Śatruñjaya is situated in the south-eastern direction;
there in Saurāṣṭra, the Daityas known as Kaṅkatālakas resided. (57)
By the thousands were the Kaṅkatālas, devoted to liquor and meat;
they resembled mountain peaks, with teeth and hair like ploughshares.
Reaching the height of heated palm trees, they touched the very crest of the path of the clouds.
They eat sea fish and likewise devour human flesh. ||59||
Then, having learned of the festival for the worship of Kṛ� wild animals, birds, and living creatures that feed on forest game arrived there. 2.16.60.
All those Asuras— vow-breakers, wicked, and bearing weapons and missiles—
fell from the path of the sky to slay the child Nārāyaṇa.
"Slay him! Strike down this Bālakṛṣṇa, the adversary, the great enemy of the Asuras, the supreme slayer of hundreds of thousands! ||62||
"Kill quickly the lord who steals the wives of those men;
furthermore, bind Lomaśa swiftly by the neck with a rope and destroy him! ||63||
"Kill the brahmins here, and destroy those who take refuge in them!
Having spoken thus, they descended from the sky with the intent to slaughter.
Lomaśa, the Lord Śrī Bhagavān himself, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, indeed paralyzed them in the sky in that manner.
Having gathered all his own forms in a mere moment and assuming the form of Vairāja,
he shone like the king of mountains.
He remembered the divine Garuḍa, and he arrived in an instant;
with his two outspread wings, he likewise covered the maidens and the hermitage.
And that king of birds protected Aśvapaṭṭasara like a canopy; having guarded that territory, which was ten yojanas in extent, he remained there.
With his wings spread wide, he stood there fearless by the command of Acyuta;
then the Lord, wielding His weapon, swiftly mounted his back.
Then, speaking thus, he effortlessly released the Sudarśana discus, saying:
"Conquer your enemies! Kaṅka and Tāla, why do you stand here inactive? (2.16.70)
"Let you who have lost your sense of shame strive to win back your lives;
here stands Lomaśa, drawing out your state of dullness. (7.1)
When Jaḍabhāva had spoken thus, those Asuras were then consumed by the illusory power (māyā) of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; their fortune destroyed, they regained their strength once more.
They made an effort for the sake of destroying Kṛṣṇa and rushed forward with great speed;
yet, as soon as they reached Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Garuḍa, their weapons first [failed them].
They then employ the Sudarśana discus for the purpose of striking;
it has the appearance of the fire of universal destruction, revolving with unbearable sharp spokes.
He cut off the heads of the Kaṅka, Tāla, and Asura demons;
their bodies, split in half, fell from the sky on all sides. (75)
Even severed heads fell down as they were falling;
hands, feet, and portions of the waist likewise fell everywhere upon the ground. (76)
Though armed with weapons in their hands, they were as powerless as those cut down by a discus; they were unable then to slay Kṛṣṇa, Garuḍa, or Lomaśa.
Then, a thousand of them perished, their weapons severed;
the rest fled, and the mace Kaumodakī herself pursued them.
Embodied and resembling a mountain, equipped with many weapons in her hands, she stood nearby, running about and blocking the path on all sides. (79)
In whichever direction the Daityas fled,
in that very direction that terrifying mace, the great Satī, assumed manifold forms.
Then my enemy, having leaped up, stood before me;
he struck them with his mace, and five or six others were left remaining.
Having assumed the forms of maidens and taken refuge with Garuḍa,
they entered into those very girls and protected them by means of the Lord.
Then Nārāyaṇa, the discus, the mace, and likewise Garuḍa,
having slain the Daityas, assumed their own subtle forms once again.
Having worshipped the Supreme Lord Śrī Hari there,
Garuḍa quickly departed for Vaikuṇṭha, with the Sudarśana discus now held in his hand.
Then the Blessed One, bestowing courage upon each maiden, laughed and said to Lomaśa: "These five or six maidens are indeed new. (85)
"O Guru, behold! Out of fear of death, the Daityas have become deceitful women here for the sake of saving their lives. (86)
"I, being compassionate, must effect the preservation of their lives.
When he had spoken thus, they wept, prostrated themselves, and entreated him. (87)
"Protection, guardianship, and likewise the status of a slave— Kṛṣṇa said, 'Let it be so for you always, and may you always possess female forms.'"
"Let this maiden-form remain eternal here in my abode";
thus Hari caused their residence to be established in the hermitage of Lomaśa. (89)
And Lomaśa bestowed upon him the Vaiṣṇava mantra, the garland for the neck,
the Tulasī, the forehead mark, the name-mantra, and a divine form.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
The virtuous wives and the young maidens, remaining composed, received this mantra. (9.1)
Having become devotees of Viṣṇu (Vaiṣṇavīs), they then took refuge in Śrī Hari;
they prayed to the Lord of Lords for the sake of liberation for those who had fallen in battle. ||9 2||
Those Daityas who died in battle by the will of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa arrived by the thousands in subtle bodies, free from all taint.
Having utterly destroyed their demonic nature, Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
the Supreme Soul, then bestowed upon them divinity, along with celestial chariots and divine attendants.
All the inhabitants of Śatruñjaya were led to Vaikuṇṭha;
thus, having taken refuge in Hari on the Ekādaśī day, they attained liberation.
Then, having taken all those maidens, the sage Śrī Lomaśa went to his own hermitage; Kṛṣṇa indeed became Bālakṛṣṇa.
That sacred ford named Kaṅkatāla arose at the Aśvapaṭṭa lake;
it became famous on the right side [of the lake], where worship of Hari was performed. (97)
Having thus brought joy to the wives of the practitioners, Bālakṛṣṇa vanished in an instant and went to his bed in the house. ||98||
Having known, heard, recited, or even remembered this auspicious account of the God of gods concerning Rādhikā, one shall certainly attain liberation. 99.
A man shall become wealthy, possessed of sons, illustrious, and attain infinite heaven; a woman shall be rich in good fortune and fame, and she shall grant the continuity of her lineage.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "The Description of Lord Bālakṛṣṇa’s Worship by the Maidens, His Assumption of Many Forms, His Vows, His Battle with and Liberation of the Daityas of Kaṅkatālā on Mount Śatrughna, and the Residence of the Remaining Maidens in Disguise at the Hermitage of Lomaśa," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, concerning the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhā; when those Daityas did not return home, their wives arrived in order to search for the army of the Daityas. || 1 ||
Then, in the month of Śrāvaṇa, during the rainy season,
ten thousand [people] were present on that auspicious ground at the field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, which was flooded with water and other elements.
Having arrived from the region of the sky, the wives of the Daityas beheld that great and beautiful hermitage situated in the forest.
It was the refuge of ten million maidens and was frequented by Lomaśa and Ṛṣi;
some there were forest-dwellers (vaikhānasa), while others were without seats (nirāsana).
Some were Yāyāvaras, others were Vānaprasthas,
some were Śālīnas, and others had adopted the lifestyle of the Kāpotī mode of subsistence.
Likewise, others adopted the auspicious livelihood of compassion toward all beings; others subsisted by gathering grains from the ground, while still others lived on food obtained from wooden bowls.
Some are unripened while others are ripened;
some possess various kinds of qualities, while others have their selves conquered.
Some were committed to the vow of silence while standing, others likewise remained lying in water; some remained lying on their backs, and others lived like deer.
Some practiced the austerity of the five fires; some subsisted on leaves and fruits; others lived on water, some on air, and likewise others on vegetables.
Therefore, others as well undertook most intense ascetic practices in that forest where millions of virtuous men and women dwell.
In that hermitage dwell ten million maidens who are the wives of Hari,
and there resides the divine Kuṅkumavāpikā, which bestows liberation.
That land where the divine Aśvapaṭṭa-sarovara flows is a place that bestows divinity, wherein the Great Lord Hari resides.
There exists a delightful palace, more brilliantly radiant than Goloka, where the goddess Śrī Kambharā Lakṣmī resides and where Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa dwells. (13)
The subjects, accompanied by the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa, shone on all sides;
such was that great divine place, possessing the splendor of the Nandana grove.
That region was observed by those Daityas from the path of the sky;
it consisted of diamond, crystal, and stone, and was strewn with sprouts of coral and gravel.
Abounding in dark-blue, pure clay, adorned with cascading streams of water,
and filled with various flowers bearing clusters of blossoming creepers.
There, the plateaus shone even more brilliantly with the outpourings of various minerals from the tall trees that seemed to scrape the very sky.
Adorned everywhere with various flowers, they appeared as if painted;
in them were groves of *ketakī* and clusters of blossoming *kunda* flowers.
The mountain ranges appear as if blossomed by the rows of *dhātaki* forests, with the waters of its springs washed clear like split, pure sapphire. (19)
With variegated carpets of minerals spread over them and covered with blossoms,
they were frequented by divine couples at play and by throngs of dancing apsarases.
The radiant region was graced by intoxicated, warbling peacocks;
it was filled with white water-lilies and frequented by swans and cranes. (21)
It was filled with lakes of clear water abounding in full-blown lotuses,
and it was frequented by herds of lions as well as by various beasts and birds.
Adorned with vessels served by hosts of sages, it was made lovely by the songs of kinnaras and resounded with the warbling of cuckoos. ||23||
It was crowded with hundreds of Vidyādharas and frequented by gods and Gandharvas;
it was filled with the falling showers of clouds and thousands of sparks [of lightning]. (24)
It was repeatedly illuminated by soft, delightful green meadows; it possessed groves and gardens of every season and was exquisitely beautified by the springtime of flowers. ||25||
It is the abode of the Kimpuruṣas who perform sacrifices, as well as the refuge of the Guhyakas;
it is the beautiful dwelling place of liberated attendants and Vaiṣṇavas. ||26||
Where the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Master, the bestower of boons, the divine teacher of all the immortals, Hari, is eternally present. ||27||
That glorious Lord, compassionate toward his devotees, dwells together with his attendants;
he is the Supreme Lord whom all those traveling in celestial chariots worship as their deity. 28.
The gods come to serve him who is excellent, unborn, and immutable;
other hosts of deities also fall down to serve him.
This region, which is the very form of that presiding power, was beheld by women;
this most enchanting region was gazed upon by the Daityas during the month of Śrāvaṇa.
Hari, the Lord, was swung by young maidens upon the branches of trees;
the Supreme Lord was beheld on every tree suspended in a swing. ||3 1||
Seeing Hari, who had brought about the destruction of their husband, they were struck with wonder; they became exceedingly enraged at Kṛṣṇa and rushed from tree to tree to kill him.
Whichever branch of a tree Kṛṣṇa’s swing hung upon, that very tree became a deity in the form of a tree, serving him. (33)
That tree instantly became a divine being bearing weapons, in order to protect the Blessed One and to slay those demonesses. (34)
Then the rākṣasīs waged war with the gods in the very sky,
using bhindipālas, tomara-spears, mallets, and weapons made of bone.
Then, with fierce tree branches, bamboo, clumps of grass, thorns,
stones, and even sticks, they fought again, hair-to-hair.
The gods fought with the rākṣasīs, yet they did not kill those who were still alive;
nor did they strike them in their vital organs, for their limbs were tender.
Thinking thus, they did not harm the female species, considering them as their own lives;
yet those fierce ones destroyed them by means of the maidens themselves.
The Lord Kṛṣṇa, having perceived that the women were intent on crushing him in battle,
the Blessed One immediately manifested himself there in two forms and approached them.
Bearing the form of Kāla-lakṣmī, the Lord, equipped with all weapons and possessing a thousand arms, arrived through the sky mounted upon an elephant.
When the white elephant, endowed with wings, roared in the sky, the rākṣasīs, their ears pierced by the clear resonance of the echo, were then overwhelmed with agitation. 41.
Some fainted and fell into the sky or onto the forest floor;
others ran to destroy the elephant, while Hari [remained] there.
Then, in the form of the Goddess of Time (Kālalakṣmī), she struck them while they were still alive;
the women fell down dead, split in two, pierced, and shattered as they died.
At that time, their very self repeatedly underwent dissolution into the splendor of Time;
yet Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa remained as a youth in another form. ||44||
And standing amidst the maidens in the hermitage of Lomaśa, he shone resplendently;
meanwhile, some wives of the Daitya leaders were struck by the trunk of an elephant. 45.
Others, slain by weapons, were entirely destroyed along with their splendor;
yet having died, they attained divinity and shone like goddesses. (46)
Having beheld the youthful Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the supreme Lord of lords, they entreated him most fervently. 47.
"Be forever our beloved, for you are the protector of us who were without a lord;
we have died [of old] and have been reborn, though devoid of the qualities of Daityas, through your majesty. (48)
And grant us residence among the maidens in the presence of Lomaśa;
O compassionate one, we always desire to perform service for you. (49)
"So be it," Hari said; ten thousand divine maidens became less than twelve years of age through the power of Kṛṣṇa.
To those beloved women, whose limbs were symmetrical to their forms and who were equal to Rādhā and Ramā,
Lomaśa gave the supreme Śrī-Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
[One should place] a garland of tulasī on the neck and an auspicious tilaka on the forehead. (52)
He placed a yellow garment and a rosary for the practice of recitation into their hands;
he bestowed upon them knowledge and wisdom, and granted them residence in his own hermitage. (53)
And they all, having washed the feet of Bālakṛṣṇa with a stream of milk, drank his grace in the form of food, fruit, and so forth.
Then, with exceeding affection and as their servants, they devoured them;
and Lomaśa then sought refuge with all of them.
He indeed awakened them in six ways, consisting of the total surrender of everything:
"Listen, all you maidens, who have made a firm resolve for the sake of Kṛṣṇa! (56)
The female body exists for the sake of another; that other is the Supreme Person, Śrī Puruṣottama.
Therefore, women must by all means be devoted to their husbands for His sake. (57)
The husband alone is the Supreme Brahman, the savior who bestows liberation;
through merit accumulated over a hundred births, a virtuous maiden is born. (58)
Through the merits of a thousand births, she may become one who is dedicated to Kṛṣṇa;
through the merits acquired over a hundred thousand births, that virtuous woman becomes the wife of Kṛṣṇa.
"You are all the wives of Kṛṣṇa; you are undoubtedly worthy of compassion. From what cause, and by whom, has such merit been acquired? (2.17.60)
Through union with Hari, the ocean of merit increases like a treasure-trove—
even when one is under the influence of desire, anger, attachment, greed, or delusion toward the Lord.
If they are absorbed in Him and dependent upon Him, then all merit has been acquired;
thus have you women today become as if held in the hand of Lakṣmī.
Indeed, even through enmity toward Hari, they have attained eternal merit by virtue of my grace, [the grace] of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
No illusion whatsoever enters this hermitage on all sides;
this place, the refuge of me, Lomaśa, is beyond all illusion.
Indeed, the defects such as lust and anger blaze forth for those who are possessed of faults, as they travel through the sky above my portion of the hermitage. (65)
Even as they ascend, the defects such as passion and the like are indeed destroyed from the hearts of those beasts and birds.
The cycle of worldly existence for gods, dānavas, daityas, and even for women— indeed, for all transmigrating beings— is composed of false mental impressions.
By resorting to my hermitage, one attains dissolution from the very root;
those embodied beings who have made their dwelling in this hermitage become divine. (68)
"I shall always grant them peace through the majesty of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
therefore, all of you, taking refuge in him, worship Hari Kṛṣṇa here. (69)
Nothing else is distinguished as worthy of being desired except for the attainment of Hari;
therefore, indeed, practice devotion to him, meditate upon him, and follow his path. (2.17.70)
"Serve him alone constantly and always without sloth;
your sin has departed, your [former] disposition has gone, your state as a Daitya is gone, and your old age has passed away."
Fear has departed and death too has gone; that which caused you distress is now gone.
All that was to be gained has been gained, and all that was to be attained has been attained. (72)
"O maidens, you have indeed accomplished what was to be done; nothing further remains to be done. Therefore, keep in your hearts the sixfold service and devote yourselves to it. (73)
"Trust must be placed in Mādhava as in a mother toward her own child;
both the granting of a boon and the choosing [of him] must be done by you alone for me. (74)
For embodied beings, renunciation of the body unto that Kṛṣṇa is in every way [the highest goal];
even servitude to the Supreme Self, like that of a servant, is likewise [meritorious]. (75)
"Constant steadfastness in both happiness and sorrow, and nothing else—this is devotion to my beloved; such is my desire. (76)

"I have no aversion toward him, yet that which is undesirable to him is not desired by me"—in this way, a woman of noble character should consider her own happiness to be found in the happiness of her lord. (77)
But she who is not at peace when her lord suffers certainly becomes sorrowful;
for she behaves toward that beloved, divine, and supreme Self as if toward her own self. (78)
Everything should be given to him who seeks refuge;
he alone here is the father, the protector, and he alone is the mother and the source of birth. (79)
Kṛṣṇa alone is the great kinsman; Hari himself is the brother and the sister.
Kṛṣṇa alone is the youngest, the younger sibling, and even the daughter. (2.17.80)
Kṛṣṇa alone is my husband, wife, daughter-in-law, and bride;
Kṛṣṇa alone is my father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and son. (81)
Son, daughter, friend, and companion, Kṛṣṇa alone is always mine;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is my brother, my king, my servant, and my slave. (82)
Kṛṣṇa is the servant, the teacher, and the priest; He is the guide, the caravan-leader, the householder, and the Lord of the home. (83)
That Mādhava is my supreme refuge and the bestower of fruits;
Hari himself is my field, my garden, and my wealth. (84)
That Keśava is my kinsman; that boy is mine, as is that girl.
He is dear to my heart, a guest of honor, and my lord. (85)
O Kṛṣṇa, my co-wife is always [the world], while my rival is the illusory power (māyā) within me;
Janārdana is the one who sees in me, hears in me, and touches in me. (86)
Kṛṣṇa is indeed the smeller in me, Hari is the taster; He is the thinker in me, the goer, the grasper, the speaker, and the one who bestows bliss in me.
He is the one who sends forth, he is Kṛṣṇa; he is the awakener, the thinker within me; he is the decider, the one who brings [the goal] to fruition, the knower, and indeed the wise one within me. 88.
Hari is my satiator, my delighter, and he is the one made of jewels;
he is my protector and my attractor, dwelling within my womb, my belly, and my heart.
The Supreme Person, Kṛṣṇa, is my life-giver, my sustainer, and my inner self; He is the witness, the conscious one, and my Lord. I am His wife, entirely absorbed in Him. (2.17.90)
"Everything belongs to him, and I belong to that Śrī Paramātman;
in this way, you daughters have been offered unto Him. (9.1)
Whatever is sweet to me, whatever is dear to my heart, whatever is delicious, and whatever is cool—all that belongs to Bālakṛṣṇa; likewise, you all have become his maidservants.
Just as one protects that which is to be protected, so Hari is the Lord, the most worthy of protection;
this very Beloved must be concealed, and nothing further remains to be done. 93.
All concealment is for the sake of the beloved; there is no concealment whatsoever in the presence of the beloved.
Kṛṣṇa is perceived as the beloved, and therefore he behaves like a beloved.
Just as a woman who desires her lover acts like a lover toward him, so Kṛṣṇa acts like Kṛṣṇā toward Kṛṣṇā, who likewise desires him. 95.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa resides within you;
He exists as an inseparable substance, indeed eternal and imperishable. 96.
He himself has now come here to the house of Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa;
that son of Kambharāśrī has indeed arrived, for he is the one who observed your vow.
In eating, lying down, bathing, meditating, traveling, sitting, wandering, sporting, drinking, resting, and in every movement; ||98||
O you who are transformed, well-made, gentle, and full of poison, enjoy him at the time of departure;
and O you who are the turning back and sleep, enjoy that beloved husband! 99.
Thus, indeed, offer your own collection of ritual acts therein;
such is the extent of the expansion of the scriptures, and such is the instruction. 2.17.100.
Oṃ! May there be peace and detachment from worldly existence for you all in Nārāyaṇa; and may there be the dissolution of all desires for you all in the Supreme Self. 101.
Having thus instructed them, the king of sages, who possesses the true power that washes away illusion,
assigned dwellings for the maidens in leaf-huts.
He himself became absorbed in meditation, while those maidens were fed,
honored, saluted, and addressed with words of welcome and the like.
Then they too, indeed, daily heard the supreme discourses of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā morning and evening, day after day.
Every morning they would constantly worship their beloved husband Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
making their very birth fruitful day and night.
Thus, O Rādhikā, has this story— which bestows divinity here,
which grants life for the sake of a husband, and which is dedicated to Kṛṣṇa— been told to you.
In those [places] where there is no virtuous conduct, where there is no service, where there is no devotion, no worship, and no contemplation of Kṛṣṇa; 107.
Pleased with them, this Hari, who is devoted to bestowing grace and is a great king to be won over by compassion, rained down [boons] beyond all bounds.
The one higher than the highest is capable of acting, not acting, or acting otherwise;
he indeed creates the races of Daityas, the races of Devas, and the races of Brahmas.
Even from a sin, one becomes even more sinful; yet by reading or even hearing [this], one becomes like a god, like a liberated soul, or like the wife of Kṛṣṇa. (2.17.110)

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Battle of the Wives of the Daityas Kaṅka and Tāla at the Kuṅkumavāpikā Field, the State of Being the Beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and the Instruction on Self-Surrender to Bālakṛṣṇa given by Lomaśa," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhā; in the month of Bhādrapada, during the fortnight of the ancestors (pitṛpakṣa), the daughters [of the gods] offered a house for Hari to the ancestors beginning with Aryaman. || 1 ||
The maidens arrived together, bringing sweet milk-rice mixed with sesame seeds,
along with fruits, flowers, agallochum, musk, saffron, and rice grains.
