Having been brought safely to their respective places here and there, all those men and women then went to their own homes and told their families what had occurred.
Filled with wonder, they took refuge in Hari, the beginningless Śrī Nārāyaṇa;
then the Blessed Lord quickly vanished along with his chariot.
And the royal sage named Udaya arrived at his own auspicious abode, the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake. ||79||
Devoted solely to the names of Hari, he performed the sacrifice of recitation (japayajña);
furthermore, in his heart, he addressed Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
"Grant me liberation, O ocean of compassion; may I attain the eternal state.
"So be it," Hari replied, and the king entered into meditation.
With the force of his vital breaths [now] withdrawn into the latent channels, he then gradually abandoned his life-breaths;
having been liberated, he then ascended a most radiant celestial chariot.
He went to the supreme, glorious abode characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss;
thus did the glorious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa uplift them. 83.
Those well-endowed beings who were born as the lame, the deaf, the blind, and so forth, each went to their own country and home and remained there in happiness. (84)
Seeing them, the subjects and the people who had come as spectators were struck with wonder;
considering his prowess to be supreme, they took refuge in the Supreme Person.
"O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Viṣṇu, O Supreme Brahman, O Lord of Śrī! Thus they performed their worship, saying: 'O Master, protect us always. (86)
Śrī Hari showed Himself to them as they were far away in a dream;
they beheld His beautiful youthful form, exceedingly radiant.
There they remained absorbed for a mere moment, and then,
awakening once more, they remembered Nārāyaṇa as the cowherd boy.
Thousands of men and women arrived from all directions at the temple of Kuṅkumavāpikā for the purpose of seeing [him]. (89)
They beheld him in exactly the same form as they had seen in their dream;
they worshipped the Lord of Śrī most intensely with their whole being.
Having established many sacred fords and having received the mantra from Lomaśa,
those Vaiṣṇavas, beloved of the Lord, returned to their own regions.
To those who observe the four-month vow and come there to that lake to bathe,
Hari indeed grants his own direct vision.
Having made the elders, whose lifespans are complete, divine and established in celestial chariots,
he sends them to his own abode, the imperishable and supreme state.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the people who had been submerged in the water were protected by Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and restored to their own lands. (94)
The eunuchs were rendered free from disease, their bodies nourished, and endowed with virility;
thus his incomparable majesty was proclaimed throughout the surface of the earth. (95)
Through chanting its name, through remembering it, through proclaiming this wonder, and even through hearing it, all sufferings indeed come to an end. (96)
Diseases perish quickly, and even great calamities vanish;
times of adversity are always destroyed by listening to the narrations of Kṛṣṇa.
O Rādhā, by the recitation of hymns of praise, protection is obtained in every way;
and by the performance of pilgrimage, people attain their desired objects. 98.
Everything undesirable dissolves away and good fortune increases;
one shall possess wealth, grain, progeny, sons, attendants, and so forth. (9)
Having attained enjoyment here and in heaven, one is thereafter glorified in liberation;
for the devotee of the Supreme Brahman, no duty remains to be performed.

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Praise Offered by Those Rescued from the Water in the Second Tretā Cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; the Restoration of Health to the Sick, the Maimed, and Others on the Eighth-Year Festival; the Hymn Composed by Them; the Hymn of Āryāyanaka; the Return of the Rescued to Their Own Country; and the Liberation of King Udayana. || 62 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen to the deeds of the glorious Bālakṛṣṇa, which provide protection to His devotees; another occurred in His eighth year, arising from the ocean.
On the bank of the Revā, however, there was a beautiful city named Candrodaya,
inhabited by all devotees and populated by subjects devoted to righteousness.
There lived a great merchant, prosperous with wealth and grain,
named Vasumedha, who was a devotee of Viṣṇu and pure in mind.
Constantly devoted to the service of the virtuous, he performs the worship of the gods:
Sūrya, Viṣṇu, Gaṇeśa, Satī, Śambhu, Śrī, and Hari.
Having bathed in the morning, he reverently worships with ritual offerings;
he always eats after sharing [with others], and he constantly gives gifts every day.
He performs service to cows, service to the virtuous, and satisfies the ancestors;
his business involving trade goods prospers with great profit.
He had five sons who were skilled, and a wife devoted to dharma named Suśīlā,
who always observed the vow of eating only once a day.
Having worshipped the Śālagrāma stone with offerings mixed with Tulasī leaves,
he partakes of the food born of divine grace (prasāda), which has been touched by the water used for washing the Lord's feet.
And all his sons were devotees of Viṣṇu, intent on wearing garlands, meditating, and chanting;
they were seekers of liberation who had properly listened to discourses on the scriptures.
Now, there was a great sage there named Śatānanda;
he was the son of Uddālaka and had established his hermitage in the forest.
Śatānanda would always come by chance to the hermitage of the brahmin not far from the vicinity of Candrodaya in the evening.
Every morning he recites the *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇasaṃhitā*; having delivered the discourse and received alms, he returns to his own hermitage.
The people of the village come together and listen to the discourse daily.
In that regard, it was heard [by me] in Saurāṣṭra at the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
In the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, within the Śrīgṛha of Kambharā,
Hari resides as the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the son of Gopāla.
The Blessed One, the Supreme Person, indeed exists in the form of a child,
bearing the conch, the discus, the mace, the lotus, the fish-banner, and the trident.
The Lord of All, the imperishable Śrīpati, is present in person, his hands marked with signs such as the bow, the svastika, and the thunderbolt.
The Supreme Lord, the master of the lives of hundreds of millions of crores of cowherdesses,
having heard this wonderful story and having heard [of] the illustrious Somatīrtha, [proceeded].
Having heard of the holy Svarṇapurī as well as Camatkārapura,
he made a formal vow for the sake of visiting the sacred sites, accompanied by his family and followers.
Having gathered provisions such as food, water, fruits, roots, and grains, and being well-stocked with wealth and grain, he boarded a spacious ship. (19)
Accompanied by a caravan of thirty men and following the waters of the Narmadā,
he traveled aboard a boat being propelled by the sailors.
For the purpose of a pilgrimage, he arrived by boat at the confluence of the Revā and the ocean, [saying]:
"O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Viṣṇu, O Supreme Brahman, O Supreme Lord! (2.1)
He constantly recited the sacred names, muttered his prayers with his rosary,
and having rested by the banks of the Revā during the month of Māgha, he bathed there together with his followers.
He gave gifts of clothing, food, gold, and silver with devotion;
then, having boarded a ship, he reached the ocean's expanse.
Having bathed at the confluence of the Kiṃnadī and having crossed the Khāta, he arrived;
there, at the junction of the Śatruñjaya and the ocean, he bathed according to the prescribed rites.
From there he went to the Gopanātha Tīrtha, which is frequented by Hari and Hara;
from there he went to Mūla, the Golden City of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Having bathed at the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the ocean, he went to Somanātha;
then, having bathed at the confluence of the Hiraṇyā and performed the rites prescribed for sacred fords (tīrthavidhi).
Having performed the ritual at the confluence of the Bhadrā and the ocean— the sacred ford known as Makarālaya—
and having completed the rites for the holy sites, he went to Kṛṣṇasvarṇapurī.
Having seen the island, he then went to Nārāyaṇasaras on the shore; and turning back on his boat, he went to Camatkārapura. ||28||
Then, turning back from the unexcavated path toward the ocean and abandoning Svarṇapurī, he proceeds by way of the water.
Then, while they were at Somanātha in the midst of the ocean, a great obstacle arose;
a powerful and tumultuous storm blew with extreme velocity, causing great agitation.
And it became as beautiful as the ocean, like a mass of frost;
the ship was being dragged in the middle by an adverse wind. ||31||
Then, by the waves, ripples, and surges as high as palm trees,
many boats were submerged, and men were broken and lost.
Even Vasumedha’s boat, filled with water and tossed by waves, leaps up and moves in a zigzag course as it falls on both sides. (33)
The sailors were indeed unable to provide protection;
so too were Vasumedha, the eminent merchant, his wife, their sons, and the rest. (34)
They remembered Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Śrī Puruṣottama), and they lamented in many ways for the sake of whom they had come. (35)
Having heard through the words of Śatānanda about that Bālakṛṣṇa, we women would have died here in this ocean water had we not seen him. (36)
In the boat, water fills up and overflows even more than it can be baled out; it is tossed by the wind and repeatedly struck by the waves. (37)
Struck by the water, it forms whirlpools on its sides;
these other merchant ships have also gone to their destruction.
Even a boat desires to dwell upon the surface of the water when in our presence;
let them remember that Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Controller. 39.
May He for whose sake we have come protect us—He who dwells in the heart;
may that Blessed One, pervading the boat, make the boat steady.
May Kṛṣṇa, who dwells amidst the stormy winds, quell the wind in an instant;
and may Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, who abides in the waters, grant stability to the waters. (41)
Or if they have met with death, let him show himself here;
in every way, O Lord, we have come to you for refuge.
O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, son of Gopāla! O Śrī Kumāra of Kambharā, O Lord, Master of the gopīs, protect me! 43.
Thus, all those devoted to Kṛṣṇa, their enthusiasm destroyed and deeply distressed, became hopeless regarding their lives as the boat was driven by the force of the wind. ||44||
The abundant water, tossed and bent by the striking of the wind, quickly reached the surface; at that very moment, the Blessed Lord himself appeared.
He arrived there instantly in the form of a tortoise at the bottom; he placed that boat upon his back and carried it across the water.
In his second form, the Lord became a boatman;
and in ten other forms, he became a water-drainer. ||47||
And with twenty other forms, he repeatedly rescued men who were submerged in the water and placed them all within the boat. ||48||
Whatever goods were on the boat that fell into the water,
he also pulled them out with his hands and threw them back onto the vessel.
By his grace, the storm was restrained and the waters became still;
the boat also became steady, and the devotees were protected by the Blessed One.
And those other devotees who, during a stormy wind, were upon a boat or submerged in the water, He rescued them effortlessly. 51.
Having thus provided protection for his devotees and assuming a single form, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, as a youth, vanished there. (52)
Slowly propelled by the sailors, that ship moved forward;
it reached Śrīsomanātha and there remained anchored for a fortnight.
Having established the nine carriages there, Vasumedha, accompanied by his caravan,
proceeded in haste with wagons toward the eastern Sarasvatī.
Having bathed there and offered libations to the ancestors and the gods,
he thereafter proceeded to the auspicious Arkatīrtha and Balimakhasthala.
Then, having bathed in Svarṇarekhā at Vāmana’s sacred site and likewise at Vastrāpatha, he went to Rāṣṭrasarovara.
Afterwards, he went to Vaṭasthalī and then to Kuṅkumavāpikā;
having beheld that sacred field from afar, he prostrated himself upon the ground like a staff.
Having gone to Aśvapaṭṭasara, bathed, and performed the rites prescribed for sacred fords (tīrtha),
he circumambulated it and paid homage to all the holy sites.
She went to the great palace to behold Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord Hari, seated upon a divine throne within the golden temple. 59.
He possessed the radiance of the midday sun, a moon-like face, and a cooling luster;
his limbs were perfectly proportioned to his form, and he was clothed in garments as pure as fire.
He wore a golden crown adorned with garlands of jewels, diamonds, and pearls;
he was praised by gods, humans, and celestial musicians, and worshipped by the people.
Having bowed down, Vasu, together with his family, praised [the Lord] with love;
shedding tears from his eyes, he was overwhelmed and spoke with a faltering voice.
He who is the Supreme Lord is attained by those rich in merit through the virtues accumulated over many births;
that Supreme Lord has been reached by me—protect me, O Parameśvara! 6.3.
That which is attained by yogis through the efforts of yoga only after many years has been obtained by me today; O Supreme Lord, protect me! 64.
He who is attained by devotees through devotion and the surrender of all one's possessions—that very Lord, the Beloved of Śrī, has been reached by me; O Hari, protect me!
"Even though I have been tormented for a long time, Hari—who is so difficult to attain—has today been reached by me as the Lord of my life; O Puruṣottama, protect me! (66)
Having indeed been rescued from drowning in the ocean together with my family by you,
O Lord of Gods, rescue me once again from the ocean of saṃsāra.
Without you there is no life; though the vital breaths exist, they are not eternal.
Without you, all prosperities indeed turn into calamities.
You shine in the heart, you shine in the eyes, and you shine within the self;
you shine in the family, on the boat, in the water, and on the land.
Today my birth has become fruitful; my pilgrimage has become fruitful;
my family has become fruitful, and everything has attained fruitfulness.
But all those sacred sites for the sake of which you abandoned your home and went forth in search of them—those sacred sites are all contained right here within this foot of yours. (71)
What was to be attained has been attained; here, nothing remains to be done.
O Lord, ocean of compassion, protect me! I have come to you for refuge. (72)
Having spoken thus, he worshipped him and fell repeatedly at his feet,
offering jewels, ornaments, garments, and the like, as well as fragrant sandalwood and other perfumes.
His entire family also worshipped that Hari;
and standing before Śrī Hari, he then performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana).
By the command of Śrī Hari, he then offered sweet food, fruits, water, and so forth,
placing them first before Hari in that vessel.
The Blessed One ate the nectar-like food with affection, and out of great favor, he gave the remainder to Vasumedha, who was accompanied by his family.
Then Vasumedha and all the others enjoyed the food, drank the water, and dwelt in the palace of rest provided by the Blessed One. (77)
In this manner they passed those ten days;
however, on the morning of the eleventh day, Vasumedha and his beloved likewise [prepared].
Early in the morning, Suśīlā saw Nārāyaṇa himself, who had arrived in a celestial chariot in her dream to lead her to his abode. ||79||
Then, at that moment, Dharmamedha and Suśīlā quickly awakened their sons and others, recounting the excellent account of the dream.
They told them everything concerning the attainment of liberation for their sons; the sons, having bathed and worshipped the deities, attained supreme joy.
Then they all went quickly to the abode of Bālakṛṣṇa;
there Hari granted them His own vision and spoke to them.
From Lomaśa, indeed, receive the mantra, the initiation, and likewise the garland;
then this evening, O children, there will be for you the attainment of liberation.
Thus addressed, they went quickly to the hermitage of the venerable Lomaśa;
there they received the Vaiṣṇava mantra, the initiation, and a garland of Tulasī.
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Having taken this mantra, they offered food and various kinds of gifts. ||85||
They returned to their own abode and attended upon the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa; meanwhile, at that time, the parents remained immersed in meditation during the afternoon.
The sons requested forgiveness and performed service as was appropriate. After a short while, a celestial chariot with divine attendants arrived.
Having transformed Vasumedha and Suśīlā into divine bodies, they led them to the abode of Brahmā; then their sons made [the king] Dhanya. 88.
With concentrated minds, they performed the funeral rites for him;
thus, those two devotees, taking refuge in Nārāyaṇa, attained the path of liberation. (89)
The sons performed the śrāddha rites and other duties as was appropriate;
they then proceeded by way of the cart-road to where the boat was operating.
Having boarded the boat, they all indeed went to their own country;
and upon reaching the land of Camatkāra, they spoke of Nārāyaṇa.
Having heard this, people took refuge in Hari, the manifest Śrī Puruṣottama.
Thus, O Rādhā, I have narrated to you this purifying account of Hari. 92.

It bestows enjoyment and liberation upon the listener and the speaker, always provides protection, grants the fruit of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites, bestows heaven, and grants auspicious prosperity. ||93||

Thus ends the sixty-third chapter, titled "The Description of How Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Rescued the Merchant Vasumedha and His Family—who were dwelling in the city of Candrodaya in the second Tretā cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā—after they had set out by boat via the Narmadā for pilgrimage in the Saurāṣṭra ocean and were submerged in water due to a storm, and how He bestowed liberation upon them."
Śrī Rādhikā said: O Supreme Brahman, ocean of mercy, O Hari, you have spoken of the auspicious holy place named Gopanātha on the shore of the ocean in Saurāṣṭra.
O Kṛṣṇa, O Beloved, O Supreme Lord, tell me truly: how and when was that [name] born, and how is it meaningful? 2.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā, to this divine narrative within my sphere of experience;
in each preceding kalpa, many Śrī Kṛṣṇas have appeared.
O Rādhā, on that very first day of the first year, in the forenoon of Brahmā, I arrived there from Goloka along with you.
Indeed, this egg was produced through the desire of the Creator;
it came there to be seen where my jewel was located by me.
And that region of Saurāṣṭra was placed within this sphere;
having arrived there, I beheld a divine chariot fashioned of gold.
Frequented by hosts of cowherds and cowherdesses, endowed with cattle, and enchanting,
it was brought down by me from the sky onto a vast region of the earth.
O Rādhā, the cowherds and cowherd girls, including you and me, dwelt near the water;
we have likewise partaken of nectar and the milk of the cows.
Cows roam there, and cowherds play in that forest;
the cowherd women and cowherds take delight in that divine place created by me.
There, O Rādhā, I wandered everywhere among the trees with you, taking up residence together with the cows, the cowherds, and the gopīs.
Then the sages, headed by Sanatkumāra, arrived there;
and knowing that Śrī Śaṅkara was a devotee, Viṣṇu also arrived at that time.
By the cowherds, by me, and by you as well, and by the cowherd girls, those two were well-honored;
they were worshipped, saluted, fed with sweet food, and served with joy.
In that place where the two gods, Śrī Viṣṇu and Śaṅkara, took up residence and were worshipped by the cowherds, there the two gods, whose essence is Hari and Hara, remained.
Just then, Brahmā arrived there; having learned of this, he was quickly honored by the cowherds, and was likewise received with hospitality by me and you.
Then other attendants of Viṣṇu, Hara, and Brahmā, as well as goddesses and female servants, having learned [of this], arrived and stood there on level ground.
Then I asked them: "On what auspicious spot on earth is it desired that [the Lord] should quickly manifest for the sake of the welfare of the world? (16)
Just then, Dharaṇī and Meruparvata arrived there and, while the virtuous were listening, they both entreated me for the sake of sons. (17)
"I shall do so," I replied to those two auspicious mind-born sons of Brahmā; they were then born as human beings in Surāṣṭra. (18)
The cowherd named Merudhara and the cowherdess Kṣamādevī established a divine residence near Somanātha. ||19||
The cowherds, the gopīs, and the cows, having fully worshipped Hari and Hara,
all departed together with the goddess Kṣamā and Meru.
Having made their dwelling in the Siṃhāraṇya forest, they remained there rejoicing:
Śambhu, the illustrious Gopanātha, Viṣṇu, and likewise Gopīśvara. (21)
In that place where they were worshipped, the two became the very embodiments of their forms;
there the cowherds and cowherd-maidens constantly came and went.
O Rādhā, that sacred ford, consisting of both Hari and Hara, has become Gopanātha;
it is supremely purifying and sanctified by the feet of you and me. 23.
O Rādhikā, where Meru himself resides and where the Earth, my mother, dwells,
there I was born as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the mind-born son.
You, along with me, the gopīs, the mānaṣīs, and others as well,
were born right there in the city called Merukoṭī.
Wherever the golden Sarasvatī flows eastward,
and wherever Someśa is located, that land is as Meru-koṭikā.
And that region of mine, consisting of divine play, became manifest before dawn;
O Rādhā, it was pervaded by your feet, and the door to liberation was thrown open.
The blessed Sanatkumāra was my guru there; the cowherds, cowherd women, and cows always dwelt with me in that place. (28)
At that time, I was Gopāla, and my original primary abode was here;
that Mūlā Dvārikā of mine is renowned as Merukoṭi.
In the east lies Śatruñjaya, and as far as the Sarasvatī in the west;
to the north is the Mahābhadrā river—this was my sacred field in ancient times.
Kṛtasmara, Parvata, the great forest of Siṃhāraṇya, the forest of Vyāghra, and Aśvapaṭṭasara—these are my lands. 3.11.
O Rādhā, there was another supreme ground of the monastery that was delightful,
where the cowherds, the cowherdesses, and the cows traveled through the path of the sky.
They always dwelt there indeed by the power of the god Meru;
my attendants, both gods and goddesses, had established their dwellings there. (33)
At that time, all of them settled in various places out of a constant desire to serve me;
Saurāṣṭra was then filled with gopīs who were devotees of Kṛṣṇa.
Goloka, that abode, was likewise present there with Rādhā and the cowherds;
and there was the Gāruḍī Saṃhitā, which discerns my sovereign power. (35)
On the bank of the Madhuvatī there was my grove-land;
and in the midst of Siṃhāraṇya, there was formerly my divine abode. (36)
It was surrounded by a moat and beautified by a natural lake in its center;
it was situated in the midst of a garden extending for two yojanas.
There, all my wives were beautiful queens; traveling by aerial chariot, those beloved ones accompanied me on every journey. (38)
O Rādhikā, all my attendants, both gods and goddesses, dwelt at various places in Saurāṣṭra by my command.
The twelve Ādityas, the eleven Rudras, both Aśvins, the eight Vasus, the Nidhis, as well as the nine and eight Siddhis; ||| 2.64.40 ||
The seven sages, the ten arrows, the Manus who are the deities of the lunar days, the digits, the principles, the circle of constellations, and millions of qualities. ||41||
The Maruts, the circle of Yoginīs, the Kalās, the Nāḍīs, and the Dāsikās—the Vālakhilyas born of the primordial creation—have taken refuge in me. 42.
Virajā, Kamalā, Gaṅgā, Ramā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Durgā, Rādhā, Padminī, Pārvatī, Mañjulā, and Prabhā. 43.
Saguṇā, Śāradā, Haṃsā, Suśīlā, Subhagā, Śrī, and others like them, having come from my Goloka to my abode, [reside there]. 44.

Likewise, the rivers, the sacred fords, the divine lands, the wish-fulfilling trees, the wish-fulfilling creepers, and the wish-fulfilling pillars, grasses, and so forth, all took up residence there. (45)
And wish-fulfilling trees, wish-fulfilling jewels, garlands of wish-fulfilling gems;
wish-fulfilling vessels, and whatever wish-fulfilling articles there may be—46.
The divine Kalpapāvaṭikās, Kalpagūṭikās, Kalpakaṇṭhikās, and Kalpormikās indeed dwell there in embodied form. 47.
Thus, O Rādhikā, have I reminded you of the former events concerning Gurjara, Maru, Kaccha, as well as the South and the North. (48)
Indeed, my previous births were infinite;
they occurred sometimes among the gods, sometimes among the ṛṣis, and sometimes in the human lineage. (49)
Whether I am born among the twice-born or in another family, I shall be so out of a desire for my purpose;
you, remaining in my heart, shall never indeed abandon me.
O Rādhikā, wherever I may be situated, I am always with you alone— in Goloka, in the cow-pen, and even among the gopīs.
O Rādhā, even among the gopīs, I shall never abandon you;
for you are considered my supreme power, just as I am myself. (52)
Those who worship me, the Supreme Lord endowed with Śakti, in this manner go to my abode, Goloka, and dwell by my side. (53)
Thus, O Rādhā, have my births and previous lives been told;
by remembering or even hearing this, enjoyment and liberation are produced. (54)
Those who shall restore what is decayed or cause it to be restored at my sacred site will dwell by my side in my world; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of All Primary Sacred Fields and Pilgrimage Sites of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in Saurāṣṭra," within the majesty of Gopanātha, in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Furthermore, O Rādhā, listen to the Vedic ritual for Kṛṣṇa who has departed for his own realm—a procedure that purifies even the purifiers of all. || 1 ||
He who, in ancient times, was himself the author of the Vedas and indeed instructed Brahmā—
having taken recourse to this world and protected his own ordinance— [he now departs].
Just as a base Brahmin-pupil receives the Vedic initiation (brahmasaṃskāra),
so too [the Lord] received that by which the state of being twice-born was created at the beginning of creation for the sake of eternal welfare.
But he, having grasped the Sūtra, becomes twice-born even if he was not twice-born;
by his touch, women, men, trees, and creepers [are likewise purified]. (4)
Even those such as animals, ghosts, and piśācas are purified when they perceive the Self;
for through whose yoga even desires and the like always attain a divine state.
By attaining union with whom even yakṣas, rākṣasas, or those born of barbarian wombs become divine in an instant— he has now become this Brahmagraha.
O Rādhikā, Lomaśa said to the father and mother of Hari:
"This purifier of sacrifices has now become fit for the sacred thread ceremony."
And the sacred thread (brahmasūtra) should be given to him, the supreme self who has bestowed the thread;
having thus heard these auspicious words from the mouth of Lomaśa.
Then, with their parents being well-pleased, Gopāla and Kṛṣṇa bowed down to the worthy sage; out of devotion, he granted them a divine elephant-throne.
He offered the honey-mixture (madhuparka), necklaces, sweet food, and water;
he also presented betel-leaf, fruit, and auspicious garments.
He said to Lomaśa: "O Lord, make this an occasion for an auspicious festival;
the month of Vaiśākha is now approaching, if it pleases you. (11)
A festival must certainly be celebrated there; it appears to me as entirely appropriate. Show me a day that is auspicious and suitable for the investiture with the sacred thread (yajñopavīta).
Then Lomaśa spoke to the illustrious Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa:
"The third lunar day, which bestows imperishability, is indeed inexhaustible and supreme. (13)
Through the purification of the strength of the moon and the lunar mansions, all auspiciousness proceeds;
and grant that same [strength] to everyone throughout the three worlds as an invitation. (14)

Accumulate the provisions and divine enjoyments that are exceedingly difficult to obtain—those which are suitable for those dwelling in different worlds and are the most excellent of the excellent to be cultivated. (15)
Having heard the words of Lomaśa, the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa dispatched divine auspicious letters everywhere.
He dispatched attendants and servants, as well as those dwelling by the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, in every direction, mounted upon celestial chariots and aerial palaces.
"In the eighth year from my birth, during the month of Vaiśākha, on the auspicious Akṣaya-tithi of the bright fortnight, the sacred thread ceremony for my son Śrī Hari shall take place. (18)
Together with the incarnations, as well as the liberated ones, along with the abodes, the Brahmas, the male attendants, and all the female attendants in every way. (19)
By virtuous women, female attendants, and those who have descended [to earth], by lords and sovereigns, and also by sages with their families. || 2.65.20 ||
One should come with respect together with virtuous ascetics, devoted followers of the Lord, and female devotees who are themselves devotees of the Lord. 21.

Together with the ancestors accompanied by their wives, the gods joined by their goddesses, the guardians of the directions and the guardians of the worlds, and the circles of planets and constellations; ||22||

And likewise by the stars, by the principles (tattvas), and also by the inhabitants of the earth, by humans, by trees, creepers, and so forth, and by those born from the lineage of the wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavṛkṣa). ||23||
With grasses, shrubs, and plants growing from the earth; with birds, singers, and people;
and also with Vidyādharas, Kinnaras, and Kimpuṃsas skilled in the art of dance. ||24||
It was surrounded on all sides by dancers and bards born of the lineages of Dharma and Adharma, as well as by the families of gods and asuras and the lords of the directions.
"You must come to the festival for my son’s sacred thread ceremony, along with all the holy fords, rivers, streams, forests, groves, and lakes. (26)

All those dwelling upon the earth—mountains, birds, and aquatic creatures such as those in the ocean, the moats, and the wells—must assemble from every direction, including all the winged beings. (27)
With reverence, [he was honored] by the qualities and the substrates of those qualities, both manifest and unmanifest, along with the times, the seasons, the primordial powers, and the years. ||28||
Even by means of the wish-fulfilling cows, the Vasus, and the Siddhis; by the treasures (Nidhis), and by Viṣṇu, Rudra, and others, as well as Brahmā and others with their many heads. ||29||
And by the best of kings beginning with Indra, as well as by men, sages, brahmins, eminent kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and likewise by servants. ||2.65.30||
Those who are of the nature of sattva, rajas, and tamas, as well as those who are illusory,
must come with their illusions and primal natures to the sacred thread ceremony.
By the Daityas, Dānavas, and Asuras dwelling in the netherworld (Atala) and below,
as well as by the Nāgas and Sarpas, together with their kinsmen, friends, family members, and physical bodies.
One should come here with vehicles, means of accomplishment, and likewise with elixirs;
and with both divine and non-divine vidyās, as well as with the kalās and so forth.
Through the essence of your splendor and your blessings, my young son has grown;
he will certainly become a mass of merit like a sacrifice. (34)
Having thus dispatched the letters by means of servants,
[he sent] whatever foods there were in the abodes of that Lord of Pure Beings.
In the Supreme Brahman, in the imperishable Goloka, in Vikuṇṭha, in the immortal world of the Lord, and in Satyaloka, there are indeed nectars. ||36||
He also quickly caused a collection to be made there of divine Brahma-jala waters, as well as those that are to be licked and sucked.
And likewise, whatever edible, drinkable, and useful things there may be in the worlds of Bhuvaḥ, Mahas, Jana, and so forth, as well as their collections— [all these he should offer].
In heaven, in ascetic groves, on Mount Meru and other peaks, upon the earth, and throughout the seven netherworlds—whatever foods, edibles, drinks, and articles of utility there may be; || 39 ||

Those things which are to be trampled, those unfit for service, those fit for enjoyment by living beings, those suitable for moving and stationary entities, and those consisting of both formal and formless objects—[all these arise from it]. (2.65.40)
Śrīmad Gopālakṛṣṇa likewise caused many types of stores for all those various articles to be established, ensuring they were neither accumulated nor depleted. ||41||
The lakes of Brahmā, the lakes of the Kalpas, the juices of the Kalpa-trees and so forth, inexhaustible vessels, and likewise plantains that fill them at will. ||42||
He gathered around him inexhaustible treasuries of lotuses, the most excellent vessels for attaining supernatural powers, as well as the eightfold magical accomplishments and enchanted pills.
He gave thousands of alms-bowls, many wish-fulfilling gems (cintāmaṇi), as well as those that produce wonders, and the most excellent *brahmapuṣpa* flowers. ||44||
The excellent illusions of the gods, the threads of the goddesses, the snares of magicians, as well as jewels and garlands numbering a hundred thousand; ||45||
He gathered from all sides mantras, yantras, tantras, and likewise various wonders, as well as the stalks of the nectar of yogic sovereignty.
He gathered together from all sides yogic hearths, yogic ladles, yogic cauldrons, yogic ovens, yogic pots, and yogic lamps.
All the yogic postures, the universal nectars, the kalpa-trees, the kalpa-throated birds, and the kalpa-vinyls with their ring-like tendrils; ||48||
He collected in many ways all manner of foodstuffs for the sake of hospitality,
both solid foods and drinks.
The foods and drinks produced from subtle elements are themselves subtle; likewise, the foods and drinks produced from manifest elements are themselves manifest. (2.65.50)
Foodstuffs produced from the unmanifest, as well as drinks produced from the unmanifest—all those born of Māyā, and likewise those which are Brāhma—[should be known]. ||51||
Even the divine syllables, which consist of the Self, as well as all those born of affection and arisen from the reality of merit; ||52||
He also gathered from all sides every kind of object of enjoyment:
charming channels of juice, channels of ghee, and channels of curd.
Rivers of honey, rivers of molasses, lakes of sugar-candies, streams of sugarcane juice, pools of nectar, and lakes of sweet water.
The illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa gathered [offerings] all around him;
he constructed mountains of thousands of sacrificial offerings.
And he [saw] heaps of jewels, gems, and pearls,
as well as mountains of gold, silver, and diamonds.
At that time, he indeed caused mountains of rubies, pearls, and ornaments, as well as heaps of garments and jewelry, to be prepared.
Likewise, [he saw] heaps of powders, of fragrant essences, of scented oils,
of ointments, of collyriums, and of pigments.
He made inexhaustible heaps of sandalwood, saffron, and kesara flowers, as well as piles of musk and medicinal herbs.
Of mirrors, combs, cleansing substances, and earth; likewise of beds, swings, and wheeled seats. ||2.65.60||
He created countless collections of vehicles and mounts;
thus, when all objects of enjoyment and the like were accomplished and reached completion, [he remained]. (61)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa indeed remembered, in due order,
the liberated souls residing in the supreme abode and all the liberated women as well.
[He perceives] the liberated classes established in the imperishable, as well as the liberated women and the imperishable itself;
the incarnations and those who do not incarnate, and the foremost of the attendants.
[He saw] the male attendants and the female devotees on all sides,
as well as the twenty-four forms of Viṣṇu and the fourfold emanations (caturvyūha) in their proper order.
And the supreme lords and their consorts, the lords and their consorts in every respect, as well as the Vairājas, Brahmās, Śambhus, Rudras, Viṣṇus, and likewise the sages. ||65||
He [honored] the virtuous men and women, the faithful wives, and his beloved goddesses such as Ramā;
[he honored] Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Prabhā, Haṃsā, and Māṇikī. (66)
He also saw his own principal wives, numbering one hundred and twelve,
as well as millions of female and male servants, the cows and other animals residing in Goloka.
And those residing in the four Vaikuṇṭhas, those dwelling at Badarikāśrama,
those established in Satyaloka, those living in heaven, and likewise those who have gone to the highest heaven.
He remembered the ancestors, the Siddhas, the Cāraṇas, the lords of sages, gods and humans,
as well as the guardians of the quarters, the kings who protect the gods.
Those dwelling in the intermediate space, those situated on the earth, and those residing in the seven netherworlds;
all those stationed in water or on land, both the immobile and the mobile. ||2.65.70||
Likewise, from the lake of Brahmā came the Apsarases, the most excellent maidens,
as well as Bhaṭas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Kiṃpuruṣas, Kinnaras, and Māgadhas.
He also [honored] wandering minstrels, musicians, singers, and dancers;
as well as actors, playwrights, and those who present theatrical troupes. ||72||
He also [summoned] wrestlers, artisans, and great magicians,
as well as sweet-makers, cooks, preparers of food, and servers.

[He saw] those worthy of sacrifice and those who know the sacrifice, as well as those devoted to the ritual section (karmakāṇḍa), Brāhmaṇas, great sages (maharṣis), and guardians of the fields, gates, and other such places. ||74||
He remembered the divine principles, the humans with divine forms,
and the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas who dwell in water and on land.

The wretched and the destitute, the virtuous, the followers of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, devoted wives, maidens, goddesses, those born of noble lineage, those worthy of honor in their families, and female practitioners of Yoga—[he honored them all]. (76)
Then Śrī Hari remembered those who dwell on Kailāsa and Badarī, those who reside in Kṣīraśveta, and those who live in the various regions upon the earth. 77.

He remembered his devotees— the cowherds and cowherd-maidens, who were as numerous as millions, billions, and trillions— as well as the Vālakhilyas and his own ascetic disciples who take refuge in knowledge.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord Narāyaṇa, who is affectionate toward His devotees, remembered His devotees with His divine mind. (79)
On the morning of the third day, known as Akṣayā, they all assembled together in vehicles that moved with the speed of Brahmā, whether by aerial chariots or by means of their own minds.
They arrived by means of self-borne vehicles, vehicles of yoga, as well as vehicles that are the mounts of meditative concentration,
vehicles drawn by the wind, and vehicles whose nature is the sky.
Likewise, Garuḍas, swans, parrots, peacocks, and mongooses, as well as Vināyakas, Gaṇeśas, and Vighneśas, arrived there. 82.
With elephants, horses, fires, and kuñjaka birds, with cranes and the like, with clouds, planets, as well as streaks of lightning and rays of light; ||83||
The sun, the moon, and others, swift carriers of light, arrived; those who carry the mind, those who carry the eon, and those who carry speed all came together. (84)
The liberated ones, as well as the incarnations, the emanations, and likewise the lords—all have gone to the abode of Brahmā, and likewise to the abode of Īśa. ||85||

Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, along with Lakṣmī, Rādhā, Ramā, and the others, together with their female companions—the Śrīs—who are as numerous as millions upon millions of arbudas and padmas of treasures, [are present]. (86)
Likewise, Rāma, Mādhava, and Govinda, along with the cowherds and cowherd-maidens, were accompanied by attendants numbering in the hundreds of millions, arbudas, and padmas.
The Viṣṇus, headed by the Vaiṣṇavī power, the deities of the earth, the Vairājas, and the Brahmās, Rudras, and others—numbering hundreds of millions—[all bowed]. (88)
The virtuous who abide in truth, the gods, ascetics, and celibate students;
the Vedas, the sciences, as well as the mantras, the sacrifices, and whatever oblations there may be—[all these are established in the Self]. (89)
The gods of celestial form, the fires, the winds,
all the luminous energies, the ancestors, the sages, and the immortals arrived there.
There were lords of sages, virtuous men, truthful women, chaste wives devoted to their husbands, those dear to Brahmā, those dear to Kṛṣṇa, and those dear to the gods, on every side. (91)
There were queens and kings of the fourteen worlds,
as well as daughters of Brahmā, daughters of Ṛṣis, daughters of the waters, and those born of the ocean.
Daughter-gods, daughter-nāgas, and daughter-kings by the millions;
as well as maiden-gandharvas and maiden-vidyādharas from all quarters. (93)
Orators and musicians, as well as those who sing his praises, arrived; along with bards, wandering minstrels, and others, there came porters, actors, and dancers. (94)
There were performers of rituals, storytellers, jesters, and even Brahmins who were mendicants, wandering for the sake of renunciation, and likewise those who wore shaven heads. (95)
Avadhūtas, celibate students, and practitioners of yoga arrived, accompanied by their wives, kinsmen, children, and others, resting in their second stage. (96)

The lineages of those devoted to their wives, the households of those faithful to their husbands, the associations with kinsmen and relatives, and the excellent unions resulting from those connections—[all these were present]. (97)
Indeed, all those who bear bodies have not arisen from a single source;
for there are countless hosts of Viṣṇu, hosts of Rudra, and hosts of Brahmā. 98.
The Dīpāvalyas, the Nālamedhyas, the Ṣaṣṭhīdevīs, the Talājikas, the Gokumāryas, the Arjantīs, the Yuvatīs, and the Śatakanyakās. ||99||
There were ten million maidens from the caves, as well as the virtuous Krodhanikā; there were one hundred thousand daughters of Rākṣasīs, and five or six Kaṅkatālīs.
Thousands of Kaṅkatālikā maidens were present, as well as thousands of Brahma-maidens, Jala-maidens, and Āryama-maidens. || 10.1 ||
The daughters of Kubera, the daughters of Indra, as well as the daughters of Yama;
the daughters of Vāyu, the daughters of the Seasons, and likewise the daughters of Viśvakarman. || 102 ||
Five thousand daughters of the Dānavas and others,
as well as the sixteen wives of Vasanta, were likewise present.
Likewise, there were thousands of daughters of Vahni, as well as thousands of daughters of Sāla and Māla, daughters of Śravaṇa, and thousands of daughters of Śāva and Dīna. || 104 ||
The fierce sorceresses of Indra, as well as a thousand maidens,
the Vidyā-kanyās, the young girls, and the sixty maidens were present there.
The daughters of the Year, the innumerable daughters of Vārkṣya,
and the maidens born from the earth, together with their water-jars, have indeed presented themselves.
Two thousand mechanical dolls were presented to Lakṣmaṇa;
at that time, three hundred mechanical dolls were presented to Viśvāvasu.
Seventy-two thousand Vedha-maidens presented themselves,
and a thousand maidens also stood before King Jumāsena.
Twelve hundred young girls of dark complexion arrived for the sake of the auspiciousness of that beloved Hari.
They indeed performed the kīrtanas of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
and the father provided lodgings for the arriving groups.
He offered various honors, such as the madhuparka, in many ways according to their merit;
nevertheless, O Rādhikā, great sages continued to arrive there.

Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, titled "The Demonstration of the Arrival of All by Means of Invitation Cards," in the second section on the Tretā Age of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, during the eighth year of the Lord’s life, in the month of Vaiśākha, on the occasion of the great festival of the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*).
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā; the divine great sages have arrived—Samīraṇa, Pavamāna, Santāraṇa, and Barbura.
Voḍhu, Ghanabheda, Dyuviśrāma, Paṅkila, Nīlakaṇṭha, Alarka, Puṇḍarīka, and Kalāyana. || 2 ||
Vītihotra, Camasa, Parṇakutsa, Aśvapāṭala, Bhāllaveya, Ūrjavrata, and also Āśvalāyana. || 3 ||
Pārṣṇirada, Sumantu, Aśokākṣa, Abhayākṣaka,
Brahmastamba, Kūpyavāla, and Cetanabrahma— these, along with Mṛtadaṇḍa, attended that great festival there,
accompanied by their wives, sons, daughters, and so forth, as well as their servants, male and female slaves. || 4-5 ||
Kauṇḍinya, Kauśika, Pautimāṣya, Gaupavana, Śāṇḍilya, Gautama, Agniveśya, and Amlāna as well. || 6 ||
Saitava, Prācīnayogya, Dhārāśarya, Maindava, Bhāradvāja, Vaijavāpāyana, and Kauśikāyani. || 7 ||
Ghṛtaka, Kauśika, Yāska, Āsurāyaṇa, Traivaṇi,
Jātūkarṇya, Aupajaghanya, Āsurī, Māṇṭi, and Vātsya.
Kaiśorya, Kāpya, Ātreya, Kumārahārīta, Vaidarbhi, Vatsanapāt, Gālava, and Saubhari; || 9 ||
Panthā Āyāsya, Ābhūti Tvaṣṭra, the Aśvins, Dadhīca, Viśvarūpa Vipracitti, and Prādhvaṃsana Ātharvaṇa. || 2.66.10 ||
Sanāru, Vyaṣṭi, Ekarṣi, Sanaga, and Sanātana;
Uddālakāyana, Jābālāyana, and Parameṣṭhika. || 11 ||
Mādhyandināyana, Kāṣāyaṇa, Saukarāyaṇa, Aupajaṅghani, Yāska, Sāṃkṛti, and Sāyakāyana. || 12 ||
These and other Vālakhilyas, as well as other preeminent sages, arrived for the great festival of the Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa Sūtra. (13)
Śauṅgī, Sukṛti, Ālambī, Jāyantī, Maṇḍukāyanī, Śāṇḍilī, Pautimāṣī, Kātyāyanī, and Gautamī. || 14 ||
The Dhārāśarī, Aupasvatī, Bhāradvājī, Kauśikī, Kāpī, Vaiyāghrapadī, Ālambī, Vātsī, and Saubhagī. || 15 ||
Vārkāruṇī, Prajāyantī, Ātreyī, Ārtabhāginī, Kāṇvī, Ālambāyanī, Māṇḍūkī, and likewise Bhālukī. || 16 ||
Rāthītarī, Krauñcikī, Vaidabhṛtyā, Surāyaṇī, Sāñjivī, Prācīnayogī, Prāśnī, and Kārśakeyikā. || 17 ||
Satī, Śāmaraduhitā, Dhanyeśvarī, Rāṇikī, and these wives of the sages all arrived there for that festival. || 18 ||
Divine and adorned with celestial ornaments, clad in garments purified by fire, they were filled with the splendor of their asceticism, auspicious and resembling a mass of merit.
Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Cyavana, Bharadvāja of great asceticism,
Garga, Gārgya, Yājñavalkya, Śvetavyāsa, and Bhīmaka.
Dharma, Vatsa, Pulaha, Jaigīṣavya, Pulastya, Agastya, Saubhari, Sanaka, and Sanātana; || 21 ||
Sananda, Sanat, and the youth Sujāta;
Ketu, Pañcaśikha, Durvāsas, and likewise Aṅgiras. || 22 ||
Śuka, Rāma, Kuśika, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Vibhāṇḍaka, Vāmadeva, as well as Śṛṅgin, Kratu, Yati, and Aruṇi; || 23 ||
Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Vāmana, Pāribhadraka, Aṣṭāvakra, Paila, Vālmīki, and likewise Madhujit. (24)
Pracetas, Purujit, Bhṛgu, Marīci, Ekaka, Dvīta, Trīta, Kātyāyana, and Sumantu. || 25 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya, Kaśyapa, Dakṣa, Sūrya, and likewise Śaśin;
Saṃvarta, Utathya, Nara, and likewise Nārāyaṇa;
Viśvāmitra, Śatānanda, Jābāli, and likewise Taitila. || 26 ||
Upamanyu, Gauramukha, Maitreya, Kaṭha, and Kaca. || 27 ||
Aditi, Diti, and the chaste Kṛttikās, accompanied by their families and disciples, went to the hermitage of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. || 28 ||
The illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa prostrated himself like a staff upon the ground before them;
then Brahmā, seated upon his swan and accompanied by Sāvitrī, departed.
Seated upon a divine vehicle, Śambhu traveled through the sky accompanied by Satī;
Nandin, Kāla, Vīrabhadra, Subhadra, Maṇibhadra, and Bhadraka [followed].
Pāribhadra, Gaṇeśa, Skanda, and Rudra arrived;
as did Kubera, Varuṇa, Mahendra, Agni, and Anila. || 31 ||
Yama, the Grahas, the Vasus, the Ādityas, and the Śeṣa-bhōginas—all these great beings arrived, worthy of worship and honor. ||32||
Gopālakṛṣṇa, with devotion, prostrated before them with his head upon the ground;
he then praised those respective lords of creation with supreme affection.
The illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa said: The Supreme Lord, the Supreme Person, shines in the supreme abode as the Supreme Brahman;
higher than the highest, he is accompanied by those who are eternally liberated.
"Today indeed the Supreme Lord of the worlds resides in my house!
Oh, what great fortune it is for me that Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa has come here! (35)
Oh, what fortune mine that Vāsudeva and the others have arrived!
Oh, what fortune that the incarnations of the Supreme Lord have arrived! (36)
The lords, those liberated from their abodes, and other liberated beings assembled there;
as did Bhūmā, Virāṭ, Viṣṇu himself, Vidhātṛ, and the Lord who creates the universe.
A great brahmin devoted to his wife has also come to my house;
he is himself the teacher of teachers, worthy of worship by perfected beings, virtuous women, ascetics, and yogis. (38)
"Brahmā himself resides in my house; indeed, great is my fortune today, for by worshipping him, a person attains enjoyment, liberation, and residence in the same world as him. || 39 ||
And by his majesty, may there be the destruction of all calamities;
this Gaṇeśa, who is the very form of the glorious Kṛṣṇa, dwells in my temple. 2.66.40.
I am foremost among the gods, worthy of worship, and in every way blessed upon this earth;
so too are the Lord Śaṅkara and Viṣṇu accompanied by Lakṣmī.
Rādhā is the mother of the worlds, Pārvatī is her primordial form;
she is the primal Mūlaprakṛti and the very nature of the Supreme Brahman.
That auspicious mother, by worshipping whose feet the practitioner obtains his desire, is herself present here in my house today. (43)
The daughters of the divine abodes, the most excellent among those liberated from their realms, and the Sādhyas dwell in my house;
blessed is this Kambharā-Lakṣmī, for whom there is this vision. 44.
And today, the vision of women created by Brahmā, of virtuous wives created by the Lord, and of sovereign goddesses has truly been fulfilled before our very eyes. (45)
Blessed is Lake Aśvapaṭṭa, blessed is Kuṅkumavāpikā,
and blessed is the land of Saurāṣṭra, where the glorious Supreme Lords reside.
The ancestors, the seers, the gods, and the goddesses, as well as the fundamental principles (tattvas), reside in my house;
and all those dwelling in the netherworlds, both the manifest and the unmanifest, dwell in my home. (47)
Today my birth has become fruitful; this age I have lived through is fruitful;
today my creation is fruitful, and my life is fruitful.
And today, indeed, the honors of the three worlds reside in whose house?
In my house are the creation of Brahmā, the creation of Īśa, and the creation of Jīva. (49)
Having thus paid homage to them all, he caused them to be seated according to protocol upon suitable thrones in the great palace of Śatamabhūmi.
The father, assuming a form at will and manifesting in ten million billion forms, worshipped [him] according to the rules and in due order throughout the ten yojanas.
The Supreme Lord individually chose the gods and others,
as well as the groups of sages, seers, holy men, liberated ones, deities, and the twice-born.
And with devotion, he chose the sage Lomaśa as his own domestic priest,
honoring him with jewels, corals, necklaces, and ornaments of pearls from the Kalpa tree.
In the midst of all, he chose Śrī Gaṇeśa for worship, who was seated upon a jeweled lion-throne adorned with garments, perfumes, garlands, gems, rubies, diamonds, and sandalwood pastes.
One should bathe with water the elephant-faced deity who is established in auspicious action. ||55||
And with waters brought from the heart of Brahmā, with the waters brought by Viraja, with the waters of the ocean-enclosure, and with the waters of the celestial Gaṅgā and of Meru; ||56||
And with the waters of the seven oceans, as well as the waters of all sacred fords (tīrtha), which are cool and endowed with the fragrance of flowers and sandalwood and the essence of nectar; ||57||
Likewise, with devotion, he bathed [the image] with milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugar, and the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||58||
He worshipped Gaṇeśa, who is the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of all obstacles,
the bestower of all auspiciousness, and the God, with various offerings.
With flowers of the *pārijāta* tree and likewise with *brāhma* and *kamala* lotuses,
with *dūrvā* grass from Vaikuṇṭha, and with ornaments of precious gems.
And also with garments purified by fire, as well as with *brāhma-sindūra*,
perfumes, sandalwood, flowers, and golden finger-ornaments.
Having thus worshipped Gaṇeśa according to the prescribed rites, one should thereafter worship Rādhā,
Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Prabhā, Śrī, Māṇikī, Ramā,
Mañjulā, Saguṇā, Haṃsā, Jayā, Lalitā, and Dayā.
Likewise, [he saw] other illustrious and virtuous chaste women dwelling in the abodes of the Lord;
he also saw the wives of Kṛṣṇa, as well as Mahālakṣmī, Sāvitrī, and Sarasvatī.
Gaṅgā, Diti, Aditi, the wives of the sages devoted to their husbands,
the goddesses who are sovereign mistresses, and the beautiful wives of the ancestors.
Kambharā worshipped the yoginīs, the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs, as well as Lopāmudrā and others, who were devoted to their husbands and honored by the earth.
Likewise, the daughters of Arbuda and Abja, though graced with great beauty,
repeatedly embraced Kambharā in the forms of Arbuda and Arbuda.
Having conversed with one another and embraced each other,
Kambharālakṣmī settled them all within the palace.
He honored him with garlands, garments, and jeweled ornaments,
as well as with the flowers of the Brahmavṛkṣa and the blossoms of the Pārijāta tree.
Likewise, she was adorned with dots of vermilion upon her parting hair,
and with beautiful crescent-moon patterns and sandalwood dots upon her forehead.
Having worshipped him with fragrant substances such as musk, saffron, and lac, he fed him various kinds of sweet foods appropriate for his station.
And Kambharāśrī gave nectar-like water and betel leaf well-scented with camphor and other fragrances to the wives of the sages in due order.
She duly honored the virtuous women who possessed husbands and sons—the beautiful daughters of the gods, the daughters of Īśa, and the daughters of the ancestors. ||72||
Daughter-goddesses of the gods, daughter-goddesses of the nāgas, and daughter-goddesses of humans who have taken refuge in the Bull;
likewise, daughter-goddesses of the Bandhus, daughter-goddesses of devotees, and those born of the Gandharvas and Asuras. ||73||
He honored him according to the prescribed rites, fed him with great respect,
and lodged him in palatial mansions provided with magnificent gardens.
The musicians played auspicious musical instruments;
he caused auspicious rites to be performed and fed the Brahmins. (75)
The illustrious queen worshipped the goddess Kuṅkumavāpikeshvarī,
as well as Ṣaṣṭhī and the deity Maṅgala, with all necessary materials.
The father worshipped the village deities and the lake deities with devotion;
indeed, he honored all the great beings with every form of offering.
Then he caused meritorious rites for well-being and auspicious ceremonies to be performed; he had the Vedas recited and had songs sung. (78)
And with the waters of the Gaṅgā held in golden jars, his mother bathed Acyuta, the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
With garments, sandalwood paste, garlands, and other ornaments, she made her appearance beautiful,
adorned with divine raiment, celestial decorations, and divine sandalwood unguents.
Then [he spoke] to the lords who had entered the assembly,
to the ascetics, to the sages, to the gods, and to the embodied beings among men.
And when Hari Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa arrived there with his father, he indeed became the perfected one for all those who had come from the three worlds. (82)
Then the incarnations, the lords, the gods, the Manus, the human beings, the sages, and others all arose and paid homage to the Supreme Lord. ||83||
You are indeed the manifest Supreme Brahman; you shine forth as Bālakṛṣṇa.
You are truly the one who assumes incarnations, the witness whose form is attained through grace. ||84||
Untainted, the bed of the Self, and the cause of all creation and so forth—
Mahāviṣṇu, Virāṭ, Bhūman, Brahmā, Śeṣa, and the others abide within You,
O Lord of Śrī, Kṛṣṇa, like gnats within a cosmic egg.
And we, being virtuous, are the gods who are portions of you in all creations. ||86||
Indeed, innumerable cosmic eggs reside upon the coils of Śeṣa;
Śeṣa rests upon the Tortoise, and the Tortoise moves within the waters. (87)
Water always exists above fire and strength like a cloud;
fire has wind as its support, and wind moves within space.

This space [of the world] shines within the space of consciousness (cidākāśa), and the space of consciousness shines within the Imperishable (akṣara); and the Imperishable shines within the state of Brahman, which is the Supreme Lord. 89.
"You are this glorious Supreme Lord; you exist as the son of Yaśodā.
You are truly the cowherd boy manifest before our very eyes."
Thus praised, Kṛṣṇa himself, whose nature is that of a child and who is the lord of the splendors of Rādhā and Ramā, shone exceedingly in the midst of the assembly.
Two-armed, rich with white luster, golden-hued, and captivating; with a face brightened by a slight smile, he shines resplendent with ornaments.
First, for the sake of purifying his body, Acyuta performed three *kṛcchra* penances;
then, when an auspicious moment and a favorable planetary alignment had arrived, [he proceeded]. 92.
When the lord of the ascendant at dawn is situated and aspected by benefic planets, one should undertake work that is not within the range of the aspect of malefic planets. 94.
For the very purpose of purifying the faults incurred from eating and drinking according to his own will,
he gave three cows as a gift and caused the recitation of benedictions.
At the command of Lomaśa, he gave a thousand gold pieces and a treasure of jewels as a gift to the Brahmins, and he paid homage to the deities.
Having worshipped Viṣṇu, Śiva, Gaṇeśa, Pārvatī, and Sūrya,
and having duly honored the Fire-god, the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa— || 97 ||
In the assembly, he performed the consecration of his son with Vedic mantras,
having duly worshipped the gods, the planetary deities, the guardians of the directions, and likewise the Mothers.
Having performed the Nāndī-śrāddha and the Mahāśānti rite immediately thereafter,
he performed a fire-oblation (homa) upon an altar and in a consecrated fire.
Then, having offered the *vasudhārā* seven times with clarified butter,

he performed the *vṛddhi-śrāddha*, the *daiva-śrāddha*, and the libations for the ancestors (*pitṛ-tarpaṇa*). To his son, who had been shaved, bathed, released from [the vow], and adorned as a celibate student (*brahmacārin*),
the father gave a waist-thread, a loincloth, and a sacred thread (*yajñasūtra*).
Having tied the three-stranded girdle of muñja grass around his waist and [the tuft] upon his hairy ear,
Lomaśa imparted the Gāyatrī mantra three times into his right ear.
Having caused the offering of clarified butter (ājyahoma) to be performed, the sage taught the dharmas;
thereafter, Śrī, Arā, and Rādhikāprabhā gave him alms.
The female lords (Īśvarāṇīs) and the liberated ones (Muktānyas), the Sādhyas and the goddesses (Devīs), the maidens (Kanyakās), Mahālakṣmī, Prakṛti, Haṃsā, Lakṣmī, and Pārvatī. || 104 ||
The beautiful and virtuous daughters of the sun, as well as the daughters of the Lord (Śiva),
the daughters of gods, nāgas, and kings, and the daughters of the three worlds and others— || 105 ||
All the daughters of Kārṣṇi residing in the hermitage of Lomaśa possessed divine forms;
they were Kaṃbharāśrī, Amṛtā, and others who were the mothers of gods, Daityas, and so forth.

The wives of the lords of sages, as well as the consorts of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, and the beloved wives of the guardians of the quarters, each separately gave alms. Having accepted the alms in a divine golden vessel adorned with priceless jewels, the Blessed One gave a small portion to Lomaśa.

Lomaśa bestowed upon him the sacred thread reaching to the crown of his head, the staff of Brahmā, the deerskin as an upper garment, the performance of worship and the twilight prayers, the water-pot, and virtuous conduct.
All the other Blessed Ones gave him highly precious alms: strings of jewels, necklaces of gems, and ornaments of gold.
And the beings of divine origin gave him various nectars and objects of enjoyment, which they had brought from their own worlds. || 111 ||
Then, having thus completed the ritual, Gopālakṛṣṇaka gave gold, diamonds, and jewels as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to Lomaśa.
The father gave his son a diamond necklace that provides protection;
likewise, the auspicious goddesses, fortunate women, maidens, and mothers bestowed auspicious blessings with white flowers and *dūrvā* grass. (113)
Whosoever arrived at the sacrifice, each of them bestowed auspicious blessings. They sang songs and musical instruments were played;
meanwhile, the father instructed [him] in his lineage, his ancestral sages, the Veda, and its branch.
The lineage (gotra) consists of the Supreme Brahman, and these are the three ancestral sages (pravaras):
they are Akṣarabrahma, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
The Veda is the single, all-encompassing essence, and the Sāman emerged from the illustrious mouth;
the Patnīvratīya is its branch, and you, O Supreme Lord, are the tree itself.
Thus, O Rādhikā, having completed the honors for the assembly,
Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa performed the dismissal of the gathering.

Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual for Bestowing the Sacred Thread and the Worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhā, after the sacred thread ceremony for Śrī Kṛṣṇa was completed, the honors [of the assembly] departed from that assembly hall toward their respective residences. || 1 ||
Then indeed Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, as well as the virtuous Śrī Kambharā, those who have transcended the qualities (guṇātīta), those who are liberated, and countless maidens likewise [departed]. || 2 ||
The sages dwelling there, the sacred fords personified as creepers, the divine principles (tattvas), and likewise the primary Śaktis headed by Śrī; || 3 ||
When the time for the meal had arrived, they signaled to the doorkeeper, the Brahmin Nādaka, to announce [the guests] there for the purpose of invitation; and in a moment, he [did so].
He sounded the sweet-toned Brahmaghaṇṭā bell, which resounds throughout the three worlds,
possesses a melodious sound, and announces the time for the meal.
Then there appeared rows of the Lords of Incarnations, of the Blessed Ones, of the liberated souls established in their abodes, and of the liberated women.
There were hundreds of rows of divine female lords, beginning with Vāsudeva and ending with Vairāja, who possessed physical bodies.
Then they presented divine arbuda-lotuses and padma-lotuses for the maidens,
and served them with nectar and other foods brought from their own abodes.
Divine foods to be chewed and eaten, as well as those to be licked and sucked; likewise, other sweet drinks and various cooked vegetables.
He partook of divine juices, such as *cāranāla*, and similar celestial liquids—
suitable for him— all originating from the Brahma-lake and produced in the Brahma-grove.
And those beloved of Brahmā respectfully served them with auspicious, well-prepared, and inexhaustible cooked foods.
In large vessels, golden bowls, and indeed in smaller vessels, there was auspicious ghee,
curd, milk, milk-preparations, honey, and sugar.
Rice, split pulses, soups, sweetmeats, and all kinds of milk-rice dishes—all these are inauspicious for me in every respect. (13)
Delicious sweetmeats made from rice flour, as well as cakes, pearls,
*sūtraphenī*, *laḍḍukas*, *catuṣkas*, and *śaṣkulis*.
Cloths, ghee-filled cakes, sweet *polikās* with a sweet interior, *phulavaṭīs*, silver-satisfying sweets, *kvathikās*, and likewise *bharjikās*. || 15 ||
There were also *kalikā* cakes, *sevikās*, and likewise *saṃyāvas*;
there were various *caṭanīs* as well, prepared with bitter and salty flavors.
And with great respect, they served him foods prepared with dry ingredients,
as well as waters, sweet drinks, buttermilk, and fresh butter.
Then those lords, being deeply immersed, gave fruits, seeds of fruit, and fragrant lotus stalks, and they made them into vessels.
Then those female lords, who were themselves liberated and the supreme sovereigns of the liberated,
forcibly gave food and other offerings to the friend of Brahmā.
They fed him until his throat was full; being satisfied, they took sips of water, partook of drinks, and accepted betel leaves. || 2.67.20 ||
Thereafter, they took the desired powders for their faces;
those created by Brahmā and Śiva then went to their respective abodes.
Then, beginning with Brahmā, [there were] Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, and their progeny;
the gods, goddesses, and the ancestors, from Satyaloka down to Bhūrloka;
as well as the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the guardians of the quarters, the lords of the gods, and so forth.
All the other celestial maidens sat down there in rows. ||23||
To them, both the daughters of Brahmā and the daughters of Kṛṣṇa joyfully and repeatedly offered seats and frequently performed the service of serving food. ||24||
They indeed gave vessels of sweet food and drink born of truth;
those were sweet foods, foods like nectar, and various kinds of edibles and meals.
He repeatedly gave all kinds of foods to be licked and sucked, as well as those to be chewed and drunk, including rice, vegetables, juices, powders, and so forth. (26)
After they had eaten, those gods then drank water;
they took betel and other mouth-fresheners, and went to their abode. ||27||
Then the sages and the earthly kings, possessing bodies, quickly sat down in rows, having emerged from the four mouths. 28.
Divine and non-divine beings, as well as those with form and without form, and the mobile and immobile,
sat down joyfully in the circular rows for the meal.
The daughters of Lomaśa’s hermitage gave them vessels and seats, and with great eagerness, they served them food.
Then, the daughters of the divine creation of eight kalpas,
along with the eight divine progenies, eagerly prepared the meal.

Then they gave to those respective classes of gods infinite nectars, radiant and sweet foods, and juices— edible, chewable, suckable, and drinkable, all endowed with exquisite flavors— each suited to its particular group. 32.
Having eaten until satisfied, they drank beverages and used mouth-fresheners.
They took betel leaves and other offerings and departed for their dwellings with eager anticipation;
then, at that time, the rows of inhabitants of the netherworlds (atala) and other realms [gathered].
There were rows of Daityas, Dānavas, Asuras, and likewise Rakṣasas, as well as Nāgas, serpents, and those who dwell in the waters. (35)
Various kinds of foods fit for the inhabitants of each respective world—both solid foods and diverse edibles, as well as things to be licked, sucked, and tasted in every way. (36)
And eager maidens served the side dishes and drinks, rich in flavor, in suitable vessels and other utensils. (37)
Of those who possess form and those who are the supreme formless principles, of the qualities endowed with virtue, of actions, and of all sacred fords seeking purification; ||38||
And they became suitable handmaidens for the poor, the blind, and the wretched—whether men, women, or eunuchs—as well as for the various guilds of both mobile and immobile beings. (39)
The servants and the brahmins served them exceedingly well;
they fed them most abundantly and gave them very cool drinks.
The essences of forests, the essences of water, the essences of fire, the juices of the earth, the essences of cows, the essences of grass, the essences of tubers, and intoxicating liquors; ||41||

Those whose essence is the body, those whose essence is mud, those whose essence is flowers, those whose essence is sap and so forth, those whose essence is leaves, those whose essence is roots, and those whose essence is craftsmanship—these are the various types of beings that arise. ||42||

Those whose essence is in the stalks, those whose essence is in the sheaths, those whose essence is in the seeds, those with excellent fruits, those whose essence is in the flower-clusters, those whose essence is in the stems, and likewise those produced from the stalks; ||43||

[He offered] the essence of the earth, the essence of the sky, the essence of the clouds, those produced by the seasons, the essence of rain, the essence of merit, the essence of faith, and those arising from the heart. (44)
The maidens gave to the worthy recipients essences of dreams, essences of time, essences of material substances, those arising from qualities,
essences of ritual action, essences of yoga, and forms created through sovereign power;
they gave all kinds of essences of food to those who were worthy.
Where Lakṣmī, Śrī, Kamalā, Haṃsā, and Ramā are the bestowers [of blessings]. ||46||
O Rādhā, what deficiency can there be among those who assist with food and drink, where Kṛṣṇa himself is the host and Lakṣmī herself is the provider? (47)
Since the wish-fulfilling creepers there gather all things together, what indeed could be considered a deficiency?
Moreover, all abodes and worlds truly resort to it in embodied form. (48)
Where the principles of reality abide, what indeed could be called a low ground?
Where fire itself is the cook, there satiety is the server. (49)
There, where the food consists of the syllables of nectar, what indeed is lowliness?
For there, the Great Lords are perpetually satisfied by supreme bliss.
There, the successes that are the wonders of all sovereignty exist like wish-fulfilling trees and wish-granting jewels; what indeed is lowliness there? (51)
Thus, O Rādhikā, after the refusal of food,
Lomaśa himself ate, and thereafter Bālakṛṣṇa did so as well.
Then the cooks and those who served the food ate;
after that, the sons of Kṛṣṇa ate, and then the kinsmen of the cowherds ate.
Then the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa himself ate, and thereafter the glorious Kaṃbharāśrī, together with her sons, ate as well. 54.
The mother gave excellent foods to the servants, and Kambharā also gave edible provisions to insects, fish, birds, and even those who live by their fortune,
as well as to those whose eating is never restricted.
He gave away gold, silver, and jewels by the tens of millions as sacrificial fees.
Having rested for a moment, in the afternoon, the assembly hall that increases the honor of men became the gathering place for the supreme lords of the gods and for all embodied beings.
Resplendent upon a golden throne and filled with millions of bards and singers, the glorious Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa shines in the midst of the sky. ||58||
In the height [of the image], there is the seat rich with the splendor of elephants; on the sides are the Father and likewise the Mother, as well as Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, Śrī, and Nārāyaṇa. (59)
Hemanta and the Blessed One both stood there holding chowries for him;
likewise were the male and female incarnations, the lords, and the hosts of goddesses.
The gods and goddesses, the ancestors and those belonging to the ancestral rites, the sages and the seers, the asuras and the female asuras, as well as human beings and women. ||61||

Beasts, birds, plants, serpents, Daityas, and women—by these sentient and insentient beings, that long and vast assembly hall shone; it was filled with various principles (tattvas) and with excellent embodied beings, both divine and non-divine. ||62||
Then a most beautiful dance by the female dancers commenced,
along with the songs of the Apsarases and the exquisite instrumental music of the Gandharvas.
An excellent and auspicious dance by the Gandharva women commenced;
when the dancing was concluded, the wrestlers displayed their skill in combat.
They displayed the battlegrounds most intensely, appearing like actors performing through the art of dramatic representation. ||65||
The art of moving through the air by means of ropes, the practice of leaping up, flying, fighting in the sky, and the display of sorcery were put on show. (66)
Then, indeed, there arose songs visible through the power of lightning, filled with the weight of Kṛṣṇa’s glory.
The most excellent expositions of the Vidyādharas took place there, and the instructions of the Siddhas were deeply moving to the heart. (68)
Those skilled in the arts of bards, wandering singers, and panegyrists, as well as those renowned for their poetic fame, praised him;
even the women sang of this festival.
At the command of the venerable Sanatkumāra, Nārada praised that supreme, divine festival, the like of which had never occurred before nor would ever occur again.
Wherein resides the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord; He is the worthy recipient of the sacrificial thread, as are His incarnations and great manifestations. ||71||
That which exists as the Great One (Mahat) is the source from which the three worlds have arisen, bestowing honor;
therein are all tastes, all fragrances, and all forms of bliss in every respect.
Wherein all truths reside, along with the manifestations of Śrī, Bhū, and Līlā—no such greatness shall ever come to be; this greatness is superior to all else. (73)
One must practice the remembrance of Him, as well as hearing and reflecting upon Him;
indeed, through the meditative absorption (nididhyāsana) upon Him alone, there is direct liberation in the abode of Hari.
Only that should be done in the world by which, once performed, one enters liberation;
by performing that, no bondage whatsoever arises within saṃsāra. (75)
These great festivals of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa must always be performed by devotees, so that they may be liberated from bondage. (76)
For those submerged in the ocean of worldly existence and sinking under the burden of family life, the refuge here is Śrī Hari, who is the savior in the form of a boat. (77)
Those who have taken refuge in Hari Nārāyaṇa, the Guru, the Supreme Lord,
and the Lord of Kamalā, do not go to the domain of Dharmarāja.
That is a true tongue which praises Hari; that is a true mind which is offered to Mādhava;
those two hands are indeed praiseworthy to be known as such which are devoted to the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (79)
Otherwise, his throat is like a withered branch of a tree, devoid of service; he who does not sing of Mādhava has the throat of a jackal. (2.67.80)
That alone is a great disease where there is no remembrance of Hari;
he alone is truly pitiable among the living who does not worship Keśava. (81)
This Supreme Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, is worshipful to all incarnations; this Supreme Person is worthy of adoration. (82)
Those worshippers are not to be pitied; for even when dead, they go to liberation.
All that is moving and unmoving here shines within Bālakṛṣṇa. 83.
By whomsoever worship is performed for him, by him the entire world of moving and non-moving beings is honored;
for just as the qualities of the ocean of jewels are innumerable, so too are the qualities of Śrī Hari.
She has taken refuge in the Lord of Lakṣmī, the husband of Rādhā, Prabhā, and Pāravatī; therefore, she is not afflicted by suffering in saṃsāra, as she is destined for liberation. (85)
This child, whose seven hands are marked with the signs of the trident, banner, bow, arrow, fish, svastika, and wheel, is being worshipped by him. (86)
He by whom this Lord Bālakṛṣṇa is worshipped—accompanied by the sixteen marks consisting of vertical lines upon his two lotus feet—is truly honored. (87)
He who worships this child—who bears all weapons and is an ocean of skill in all arts—shall undoubtedly attain liberation. 88.
In whose inner organ is Kṛṣṇa, and in whose self is Nārāyaṇa;
pervaded by Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa, he has no fear of death anywhere. (89)
For those who have taken refuge in the Supreme Goal and who delight in Bālakṛṣṇa, there is never any downward descent; for they are qualified for the supreme abode.
Devotees of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa attain the supreme liberation of the virtuous, as praised by Rādhā, Ramā, and others. 91.
For those who engage in battle, who are righteous, of virtuous nature, and great-souled—
those who know the Blessed One— there exists the auspicious, supreme goal beyond all other goals.
Devotees alone behold Kṛṣṇa, who is subtle, all-pervading, and dark; others do not.
Likewise, those great-souled ones who are abodes of compassion behold that Kṛṣṇa. 93.
He whose every action is directed toward Kṛṣṇa and offered unto Him—though he be the doer of all—he is not a doer; he is not bound, but is liberated. (94)
Those for whom Hari is eternally dear are always dear to Hari;
and he who meditates upon Hari, Hari meditates upon him as one who has taken refuge at His feet. (95)
Rising at dawn, one should devotedly remember this Bālakṛṣṇa;
for he is indeed to be heard, to be made to hear, and the savior from all difficulties. 96.
Indeed, those who possess unwavering devotion toward this Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa cross over [the ocean of existence] by drinking the nectar of His stories. 97.
They will perform [these acts] and go to where Hari himself resides;
such is the destination in the supreme abode for those who are devoted to the service of Kṛṣṇa.
Indeed, that [state] is not attained even in a thousand lifetimes through ascetic penances;
what need is there for recitations, for the utterance of mantras, or for efforts involving various supports? (99)
What is the use of sacrifices, what of gifts, what of religious duties, and what of fame—
for one by whom Śrī Hari has been attained, even if it be through many other means?
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
If this mantra, the bestower of all goals, is recited, what need is there for other learning? (101)
Victory belongs to those for whom Hari is their goal; liberation, which is higher than the highest, belongs to them;
and gain as well as auspiciousness belong to those in whose hearts the Supreme Lord resides.
Thousands of millions of sacred fords and hundreds of millions of acts of charity do not equal even a sixteenth part of bowing to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (103)
By the name Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the fruit of all holy places is attained;
through meditation on Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the yogin attains the supreme goal.
Even those who perform the worship of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa with water alone shall go to the supreme abode of the virtuous, the performers of meritorious deeds.
For those women who remember Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa as their husband at the three junctions of the day, there is liberation even while they remain in their bodies; of this there is no doubt. (106)
Men and women, asuras and gods, as well as lords and even those who rule over the northeast— if you serve Bālakṛṣṇa, you shall attain the supreme goal.
Blessed are Rādhā, Ramā, and the others; blessed are the artisans and the young maidens;
blessed is the Kuṅkumavāpī pond, for its beloved is the Lord himself.
